records.title: [Tracking] Multi-tenant LoRA for MoE under Expert Parallelism on Blackwell
records.body:
## Goal

Enable **multi-tenant LoRA for MoE models under Expert Parallelism** on Blackwell (GB200), end-to-end. This is a tracking issue — the implementation work is split across the two sub-issues linked below.

Use case: multi-tenant RL training and inference serving platforms that run many LoRA adapters concurrently against a shared FP8 MoE base model. Without a fully-fused per-expert LoRA path *and* EP-aware LoRA routing, these workloads cannot scale to large MoE models.

## Sub-tasks

- [x] #3108 — FusedMoE: per-sequence LoRA ID + per-expert LoRA weights fused into the kernel (`op: moe`)
- [x] #3109  — NVLink EP dispatch: carry per-token LoRA IDs through all-to-all (`op: comm`)

Sub-issue #3108 is independently useful for TP-only deployments. Under EP, both are required for a correct end-to-end result.

## End-to-end success criteria

- FusedMoE kernel on Blackwell (GB200) applies per-expert LoRA deltas selected by a per-token LoRA ID, with FP8 base weights + BF16 LoRA A/B weights.
- Under Expert Parallelism, LoRA IDs reach the destination rank in sync with their tokens via the NVLink EP dispatch — no host-side reconstruction needed.
- Functional on a representative large MoE model (e.g. GLM-family) with up to ~8 concurrent adapters and ~2K active sequences per step.
- End-to-end overhead vs. the non-LoRA fused path is ≤ ~30% for v1.

## Notes
- v1 scope is inference / RL rollout forward. Training-time backward and per-token rank variation are out of scope for v1 (tracked separately if needed).
records.author: mferrato

records.title: [Feat] FusedMoE: per-sequence LoRA ID + per-expert LoRA weights fused into the kernel
records.body:
> Sub-task of umbrella issue **#3107** (multi-tenant LoRA for MoE under EP).
> Companion issue for EP dispatch: **#3109**.

## Motivation

Multi-tenant RL training and inference serving platforms need to run many LoRA adapters concurrently against a shared MoE base model. Today there is no fused MoE kernel that accepts LoRA IDs per sequence and applies the corresponding per-expert LoRA weights inside the kernel — users are forced into unfused post-hoc LoRA paths that don't hold up at MoE scale (EP, large expert counts, high concurrency).

A fully-fused per-expert LoRA path inside FusedMoE would unblock multi-tenant MoE on Blackwell (GB200) for both RL rollout/training and serving.

This issue covers the **kernel side** only. It is independently useful for TP-only deployments. Under Expert Parallelism it additionally requires **#3109** to route per-token LoRA IDs through the EP all-to-all.

## Proposal

Extend FusedMoE to accept a per-sequence LoRA ID tensor and apply the corresponding LoRA deltas on a per-expert basis inside the kernel:

```python
flashinfer.fused_moe(
    hidden_states,             # FP8 activations
    w1, w2,                    # FP8 expert base weights
    topk_ids, topk_weights,
    lora_ids=lora_ids,         # [num_tokens] int32, adapter index per token
    lora_a=lora_a,             # BF16, [num_experts, num_adapters, rank, hidden]
    lora_b=lora_b,             # BF16, [num_experts, num_adapters, out, rank]
    ...,
)
```

Semantics: for each routed (token, expert) pair, pick `lora_ids[token]`, apply `W_e · x + (B_{e,lora} · A_{e,lora}) · x` within the fused expert GEMM epilogue.
A "no-adapter" sentinel ID should short-circuit the LoRA path for that token.

## Requirements

- **Dtypes:** FP8 base weights + FP8 activations, BF16 LoRA A/B weights. Activations are upcast before the LoRA path; base GEMM stays in FP8.
- **Concurrency:** support up to ~8 concurrent adapters with ~2K active sequences per step.
- **Expert Parallelism compatible:** kernel must run correctly on the post- dispatch local expert slice (see companion issue on EP dispatch LoRA-ID passthrough).
- **Overhead budget:** up to ~20–30% over the non-LoRA fused path is acceptable for v1.
- **HW:** GB200 / SM100 priority; generalize to other Blackwell SKUs.

## Out of scope for v1

- Per-token rank (all adapters assumed same rank for a given deployment).
- Training-time backward (inference + RL-rollout forward first; bwd can follow).
records.author: mferrato

records.title: [Feat] NVLink EP dispatch: carry per-token LoRA IDs through all-to-all
records.body:
> Sub-task of umbrella issue **#3107** (multi-tenant LoRA for MoE under EP).
> Consumer of this metadata passthrough: **#3108** (fused MoE kernel with per-expert LoRA).

## Motivation

Fused MoE with multi-tenant LoRA (**#3108**) needs the per-token LoRA adapter ID to be available on the destination rank *after* the EP all-to-all dispatch — otherwise the fused expert kernel has no way to pick the right adapter weights for each token it receives.

Today, FlashInfer's NVLink EP dispatch shuffles tokens (and topk metadata) but does not have a sanctioned way to carry arbitrary per-token side-band metadata through the dispatch/combine pair.

## Proposal

Add a per-token metadata passthrough to the NVLink EP dispatch/combine APIs — at minimum an `int32` LoRA-ID channel, ideally a small generic side-band tensor so future per-token routing hints can reuse the same path:

```python
dispatched_tokens, dispatched_lora_ids, handle = flashinfer.ep.dispatch(
    hidden_states,
    topk_ids, topk_weights,
    extra_per_token={"lora_id": lora_ids},  # [num_tokens] int32
    ...,
)
# ... fused MoE with per-expert LoRA using dispatched_lora_ids ...
combined = flashinfer.ep.combine(expert_out, handle)
```

On combine, the per-token side-band is dropped (it's only needed on the forward dispatch).

## Requirements

- Zero/near-zero overhead vs. the existing dispatch when the side-band is unused.
- Supports ~2K sequences, up to 8 concurrent adapter IDs (IDs are small ints — no hashing needed).
- Compatible with the existing NVLink dispatch kernel and CUDA-graph capture.
- HW: Blackwell (GB200) priority.
records.author: mferrato

records.title: [Feat] Modular BF16 MoE expert kernel — parity with FP8 / NVFP4 modular path
records.body:
> Related: existing umbrella **#3107** (multi-tenant LoRA for MoE under EP) —  this issue is a prerequisite for the BF16 training/LoRA path of that work,  but is independently useful for any BF16 MoE deployment that uses the FlashInfer NVLink all-to-all backend.

## Motivation

The modular MoE path in vLLM (dispatch / compute split) works correctly with the FlashInfer NVLink all-to-all backend for the TRT-LLM **FP8** and **NVFP4** expert kernels — a modular version exists for those dtypes.

The **BF16** TRT-LLM expert kernel is still monolithic: dispatch and compute are entangled in the same call, so it cannot be plugged into the modular MoE flow. When a user tries to combine the BF16 expert kernel with FlashInfer NVLink all-to-all dispatch today, outputs are **silently incorrect** (garbage tensors, no error). Users are forced to fall back to the Triton BF16 expert kernel, which is significantly slower and blocks BF16 MoE training paths (e.g. BF16 LoRA) on Expert Parallelism.

## Proposal

Provide a modular BF16 expert kernel with the same split already used for FP8 and NVFP4:

- Expose expert **compute** as a standalone callable that takes already - dispatched tokens (post FlashInfer NVLink all-to-all) and returns per-expert outputs ready for combine.
- Keep API / tensor layouts / metadata shapes consistent with the FP8 and NVFP4 modular paths, so downstream callers (vLLM, custom stacks) can swap dtype without restructuring the pipeline.
- Numerics must match the monolithic BF16 kernel within acceptable tolerance on dense (non-dispatched) workloads.

## Success criteria

- A BF16 expert kernel usable in the same modular MoE flow as FP8 / NVFP4.
- Correct outputs end-to-end when combined with FlashInfer NVLink all-to-all dispatch on Blackwell (GB200).
- Parity with FP8 / NVFP4 modular path on the API surface and EP semantics.

## Scope

- **HW:** Blackwell / GB200 priority.
- **Models:** any BF16 MoE in vLLM; representative target is a large MoE in the GLM / DeepSeek family.
- **Out of scope for v1:** FP16, non-NVLink dispatch backends (nice-to-have but not required).
records.author: mferrato

records.title: [Feat] HiSparse sparse attention (DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM 5.1) on Blackwell
records.body:
## Motivation

Recent frontier MoE models — notably **DeepSeek V3.2** and **GLM 5.1** — use **HiSparse** sparse attention (LMSYS, *"HiSparse: Turbocharging Sparse Attention with Hierarchical Memory"*) in place of dense attention at long context. HiSparse has already been integrated into SGLang; there is currently no equivalent kernel available in FlashInfer, so serving stacks that build on FlashInfer (vLLM in particular) cannot run these architectures efficiently without falling back to dense attention, which is prohibitively expensive at the context lengths these models are designed for.

FlashInfer already tracks some adjacent pieces of the DeepSeek V3.2 stack (e.g. `model: dsv3.2` labelled issues such as the segmented top-K work in #3096) — this issue is to track the HiSparse attention kernel itself.

## Proposal

Implement HiSparse attention as a FlashInfer attention kernel on Blackwell:

- Support the hierarchical-memory sparse-attention pattern as described in the HiSparse reference (LMSYS) and as used in DeepSeek V3.2 / GLM 5.1.
- Prefill and decode paths.
- Integrate with FlashInfer's existing attention launchers / planner APIs so downstream serving stacks can select HiSparse the same way they select other attention variants today.
- Blackwell / SM100 as the primary target; other SMs as a follow-up.

## Success criteria

- Functional parity with the reference HiSparse implementation on representative shapes.
- Usable end-to-end on DeepSeek V3.2 and GLM 5.1 model architectures (validated against expected logits / generations).
- Performance advantage over dense attention at the context lengths these models are deployed at; reasonable parity with the SGLang HiSparse integration as a public baseline.

## Notes

- This is **not** the same as the ModelOpt sparse-attention integration (different sparsity mechanism).
- Reference: https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-04-10-sglang-hisparse/

records.title: [SM120] Only one valid FP8×FP4 MoE tile shape (128×128×128); other shapes fail Stages≥2 constraint
records.body:
<!-- obsidian -->
Component | Version
-- | --
OS | Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS
Kernel | 6.17.0-14-generic
GPU | NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition
GPU Memory | 97,887 MiB (~96 GB)
GPU Driver | 580.126.16
GPU Compute Capability | SM120 (12.0)
CUDA Toolkit | 12.8 (V12.8.93)
Python | 3.12.3
PyTorch | 2.10.0+cu128
vLLM | 0.19.0
FlashInfer | 0.6.6
Model | openai/gpt-oss-20b (MXFP4 quantized)





On FlashInfer `0.6.6` / `SM120` (`compute_120a`), CUTLASS fused MoE for `FP8 activations x FP4 weights` appears to have limited valid kernel coverage.

During autotuning, many `SM120` TMA warp-specialized tactics fail at profile time and are skipped. The failing path is:

```text
dispatchMoeGemmSelectClusterShapeTmaWarpSpecialized(...)
```

with errors such as unsupported tile/cluster combinations for `arch 120`.

As a result, the backend runs from a reduced set of surviving tactics and is observably slower than Marlin on this workload.

Separately, Blackwell support is still incomplete in some areas. For example, `cutlass_fused_moe()` explicitly raises `NotImplementedError` for `min_latency_mode` on Blackwell.

## Environment

- FlashInfer `0.6.6`
- CUDA `12.8`
- GPU: `SM120` / `compute_120a`

## Relevant Source References

### `flashinfer/jit/fused_moe.py`

SM120 CUTLASS fused MoE is compiled with TMA-focused flags:

```python
# flashinfer/jit/fused_moe.py:33-47
def gen_cutlass_fused_moe_sm120_module(use_fast_build: bool = False) -> JitSpec:
    nvcc_flags = [
        "-DCOMPILE_BLACKWELL_TMA_GEMMS",
        "-DCOMPILE_BLACKWELL_SM120_TMA_GROUPED_GEMMS",
        "-DENABLE_BF16",
        "-DENABLE_FP8",
        "-DENABLE_FP4",
        "-DUSING_OSS_CUTLASS_MOE_GEMM",
    ]

    nvcc_flags += current_compilation_context.get_nvcc_flags_list(
        supported_major_versions=[12]
    )

    return gen_cutlass_fused_moe_module(nvcc_flags, "120", use_fast_build)
```

### `flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py`

Blackwell `min_latency_mode` is explicitly not implemented:

```python
# flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py:884-885
if min_latency_mode:
    raise NotImplementedError("min latency mode not yet implemented for Blackwell.")
```

## Observed Runtime Errors

Example autotuner failures from vLLM debug logs:

```error
[Autotuner]: Skipping tactic ... 1, due to failure while profiling:
void tensorrt_llm::kernels::cutlass_kernels_oss::
dispatchMoeGemmSelectClusterShapeTmaWarpSpecialized(...)
[with Arch = cutlass::arch::Sm120;
 T = __nv_fp8_e4m3;
 WeightType = __nv_fp4_e2m1;
 OutputType = __nv_bfloat16;
 TileShape = cute::tuple<cute::C<128>, cute::C<128>, cute::C<64> >;
 bool IsMXFPX = true]
```

```error
Unsupported tile (128, 128, 64) and cluster (1, 1, 1) shape combination for arch 120.
Config was Cutlass GEMM Tactic
    style=TMA Warp Specialized
    sm: 120
    tile shape ID: 128x128x64
    cluster shape ID: 1x1x1
    dynamic cluster shape ID: undefined
    fallback cluster shape ID: undefined
    mainloop sched: 0
    epi sched: 0
    enable cuda kernel: false
```

Additional failing shapes observed:

```error
Unsupported tile (128, 256, 64) and cluster (1, 1, 1) shape combination for arch 120.
```

```error
Unsupported tile (256, 128, 64) and cluster (1, 1, 1) shape combination for arch 120.
```

These failures repeatedly occur during autotuning for the `FP8 x FP4` path on `SM120`.

## Why This Looks Like a Kernel Coverage Issue

- The `SM120` fused MoE module is compiled around TMA grouped-GEMM support.
- During profiling, many `TMA Warp Specialized` tactics for `FP8 act x FP4 weight` fail and get skipped.
- The backend therefore runs from a reduced set of surviving tactics.
- On this workload, that surviving set is slower than Marlin.

## Request

Please consider one of the following:

- Add valid `SM120` `FP8 x FP4` tile/schedule coverage for CUTLASS fused MoE.
- Provide a reliable non-TMA fallback path for `SM120` `FP8 x FP4` fused MoE GEMMs.

## Notes

This issue is specifically about the observed `SM120` CUTLASS fused MoE behavior for `FP8 activations x FP4 weights`, not Blackwell support in general.

The `min_latency_mode` `NotImplementedError` is included as an additional indicator that Blackwell support in this path is still incomplete, but the main functional problem here is the repeated autotuner rejection of many TMA warp-specialized tactics on `SM120`.
records.author: dhayanesh

records.title: [Feature Request] Fused top-k/top-p sampling with filtered probability output
records.body:
# [Feature Request] Fused top-k/top-p sampling with filtered probability output

## Motivation

In reinforcement learning training (e.g., PPO/GRPO), we often need to obtain both:
1. **Sampled token** - the sampling result
2. **Filtered probability distribution** - after top-k/top-p filtering, used for computing action probability

## Current Limitation

Currently, FlashInfer's `top_k_top_p_sampling_from_probs` only returns the sampled token. To get the filtered probability distribution, users must:
1. First call a separate filter kernel (e.g., `top_k_top_p_filter`)
2. Then call the sampling kernel

This introduces:
- Additional kernel launch overhead
- Extra memory bandwidth consumption (reading probs twice)

## Proposal

Add a new fused API that performs top-k/top-p filtering and sampling in a single kernel pass:

```python
def top_k_top_p_sampling_and_filter(
    probs: torch.Tensor,           # (batch_size, vocab_size)
    top_k: Union[torch.Tensor, int],
    top_p: Union[torch.Tensor, float],
    ...
) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """
    Returns:
        samples: (batch_size,) - sampled token indices
        filtered_probs: (batch_size, vocab_size) - filtered probability distribution
    """
```

## Implementation

I have a working implementation with the following optimizations:
- **Loop-external threadlocal accumulation** - reduces BlockReduce calls in dual-pivot rejection sampling
- **CUDA Cluster / DSM optimization (SM 9.0+)** - leverages Distributed Shared Memory for small batch sizes

### Benchmark Results

Test environment: vocab_size=151936 (Qwen2.5), top_k=1024, top_p=0.98

| batch_size | original | fused | fused vs original | PyTorch baseline | fused vs PyTorch |
|------------|----------|-------|-------------------|------------------|------------------|
| 1          | 0.531ms  | 0.360ms | **1.47x faster** | 0.749ms | **2.08x** |
| 4          | 0.750ms  | 0.467ms | **1.61x faster** | 1.054ms | **2.26x** |
| 64         | 1.109ms  | 1.551ms | 0.71x | 2.427ms | **1.56x** |
| 128        | 1.526ms  | 2.339ms | 0.65x | 4.468ms | **1.91x** |

- Small batch (1-16): fused kernel is faster than original (CUDA Cluster optimization)
- Overall average **1.8x speedup** vs PyTorch baseline

## Draft PR

I have submitted a Draft PR: #3121

Note: The implementation is based on an earlier commit using PyTorch native binding instead of the latest TVM-FFI system.

records.title: trtllm-gen attention error on large batch size
records.body:
Batch size (number of tokens) maps directly to numCtasZ in https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh#L380
CUDA's limit for gridDim.z is 65535, so cuLaunchKernelEx returns CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE on batch size >65535.
However, no python exception is thrown and if users don't notice the error in the logs, will run with incorrect results.
This affects all trtllm-gen attention kernels.

The following is a reproducer (`trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` is used in prefill so hitting batch size >65535 is possible)
```py
import sys
import torch
import flashinfer

BATCH_SIZE = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 65536

# GLM-5 shapes
NUM_HEADS = 64
KV_LORA_RANK = 512
QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM = 64
QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM = 192
HEAD_DIM_QK = KV_LORA_RANK + QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM  # 576

SPARSE_MLA_TOP_K = 2048
PAGE_SIZE = 32
MAX_SEQ_LEN = SPARSE_MLA_TOP_K
NUM_PAGES = MAX_SEQ_LEN // PAGE_SIZE

DEVICE = "cuda:0"

torch.manual_seed(0)

query = torch.randn(BATCH_SIZE, 1, NUM_HEADS, HEAD_DIM_QK, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE)

kv_cache = torch.randn(NUM_PAGES, 1, PAGE_SIZE, HEAD_DIM_QK, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE)

token_indices = torch.arange(SPARSE_MLA_TOP_K, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
block_tables = token_indices.view(1, 1, SPARSE_MLA_TOP_K).expand(BATCH_SIZE, 1, SPARSE_MLA_TOP_K).contiguous()

seq_lens = torch.full((BATCH_SIZE,), MAX_SEQ_LEN, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)

workspace = torch.zeros(256 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.int8, device=DEVICE)

bmm1_scale = 1.0 / (HEAD_DIM_QK**0.5)

print(f"Launching trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla with batch_size={BATCH_SIZE}, sparse_mla_top_k={SPARSE_MLA_TOP_K}")

output = flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(
    query=query,
    kv_cache=kv_cache,
    workspace_buffer=workspace,
    qk_nope_head_dim=QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM,
    kv_lora_rank=KV_LORA_RANK,
    qk_rope_head_dim=QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM,
    block_tables=block_tables,
    seq_lens=seq_lens,
    max_seq_len=MAX_SEQ_LEN,
    sparse_mla_top_k=SPARSE_MLA_TOP_K,
    bmm1_scale=bmm1_scale,
    bmm2_scale=1.0,
    backend="trtllm-gen",
)

assert (
    BATCH_SIZE < 65536
), "Batch size >= 65536 triggers gridDim.z overflow, shouldn't reach here"
```

records.title: Add backend validation guard for MIS v2 (item_offsets) in BatchPrefill plan()
records.body:
## Summary

`plan()` in `flashinfer/prefill.py` accepts the `item_offsets` parameter (introduced in PR #2921) for all backend/dtype configurations, but several built-in execution paths **do not** forward the precomputed `_item_start_ptr` to the kernel. This means a caller can opt into MIS v2 and silently execute with the wrong attention mask instead of receiving a clear error.

## Affected paths

The following paths in `flashinfer/prefill.py` currently accept `item_offsets` in `plan()` but do not consume `_item_start_ptr` during `run()`:

- **`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`**: `cudnn` backend
- **`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`**: `trtllm-gen` backend
- **`BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper`**: `cutlass` backend
- **`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper` / paged `run()`**: FP8 branch in `paged_run()`

## Proposed fix

After the backend/dtype/path is resolved in `plan()`, add an early `ValueError` guard:

```python
if item_offsets is not None and self._backend in ("cudnn", "trtllm-gen", "cutlass"):
    raise ValueError(
        "item_offsets (MIS v2) is not supported for the selected backend. "
        "Use the 'fa2' or 'fa3' backend instead."
    )
```

A similar guard should also cover the paged FP8 branch (`is_float8(q)` + non-FA2 backend).

## References

- PR #2921 (feat: MIS v2)
- Review comment: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/2921#discussion_r3013546656
- Reported by: @coderabbitai
- Requested by: @chanh

1.qwen3-vl-4B-FP8量化attention+linear+ kv cache模型设置flashinfer后端比fa3要慢，这个为啥？ 看attention
的是否走fp8的tensor core，目前我已经在vllm里面设置了 经过linera之后的q是fp8读取，不是bf16，然后qkv计算是fp8读取 所以attention的gemm命中的是fp8的tensor core， fa3后端的attention计算是fp8的qkv。

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import argparse
import base64
import csv
import mimetypes
import statistics
import time
from pathlib import Path

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams


# =========================
# 工具函数
# =========================
def percentile(values, p):
    if not values:
        return None
    values = sorted(values)
    k = (len(values) - 1) * (p / 100.0)
    f = int(k)
    c = min(f + 1, len(values) - 1)
    if f == c:
        return values[f]
    return values[f] + (values[c] - values[f]) * (k - f)


def safe_mean(values):
    return statistics.mean(values) if values else None


def file_to_data_url(path: str) -> str:
    mime, _ = mimetypes.guess_type(path)
    if mime is None:
        mime = "application/octet-stream"
    data = Path(path).read_bytes()
    b64 = base64.b64encode(data).decode("utf-8")
    return f"data:{mime};base64,{b64}"


def build_prompt(image_data_url: str, prompt: str):
    return [{
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": image_data_url}},
            {"type": "text", "text": prompt},
        ],
    }]


# =========================
# 核心：创建 LLM（含 profiler）
# =========================
def create_llm(
    model_path: str,
    tensor_parallel_size: int,
    gpu_memory_utilization: float,
    max_num_seqs: int,
    enable_profiler: bool,
    profiler_dir: str,
):
    import pathlib

    profiler_config = None

    if enable_profiler:
        pathlib.Path(profiler_dir).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # profiler_config = {
        #     "profiler": "torch",
        #     "torch_profiler_dir": profiler_dir,
        #     "torch_profiler_record_shapes": True,
        #     "torch_profiler_with_memory": True,
        #     "torch_profiler_with_stack": True,
        #     "torch_profiler_use_gzip": True,
        #     "torch_profiler_dump_cuda_time_total": True,
        # }




        profiler_config = {
            "profiler": "torch",
            "torch_profiler_dir": profiler_dir,

            "torch_profiler_record_shapes": True,
            "torch_profiler_with_memory": True,
            "torch_profiler_with_stack": True,
            "torch_profiler_use_gzip": True,
            "torch_profiler_dump_cuda_time_total": True,

            # 👇关键参数
            "wait_iterations": 0,
            "warmup_iterations": 1,
            "active_iterations": 10,
        }

        print("\n🔥 Torch Profiler ENABLED")
        print(f"📁 output dir: {profiler_dir}\n")

    return LLM(
        model=model_path,
        trust_remote_code=True,

        tensor_parallel_size=tensor_parallel_size,
        gpu_memory_utilization=gpu_memory_utilization,
        max_num_seqs=max_num_seqs,

        # ✅ 核心：KV cache FP8（vLLM真正支持的）
        # kv_cache_dtype="fp8",
        enable_chunked_prefill =  False,  #禁用 chunk prefill分块
        # 多模态
        limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1},
        enable_prefix_caching=False,
        # attention_config={"disable_flashinfer_q_quantization": False},
        attention_config={"flashinfer_allow_fp8_query_on_hopper": True},
        # CUDA Graph
        compilation_config={
            "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [
                1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,768,1024
            ],
            "max_cudagraph_capture_size": 1024,
        },

        profiler_config=profiler_config,
    )


# =========================
# 单次运行
# =========================
def run_once(llm, prompts, sampling_params):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    outputs = llm.chat(prompts, sampling_params, use_tqdm=False)
    t1 = time.perf_counter()

    total_tokens = 0
    for out in outputs:
        if out.outputs:
            token_ids = out.outputs[0].token_ids
            total_tokens += len(token_ids)

    wall = t1 - t0

    return {
        "wall_s": wall,
        "req_per_s": len(prompts) / wall,
        "tok_per_s": total_tokens / wall,
    }


# =========================
# benchmark
# =========================
def benchmark_one_setting(
    llm,
    image_data_url,
    prompt,
    batch_size,
    num_test,
    warmup_batches,
    max_tokens,
):
    sampling_params = SamplingParams(
        temperature=0.0,
        max_tokens=max_tokens,
        min_tokens=max_tokens,
        ignore_eos=True,
    )

    prompts = [build_prompt(image_data_url, prompt) for _ in range(batch_size)]

    # warmup
    for _ in range(warmup_batches):
        llm.chat(prompts, sampling_params, use_tqdm=False)

    results = []
    for _ in range(num_test):
        results.append(run_once(llm, prompts, sampling_params))

    return {
        "batch_size": batch_size,
        "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "req_per_s": safe_mean([x["req_per_s"] for x in results]),
        "tok_per_s": safe_mean([x["tok_per_s"] for x in results]),
        "p50": percentile([x["wall_s"] for x in results], 50),
        "p95": percentile([x["wall_s"] for x in results], 95),
    }


# =========================
# main
# =========================
def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()

    parser.add_argument("--fp8-model", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--image-path", required=True)

    parser.add_argument("--prompt", default="Read all text.")
    parser.add_argument("--num-test", type=int, default=5)

    parser.add_argument("--batch-sizes", default="64,128,256")
    parser.add_argument("--max-tokens-list", default="64,128,256")

    parser.add_argument("--warmup-batches", type=int, default=1)

    parser.add_argument("--tensor-parallel-size", type=int, default=1)
    parser.add_argument("--gpu-memory-utilization", type=float, default=0.7)
    parser.add_argument("--max-num-seqs", type=int, default=1024)

    # ✅ profiler参数
    parser.add_argument("--enable-profiler", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--profiler-dir", default="./torch_profile")

    parser.add_argument("--output-csv", default="result.csv")

    args = parser.parse_args()

    batch_sizes = [int(x) for x in args.batch_sizes.split(",")]
    max_tokens_list = [int(x) for x in args.max_tokens_list.split(",")]

    image_data_url = file_to_data_url(args.image_path)

    print("🚀 Loading model...")

    llm = create_llm(
        model_path=args.fp8_model,
        tensor_parallel_size=args.tensor_parallel_size,
        gpu_memory_utilization=args.gpu_memory_utilization,
        max_num_seqs=args.max_num_seqs,
        enable_profiler=args.enable_profiler,
        profiler_dir=args.profiler_dir,
    )

    all_results = []
    if args.enable_profiler:
        # vLLM 的 torch profiler 需要显式 start/stop；trace 会在 stop 时写入 torch_profiler_dir
        llm.start_profile(profile_prefix="offline_fp8")

    try:
        for batch_size in batch_sizes:
            for max_tokens in max_tokens_list:
                print(f"\n[RUN] batch={batch_size}, tokens={max_tokens}")

                result = benchmark_one_setting(
                    llm,
                    image_data_url,
                    args.prompt,
                    batch_size,
                    args.num_test,
                    args.warmup_batches,
                    max_tokens,
                )

                print(result)
                all_results.append(result)
    finally:
        if args.enable_profiler:
            llm.stop_profile()

    with open(args.output_csv, "w", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=all_results[0].keys())
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(all_results)

    print(f"\n✅ Saved to {args.output_csv}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()






# python /nfs/dataset-ofs-heterogeneous-computing/cuihangbin/vlm_infra/vllm/offline_sweep_qwen3vl_compare_fp8.py   --fp8-model /nfs/dataset-ofs-heterogeneous-computing/cuihangbin/llm_model/Qwen3-VL-4B/FP8BLOCK-ATTNHEAD   --image-path /nfs/dataset-ofs-architecture/liweijie/workspace/sglang_git/sglang_0_5_9/sglang/receipt.png   --batch-sizes 64,128   --max-tokens-list 64,128   --max-num-seqs 1024  --enable-profiler --profiler-dir  ./trace_fp8

The benchmark passes `scale` as a Python float to `fused_add_rmsnorm_quant`, which internally creates a new CPU tensor and copies it to CUDA during CUDA graph capture, an operation CUDA graphs forbid unless the CPU tensor is pinned. The fix converts `scale` to a CUDA tensor before the benchmark closure is captured, so no CPU→CUDA copy happens during graph replay.

Edit: the same issue applies for this benchmark command:

```bash
python benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine rmsnorm_quant --batch_size 32 --hidden_size 4096 --input_dtype bfloat16 --out_dtype fp8_e4m3 --scale 1.0 --refcheck -vv --generate_repro_command --case_tag "rmsnorm_quant_fp8_e4m3"
```

Root Cause (By Claude Code)

  #3091 rewrote fastdiv.cuh to wrap cuda::fast_mod_div<uint32_t> from <cuda/cmath>, which requires CCCL ≥ 3.x. The same PR

  the CTK-bundled copy.

  The build fails when flashinfer/data/cccl is missing — either because:
  - The 3rdparty/cccl submodule was not initialized after pulling this commit (i.e., git submodule update --init --recursive
  was not run), or
  - An old flashinfer-jit-cache wheel (built before #3091) is installed and does not contain the CCCL headers under
  flashinfer/data/cccl/

  Without the vendored CCCL headers, the compiler falls back to the CTK-bundled CCCL (CTK 12.x ships CCCL ≤ 2.x), which does
  not have cuda::fast_mod_div, causing the compilation to fail.

records.title: perf: MIS-aware tile scheduling to skip fully-masked (Q tile, KV chunk) pairs
records.body:
## Summary

The tile scheduler in `plan()` currently launches CTAs for all (Q tile, KV chunk) pairs regardless of mask mode. For MIS v1/v2, many of these pairs are entirely masked (Q tile is in item A, KV chunk is in item B's region). These CTAs launch, iterate through the three-phase loop, skip all tiles internally, and exit — wasting SM occupancy and launch overhead.

## Proposed optimization

Make the tile scheduler MIS-aware: during `plan()`, use `prefix_len_ptr` and `item_offsets` (or `token_pos_in_items`) to determine which (Q tile, KV chunk) pairs have any valid attention, and only emit those into `request_indices` / `qo_tile_indices` / `kv_tile_indices`.

## Expected benefit

- Fewer CTAs launched → less SM time wasted on no-op work
- Most impactful for workloads with many items and KV partitioning (`partition_kv=true`), where multiple KV chunks span different items' regions

## Complexity

- Scheduler (`scheduler.cuh`) would need mask-mode-specific logic
- CPU-side `plan()` would iterate over items to determine valid tile pairs
- Merge step for `partition_kv` would need to handle gaps in tile assignments
- Different scheduling paths per mask mode adds code complexity

## References

- PR #2921 (MIS v2)
- Current three-phase skip: `include/flashinfer/attention/prefill.cuh` lines 2345-2356
- Scheduler: `include/flashinfer/attention/scheduler.cuh`

### Summary
 Since nightly release #224 (Apr 14, 2026 US evening time), cubin downloads from the NVIDIA Artifactory endpoint are intermittently returning HTTP 403 errors, even though the files are accessible when the URL is opened in a browser. records.title: [Bug] trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe autotune corrupts device state on num_tokens=16384 bucket (SM100/SM103, NVFP4 MoE, vLLM-padded hidden 2688→2816)
records.body:
## Summary
On SM100 (GB200) and SM103 (GB300), `flashinfer.fused_moe.trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` produces incorrect behavior when the MoE hidden dim is not a multiple of 512 and the caller has zero-padded weights to the next 256-multiple. Two manifestations, same root cause:

1. **Autotune corruption.** At `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, autotune profile 6 corrupts the CUDA device context; the next probe surfaces `torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`.
2. **Silent numerical corruption.** Engine initialises, autotune completes, generation produces garbage — factual prompts return incorrect tokens.

Both disappear when `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` is replaced by `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` on the same padded weights.

## Hardware scope

Verified across four Blackwell devices on `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4` (hidden=2688):

| Device | SM | Selected backend | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB200 | 100 | `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` + padding 2688→2816 | **Fails** |
| GB300 | 103 | `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` + padding 2688→2816 | **Fails** |
| Thor AGX | 110 | `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` | Passes |
| DGX Spark (GB10) | 121 | `VLLM_CUTLASS` (all FI rejected) | Passes |

SM100 / SM103 specific for the TRTLLM-GEN NVFP4 padded path.

## Reproduction
```bash
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP4=1 \
vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --trust-remote-code
```
The model's `hidden_size=2688`. vLLM's `align_trtllm_fp4_moe_hidden_dim_for_fi` zero-pads weights to 2816 at load time, then calls `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`. First inference request hits either manifestation above.

## `max_num_batched_tokens` threshold

Autotune sweeps 14 token-count buckets. The `num_tokens=16384` bucket is the corrupting one:

| MNBT | outcome |
|---|---|
| ≤ 12288 (top bucket = 8192) | 14/14 clean |
| 16384 (vLLM default) | crash at profile 6 |

Smaller buckets all complete. `gpu_memory_utilization` has no effect.

## Workarounds

1. `--max-num-batched-tokens=12288` — autotune passes.
2. `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP4=0` — falls to `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS`.

Disabling autotune alone is **not** a fix: `enable_flashinfer_autotune=False` moves the IMA into `cublasGemmEx(..., K=2688, BF16, ...)` during cudagraph capture.

## Related

- [vllm-project/vllm#39510](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39510) — enabled the padded TRTLLM path for non-512-aligned hidden.
- [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2776](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/2776) — same model and IMA symptom but on SM121 / GB10 during CUDA graph capture (different phase, different device).
- [vllm-project/vllm#40047](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/40047), [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#3057](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3057), [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2861](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/2861) — NaN contamination from cudagraph padding in other per-token kernels.

records.title: DGX Spark (SM121) Current Support Audit
records.body:
# FlashInfer — DGX Spark (SM121) Current Support Audit

**Date:** 2026-04-24
**Scope:** Audit of SM121 (compute capability 12.1, DGX Spark) support across FlashInfer ops, APIs, backends, and testing.
**Goal:** Improve Spark usability on FlashInfer by identifying existing gaps.

**Note: skip to "15. Consolidated Action Items" for TLDR.**

---

## Architecture Context

| Gencode | Target | CUDA Requirement |
|---------|--------|------------------|
| `compute_120a` / `sm_120a` | RTX 5090 (SM120) | CUDA 12.8 |
| `compute_120f` / `sm_120f` | SM12x family (120 + 121) | CUDA 12.9 |
| `compute_121a` / `sm_121a` | DGX Spark (SM121) | CUDA 12.9 |

### SM120 vs SM121: Implications for FlashInfer

Per the [CUDA 13.2 Programming Guide — Compute Capabilities](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html) (Tables 29–33), SM120 and SM121 share a single "12.x" spec column: identical shared memory (99 KB/block, 100 KB/SM), warps (48/SM), registers (64K/SM), tensor core data types (TF32, BF16, FP16, FP8, FP6, FP4, INT8), TMA, and cluster support. [Table 28](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/cuda-programming-guide/05-appendices/compute-capabilities.html#compute-capabilities-family-specific-compatibility) confirms `compute_120f` is compatible with **both** CC 12.0 and 12.1. The chip-level differences (SM121 = aarch64 host, unified LPDDR5x, 84 SMs vs SM120's x86_64, discrete GDDR7, up to 170 SMs) do not affect kernel correctness — only SM-count-based heuristics and host toolchain.

### `f` vs `a` compilation targets: performance implications

Per the [PTX ISA 9.3](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/index.html) (§9.7.15.5.14 for dense `mma`, §9.7.15.6.3 for sparse `mma.sp`), `120f` (family) is a subset of `120a`/`121a` (arch-specific). Most SM12x features — including **dense** NVFP4/MXFP4 block-scaled MMA — are family-specific and available via `120f` from PTX ISA 8.8. The arch-specific restriction (requiring `sm_120a`/`sm_121a`) applies **only to sparse MMA** (`mma.sp`) with `.kind::mxf4nvf4`/`.kind::mxf4`:

| PTX Feature | `compute_120` (baseline) | `compute_120f` (family) | `compute_120a` / `compute_121a` (arch) |
|-------------|--------------------------|------------------------|----------------------------------------|
| FP4/FP6/FP8 conversions (`cvt`) | No | Yes | Yes |
| FP4/FP6 MMA, block-scaled MMA (`.kind::mxf8f6f4`) | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Dense** NVFP4 MMA (`.kind::mxf4nvf4`) | No | **Yes** (PTX ISA ≥ 8.8) | **Yes** |
| **Dense** MXFP4 MMA (`.kind::mxf4`) | No | **Yes** (PTX ISA ≥ 8.8) | **Yes** |
| **Sparse** NVFP4 MMA (`mma.sp` `.kind::mxf4nvf4`) | No | **No** | **Yes** |
| **Sparse** MXFP4 MMA (`mma.sp` `.kind::mxf4`) | No | **No** | **Yes** |

FlashInfer's b12x GEMM kernel (`dense_blockscaled_gemm_sm120_b12x.py`) uses `cute.nvgpu.warp.MmaMXF4NVF4Op` — a **dense** block-scaled MMA atom. This means `sm_120f` wheels already emit native NVFP4/MXFP4 dense MMA instructions. Only **sparse** NVFP4/MXFP4 MMA (not currently used in FlashInfer) requires `sm_120a`/`sm_121a`.

> **Correction (2026-06-12):** An earlier version of this table stated that ALL `.kind::mxf4nvf4`/`.kind::mxf4` MMA was arch-specific-only. Per [Harry-Chen's feedback](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3170#issuecomment-4677810517) and PTX ISA §9.7.15.5.14 vs §9.7.15.6.3, the restriction is limited to the sparse (`mma.sp`) variant.

### Wheel build arch targets

The release wheel CI (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) builds the following SM12x targets:

| CUDA Version | SM12x target in `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` |
|---|---|
| < 12.9 | `12.0a` (SM120 arch-specific; no SM121 support) |
| >= 12.9, < 13.0 | `12.0f` (family; covers SM120 + SM121; includes dense NVFP4/MXFP4 MMA) |
| >= 13.0 | `12.0f` (same) |

**No `121a` target is included in any wheel build.** However, since FlashInfer's FP4 kernels use **dense** block-scaled MMA (`MmaMXF4NVF4Op`, not sparse), the `120f` wheels already emit native NVFP4/MXFP4 MMA instructions. The `121a` target would only be needed for future sparse MMA kernels. JIT compilation on SM121 still produces `121a` cubins for forward-compatibility.

### What this means for FlashInfer

- **Any kernel that runs on SM120 is architecturally compatible with SM121.** Hardcoded `sm_version == "sm_120"` or `minor == 0` checks in backend dispatch are over-restricting without justification.
- **Separate cubins matter for JIT but not for wheels.** `CompilationContext` correctly emits `sm_121a` for JIT on SM121. Since FlashInfer uses only dense block-scaled MMA (available on `120f`), the wheels do not lose FP4 GEMM performance. The `121a` JIT path provides forward-compatibility for future sparse MMA use.
- **SMEM capacity maps, tile configs, and MMA atoms are identical.** Code using `get_smem_capacity_in_bytes("sm_120")` returns the correct value for SM121 too — the only risk is `KeyError` if a map expects an `"sm_121"` key and doesn't have one.

### Key utility functions

| Function (`utils.py`) | Behavior for SM121 |
|------------------------|--------------------|
| `is_sm12x_supported` | True (CUDA ≥ 12.9) |
| `is_sm121a_supported` | True (CUDA ≥ 12.9) |
| `is_sm120a_supported` | **False** (12.0 only) |
| `device_support_pdl` | True (`major >= 9`) |
| `determine_attention_backend` | Returns `fa2` (fa3 is SM90-only) |
| `determine_gemm_backend` | Returns `sm80` (no SM12x branch) |

---

## 1. Attention

### 1.1 Decode (batch paged KV)

| Backend | CC Gate | SM121 Status | Notes |
|---------|---------|--------------|-------|
| **fa2** | Generic | **Supported** | Default via `determine_attention_backend` for non-FP8 tensor-core decode |
| **fa3** | SM90 only | **Not available** | `determine_attention_backend` returns fa3 only on SM90 |
| **xqa** | `major in {9, 10, 12}` | **Supported** | `trtllm_batch_decode` auto → xqa when `major != 10` |
| **trtllm-gen** | `major == 10` only | **Not available** | Auto selects this only for SM100 |
| **cudnn** | Runtime-dependent | **Unknown** | No explicit CC exclusion; depends on cuDNN + driver |
| **MLA tensor path** | `device_arch == 80` | **Not available** | SM80-only legacy path; use XQA MLA instead |

**Dispatch:** `decode.py:~2429` (trtllm batch), `~1057` (tensor-core), `~1934` (MLA legacy).

### 1.2 Prefill (batch paged KV)

| Backend | CC Gate | SM121 Status | Notes |
|---------|---------|--------------|-------|
| **fa2** | Generic | **Supported** | Default auto path |
| **fa3** | SM90 only | **Not available** | |
| **cudnn** | Runtime-dependent | **Unknown** | No explicit CC block |
| **cutlass FMHA** | `is_sm100a_supported \|\| is_sm110a_supported` | **Not available** | Explicitly excluded for SM12x (no tcgen05); error message names RTX 5090 / DGX Spark |
| **FMHAv2 (TRT-LLM)** | `is_sm12x_supported` | **Supported** | Intended Blackwell 12x path; FP8 FMHAv2 explicitly blocked |
| **cute-dsl** | SM100+ code paths | **Uncertain** | Kernels use SM100-oriented helpers (`get_smem_capacity_in_bytes("sm_100")`); needs on-device validation |

**Dispatch:** `prefill.py:~132–163` (CUTLASS FMHA gate), `~1973` (auto), `~4416` (FMHAv2).

### 1.3 MLA (Multi-Latent Attention)

| Backend | CC Gate | SM121 Status | Notes |
|---------|---------|--------------|-------|
| **xqa** | `major == 12` | **Supported** | Auto for decode MLA on SM12x |
| **xqa (FP8/NVFP4)** | `major in {12}` | **Supported** | Docstring says "SM120" but gate is `major == 12` (includes 121) |
| **trtllm-gen** | `major == 10` | **Not available** | |
| **cute-dsl** | `cc[0] >= 10` | **Supported (gate)** | SM121 passes the check; SM100-oriented internals need validation |
| **fa2** | Generic | **Supported** | Fallback path |

**Dispatch:** `mla/_core.py:~677` (trtllm MLA decode), `~686` (XQA MLA).

### 1.4 XQA

| Backend | CC Gate | SM121 Status | Notes |
|---------|---------|--------------|-------|
| **xqa** | `major in {9, 10, 12}` | **Supported** | |
| **xqa_mla** | `major in {12}` | **Supported** | JIT `gen_xqa_module_mla` uses `supported_major_versions=[12]` |
| **xqa NVFP4** | `major in {12}` | **Supported** | Error message says "SM120 GPUs" — misleading for SM121 |

**Dispatch:** `xqa.py:~316` (general), `~536` (MLA). **JIT:** `jit/xqa.py:~97` (xqa), `~172` (xqa_mla).

### 1.5 POD / Cascade / Sparse / Attention Sink

| API | SM121 Status | Notes |
|-----|--------------|-------|
| **POD** | Inherits prefill + decode | Same as §1.1 / §1.2 |
| **Cascade** (`merge_state`) | **Supported** | No arch filter |
| **Sparse** | **Supported (fa2)** | Auto → fa2 on SM121 |
| **Attention sink** | **Supported (fa2)** | Auto → fa2 on SM121 |

### 1.6 cuDNN Attention

No explicit CC exclusion in `cudnn/prefill.py` or `cudnn/decode.py`. **Runtime-dependent** on cuDNN version and driver support for Spark hardware.

---

## 2. GEMM

### 2.1 `mm_fp4` / FP4 Dense GEMM

| Backend | CC Gate | SM121 Status | Notes |
|---------|---------|--------------|-------|
| **cutlass** | `[100, 103, 110, 120, 121]` | **Supported** | `get_gemm_sm120_module_cutlass_fp4()` for `sm_major == 12` |
| **cudnn** | `[100, 103, 110, 120, 121]` | **Supported** | MXFP4 on 12x needs cuDNN ≥ 9.14.0 |
| **b12x** | `[120, 121]` (decorator) | **Supported (gate) but excluded from auto** | Heuristic checks `major == 12 and minor == 0` — **SM121 never gets b12x in auto** |
| **trtllm** | `[100, 103]` | **Not available** | |
| **cute-dsl** | `[100, 103]` | **Not available** | Uses SM100-style kernel; not enabled for SM12x |

**Key issue:** `_heuristic_func_mm_fp4` (`gemm_base.py:5065–5071`) sets `is_sm120 = major == 12 and minor == 0`; only then prepends b12x. **SM121 falls through to cutlass/cudnn only.** A prior internal FP4 audit also identified this as the likely root cause of DGX Spark NVFP4 performance complaints, along with related issues: AOT building `fp4_quantization_121` while runtime redirects to `120f`, the `sm120a` FP4 quant module being dead code, and an upstream `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` blocker (missing `"sm_121"` in `SMEM_CAPACITY_MAP`, pending cutlass-dsl 4.5).

### 2.2 `mm_bf16` / `bmm_bf16`

| Backend | CC Gate | SM121 Status | Notes |
|---------|---------|--------------|-------|
| **cudnn** | `[80, 86, 89, 90, 100, 103]` | **Not available** | 121 not in list |
| **cutlass** | `[100, 103]` | **Not available** | |
| **tgv** | `[100, 103]` | **Not available** | |

**SM121 has no BF16 mm/bmm backend through the standard `bf16_gemm_sm100` path.** Falls back to generic segment GEMM or PyTorch.

### 2.3 `mm_mxfp8` / `bmm_mxfp8`

| Backend | CC Gate | SM121 Status | Notes |
|---------|---------|--------------|-------|
| **cutlass** | `[120, 121]` for mm; `[120, 121]` for bmm | **Supported** | Enforces 1D swizzled scales, 128×4 block, K/N multiples of 32 on SM12x |
| **cute-dsl** | `[100, 103]` | **Not available** | |
| **trtllm** | `[100, 103]` | **Not available** | |
| **cudnn** (bmm) | `[100, 103]` | **Not available** | |

**Dispatch:** `gemm_base.py:~3984+` (mm_mxfp8), `~7503+` (bmm_mxfp8).

### 2.4 `bmm_fp8`

| Backend | CC Gate | SM121 Status | Notes |
|---------|---------|--------------|-------|
| **cutlass_sm12x** | `_match_sm_version(["120", "121"])` | **Supported** | Uses `get_gemm_sm120_module_cutlass_fp8` |
| **cudnn** | CC-dependent | **Unknown** | |
| **cublas** | Generic | **Supported** | |

### 2.5 Groupwise / Blockscaled GEMM

| API | CC Gate | SM121 Status | Notes |
|-----|---------|--------------|-------|
| `gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise` | `[100, 103, 120, 121]` | **Supported** | Uses `get_gemm_sm120_module()` on SM12x |
| `gemm_fp8_nt_blockscaled` | `[100, 103, 120, 121]` | **Supported** | |
| `group_gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise` | `[100, 103, 120, 121]` | **Supported** | **Correctness issues for `num_groups > 1` on SM120/121** (documented) |
| `group_gemm_mxfp4_nt_groupwise` | `[120, 121]` | **Supported** | |
| `group_gemm_nvfp4_nt_groupwise` | `[120, 121]` | **Supported** | |

### 2.6 DeepGEMM

| API | CC Gate | SM121 Status |
|-----|---------|--------------|
| `group_deepgemm_fp8_nt_groupwise` | `[100, 103]` | **Not available** |
| `batch_deepgemm_fp8_nt_groupwise` | `[100, 103]` | **Not available** |

### 2.7 Other GEMM

| API | SM121 Status | Notes |
|-----|--------------|-------|
| `SegmentGEMMWrapper` | **Not SM12x-optimized** | Uses `determine_gemm_backend → "sm80"`; no SM12x branch |
| `routergemm` (`tinygemm_bf16`, etc.) | **Not available** | `[100, 103]` only |
| `tgv_gemm_sm100` | **Not available** | SM10x stack |
| `mm_fp8` (TRT-LLM low-latency) | **Unknown** | No explicit CC gate in Python |

### 2.8 GEMM JIT

All `gen_gemm_sm120_*` generators use `get_nvcc_flags_list(supported_major_versions=[12])` — `CompilationContext` supplies `sm_121a` when device is SM121. CUTLASS kernel generation (`generate_kernels.py:1049`) explicitly checks `has_arch(120) or has_arch(121)`.

---

## 3. MoE (Mixture of Experts)

### 3.1 `cutlass_fused_moe` (FP8)

| Backend | CC Gate | SM121 Status | Notes |
|---------|---------|--------------|-------|
| **cutlass SM120** | `major*10+minor` → "120"/"121" both → `gen_cutlass_fused_moe_sm120_module` | **Supported** | JIT uses `supported_major_versions=[12]`; FP8 MoE may fall back to SM89 tactics when native occupancy is zero |
| **trtllm MoE** | `arch[0] >= 10` | **Supported** | No 120/121 split |

### 3.2 `b12x_fused_moe` (NVFP4 MoE)

Falls through to SM90 path, but that JIT module is compiled with `sm90a_nvcc_flags` (`compute_90a,code=sm_90a`), producing SM90-only SASS with no PTX fallback. **Will fail to load on SM121.** |

records.title: Silent memory corruption when custom_mask shape doesn't match (qo_len, kv_len) in single_prefill_with_kv_cache
records.body:
While vllm-omni was adding support for flashinfer a [data corruption/illegal access] issue was detected due to lack of validation of the `custom_mask`'s shape. The [functions documentation](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/generated/flashinfer.prefill.single_prefill_with_kv_cache.html) states
> custom_mask (Optional[torch.Tensor]) –
>
> The custom boolean mask tensor, shape: [qo_len, kv_len]. The elements in the mask tensor should be either True or False, where False means the corresponding element in the attention matrix will be masked out.

I am unable to provide a simple reproducer for illegal access. @lishunyang12 was able to produce it on end to end test of Hunyuan Video 1.5 with https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/3079/changes/b25c755322cba84e14802e1f62acf5f982480618. A simpler reproducer that detects corruption is:
```
import torch
import flashinfer


def test_bad_mask_shape():
    qo_len, kv_len = 10, 20
    num_qo_heads, num_kv_heads = 8, 4
    head_dim = 128
    kwargs= {}

    q = torch.randn(qo_len, num_qo_heads, head_dim, dtype=torch.float16)
    k = torch.randn(kv_len, num_kv_heads, head_dim, dtype=torch.float16)
    v = torch.randn(kv_len, num_kv_heads, head_dim, dtype=torch.float16)

    bad_mask = torch.ones(qo_len, kv_len - 5, dtype=torch.bool)

    # Correct mask for comparison
    correct_mask = torch.ones(qo_len, kv_len, dtype=torch.bool)
    # Mask out the last 5 columns to make it meaningful
    correct_mask[:, 15:] = False

    print(f"Q shape: {q.shape} (qo_len={qo_len})")
    print(f"K shape: {k.shape} (kv_len={kv_len})")
    print(f"V shape: {v.shape}")
    print(f"Bad mask shape: {bad_mask.shape} (expected [{qo_len}, {kv_len}])")
    print(f"Correct mask shape: {correct_mask.shape}")
    print(f"Bad packed mask size: {(bad_mask.numel() + 7) // 8} bytes")
    print(f"Correct packed mask size: {(correct_mask.numel() + 7) // 8} bytes")
    print()

    print("Running with CORRECT mask...")
    kwargs["custom_mask"] = correct_mask
    o_correct = flashinfer.single_prefill_with_kv_cache(q, k, v, ** kwargs)
    print(f"Correct output (first head, first 5 tokens): {o_correct[0, 0, :5]}")

    # Run with bad mask
    print("\nRunning with BAD mask (shape mismatch)...")
    try:
        kwargs["custom_mask" = bad_mask
        o_bad = flashinfer.single_prefill_with_kv_cache(q, k, v, ** kwargs)
        print(f"Bad output (first head, first 5 tokens): {o_bad[0, 0, :5]}")
        
        # Check for corruption
        diff = (o_correct - o_bad).abs().max().item()
        print(f"\nMax absolute difference: {diff:.6f}")
        
        if diff > 1e-5:
            print("Results differ significantly!")
            
    except RuntimeError as e:
        print("This is the kernel detecting the illegal access.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_bad_mask_shape()
```

[Tracking] In-kernel output quantization for prefill attention (CUTLASS SM100 + TRT-LLM Gen ragged + cuDNN) ## Background Several downstream consumers (vLLM MLA `forward_mha`, see [vllm-project/vllm#35792](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35792)) want the prefill attention kernel to write its output directly in a quantized format, fused with the post-attention quant op. This avoids the BF16 temp + post-kernel quant (`scaled_fp8_quant`, `per_token_group_fp8_quant`, `scaled_fp4_quant`) that today hangs off `attention → o_proj` paths. Three quantization flavors are in scope: | Flavor | Output layout | Scale layout | |---|---|---| | **Static per-tensor FP8** | dense `e4m3` | single host scalar `o_scale` | | **Dynamic per-group FP8** | dense `e4m3` | per-128 / per-64-element group scale tensor along the head_dim axis | | **NVFP4** | uint8-packed `e2m1` | per-16-element block scale tensor (e4m3) + host scalar `o_sf_scale` | Three prefill kernel families are in scope: - **CUTLASS Blackwell FMHA** (`backend="cutlass"` in `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper`, dispatched into `csrc/fmha_cutlass_sm100.cu` → `include/flashinfer/attention/blackwell/`). - **TRT-LLM Gen FMHA ragged DeepSeek** (`trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek` in `flashinfer/prefill.py`, dispatched into `trtllm_ragged_attention_launcher` in `csrc/trtllm_fmha_kernel_launcher.cu`, kernels from the `TLLM_GEN_FMHA_METAINFO_HASH` artifact bundle). - **cuDNN SDPA** (`backend="cudnn"` in `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper`, dispatched into `cudnn_batch_prefill_with_kv_cache` in `flashinfer/cudnn/prefill.py`, which builds a cuDNN SDPA graph at runtime). ## Status Details **Static per-tensor FP8** - **cuTLASS**: 🟡 PR: #3177 — scaled output is already supported in the mainloop collective `Sm100FmhaFwdMainloopTmaWarpspecialized`. This PR surfaces the param with added type handling - **trtllm-gen**: 🔴 blocked on artifact bundle.
- `(BF16, BF16, E4M3)` and `(FP16, FP16, E4M3)` SeparateQkv Context cubins are absent at every head dim
- `(E4M3, E4M3, E4M3)` is missing for the DSR1 MLA shape `192/128` (the shape vLLM `forward_mha` exercises). - **cuDNN**: 🟡 wiring needed **Dynamic per-group FP8** - **cuTLASS**: 🔴 needs new epilogue — `Sm100FmhaFwdEpilogueTmaWarpspecialized::Arguments` has only `ptr_O` and `ptr_LSE`, no scale-factor output buffer; needs an epilogue variant that reduces abs-max per group and writes a second tensor - **trtllm-gen**: 🔴 blocked on artifact bundle — no per-group cubins exist for any layout - **cuDNN**: 🔴 blocked on cuDNN API support **NVFP4** - **cuTLASS**: 🔴 needs new epilogue — same blocker as per-group FP8 (no scale-factor output mechanism in epilogue); CUTLASS Blackwell does have device-level FP4 + block-scale support (e.g. `examples/75_blackwell_grouped_gemm_block_scaled.cu`, `cutlass::nv_float4_t`, `LinCombEltActBlockScaleFactor` fusion), so the work is porting that into the FMHA epilogue collective - **trtllm-gen**: 🔴 blocked on artifact bundle. — bundle has 216 PagedKv Context FP4 cubins (added in #1360) but no SeparateQkv Context FP4 cubins. The paged sibling `trtllm_batch_context_with_kv_cache` is fully wired. - **cuDNN**: 🔴 blocked on cuDNN API support Legend: 🟢 ships today / 🟡 in flight or partial / 🔴 not started. ## Cross-references - vLLM tracking issue: vllm-project/vllm#35792 - flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/2597

records.title: `AutoTuner.choose_one` picks divergent tactics per rank under TP, deadlocking NCCL symmetric-memory allocations
records.body:
## Summary

`flashinfer.autotuner.AutoTuner.choose_one` runs entirely independently on every rank, with no cross-rank coordination. GPU timing noise makes different ranks pick different "winning" tactics for the same `(op, runner, profile)` key. When the chosen kernel is then invoked under a `use_symmetric_memory(...)` context (common in TP serving with NCCL symmetric memory), the per-rank tactic mismatch makes the kernel allocate different-sized scratch tensors per rank, and the resulting `ncclCommWindowRegister(NCCL_WIN_COLL_SYMMETRIC)` calls deadlock because the collective requires every rank to call it with the same size in the same order.

The bug is reproducible deterministically on Qwen3-235B + TP=8 + flashinfer + `--enable-symm-mem` in SGLang: CUDA-graph capture hangs at exactly `bs=144, step 30/52`. The straggler rank is non-deterministic (we observed TP2 and TP5 across separate runs), consistent with timing-noise-driven decisions.

This issue has been independently observed and partially worked around downstream (sglang [#18908][sglang-18908], [#23317][sglang-23317]), but the root cause has never been addressed at the autotuner layer.

## Environment

```
GPU         8x NVIDIA B200 (SM100)
CUDA        12.x (lmsysorg/sglang:latest container)
FlashInfer  0.6.7.post3 (also reproduces on 0.6.9 main)
Framework   SGLang (autotune ON, --enable-symm-mem)
Model       Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 (94-layer MoE, trtllm_bf16_moe path)
Backend     flashinfer attention + flashinfer_trtllm MoE runner
```

## Reproduction

```bash
docker run -d --gpus all --shm-size 32g --network host \
    --ulimit memlock=-1 --init --name sglang-bench \
    -v <hf-cache>:/root/.cache/huggingface \
    --entrypoint sleep lmsysorg/sglang:latest infinity

docker exec sglang-bench python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 \
    --tp 8 --attention-backend flashinfer --enable-symm-mem \
    --port 30000
```

Observed (truncated):

```
Capturing batches (bs=152 avail_mem=15.10 GB):  58%|██▌| 30/52 [00:07<00:05]
Capturing batches (bs=144 avail_mem=15.07 GB):  58%|██▌| 30/52 [00:07<00:05]
                                                       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
                                                        progress freezes here
                                                        for hours
```

No exception, no NCCL error, no watchdog. All 8 scheduler procs sit at 99 % CPU (busy NCCL spin) forever.

## Trigger

The hang occurs during CUDA-graph capture when the model forward calls into the trtllm-gen BF16 MoE op (`flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py::trtllm_bf16_moe`) inside a SGLang `use_symmetric_memory(tp_group)` context. SGLang already auto-enables `enable_flashinfer_allreduce_fusion=True` for this config — the MoE compute and the cross-rank allreduce are fused into a single kernel pipeline, so the *kernel-side* communication path is not the problem. The deadlock fires *before the kernel runs*, in the host-side scratch-buffer allocation step:

```
1. AutoTuner.choose_one returns a tactic    (host-side, before kernel launch)
2. Kernel allocates scratch buffers via torch.empty(...) inside
   use_symmetric_memory(...) -> ncclMemAlloc + ncclCommWindowRegister
   -> COLLECTIVE -- must match across ranks   <-- HANG HERE
3. Fused MoE+allreduce kernel runs           (never reached on stragglers)
```

Smaller models (≤ 8B class) finish capture before the divergence window opens, which is why per-commit CI doesn't surface this. The bug requires a model with enough autotune-eligible ops × distinct profiles to fan the per-rank cache out enough that at least one allocation size disagrees.

## Direct measurement of per-rank tactic divergence

We instrumented `AutoTuner.choose_one` with a probe that logs every `profiling_cache[cache_key] = (runner_id, tactic, p)` write per rank:

```python
# inside choose_one, right after the cache-set
self.profiling_cache[cache_key] = (runner_id, tactic, p)
# --- probe ---
import torch.distributed as dist
rank = dist.get_rank() if dist.is_initialized() else "?"
with open(f"/tmp/tactic_log_rank_{rank}.txt", "a") as fh:
    fh.write(f"{custom_op}\t{p.get_opt_shapes()}\trunner={runner_id}\ttactic={tactic}\n")
```

Ran the failing config until the hang, then diffed the 8 per-rank logs.
Result for `flashinfer::trtllm_bf16_moe` across the 13 distinct profiles that got tuned before the hang:

| `num_tokens` (profile leading dim) | distinct tactics across 8 ranks |
|---:|---:|
| 1    | **8** (every rank disagrees) |
| 2    | 6 |
| 4    | 6 |
| 8    | 6 |
| 16   | 7 |
| 32   | 4 |
| 64   | 7 |
| 128  | 7 |
| 256  | 6 |
| 512  | 3 |
| 1024 | 6 |
| 2048 | 2 |
| 4096 | 3 |

**0 of 13 profiles have unanimous agreement across ranks.** For `num_tokens=1`, every one of the 8 ranks picked a different tactic — the maximum possible divergence on 8 ranks. Example:

| Rank | Tactic | Measured time |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `(32, 59)` | 0.119 ms |
| 5 | `(32, 14)` | 0.119 ms |
| 7 | `(32, 11)` | 0.119 ms |

All three measurements are numerically identical to 3 decimal places — they're all in the "near-tied top cluster" of tactics. Which one wins the local `argmin` race depends entirely on per-rank timing noise.

## py-spy evidence at the hang point

```
TP0..TP4, TP6, TP7  →  torch.distributed.barrier(...)  in pynccl_allocator.py
                       (waiting on the next ncclCommWindowRegister
                        collective)

TP5 (or TP2 in another run, randomised)  →  trtllm_bf16_moe_op
                       (flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py:1301)
                       blocked inside the C++ kernel-launch shim,
                       presumably on its own ncclCommWindowRegister
                       call which has a different size argument from
                       what the other 7 ranks are about to issue
```

The non-determinism of the straggler rank rules out "the bug lives on a specific rank" and instead points directly at "the rank whose noisy timing happened to disagree on this iteration".

## Root cause

`AutoTuner.choose_one` in tune mode (lines ~656–825 of
`flashinfer/autotuner.py` on main):

```python
for r_id, r in enumerate(runners):
    for tac in r.get_valid_tactics(tensors, p):
        time_measured = self._profile_single_kernel(r, tensors, tac, ...)
        if time_measured < min_time:
            min_time = time_measured
            runner_id, tactic = r_id, tac
self.profiling_cache[cache_key] = (runner_id, tactic, p)
```

`grep -n "torch.distributed\|dist\." flashinfer/autotuner.py` returns nothing — the autotuner is fundamentally unaware of the distributed context it's running inside. Every rank is running its own local tournament with its own noisy stopwatch, so different ranks pick different winners whenever multiple tactics are tied within the noise band.

The link from "different tactic" to "different `ncclCommWindowRegister` size" is the kernel's internal scratch shape: each tactic uses a different tile/pipeline configuration, so `[N_experts, tile, hidden]` buffers come out at different sizes. Under `use_symmetric_memory(...)`, those allocations route through SGLang's NCCL-aware allocator plugin, which calls `ncclCommWindowRegister(NCCL_WIN_COLL_SYMMETRIC)` per allocation. The collective deadlocks on size mismatch.

## Expected vs. actual behaviour

**Expected**: under TP, all ranks are computing the same model on the same input, so they should converge on the same kernel tactic for the same shape. The cache should be coherent across ranks.

**Actual**: `profiling_cache` is per-process and per-rank-noisy. Two ranks computing the same forward end up running different kernel binaries.

This is invisible without symmetric memory (regular allreduce tolerates small per-rank speed differences). With symm-mem on the fast path, the divergence becomes a hard collective deadlock.

## Fix direction 

The minimal fix is to add a small opt-in API (`set_autotune_process_group(group)`) that makes `_profile_single_kernel` all reduce the measured time across ranks before the `argmin` comparison. With identical (averaged) inputs, every rank's `argmin` produces the same answer.

## Related

- sglang [#18908][sglang-18908] — same root cause identified months ago (Alison Shao, NVIDIA): *"different ranks may profile different kernel configs, causing NCCL collective divergence"*. The PR took the workaround route (disable symm-mem during autotune + capture) and was closed without merging after reviewer feedback that disabling symm-mem during capture defeats the purpose.
- sglang [#23317][sglang-23317] — independent re-attempt of the same workaround; superseded by the autotuner-side fix.
- sglang [#20153][sglang-20153] — adjacent issue: per-comm-group symmetric memory pool isolation.
- vLLM [#33996][vllm-33996] — RFC for NCCL symmetric memory option; affected the same way once enabled.

[sglang-18908]: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18908
[sglang-23317]: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23317
[sglang-20153]: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20153
[vllm-33996]: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/33996

We have applied this weight folding trick to a few LLMs (Llama, Qwen, SMolLM) here: https://huggingface.co/models?other=weightless-rmsnorm ### Motivation FlashNorm's removal of norm weights reduces inference overhead at zero accuracy cost, and we'd like to share these optimized models with the broader community. ### Possible Implementation Remove norm weights from your RMSNorm implementation. records.title: [Bug] Release `nightly-v0.6.9-20260501` is tagged incorrectly
records.body:
### Summary

The commit shown in the releases page for the nightly and the git tag **do not match** the commit from which the nightly was built.

### Details

I wanted to use the latest nightly release to test the per-token quantization in NVFP4 MoE, which is available in the commit of the release (537a3b56) according to [the release page](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/tag/nightly-v0.6.9-20260501). Also the git log points to the same commit as `nightly-v0.6.9-20260501`:
```
$ git log --oneline
537a3b56 (HEAD -> main, tag: nightly-v0.6.9-20260501, origin/main, origin/HEAD) feat: Trtllm-gen Per-token Nvfp4 MoE (#3027)
cd6c7030 [fmha-v2] Support HND and NHD paged KV cache layouts with conditional stride handling (#2799)
a3683bea feat: Add DiT-oriented kernels where Qk (Bmm1) type can be reinterpreted into Int8 or BFloat16 (#2711)
f6d49c42 Fix trace-bmm-fp8 test: B should be K-major for subword types (#3184)
```

However, after installing I realized that the new code was not there. Looking at the [logs of the release creation](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/25201689556/job/73908016175#step:2:72), it seems that it corresponds to the commit a3683bea and not 537a3b56. It seems that the release creation uses the head of `main` 537a3b56 at the time of call, which is this case is 4 hours and 2 commits past the one that was built (a3683bea).

records.title: [BUG] BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper(backend="fa2") returns zeros for non-contiguous kv_indices on Ampere bf16
records.body:
## Summary

`flashinfer.mla.BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper(backend="fa2")` produces incorrect attention output when `kv_indices` contains non-contiguous (scattered) physical page indices, on Ampere (SM 8.6) with bfloat16 inputs.

The same logical KV data placed at scattered physical pages produces a different result (specifically, **all zeros**) than the same data placed at contiguous physical pages. Both should produce identical attention output for identical Q.

This was observed when integrating the wrapper into vLLM's MLA decode path on Ampere, where the BlockManager fragments page assignments across the global cache pool. Single-prompt isolation (one page assigned, trivially "contiguous") produces correct output; multi-prompt scenarios (scattered pages) produce gibberish from the very first decode token.

## Environment

- **GPU**: NVIDIA RTX A4000 (Ampere SM 8.6)
- **PyTorch**: 2.11.0+cu130
- **FlashInfer**: 0.6.8.post1
- **dtype**: torch.bfloat16
- **backend**: "fa2"

## Minimal repro

Self-contained, ~150 lines, no external dependencies beyond `torch` and `flashinfer`. Runs in under a minute.

```python
"""
Minimal reproduction of FlashInfer fa2 MLA paged-indexing bug on Ampere.

The BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper(backend="fa2") produces different output
when given the SAME logical KV data via two different paged layouts:
  (A) data placed at physical pages [0, 1, 2, ...] with kv_indices = [0, 1, 2, ...]
  (B) data placed at scattered physical pages [P0, P1, P2, ...] with kv_indices = [P0, P1, P2, ...]

Both should produce identical attention output for the same q.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import sys
import torch
import flashinfer


def build_metadata(num_pages, page_size, kv_lens, page_assignment, device):
    batch_size = len(kv_lens)
    qo_indptr = torch.arange(0, batch_size + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    pages_per_batch = [len(p) for p in page_assignment]
    kv_indptr = torch.zeros(batch_size + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    cum = 0
    for i, n in enumerate(pages_per_batch):
        cum += n
        kv_indptr[i + 1] = cum
    flat = []
    for p in page_assignment:
        flat.extend(p)
    kv_indices = torch.tensor(flat, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    kv_len_arr = torch.tensor(kv_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    return qo_indptr, kv_indptr, kv_indices, kv_len_arr


def main() -> int:
    cap = torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0)
    print(f"Device: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}, compute capability {cap}")
    print(f"FlashInfer: {flashinfer.__version__}\n")

    num_heads = 4
    head_dim_ckv = 512
    head_dim_kpe = 64
    page_size = 64
    pool_size = 256
    batch_size = 4
    kv_len = 50

    device = torch.device("cuda:0")
    dtype = torch.bfloat16

    ckv_pool = torch.zeros((pool_size * page_size, 1, head_dim_ckv), dtype=dtype, device=device)
    kpe_pool = torch.zeros((pool_size * page_size, 1, head_dim_kpe), dtype=dtype, device=device)

    torch.manual_seed(42)
    test_ckv = [torch.randn(page_size, 1, head_dim_ckv, dtype=dtype, device=device) for _ in range(batch_size)]
    test_kpe = [torch.randn(page_size, 1, head_dim_kpe, dtype=dtype, device=device) for _ in range(batch_size)]

    workspace = torch.empty(64 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.int8, device=device)
    sm_scale = 1.0 / ((128 + 64) ** 0.5)

    def run_with_assignment(label, page_assignment):
        ckv_pool.zero_()
        kpe_pool.zero_()
        for batch_idx, pages in enumerate(page_assignment):
            phys_page = pages[0]
            start = phys_page * page_size
            end = start + page_size
            ckv_pool[start:end] = test_ckv[batch_idx]
            kpe_pool[start:end] = test_kpe[batch_idx]

        qo_indptr, kv_indptr, kv_indices, kv_len_arr = build_metadata(
            pool_size, page_size, [kv_len] * batch_size, page_assignment, device
        )
        wrapper = flashinfer.mla.BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper(workspace, backend="fa2")
        wrapper.plan(qo_indptr, kv_indptr, kv_indices, kv_len_arr,
                     num_heads, head_dim_ckv, head_dim_kpe, page_size,
                     False, sm_scale, dtype, dtype)
        torch.manual_seed(99)
        q_nope = torch.randn(batch_size, num_heads, head_dim_ckv, dtype=dtype, device=device)
        q_pe = torch.randn(batch_size, num_heads, head_dim_kpe, dtype=dtype, device=device)
        out = wrapper.run(q_nope, q_pe, ckv_pool, kpe_pool, return_lse=False)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        print(f"--- {label} ---")
        print(f"  page_assignment={page_assignment}")
        print(f"  output norm = {out.norm().item():.6f}")
        return out

    out_a = run_with_assignment("Case A: contiguous pages", [[0], [1], [2], [3]])
    out_b = run_with_assignment("Case B: scattered pages",  [[16], [47], [89], [203]])

    diff = (out_a.float() - out_b.float()).abs()
    rel_err = diff.max().item() / max(out_a.float().abs().max().item(), 1e-9)
    print(f"\n=== max abs diff = {diff.max().item():.6e}, relative error = {rel_err:.6e} ===")
    if rel_err < 1e-2:
        print("PASS")
        return 0
    print("FAIL — fa2 MLA mishandles non-contiguous kv_indices on Ampere")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

## Observed output on RTX A4000 (SM 8.6) with bf16

```
Device: NVIDIA RTX A4000, compute capability (8, 6)
FlashInfer: 0.6.8.post1

--- Case A: contiguous pages ---
  page_assignment=[[0], [1], [2], [3]]
  output norm = 32.750000

--- Case B: scattered pages ---
  page_assignment=[[16], [47], [89], [203]]
  output norm = 0.000000

=== max abs diff = 1.710938e+00, relative error = 1.000000e+00 ===
FAIL — fa2 MLA mishandles non-contiguous kv_indices on Ampere
```

With contiguous `kv_indices`, the kernel produces sensible nonzero attention output (norm 32.75). With scattered `kv_indices` over the same logical data, the kernel produces a tensor of all zeros. This points to the kernel mishandling page-table indirection when indices are non-contiguous.

## Impact

This blocks `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper(backend="fa2")` for any production inference engine on Ampere hardware with paged KV caches and multi-sequence batching, because real-world page assignments are inherently scattered. We hit it integrating the wrapper into vLLM's MLA backend — once we worked around it via a "compaction" step (gathering active pages into a contiguous buffer and remapping `kv_indices` to `[0..N-1]` before calling the wrapper), the entire test prompt set produced coherent output.

## Workaround for downstream users

```python
ckv_paged = ckv_pool.view(num_pages_total, page_size, 1, head_dim_ckv)
kpe_paged = kpe_pool.view(num_pages_total, page_size, 1, head_dim_kpe)
sel = kv_indices.long()
ckv_compact = ckv_paged.index_select(0, sel).reshape(-1, 1, head_dim_ckv).contiguous()
kpe_compact = kpe_paged.index_select(0, sel).reshape(-1, 1, head_dim_kpe).contiguous()
new_kv_indices = torch.arange(kv_indices.shape[0], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
wrapper.plan(qo_indptr, kv_indptr, new_kv_indices, kv_len_arr, ...)
out = wrapper.run(q_nope, q_pe, ckv_compact, kpe_compact)
```

The `index_select` overhead is within measurement noise on the integration path we tested (vLLM MLA decode at TP=8 on 8× A4000), so this workaround is functionally viable for production while the root cause is being investigated.

## Hypothesis on root cause

We did not patch the kernel directly. Empirically, the failure mode is consistent with an offset calculation that assumes contiguous physical pages — for example, computing a base pointer as `cache_base + kv_indices[0] * page_stride` and then advancing by `page_stride` for subsequent pages, instead of resolving each `kv_indices[i]` independently. Sequential `kv_indices = [0, 1, 2, ...]` always works; scattered ones produce zeros.

## Related

- Issue #3047 — earlier reported correctness issues on the FlashInfer-backed MLA path with batch-composition dependency. This bug exhibits the same "fails on certain batch compositions" pattern.

## What would resolve

A fix to the fa2 MLA kernel's paged-indexing on non-Blackwell architectures so that arbitrary (non-contiguous, non-monotonic) `kv_indices` produce correct output, matching the contiguous-indices case.

Happy to provide additional diagnostics, capture Nsight traces, or test fixes against the integration. The standalone repro above and a vLLM-side end-to-end repro (linked from https://github.com/MidasMining/universal-translator) both reproduce the failure.

records.title: [Bug][integration_test]`flashinfer-jit-cache` wheel build fails in Docker when Git metadata is incomplete
records.body:
### Summary

 Found this issue in integration test: https://gitlab-master.nvidia.com/dl/flashinfer/flashinfer-ci/-/pipelines/50383220  
 Building the `flashinfer-jit-cache` wheel can fail inside Docker if the `/flashinfer` source tree does not contain complete Git metadata.

  This appears related to PR #3190, which added an unconditional `git submodule update --init --recursive` call in `flashinfer-jit-cache/
  build_backend.py`. 

  ### Failure

  During Docker build, the `flashinfer` and `flashinfer-cubin` wheels are built successfully, but the build fails when entering `flashinfer-
  jit-cache`:

  ```
  fatal: not a git repository: /flashinfer/../.git/modules/flashinfer
  File "/flashinfer/flashinfer-jit-cache/build_backend.py", line 88, in _compile_jit_cache
      subprocess.run(
  subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['git', 'submodule', 'update', '--init', '--recursive']' returned non-zero exit status 128.
  ERROR Backend subprocess exited when trying to invoke build_wheel
```


  ### Suspected Cause

  In this Docker environment, /flashinfer/.git appears to be a submodule-style Git file, likely pointing to a parent repository path such as:
  gitdir: ../.git/modules/flashinfer

  However, the Docker build context only contains the /flashinfer source tree and does not include the parent repository’s .git/modules/
  flashinfer directory. As a result, Git cannot resolve the repository metadata and fails before it can update submodules.

  This makes the flashinfer-jit-cache build depend on complete Git metadata being available inside the Docker image.

  ### Related Change

  PR #3190 added this command to flashinfer-jit-cache/build_backend.py:
```
  subprocess.run(
      ["git", "submodule", "update", "--init", "--recursive"],
      cwd=str(project_root),
      check=True,
  )
```
  This helps when submodules are missing, but it breaks environments where the source tree is present and submodules may already be populated,
  while Git metadata is not complete inside Docker.

  ### Expected Behavior

  flashinfer-jit-cache should build successfully if the required 3rdparty submodule contents are already present, even when the Docker image
  does not contain complete .git metadata.

  ### Suggested Fix (By Codex)

  Make the submodule update more robust. For example:

  - Check whether required submodule directories are already populated before running git submodule update.
  - Only run git submodule update --init --recursive if the project root is a valid Git repository.
  - If submodules are missing and Git metadata is unavailable, raise a clearer error message.
  - Optionally provide an environment variable to skip the Git submodule update in packaging/Docker builds.

  This would avoid failing builds where the source tree is complete enough to build but Git metadata is intentionally not included in the
  Docker context.
