records.title: DeepSeek V4 kernel support status tracker
records.body:
Last updated: 2026-06-15 01:46 PDT

This tracks DeepSeek-V4 kernel-provider coverage from the FlashInfer side. It is the provider-facing companion to the SGLang framework tracker: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/23666.

Current status used for this update:

- SGLang current status commit: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/0417951a86c6bf60f1065c204dedab46e6ddccc0
- FlashInfer current status commit: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/c15ac84c922f78123be7a19d32e44d705f2a0ec1

Legend:

- `Wired`: SGLang DSV4 can call a FlashInfer implementation today.
- `API exists (...), not wired`: FlashInfer exposes a relevant API, but SGLang DSV4 is not wired to it today.
- `Missing`: no matching DSV4 FlashInfer API/kernel identified.
- `External/custom`: current SGLang uses a non-FlashInfer backend.
- `Needs validation`: implementation exists or is likely close, but SM-specific correctness/perf needs explicit validation.

Table row IDs are stable handles for follow-up discussion. Diagrams are the unannotated source diagrams from the SGLang tracker. SGLang remains the reference implementation/status source; this tracker is still provider oriented.

## Overview

![DSV4 overall network diagram](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c26ba943-9d86-4f07-9481-28d720a9907a)

## mHC / Hyper-Connections

HF reference: `hc_pre` uses RMS scaling, `hc_split_sinkhorn`, and weighted reduction; `hc_post` expands residual HC copies; `hc_head` reduces before logits.

Desired FlashInfer backend for mHC kernels: `cute-dsl` or CUDA. If the `fc_hc_fn` / `gemm_sqrsum` part does not use TF32 Tensor Cores, one shared kernel source should cover SM90/SM100/SM120. If it uses TF32 Tensor Cores, then SM90/SM100/SM120 need separate implementations tuned for each architecture's TF32 Tensor Core path.

![DSV4 mHC diagram](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvpohanh/flashinfer/dsv4-tracker-3346-assets/dsv4_tracker/dsv4_mhc_updated.png)

| ID | Kernel / API needed | Current SGLang backend | Uses FlashInfer today? | SM90 | SM100 | SM120 | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MHC-PRE-GEMM | `hc_pre` first stage: `1/RMS` + `fc_hc_fn`, aka `gemm_sqrsum` / `prenorm_gemm` | Three SGLang paths in [`mhc.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/6ccc5b807d294d92fbcd8872d3e4c898c2058d8e/python/sglang/srt/layers/mhc.py#L674-L758): DeepGEMM `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` when `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=1`; split-K TileLang `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_splitk` for `num_tokens <= 2048`; simple TileLang `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum_tilelang` otherwise. PR #24692 guards DeepGEMM/TileLang `hc_pre` off on SM120 and falls back to Torch `hc_pre_torch_impl`. | No | Missing | Missing | Missing FlashInfer; PR #3285 does not cover `gemm_sqrsum` / `prenorm_gemm` | Split-K is needed when num_tokens is small to increase SM utilization. |
| MHC-PRE-BIGFUSE | Rest of `hc_pre`, aka `mhc_pre_big_fuse`; optionally fuses RMSNorm when `norm_weight` is provided | SGLang `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` or `mhc_pre_big_fuse_tilelang` in [`mhc.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/6ccc5b807d294d92fbcd8872d3e4c898c2058d8e/python/sglang/srt/layers/mhc.py#L760-L818). PR #24692 bypasses this TileLang path on SM120. | No | API exists ([`flashinfer.mhc_pre_big_fuse`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/c15ac84c922f78123be7a19d32e44d705f2a0ec1/flashinfer/mhc.py)), not wired | API exists ([`flashinfer.mhc_pre_big_fuse`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/c15ac84c922f78123be7a19d32e44d705f2a0ec1/flashinfer/mhc.py)), not wired | API exists ([`flashinfer.mhc_pre_big_fuse`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/c15ac84c922f78123be7a19d32e44d705f2a0ec1/flashinfer/mhc.py)), not wired | FlashInfer also exposes [`flashinfer.mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_prenorm`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/c15ac84c922f78123be7a19d32e44d705f2a0ec1/flashinfer/mhc.py); current SGLang DSV4 is not wired to them. |
| MHC-PRE-FULL | Full `hc_pre` fusion: `gemm_sqrsum` + `big_fuse` + RMSNorm (+ quant) in one kernel | Not fused today; SGLang executes `MHC-PRE-GEMM` + `MHC-PRE-BIGFUSE` and leaves quant as a separate prep step | No | Missing full `hc_pre` fusion | Missing full `hc_pre` fusion | Missing full `hc_pre` fusion | PR #3285 covers the big-fuse half only. Quant fusion is optional; if fused, the kernel must output both unquantized BF16 and quantized FP8/MXFP8/MXFP4/NVFP4 outputs because different Linear ops after RMSNorm require different input dtypes. The challenge is to ensure good SM utilization for the `gemm_sqrsum` part. |
| MHC-POST | `hc_post`: post/comb residual expansion | TileLang `mhc_post_tilelang` in [`mhc.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/6ccc5b807d294d92fbcd8872d3e4c898c2058d8e/python/sglang/srt/layers/mhc.py#L821-L889) | No | API exists ([`flashinfer.mhc_post`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/c15ac84c922f78123be7a19d32e44d705f2a0ec1/flashinfer/mhc.py)), not wired | API exists ([`flashinfer.mhc_post`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/c15ac84c922f78123be7a19d32e44d705f2a0ec1/flashinfer/mhc.py)), not wired | API exists ([`flashinfer.mhc_post`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/c15ac84c922f78123be7a19d32e44d705f2a0ec1/flashinfer/mhc.py)), not wired | Current SGLang DSV4 still uses TileLang. |
| MHC-HEAD | `hc_head`: final HC reduction before logits | Triton fused HC head in [`mhc_head.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/6ccc5b807d294d92fbcd8872d3e4c898c2058d8e/python/sglang/srt/layers/mhc_head.py#L90) | No | Missing | Missing | Missing |  |
| MHC-MEGA | mHC Mega Kernel: fuse `hc_post` + next full `hc_pre` + RMSNorm (+ quant) into one large transition kernel | Latest SGLang has an opt-in fused boundary path gated by `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=1` in [`deepseek_v4.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/0417951a86c6bf60f1065c204dedab46e6ddccc0/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py#L143-L148), using the fused wrapper in [`mhc.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/0417951a86c6bf60f1065c204dedab46e6ddccc0/python/sglang/srt/layers/mhc.py#L1155-L1188). The default path still executes separate `MHC-POST`, `MHC-PRE-GEMM`, `MHC-PRE-BIGFUSE`, and quant/prep work. | No | Missing mega fusion | Missing mega fusion | Missing mega fusion | SGLang's fused path is framework-side and opt-in; FlashInfer still has no merged mega-fusion API for this boundary. |


## Attention-Side FC / Linear Projections

These rows track the Linear / FC GEMM work items around Dense/Sparse MQA, the HCA/CSA compressors, and the CSA indexer.

![DSV4 HCA diagram](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvpohanh/flashinfer/dsv4-tracker-3346-assets/dsv4_tracker/dsv4_hca_rmsnorm.png)

![DSV4 CSA diagram](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvpohanh/flashinfer/dsv4-tracker-3346-assets/dsv4_tracker/dsv4_csa_rmsnorm.png)

Shape uses `T` for active tokens and `tp` for attention tensor-parallel size. Logical GEMM shape is `M x N x K` for `Y[M,N] = X[M,K] @ W[N,K]^T`.

Desired implementation backend for FC GEMMs: `cutedsl`, cuBLAS, or cuDNN, whichever is faster for the shape/dtype. To use each architecture's BF16/FP8 Tensor Cores, expect separate kernels or backend specializations for SM90/SM100/SM120.

| ID | Kernel / API needed | Logical GEMM shape | Local shape | GEMM input dtype | GEMM weight dtype | GEMM output dtype | Current SGLang backend | Uses FlashInfer today? | SM90 | SM100 | SM120 | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FC-FP8-GEMM | FP8 attention-side Linear GEMMs: fused `wqkv_a`, main MQA `wq_b`, main MQA `wo_b`, and CSA indexer `wq_b` | `wqkv_a`: `T x 2048 x 7168`; main `wq_b`: `T x 65536 x 1536`; `wo_b`: `T x 7168 x 16384`; indexer `wq_b`: `T x 8192 x 1536` | `wqkv_a`: replicated; main `wq_b`: `T x (65536/tp) x 1536`; `wo_b`: `T x 7168 x (16384/tp)` with row-parallel reduce; indexer `wq_b`: replicated | block-scale FP8 activation + scales | block-scale FP8 weight + scales | BF16 | SGLang `Fp8LinearMethod.apply` W8A8 block-FP8 dispatcher; `auto` uses DeepGEMM first when enabled, then FlashInfer/CUTLASS/AITER/Triton fallback. SM120 auto is forced to Triton in `initialize_fp8_gemm_config`; PR #24692 also disables DeepGEMM on SM120. | No by default | Missing DSV4 FC API; SGLang usually DeepGEMM when available | Missing DSV4 FC API; DeepGEMM remains the preferred practical path | Missing FlashInfer; SGLang PR #24692 uses Triton FP8 GEMM fallback | FlashInfer team note says no TRTLLM-gen/CUTLASS replacement is planned on SM100 because DeepGEMM is already performant. |
| FC-FP8-GROUP-GEMM | Main MQA grouped output projection `wo_a` | `T*16 x 1024 x 4096` grouped `wo_a` | `T*(16/tp) x 1024 x 4096` | SM100+: block-scale FP8 activation + scales; SM90 fallback: BF16 | SM100+: block-scale FP8 weight + scales; SM90 fallback: BF16 | BF16 | SM100+ default directly calls DeepGEMM `fp8_einsum`; SM90 fallback uses SGLang/Torch BF16 path in [`deepseek_v4.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/6ccc5b807d294d92fbcd8872d3e4c898c2058d8e/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py#L588-L608). PR #24692 does not replace this `wo_a` path with FlashInfer. | No | Missing; current fallback is SGLang/Torch BF16 | Missing; DeepGEMM remains the preferred practical path | Missing/needs validation; PR #24692 leaves direct `fp8_einsum` path | FlashInfer team note says DeepGEMM is already performant on SM100/SM120. |
| FC-BF16-FP32-GEMM | BF16->FP32 compressor gate projections `wkv_gate` for HCA C128, CSA C4, and CSA indexer | HCA C128: `T x 1024 x 7168`; CSA C4: `T x 2048 x 7168`; CSA indexer: `T x 512 x 7168` | replicated | BF16 | BF16 | FP32 | SGLang compressor calls `linear_bf16_fp32`, whose default `SGLANG_OPT_BF16_FP32_GEMM_ALGO=cublas` path JITs a cuBLAS BF16xBF16->FP32 GEMM; env can select DeepGEMM or Torch fallback. | No | Needs validation | Needs validation | Needs validation | FlashInfer team note says regular BF16 GEMMs should already be supportable through cuDNN or other generic paths, but DSV4-specific API/perf validation is still needed. |
| FC-BF16-BF16-GEMM | CSA indexer per-head weight projection `weights_proj` | `T x 64 x 7168` CSA indexer `weights_proj` | replicated | BF16 | BF16 | BF16 | SGLang unquantized Linear path: `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply` calls `torch.nn.functional.linear` on CUDA. | No | Needs validation | Needs validation | Needs validation | FlashInfer team note says regular BF16 GEMMs should already be supportable through cuDNN or other generic paths, but DSV4-specific API/perf validation is still needed; `gemmN` is small, so split-K may still matter. |

## HCA / CSA / Compressed MQA Attention

HF reference imports `sparse_attn`, uses sliding-window KV plus compressed KV, and uses compression ratios 4 and 128. SGLang forces the `dsv4` attention backend with FP8 KV cache and page size 256 in [`deepseek_v4_hook.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/6ccc5b807d294d92fbcd8872d3e4c898c2058d8e/python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/deepseek_v4_hook.py#L10-L34).

Terminology note: although SGLang's current backend package is named `flash_mla`, DSV4 attention is tracked here as MQA: Dense MQA for HCA, where no `topk_index` is needed, and Sparse MQA for CSA, where `topk_index` selects compressed pages.

Desired implementation backends for HCA/CSA attention: SM100 should target TRTLLM-gen or `cutedsl`; SM90/SM120 should target Triton, `cutedsl`, or CUDA.

![DSV4 HCA diagram](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvpohanh/flashinfer/dsv4-tracker-3346-assets/dsv4_tracker/dsv4_hca_rmsnorm.png)

![DSV4 CSA diagram](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvpohanh/flashinfer/dsv4-tracker-3346-assets/dsv4_tracker/dsv4_csa_rmsnorm.png)

| ID | Kernel / API needed | Current SGLang backend | Uses FlashInfer today? | SM90 | SM100 | SM120 | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## MoE / Routing / Expert GEMM

SGLang DSV4 reuses `DeepseekV2MoE` and overrides routing to full-expert sqrtsoftplus rather than V3 grouped sigmoid routing. FP4 expert layout is enabled by default for DSV4 in [`model_config.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/6ccc5b807d294d92fbcd8872d3e4c898c2058d8e/python/sglang/srt/configs/model_config.py#L248-L274). Routing is tracked as two stages: router FC first produces `router_logits`, then either HashTopK or TopK consumes those logits to select experts.

records.title: FI TRTLLM-gen fused MoE exposes ActivationType.Silu but rejects it in the runner
records.body:
`ActivationType.Silu` is exposed in FlashInfer's TRTLLM-gen enum definitions, but the TRTLLM-gen fused MoE path appears to reject it at runtime.
When TensorRT-LLM routes a Silu MoE case to the FlashInfer op backend, the call fails with:
```
Unsupported eltwise activation type Silu of enum 2
```
 in csrc/trtllm_fused_moe_runner.cu, `Silu` is treated as a non-gated activation, and then routed through activationTypeToEltwiseActType(). That function currently only accepts Relu2 and Identity [code](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/ce43023803d7ad80f14b9c5333c32acef897bd14/csrc/trtllm_fused_moe_runner.cu#L338)

For now, TensorRT-LLM currently needs to fall back to its native TRTLLM-gen op backend for Silu MoE cases. Otherwise, selecting the FlashInfer op backend for Silu causes the runtime failure above.

Could you please let me know whether there are any plans for the subsequent FI release to support the SiLU activation function in the TensorRT-LLM Gen fused MoE API? Thank you.

records.title: MnnvlMoe.mnnvl_moe_alltoallv requires 16-byte aligned row payloads, unlike TRT-LLM native MoE comm
records.body:
Hi FlashInfer team,
While integrating `flashinfer.comm.trtllm_alltoall.MnnvlMoe.mnnvl_moe_alltoallv` with TensorRT-LLM's NVLink two-sided MoE path, i found that `moe_comm` rejects valid TRT-LLM MoE payload tensors whose row size is not 16-byte aligned.
The failure comes from `csrc/trtllm_alltoall.cu`:
```cpp
size_t eltSize = get_element_size(input);
size_t eltCountPerU64 = sizeof(uint64_t) / eltSize;
TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(input.size(1) % (eltCountPerU64 * 2), 0)
    << "input.size(1) must be aligned to 16 bytes";
```
This means input.size(1) * element_size must be a multiple of 16 bytes. Some TensorRT-LLM MoE alltoall payloads are naturally smaller, for example:

> token_selected_slots: int32, shape [tokens, top_k]; top_k=1 is 4 bytes per row.
> token_final_scales: bf16, shape [tokens, top_k]; top_k=1 is 2 bytes per row, top_k=4 is 8 bytes per row.

The native TensorRT-LLM two-sided path accepts these payloads directly through torch.ops.trtllm.moe_comm with multiple payload descriptors. It appears to handle per-field layout/alignment internally, so TensorRT-LLM does not need Python-side row padding for these tensors.

As a local workaround, we padded each FlashInfer payload's second dimension to 16-byte row alignment before calling MnnvlMoe.mnnvl_moe_alltoallv, then sliced the output back to the original width. This resolves the failure, but adds extra allocation/copy overhead and makes FlashInfer's API behavior different from the native TRT-LLM comm path.

Could FlashInfer mnnvl_moe_alltoallv support non-16B row payloads internally, similar to TRT-LLM native moe_comm?
This would avoid requiring every integration caller to add its own padding workaround.

Thanks!

records.title: [Bug]`test_tgv_gemm_sm100_reference_correctness` can trigger CUDA illegal instruction due to incorrect `b` layout in trace init
records.body:
## Summary
Found this issue in [51571414](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/pipelines/51571414)
Failed jobs: [unit_test_gb200_pretyche: [cu130]](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/320010533) | [unit_test_gb200_pretyche: [cu129]](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/320010507)

- tests.trace.test_tgv_gemm_sm100_reference_correctness

  The new trace reference test for `tgv_gemm_sm100` fails with:

```
2026-05-17T15:16:12.945930Z 01O FAILED tests/trace/test_tgv_gemm_sm100_reference_correctness.py::test_tgv_gemm_sm100_reference_correctness[shape_kwargs1] - torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered
2026-05-17T15:16:12.945931Z 01O Search for `cudaErrorIllegalInstruction' in https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html for more information.
2026-05-17T15:16:12.945932Z 01O CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
```

  The pytest output shows sF, which suggests the first parameterized case likely triggered an asynchronous CUDA failure and
  was converted into a skip by the broad except Exception, leaving the CUDA context in a bad state. The second case then
  reports the error later during torch.cuda.random.manual_seed, so the stack trace is probably not pointing at the original
  failing launch.

  ## Failure

  FAILED tests/trace/test_tgv_gemm_sm100_reference_correctness.py::test_tgv_gemm_sm100_reference_correctness[shape_kwargs1]
  torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered

  Test cases:

  dict(device="cuda", M=16, N=1024, K=1024),
  dict(device="cuda", M=8, N=2048, K=1024),

  ## Suspected Root Cause (By Codex)

  tgv_gemm_sm100 expects b to be a column-major [K, N] tensor. The existing GEMM test constructs it as:

  B = torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda", dtype=dtype).t()

  However, the trace init currently constructs b as a contiguous row-major tensor:

  b = torch.randn(K, N, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)

  This conflicts with the documented/layout expectation for TGV GEMM and may cause the kernel to read the tensor with invalid
  stride assumptions.

  ## Suggested Fix (By codex)

  Update the trace init to construct b in column-major layout:

  b = torch.randn(N, K, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device).t()

  Also consider avoiding the broad except Exception: pytest.skip(...) around the kernel call, because CUDA illegal-instruction
  failures can poison the CUDA context and make the next parameterized case fail at an unrelated API call.

  ## Relevant Files

  - tests/trace/test_tgv_gemm_sm100_reference_correctness.py
  - flashinfer/trace/templates/page.py
  - tests/gemm/test_tgv_gemm.py
  - flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py

records.title: [Bug]`test_xqa_mla_reference_correctness` has invalid reference shape handling and an unsupported 64-query-head test case
records.body:
## Summary
Found this issue in [51571414](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/pipelines/51571414)
Failed Jobs: [unit_test_spark_colossus: [cu130]](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/320010645) | [unit_test_spark_colossus: [cu129]](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/320010617)

  `tests/trace/test_xqa_mla_reference_correctness.py` currently fails both parameterized cases on SM120/SM121.
Failed Test:
tests/trace/test_xqa_mla_reference_correctness.py::test_xqa_mla_reference_correctness[shape_kwargs0]
tests/trace/test_xqa_mla_reference_correctness.py::test_xqa_mla_reference_correctness[shape_kwargs1]

  1. The reference path squeezes the beam dimension from `q` and `seq_lens`, but still passes an unsqueezed output buffer.
  2. The second test case uses `num_heads_qo=64`, while `xqa_mla` explicitly only supports 128 query heads.

  ## Failures

  ```
  RuntimeError: output with shape [2, 1, 128, 512] doesn't match the broadcast shape [2, 2, 128, 512]
  /tmp/flashinfer/flashinfer/trace/templates/page.py:514

  ValueError: XQA MLA only supports 128 query heads (head_group_ratio=128), got 64 query heads
  /tmp/flashinfer/flashinfer/xqa.py:526
```
  ## Suspected Root Cause (By Codex)

  ### 1. Reference output shape mismatch

  The test constructs reference inputs like this:

  q_ref = inputs["q"].float().squeeze(1)          # [B, H, QK]
  seq_lens_ref = inputs["seq_lens"].squeeze(1)    # [B]
  ref_buffer = torch.empty_like(inputs["output"]) # [B, 1, H, CKV]

  But _xqa_mla_reference() derives its result shape from q:

  out_shape = q.shape[:-1] + (v_head_dim,)
  result = out.reshape(out_shape).to(dtype)
  output.copy_(result)

  Since q_ref is squeezed, result has shape [B, H, CKV], while output still has shape [B, 1, H, CKV]. This causes the
  broadcast mismatch.

  ### 2. Unsupported num_heads_qo=64

  The second parameterized case uses:

  num_heads_qo=64

  But xqa_mla() enforces:

  head_group_ratio = num_q_heads
  if head_group_ratio != 128:
      raise ValueError(...)

  So this is not a valid correctness-test case for the current kernel.

  ## Suggested Fix (By Codex)

  Keep the beam dimension consistently in the reference call:

  q_ref = inputs["q"].float()
  seq_lens_ref = inputs["seq_lens"].to(torch.int32)
  ref_buffer = torch.empty_like(inputs["output"])

  and compare without squeezing:

  _close_pass_ratio(
      inputs["output"].float(),
      ref_out.float(),
      atol=0.05,
      rtol=0.05,
      pass_ratio=0.95,
  )

  Also replace the second test case with num_heads_qo=128, or move the num_heads_qo=64 case into a separate negative test that
  explicitly asserts ValueError.

records.title: [Bug] b12x MoE dispatch missing max_active_clusters argument — TypeError: Expects 42 parameters
records.body:
## Environment

- **FlashInfer**: 0.6.11.post2, 0.6.11.post3 (both affected)
- **Hardware**: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, SM120
- **CUDA**: 13.2

## Bug description

When running `b12x_fused_moe` / `launch_sm120_moe` against a real model (e.g. `RedHatAI/Qwen3-Coder-Next-NVFP4`, 512 experts, compressed-tensors W4A4), inference crashes on the first forward pass:

```
TypeError: Expects 42 parameters when calling: __call__(
  a_ptr: DataPointer, topk_ids_ptr: DataPointer, topk_weights_ptr: DataPointer,
  packed_a_ptr: DataPointer, sfa_ptr: DataPointer, packed_a_storage_ptr: DataPointer,
  scale_storage_ptr: DataPointer,
  barrier_count: Tensor([1], int32), barrier_epoch: Tensor([1], int32),
  pair_head: Tensor([1], int32), producers_done_count: Tensor([1], int32),
  all_work_published: Tensor([1], int32), task_head: Tensor([1], int32),
  task_tail: Tensor([1], int32), task_ready_ptr: DataPointer,
  task_expert_ptr: DataPointer, task_m_tile_ptr: DataPointer,
  task_slice_begin_ptr: DataPointer, task_slice_count_ptr: DataPointer,
  task_valid_rows_ptr: DataPointer, tile_write_count_ptr: DataPointer,
  b_w13: Tensor([512, 1024, 512], float4_e2m1fnx2), sfb_w13_ptr: DataPointer,
  b_down: Tensor([2048, 128, 512], float4_e2m1fnx2), sfb_down_ptr: DataPointer,
  row_counts: Tensor([512], int32), expert_write_rows: Tensor([512], int32),
  expert_tile_base: Tensor([513], int32),
  input_global_scale: Tensor([512], float32), alpha: Tensor([512], float32),
  down_alpha: Tensor([512], float32), global_scale: Tensor([512], float32),
  scatter_ptr: DataPointer, token_map_ptr: DataPointer,
  token_weights_ptr: DataPointer,
  num_tokens: int32, max_rows: int32, rows_padded: int32,
  max_tasks: int32, max_phys_tiles: int32, max_active_clusters: int32,
  stream: Stream)
```

## Root cause

In `moe_dispatch.py`, two dispatch call sites compile a 42-parameter kernel but omit the `max_active_clusters` (`mac`) argument when calling it.

**`_get_dynamic_kernel`** already returns `(compiled, mac)`:

```python
compiled, mac = _get_dynamic_kernel(...)
# Later, dispatch calls:
compiled(*runtime_args, current_cuda_stream())   # ← mac missing!
```

The `compiled` object has signature `(..., max_active_clusters: int32, stream: Stream)`, so calling it without `mac` raises the error.

**Affected locations** (line numbers approximate, may shift with rebases):

1. Static/micro kernel dispatch in `launch_sm120_moe` — `_get_static_kernel` / `_get_micro_kernel` also return `(compiled, mac)`, and the call site drops `mac`:
   ```python
   compiled(*runtime_args, current_cuda_stream())
   ```

2. Dynamic kernel dispatch in `launch_sm120_dynamic_moe`:
   ```python
   compiled, mac = _get_dynamic_kernel(...)
   # ...
   compiled(*runtime_args, current_cuda_stream())
   ```

## Fix

Add `mac,` before `current_cuda_stream()` at both call sites:

```python
# static/micro path
compiled, mac = _get_static_kernel(...)   # or _get_micro_kernel
compiled(*runtime_args, mac, current_cuda_stream())

# dynamic path  
compiled, mac = _get_dynamic_kernel(...)
compiled(*runtime_args, mac, current_cuda_stream())
```

## Notes

- The `mac` value is already correctly computed and returned by all three `_get_*_kernel` helpers — it just wasn't being forwarded to the compiled kernel.
- Both 0.6.11.post2 and 0.6.11.post3 are affected; workaround is to patch the installed wheel.
- This only manifests at runtime (not during the CuTe DSL compile step), so unit tests using synthetic small shapes may pass if they exercise a code path where `mac` happens to have no effect.

records.title: Add MXFP8 support for DeepEP-style MoE dispatch/combine kernels
records.body:
The current DeepEP dispatch/combine paths used by vLLM are compatible with block-FP8 quantization, but do not yet support MXFP8. They would like to use MXFP8, specifically for decode nodes.

DeepEP currently has two dispatch/combine collective implementations for MoE models in vLLM:
- prefill / high_throughput: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_ht.py
- decode / low_latency: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/deepep_ll.py

Support ask:
- Add MXFP8 quantization format support to the dispatch/combine kernels
- Add support for a batched-format MXFP8 MoE kernel.
- Integrate the MXFP8 MoE kernel support into vLLM so that it is compatible with the low_latency DeepEP communication path.
 
The highest-priority path is: MXFP8 + decode / low_latency. It would also be useful to support: MXFP8 + prefill / high_throughput but low_latency decode support is the more important use case.

  The failure appears to be in the LSE comparison (`lse_out` vs `lse_ref`), not the final attention output comparison.

  ## Example Failures

  ```
  FAILED tests/attention/test_trtllm_gen_attention.py::test_trtllm_batch_decode[
  True-False-False-128-110-False-None-bf16-fp8-bf16--1-256-4-32-2-8-HND-trtllm-gen]

  Mismatched elements: 4 / 15360
  Greatest absolute difference: 0.0017115473747253418 (up to 0.001 allowed)
  Greatest relative difference: 0.009495969861745834 (up to 0.001 allowed)

  FAILED tests/attention/test_trtllm_gen_attention.py::test_trtllm_batch_decode[
  True-False-False-128-110-False-None-bf16-fp8-bf16--1-256-4-32-2-8-NHD-trtllm-gen]

  Mismatched elements: 129 / 16384
  Greatest absolute difference: 0.009348392486572266 (up to 0.001 allowed)
  Greatest relative difference: 0.1515425443649292 (up to 0.001 allowed)
```
  ## Why This Looks Like LSE

  The failing tolerance is 1e-3, which matches the LSE check:

  torch.testing.assert_close(
      lse_out[:n], lse_ref[:n].float(), rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-3
  )

  For the failing case:

  batch_size=256
  q_len_per_req=4
  num_kv_heads=2
  head_grp_size=8
  num_qo_heads=16

  Expected LSE shape is:

  [batch_size * q_len_per_req, num_qo_heads]
  = [1024, 16]
  = 16384 elements

  This matches the failure log (129 / 16384, 142 / 16384). Final output would include head_dim=128, so it would have far more elements.

  ## Suspected Regression (by Codex)

  This appears related to #3116:

  a73c281a78faecaf561c807126c2cefa49da914a
  feat: Reland support lse in trtllm paged attn kernels (#3116)

  That PR introduced LSE return/checking for trtllm paged attention. The failing cases are fp8-KV decode cases where LSE differs from reference by about 0.0017 ~ 0.010, while the current tolerance is 1e-3.

  ## Expected Behavior

  test_trtllm_batch_decode should pass for bf16/fp8/bf16 trtllm-gen decode cases, or the LSE check should use a tolerance appropriate for fp8 KV cache precision.

  ## Suggested Direction (By Codex)

  For kv_dtype == "fp8", either relax the LSE tolerance, for example:

  if kv_dtype == "fp8":
      lse_rtol, lse_atol = 1e-2, 1e-2
  else:
      lse_rtol, lse_atol = 1e-3, 1e-3

  or temporarily skip exact LSE validation for fp8-KV cases while keeping the final output comparison enabled.

  This should be treated as an LSE accuracy/tolerance issue rather than a confirmed final attention output correctness regression unless output comparison also fails
  independently.

cc @aleozlx

records.title: Add sparse-MLA paged attention for SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell)
records.body:
Tracking issue for a forthcoming PR. Filing this first to lock down API/scope with maintainers before the code review cycle.

**Source code (existing, validated implementation):** https://github.com/leavelet/sparse_mla_sm120

## Relation to #3346

Fills two cells in @nvpohanh's DSV4 tracker currently marked **"Missing FlashInfer"** on SM120:

| Row | What it needs | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| **HCA-MQA** | Dense MQA over SWA + C128 cache + `attn_sink` | `topk_index=None` path |
| **CSA-MQA** | Sparse MQA over SWA + C4 cache + `attn_sink` + `topk_index` | Native path |

InvRoPE-fused variants (HCA-MQA-INVROPE / CSA-MQA-INVROPE) are out of scope here.

## Gap vs existing backends

| Backend | SM | sparse_top_k | q_len>1 | attn_sink | Prefill | Dual cache |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper` | 90/100 | no | yes | no | partial | no |
| `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` | 100/103 | yes | yes | partial | no | no |
| `xqa_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` | **120** | no | no | no | no | no |
| `BlockSparseAttentionWrapper` | all | block-mask | yes | no | yes | no |
| **This PR** | **120** | **yes** | **yes** | **yes** | **yes** | **yes** |

XQA is the closest hardware target but lacks every DSv4-required feature.

## Scope

- **Public surface (both function and wrapper)**, matching the precedent set by `b12x_fused_moe` + `B12xMoEWrapper` for SM120/121:
  - `flashinfer.sparse_mla_sm120_paged_attention(...)` — function-shaped, matching `xqa_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` / `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla`. Auto-dispatches decode vs prefill on `num_tokens`.
  - `flashinfer.BatchSparseMLAPagedAttentionWrapper` — class with pre-allocated workspace for `use_cuda_graph=True`. Already exists in the downstream package.
- **Naming**: `sparse_mla_sm120_*` (descriptive). Deliberately not adopting the `b12x_*` prefix — that brand is for the cute_dsl port subsystem; we are C++/JitSpec and conflating the two would mislead readers about the implementation.
- **SM gating**: `@supported_compute_capability([120, 121])` (canonical per `flashinfer/utils.py`; matches b12x).
- **Cudagraph contract**: `output` + `workspace_buffer` mutated in place; returns `None`; function wrapped in `@register_custom_op` + `@register_fake_op` (matching the XQA precedent, since we are C++/JitSpec like XQA; b12x doesn't need this because cute_dsl integrates differently).
- **One monolithic JIT module**: `gen_sparse_mla_sm120_module()`, URI `"sparse_mla_sm120"` — mirrors `gen_mla_module()`. Parameterized would explode to ~48 variants; not worth it.
- **`TraceTemplate` entry** + AOT registration gated on `has_sm120 or has_sm121`.

**Size**: ~4,300 LOC total (~2,700 kernel headers, ~150 launcher+binding, ~500 Python, ~600 tests, ~50 docs). Sits between `cutlass_mla` (~262 LOC) and `xqa` (~18k). Headers go under `include/flashinfer/attention/sparse_mla_sm120/` following the hopper/blackwell pattern; ~460 LOC of duplication dropped by reusing upstream `math.cuh`, `utils.cuh`, `mma.cuh` FP8 instructions, and `cp_async.cuh` non-TMA variants. Kept local: cp.async.bulk TMA, MXFP8 block-scaled mma, kernel-private softmax/RoPE register layouts.

**PR shape**: single atomic PR. The kernels, binding, Python wrapper, tests, and docs only have meaning together — any split would leave an intermediate broken state (headers that nothing links to, or a Python module that imports nonexistent symbols).

## Validation

Tested via vLLM on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (TP=2), DSv4-Flash:

- 5× stress on long-context decode: **240/240 successful, 0 IMAs**.
- GSM8K 5-shot, 200q: **0.970**, 0 invalid.
- `bench-serve` throughput and P99 TPOT inside clean-baseline band.

## Licensing

Source is BSD-3-Clause. Two precedents in-tree:
- Apache-2.0 (XQA, FlashInfer-authored core)
- **BSD-3-Clause** (b12x port: `flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell_sm12x/*` and `flashinfer/gemm/kernels/dense_blockscaled_gemm_sm120_b12x.py`)

We will ship BSD-3-Clause headers matching the b12x precedent (same NVIDIA-adjacent lineage). Happy to relicense to Apache-2.0 instead if maintainers prefer uniformity — it's a same-author act for @lucifer1004 and @leavelet with no third-party copyright entanglement.

## Open questions

**Q1 — Dual cache.** Main SWA and compressed caches use **different page block sizes** (C128 / C4), so they can't share one tensor. Options: (a) accept dual-cache args; (b) concatenate at wrapper level + slice internally (adds copy cost, doesn't help — different page sizes); (c) document non-support for non-DSv4 shapes. Prefer (a).

**Q2 — `sparse_mla_top_k` naming.** trtllm-gen uses `sparse_mla_top_k: int = 0` as a mode flag. Ours is always sparse — required positional. Align on the name but make it required?

**Q3 — `topk_length` (per-token variable top-k).** Needed for sliding-window MLA near sequence start. New concept — OK to introduce, or prefer a sentinel-in-`indices` mechanism?

**Q4 — `attn_sink` semantics.** Per-head learnable bias added pre-softmax. trtllm-gen's matrix shows "partial" sink support — same name/semantics OK?

**Q5 — SM121 coverage.** Plan to gate on `[120, 121]` matching the b12x convention. Our kernels target sm120a — please flag if there are SM121 variants we should explicitly test on or exclude.

**Q6 — License.** Two precedents in-tree: Apache-2.0 (XQA, core) and BSD-3-Clause (b12x port). Our upstream is BSD-3-Clause; we'd ship BSD-3-Clause matching b12x by default. Confirm, or do you want Apache-2.0 for uniformity?

## Coordination

1. Is this within FlashInfer's intended scope?
2. Are Q1–Q6 answerable in-thread, or sync preferred?
3. Preferred reviewer for sparse-MLA kernel code?

cc: @leavelet, @nvpohanh

---

The implementation is already validated; this issue exists purely to align API/scope/process before PR.

records.title: [RFC] Add SVDQuant W4A4 (NVFP4 + low-rank) GEMM and activation quantize for SM_100 / SM_103
records.body:
### Motivation.

[SVDQuant](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05007) (W4A4 with low-rank correction) is currently the only practical quantization method for diffusion transformers, delivering 2x+ speedup with minimal quality loss. The reference implementation is [Nunchaku](https://github.com/nunchaku-ai/nunchaku), and I have an in-flight vLLM RFC ([vllm#37908](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/37908)) to add `NunchakuLinearMethod` as a vLLM upstream `QuantizationConfig` + `LinearMethodBase` backend, so that vllm-omni can drop its diffusion-side integration ([vllm-omni#1986](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/1986)) on top.

Nunchaku's W4A4 FP4 path is double-gated to SM_120+:
- Kernel source: `FP4_AVAILABLE` is `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 1200` ([gemm_w4a4.cuh:28](https://github.com/nunchaku-ai/nunchaku/blob/main/src/kernels/zgemm/gemm_w4a4.cuh#L28)); the FP4 kernel template declares `static constexpr int MIN_ARCH = 1200` ([gemm_w4a4.cuh:360](https://github.com/nunchaku-ai/nunchaku/blob/main/src/kernels/zgemm/gemm_w4a4.cuh#L360)).
- Build: `setup.py` whitelists SM to `{75, 80, 86, 89, 120a, 121a}` ([setup.py:54](https://github.com/nunchaku-ai/nunchaku/blob/main/setup.py#L54)).

SM_100 (arch 1000) and SM_103 (arch 1030) fall below both gates, so data-center Blackwell (B200 / B300 / GB200 / GB300) has no SVDQuant kernel today and the vllm#37908 backend has nothing to call on the GPUs that actually serve production diffusion traffic.

I have written an SVDQuant W4A4 kernel pair targeting SM_100 / SM_103 in [ultism/svdquant-kernels](https://github.com/ultism/svdquant-kernels) (Apache-2.0, I am the author). The pair implements the same W4A4 linear contract as nunchaku ([nunchaku/models/linear.py:162-269](https://github.com/nunchaku-ai/nunchaku/blob/main/nunchaku/models/linear.py#L162-L269)), so `NunchakuLinearMethod.apply()` from vllm#37908 can dispatch into either backend with one SM check:

1. **Quantize + LoRA-down (Triton)** — `input → (qout, ascales, lora_act_out)`, a 3-output kernel that NVFP4-packs the activation **and** computes `lora_act_out = input @ lora_down` in the same pass. The fuse is the point: one HBM read of `input` feeds both the quantize and the small low-rank matmul, sharing a register tile. Memory-bound on B200 (measured AI 26–99 FLOP/B vs the 281 FLOP/B FP16 tensor-core ridge), so `tcgen05` / TMEM / 2-CTA buy nothing here — Triton is the load-bearing choice, not a stylistic one. SmoothQuant `diag(1/smooth)` is absorbed offline into `lora_down` weights, so the quant path divides by `smooth` but the LoRA path does not; this asymmetry matches nunchaku's runtime contract.
2. **W4A4 GEMM with low-rank residual (CuTe DSL)** — `(qout, qweight, ascales, wscales, lora_act_in, lora_up, [bias], [alpha], [wcscales]) → out`. FA4-style warp-specialized: `tcgen05.mma.kind::mxf4nvf4.block_scale.scale_vec::4X` main path, β-interleaved low-rank residual MMA sharing the same TMEM accumulator with the main MMA (no chained dependency), per-column `* wcscales + bias` epilogue.

The two ops are co-designed: the quantize op's three outputs are exactly the GEMM op's three new inputs (`qout`, `ascales`, `lora_act_in`). The signatures intentionally line up with nunchaku's `svdq_quantize_w4a4_act_fuse_lora_cuda` / `svdq_gemm_w4a4_cuda` so the vllm#37908 linear method branches by SM with no other code differences.

The submission shape mirrors existing FlashInfer integrations: `nvfp4_quantize` (`flashinfer/quantization/`) + `mm_fp4` (`flashinfer/gemm/`) is the established pattern of a separately-shippable quantize op plus a separately-shippable GEMM, with the user (here: vllm#37908's `LinearMethodBase`) wiring them. Compared to that pair, both halves here carry more state (LoRA-down projection on the producer side, low-rank residual + per-channel affine on the consumer side); neither half has an existing FlashInfer analog.

### Proposed Change.

Two new APIs, both `@supported_compute_capability([100, 103])`:

- **`flashinfer.quantization.quantize_w4a4_svdquant_with_lora_down(...)`** — Triton kernel at `flashinfer/triton/kernels/svdquant_quant.py`, Python API at `flashinfer/quantization/svdquant.py`.
  - Signature: `(x, *, lora_down, smooth=None, fp4=True, pad_size=256) -> (qout, ascales, lora_act_out)`. Matches `nunchaku.ops.quantize.svdq_quantize_w4a4_act_fuse_lora_cuda` shape-for-shape so the vllm#37908 linear method can swap backends with no other code differences.
  - Outputs: `qout [M, N//2] uint8` (NVFP4-packed activation), `ascales [N/16, M] fp8_e4m3` (per-16-K-block scales), `lora_act_out [M, R] fp32` (LoRA-down projection of the *unsmoothed* input — SmoothQuant's `diag(1/smooth)` is pre-absorbed offline into `lora_down`).

- **`flashinfer.gemm.mm_w4a4_svdquant_nvfp4(...)`** — CuTe DSL W4A4 GEMM with low-rank residual and per-column affine epilogue.
  - Kernel class `Sm100SvdQuantW4A4Kernel` at `flashinfer/gemm/kernels/dense_w4a4_svdquant_sm100.py` (sibling of `Sm100BlockScaledPersistentDenseGemmKernel`).
  - Backend `"cute-dsl"` only, gated on `is_cute_dsl_available()`. Lazy-imports `cutlass.cute`.
  - Signature: `(qout, qweight, ascales, wscales, lora_act_in, lora_up, *, bias=None, alpha=None, wcscales=None, out=None, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16, ...) -> out`. Matches `nunchaku.ops.gemm.svdq_gemm_w4a4_cuda`. `lora_act_in` and `lora_up` are required (low-rank residual is part of the quant scheme); `wcscales` / `bias` / `alpha` are optional per nunchaku's contract.
  - Tactic space: `(mma_tiler_mn, cluster_shape_mn, lora_schedule)`; cluster_shape `(2,1)` opt-in for 2-CTA.

A small CuTe DSL utility lands as a side effect: an FA4-style explicit per-warp `PipelineStateSimple` at `flashinfer/cute_dsl/pipeline.py`. Not upstream in `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` yet; the alternative is to upstream there first and vendor here in the interim. Either is fine, asking maintainer preference.

**Out of scope for this PR**: SM_120 / SM_121 (Nunchaku covers); the fused linear wrapper (lives in vllm#37908's `NunchakuLinearMethod.apply()`, exactly the way `nunchaku.SVDQW4A4Linear.forward` ([linear.py:162-189](https://github.com/nunchaku-ai/nunchaku/blob/main/nunchaku/models/linear.py#L162-L189)) composes the two ops today — not FlashInfer's responsibility); AscendC / non-NVIDIA backends; epilogue requantize to next-layer NVFP4 (production diffusion shapes don't reach it; see svdquant-kernels README §v3-dropped).

### Implementation quality.

Head-to-head against nunchaku at the production shape `M=4352 K=3840 N=3072 R=128`. Nunchaku ships SM_120a/121a only, so the comparison is cross-chip — ours on B200 (SM_100a), nunchaku on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM_120a). Cross-chip MFU is dominated by clock-frequency drift between consumer-Blackwell (variable boost) and data-center-Blackwell (sustained boost), not kernel quality, so we skip it. The kernel-level apples-to-apples metric is `sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_*` (per-cycle tensor-pipe saturation, frequency-independent). Single-launch ncu, LoRA on, bias + wcscales on, `fp4=True`:

| Kernel             | Device                | dtype | Duration   | Tensor Pipe (active) | Tensor Pipe (elapsed) |
| ------------------ | --------------------- | ----- | ---------: | -------------------: | --------------------: |
| v2_fa4 (post-LU)   | B200, SM_100          | fp16  |  32.13 µs  |   52.0 %             |   **45.2 %**          |
| nunchaku           | RTX PRO 6000, SM_120a | fp16  | 185.25 µs  |   58.8 %             |   **45.4 %**          |
| nunchaku           | RTX PRO 6000, SM_120a | bf16  | 157.54 µs  |   73.7 %             |   **54.6 %**          |

Elapsed-% is the kernel-level reading ("over total wall time, what fraction of cycles the tensor pipe is active"). Ours-fp16 and nunchaku-fp16 land within 0.2 pp — **the kernel saturates its respective hardware to the same extent**; the ~5.8× absolute duration gap is the B200's larger SM count and higher per-cycle FP4 peak, not a code-quality gap.

Nunchaku bf16 leads nunchaku fp16 by 9.2 pp on elapsed-% because nunchaku's fp16 hits a register-pressure cliff (255 regs, 2.28M LMEM, 101 % spill overhead). Ours does not have this cliff at either dtype.

Caveat: the `peak_sustained_active` denominator is per-arch and may or may not include the consumer fp32-accumulate throttle. Raw `.ncu-rep` files can be shared on request.

### Feedback Period.

2 weeks.

### CC List.

@yzh119 @aleozlx @bkryu @dhiraj113 (GEMM CODEOWNERS) — cross-ping @Isotr0py from vllm#37908 so the two RFCs stay in sync.

### Any Other Things.

- Reference kernel source: <https://github.com/ultism/svdquant-kernels/tree/main/cute_kernels/gemm_w4a4> and <https://github.com/ultism/svdquant-kernels/tree/main/triton_kernels/quantize_w4a4_act_fuse_lora>. Apache-2.0.
- Quantized checkpoint (Z-Image-Turbo, used in the vllm#37908 thread): <https://huggingface.co/ultranationalism/nunchaku-z-image-turbo>.
- Two pre-PR items I will resolve before opening the PR regardless of RFC outcome: (1) the `os.environ.setdefault("CUTE_DSL_ARCH", "sm_100a")` import-time side effect in the kernel will be removed; (2) `PipelineStateSimple` placement per maintainer preference above.
- CI: this needs the NVIDIA internal `unit_test_b200` / `unit_test_b300` runners to exercise SM_100 / SM_103. Confirming `/bot run` authorization is available for this PR.

records.title: [bug] flashinfer_b12x MoE on sm_121a / EP>1: spec validator uses weight_E, kernel still hits illegal address after state_E patch
records.body:
Filing as a follow-up to #3294 (closed) per @meena-at-work's request — splitting the EP>1 correctness work out of that thread, which started life as a wheel-contents question.

## TL;DR

On 8× DGX Spark (GB10, `sm_121a`), TP=8, EP=8 with `festr2/MiMo-V2.5-Pro-NVFP4-MXFP8-attn-TP8` (384 routed experts → 48 local/rank), `flashinfer_b12x_fused_moe` fails in two layered ways:

1. **Spec-validator side** — kernel's fake-tensor spec sizes `b_w13` / `b_down` and the per-expert scale tensors with `weight_E` (global), while vLLM correctly passes the local `num_local_experts`-sized weight tensors on EP runs. Rejected with `Mismatched b_w13.shape[2] on argument #9 ... expected to be 384`.
2. **Kernel-internal side** — patching the fake-tensor sizes to `state_E` (see diff below) makes the spec validator accept local weights and the kernel JIT-compiles, but `launch_sm120_moe` then hits `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` intermittently across ranks. `output.isnan().any()` immediately after `flashinfer_b12x_fused_moe` shows finite output on the calls that complete — i.e. the patched spec isn't producing degenerate numerics, the kernel is just still indexing past the local weight tensor somewhere inside the launch.

Non-EP (plain TP=8, all 384 experts per rank) fails separately with `cudaErrorInvalidValue` from inside `launch_sm120_moe` — so the b12x kernel doesn't get through a clean forward pass on `sm_121a` regardless of EP.

## Necessary-but-not-sufficient patch

`flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell_sm12x/moe_dispatch.py` (`_get_static_kernel` ~L438 and `_get_dynamic_kernel` ~L674):

```diff
-    (w1_rows, k, weight_E),         # b_w13_fake
+    (w1_rows, k, state_E),
-    (k, n, weight_E),               # b_down_fake
+    (k, n, state_E),
-    (weight_E,)                     # input_gs_fake / alpha_fake / down_alpha_fake / global_scale_fake
+    (state_E,)
```

`global_to_local_expert_fake` keeps `weight_E` (it's the bridge map). After this, `state_E = num_local_experts` is consistent across `packed_a` / `row_counts` / `weight_expert_ids` / `compact_topk_ids` / `token_map` / `token_weights` and the patched weight + scale buffers. Kernel JIT-compiles once and accepts the call across all MoE layers × all 8 ranks. Subsequent `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` from inside the launch is the remaining issue.

## Reproducer

- Hardware: 8× DGX Spark (GB10, `sm_121a`), aarch64
- Model: `festr2/MiMo-V2.5-Pro-NVFP4-MXFP8-attn-TP8` (384 experts, intermediate-size 2048)
- vLLM `--moe-backend flashinfer_b12x`, `-tp 8 --enable-expert-parallel`
- `flashinfer-python==0.6.11`, `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.11`, `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.11+cu130`
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.5.1` (clean install per NVIDIA/cutlass#3227)
- Full setup: https://github.com/idonati/spark-vllm-docker-festr2

Confirmed 4.5.1 fixes the prior cute-dsl `_mma` ptxas lowering bug (NVIDIA/cutlass#3227), so this report is on a clean cutlass-dsl baseline.

## Current state on our side

Production path on this cluster is `--moe-backend marlin` (FP4→FP8 dequant + Marlin GEMM), which is correct and ~7-25% faster than native NVFP4 was on the few configs cutlass-dsl 4.5.1 + b12x got far enough to benchmark. So this isn't a blocker for us, but it leaves consumer-Blackwell EP NVFP4 MoE unusable via b12x. Happy to test any candidate kernel patch on the cluster.

records.title: [Sampling Perf] top_k_top_p_sampling on SM 120 is significantly slower than naive insertion sort-based speclialized kernel

```yaml
flashinfer                               mean time: 0.307686 ms, speedup: 7.53, 26.62 GB/s
sampling_topk_topp_batched               mean time: 0.102009 ms, speedup: 22.72, 80.31 GB/s
####################################################################################################
bs: 32, vocab_size: 256000
torch                                    mean time: 4.632301 ms, 3.54 GB/s
flashinfer                               mean time: 0.598686 ms, speedup: 7.74, 27.37 GB/s
sampling_topk_topp_batched               mean time: 0.127663 ms, speedup: 36.29, 128.34 GB/s
```
Reproduction and benchmark results can be found on [here](https://github.com/WingEdge777/vitamin-cuda/tree/main/kernels/sampling)
Maybe I did the benchmark in a wrong way, so any correction or review on the evaluation pipeline would be highly appreciated.

## Environments
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop (SM 120)
CUDA: 13.2
flashinfer-python：0.6.9

## My Analysis & Guess
I guess the gap comes from a few architectural differences:
- Template Specialization vs. Dynamic Generalization : In my implementation, `top_k` is specialized as a template parameter. nvcc can resolve loop boundaries at compile time, leading to aggressive branchless unrolling and scalar replacement of aggregates (SRA) on register files. FlashInfer, as a general library, has to support dynamic/arbitrary top_k which inevitably introduces dynamic branches or state machines.
- Hardware Specific Tuning: FlashInfer's dual-pivot/rejection sampling might be highly tuned for datacenter GPUs (like H100/B200) but hasn't been optimized for SM 120 consumer architectures yet.

Is this behavior expected for FlashInfer's sampling algorithm when handling small top_k or when deployed on smaller laptop GPUs? Are there plans to introduce template-specialized sampling APIs for specific constraints?

Thanks for this amazing project! Looking forward to any insights.

records.title: [Bug] CuTe DSL RMSNorm illegal memory access for contiguous tensors just above 2^31 elements
records.body:
## Bug Description

`flashinfer.norm.kernels.rmsnorm.rmsnorm_cute` fails with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` for large contiguous tensors whose total element count is just above `2^31`.

The failure boundary appears tied to the number of tensor elements, not to `M` alone and not directly to dtype byte size. The exact `2^31` element case passes, while cases just above `2^31` fail.

 ## Observed Results

On H200:

| Shape | Dtype | Elements | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| (150000, 12980) | fp16 | 1,947,000,000 | pass |
| (131072, 16384) | fp16 | 2,147,483,648 | pass |
| (175000, 12288) | fp16 | 2,150,400,000 | fail |
| (4194305, 512) | fp16 | 2,147,484,160 | fail |
| (150000, 16384) | fp32 | 2,457,600,000 | fail |
| (150000, 16384) | bf16 | 2,457,600,000 | fail |

The exact 2^31 element case passes, which is consistent with the maximum valid flat element offset being 2^31 - 1.

## Reproduction

```python
import torch
from flashinfer.norm.kernels.rmsnorm import rmsnorm_cute

M = 175000
H = 12288
dtype = torch.float16
eps = 1e-6

x = torch.zeros((M, H), device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
weight = torch.zeros((H,), device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
out = torch.zeros_like(x)

rmsnorm_cute(x, weight, out, eps, weight_bias=0.0, enable_pdl=False)
torch.cuda.synchronize()

print("ok")
```

## Notes

This looks related to #3005 / #3007, but appears to be a different case.

This issue reproduces with contiguous tensors. The wrapper reshapes to 2D and computes:

```python
M = input.shape[0]
H = input.shape[-1]
```

For the failing examples, M itself fits in Int32, so the issue does not appear to be simply passing M as Int32.

The observed threshold is consistent with a 32-bit flat element offset overflow in compact-layout addressing, for example an effective offset like `row * H + col` crossing signed 32-bit range when M * H > 2^31

records.title: SSDCombined fails to compile when dstate != chunk_size
records.body:
**Environment**
  - flashinfer-python: 0.6.11.post1 (also present in current main as of 2026-05-22)
  - nvidia-cutlass-dsl: 4.5.0
  - GPU: NVIDIA B200 (SM100)
  - Python: 3.12

**Bug description**

SSDCombined fails to JIT-compile with a ValueError: Operation creation failed whenever dstate != chunk_size. The kernel was tailored for the the Nemotron-H reference configuration (chunk_size=128, dstate=128), which accidentally masks the bug because the two values are equal.


**Minimal repro**
```
  import torch
  from flashinfer.mamba import SSDCombined

  common = dict(
      io_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
      state_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
      has_d=True,
      d_has_hdim=False,
      has_initial_states=True,
      has_varlen=False,
      has_z=False,
      seq_idx_dtype=torch.int32,
  )

  # Works — dstate == chunk_size (both 128, coincidental match)
  SSDCombined(chunk_size=128, nheads=128, headdim=64, dstate=128, ngroups=8, **common)
  print("dstate=128: OK")

  # Fails — dstate != chunk_size
  SSDCombined(chunk_size=128, nheads=128, headdim=64, dstate=64, ngroups=8, **common)
  print("dstate=64: OK")  # never reached
```

  Error output:
```
  dstate=128 (chunk_size==dstate): OK
  dstate=64  (chunk_size!=dstate): FAIL
    loc("...ssd_kernel.py":3652:31): error: expects smem and gmem have the same size in the
    first rank, but got smemShape: (((128,16),1,4),2) and gmemShape: (((128,16),1,8),2,1,?,?,?)
    ValueError: Operation creation failed
```

**Root cause**
  
 SSDKernel defines two intra-chunk MMA tile shapes:
```
# ssd_kernel.py line 101-102
self.tile_shape_mnk_intra1 = (L, L, N)   # L=chunk_size, N=dstate - for B/C SSM operands
self.tile_shape_mnk_intra2 = (L, D, L)   # L=chunk_size, D=headdim - for X operand
```
tma_partition_for_mma_b_operand (line 3624) is called by two @cute.jit methods:
- _warp_tma_x_deltas
- _warp_tma_b_c

The function always uses self.tile_shape_mnk_intra2[1:] regardless of which operand it's partitioning. For the B/C SSM operands this produces gmem K-mode = chunk_size/16, while smem was allocated for dstate/16.
TMA partition requires them to match - they only agree accidentally when dstate == chunk_size.

Note: tma_partition_for_mma_a_operand (line 3661) correctly derives (L, N) from tile_shape_mnk_intra1 for the C operand, so only the B operand path is affected.

**Proposed fix**

```
  --- a/flashinfer/mamba/ssd_kernel.py
  +++ b/flashinfer/mamba/ssd_kernel.py
  @@ -3624,10 +3624,16 @@ class SSDKernel:
       def tma_partition_for_mma_b_operand(
           self,
           tma_atom_x,
           tma_tensor_x,
           smem_x,
           tiled_mma_intra2,
           cluster_layout_vmnk,
           mma_tile_coord_v,
           block_in_cluster_coord_vmnk,
  +        tile=None,
       ):
           # Local_tile partition global tensors
           # (D, L, 1, 1, C, EH, B)
  +        # tile overrides the default intra2 tile (headdim, chunk_size); callers
  +        # that partition a B/C SSM operand (shape chunk_size × dstate) must pass
  +        # tile=self.tile_shape_mnk_intra1[1:] = (chunk_size, dstate) instead.
  +        tile_shape = self.tile_shape_mnk_intra2[1:] if tile is None else tile
           gX = cute.local_tile(
               tma_tensor_x,
  -            self.tile_shape_mnk_intra2[1:],  # mnk = (L, D, L)
  +            tile_shape,
               (None, None, None, None, None),
           )

  @@ -2967,6 +2967,7 @@ class SSDKernel:
           tBsB, tBgB_pre_slice = self.tma_partition_for_mma_b_operand(
               tma_atom_b,
               tma_tensor_b,
               smem_b,
               tiled_mma_intra1,
               cluster_layout_vmnk,
               mma_tile_coord_v,
               block_in_cluster_coord_vmnk,
  +            tile=self.tile_shape_mnk_intra1[1:],
           )
```

  Two changes:
  1. tma_partition_for_mma_b_operand — add tile=None parameter; replace the hardcoded self.tile_shape_mnk_intra2[1:] with tile_shape that respects the override.
  2. _warp_tma_b_c call site — pass tile=self.tile_shape_mnk_intra1[1:] so the B SSM operand (shape chunk_size × dstate) uses (chunk_size, dstate) instead of the wrong (headdim, chunk_size).

  The X call site in _warp_tma_x_deltas is unchanged — it passes no tile= argument, keeping the existing intra2[1:] = (headdim, chunk_size) which is correct for the X operand.

records.title: mm_fp4 NVFP4 returns erratic M-dependent zeros on SM120: both b12x and cutlass backends affected in FlashInfer 0.6.12
records.body:
### Summary

This may be related to #2577, but I am opening a separate issue because this is on FlashInfer 0.6.12 with the new `b12x` backend, and the failure is non-monotonic across M rather than a simple "all shapes fail" case.

On NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120, compute capability 12.0), `flashinfer.mm_fp4` returns all-zero outputs for specific M values. The pattern is erratic: M=1536/2048/4096 work, but M=3072 returns all zeros despite being between two working values.

Both `b12x` and `cutlass` show the same failure/work pattern in this M sweep, which suggests this may be a shared SM120 FP4 dispatch/tile-selection issue rather than a wrapper-only problem.

### Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition
- Compute capability: SM120 / CC 12.0
- Driver: 580.126.09
- CUDA toolkit: 12.8.93 system toolkit
- nvcc used for JIT: 13.2.78 from PyPI wheel `nvidia-cuda-nvcc==13.2.78`
- FlashInfer: 0.6.12
- PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130
- OS: Linux 6.6.122 x86_64

### JIT workaround used

The default environment could not JIT-compile the SM120 FP4 kernels cleanly. To get the kernel to compile and launch, I used the following local workarounds:

1. Installed `nvidia-cuda-nvcc==13.2.78` because nvcc 12.8 does not accept `compute_120f`.
2. Symlinked `nvidia/cu13/lib/*` into `nvidia/cu13/lib64/` so the JIT linker could find CUDA runtime libraries.
3. Patched `flashinfer/compilation_context.py` locally so the CUDA 12.8 path does not emit an unsupported `compute_120f` target.

After these workarounds, JIT compilation succeeds and the kernels launch without crashing. The issue is silent incorrect output: many shapes return all zeros.

### Reproduction

```python
import os
os.environ["FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK"] = "1"

import torch
from flashinfer import mm_fp4, nvfp4_quantize

print("flashinfer:", __import__("flashinfer").__version__)
print("GPU:", torch.cuda.get_device_name())
print("capability:", torch.cuda.get_device_capability())

K, N = 2048, 8192  # Gemma-style MLP up-projection shape
torch.manual_seed(42)

for M in [256, 384, 512, 1024, 1280, 1536, 2048, 3072, 4096]:
    a = torch.randn(M, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 5
    b = torch.randn(N, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 5

    a_scale = (448.0 * 6.0) / a.abs().max()
    b_scale = (448.0 * 6.0) / b.abs().max()

    # Use nvfp4_quantize defaults, matching the run that produced the output below.
    a_fp4, a_sf = nvfp4_quantize(a, a_scale)
    b_fp4, b_sf = nvfp4_quantize(b, b_scale)

    alpha = torch.tensor(
        1.0 / (a_scale.item() * b_scale.item()),
        device="cuda",
        dtype=torch.float32,
    )

    for backend in ["b12x", "cutlass"]:
        kwargs = {"backend": backend}
        if backend == "b12x":
            kwargs["use_nvfp4"] = True

        out = mm_fp4(
            a_fp4,
            b_fp4.T,
            a_sf,
            b_sf.T,
            alpha,
            torch.bfloat16,
            **kwargs,
        )
        torch.cuda.synchronize()

        zero = bool((out == 0).all().item())
        max_abs = float(out.abs().max().item())
        print(f"M={M:5d}  {backend:8s}  zero={zero}  max={max_abs:.1f}")
```

### Actual output

```text
M=  256  b12x      zero=True   max=0.0
M=  256  cutlass   zero=True   max=0.0
M=  384  b12x      zero=True   max=0.0
M=  384  cutlass   zero=True   max=0.0
M=  512  b12x      zero=True   max=0.0
M=  512  cutlass   zero=True   max=0.0
M= 1024  b12x      zero=True   max=0.0
M= 1024  cutlass   zero=True   max=0.0
M= 1280  b12x      zero=True   max=0.0
M= 1280  cutlass   zero=True   max=0.0
M= 1536  b12x      zero=False  max=264.0
M= 1536  cutlass   zero=False  max=264.0
M= 2048  b12x      zero=False  max=231.0
M= 2048  cutlass   zero=False  max=231.0
M= 3072  b12x      zero=True   max=0.0
M= 3072  cutlass   zero=True   max=0.0
M= 4096  b12x      zero=False  max=276.0
M= 4096  cutlass   zero=False  max=276.0
```

### Expected behavior

All tested M values should produce non-zero output close to the BF16 reference matmul. M=3072 should not fail while both M=2048 and M=4096 work.

### Why this matters

Autoregressive decode commonly runs at small M values:

- single-sequence decode: M=1
- batch decode: M=batch size, often 1-256
- chunked prefill: M depends on chunk and batch shape

With this behavior, SM120 deployments cannot safely use `mm_fp4` for NVFP4 decode or mixed prefill/decode workloads, because some otherwise normal M values silently produce zeros. This forces users on RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090-class SM120 GPUs to fall back to Marlin W4A16 paths instead of native FP4 Tensor Core GEMM.

### Secondary observation

For a working case such as M=4096, I also saw relatively high error compared to BF16 matmul in my quick local check. I am not treating this as the primary bug because the scale choice in this synthetic repro may not match production calibration. The main bug here is the all-zero output for specific M values.

### Possible root cause

This looks like a shape-dependent tile selection or dispatch issue in the SM120 FP4 path. The non-monotonic behavior is the key fingerprint:

- M=1536 works
- M=2048 works
- M=3072 returns all zeros
- M=4096 works

The fact that `b12x` and `cutlass` show the same pattern suggests either shared kernel code, shared layout assumptions, or a shared dispatch/tile selection problem.

Happy to provide additional K/N sweeps, more M values, or rerun this in a clean environment if useful.

### Summary

Failed Jobs: [unit_test_spark: [cu130]](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/325303974) | [unit_test_spark_colossus: [cu129]](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/325303974)

 tests/mamba/test_checkpointing_ssu.py::test_philox_rounding_unbiased fails on Spark, while the same test passes on other configurations.

  This test appears to have been introduced recently by PR #3324:
  - Commit: 194930ce26d07a7d9d558f29d98f0502baf9a22a
  - Title: checkpointing_ssu kernel: fused replay + conditional state-write for Mamba2 (#3324)
  - Date: 2026-05-19T09:47:01-07:00
  - File added: tests/mamba/test_checkpointing_ssu.py

### Failure:
```
  AssertionError: Stochastic rounding appears biased:
  stoch_mean=0.000053, determ_mean=-0.000001, n_elements=2096481
```
  The failing assertion is:
  assert abs(stoch_mean) < abs(determ_mean) or abs(stoch_mean) < 1e-5

### Suspected Root Cause (By Codex)
  This looks potentially over-strict/flaky for a statistical unbiasedness check: 
  - determ_mean is nearly zero, so the "less biased than deterministic" branch is almost impossible to satisfy.
  - the absolute 1e-5 threshold does not account for stochastic residual variance / standard error.
  - nearby int8/fp8/upstream-style unbiased tests use an SE-based check:
    abs(stochastic_mean) < K * stochastic_std / sqrt(N)

  Also, Spark may be using a different architecture path from GB300. Other Philox/cvt.rs tests in this file are gated on is_cvt_rs_supported(), but this specific test is not.

### Suggestion: （By Codex)
  Consider changing this test to an SE-based statistical check and/or gating it consistently with the other Philox/cvt.rs tests.

records.title: CuteDslMoEWrapper autotuner picks tactics ~10-25% slower than TRT-LLM equivalent at EP=16/32, small-mid N (B200)
records.body:
## Summary

  On B200 (SM100), `flashinfer.CuteDslMoEWrapper` autotune-selects tactics that produce **10-25% slower per-call timing** than `tensorrt_llm._torch.modules.fused_moe.CuteDslFusedMoE` at certain `(EP, N)` shapes, despite both running on the same
  underlying CuteDSL kernels. The gap is in autotune-time tactic selection, not in kernel implementation.

  Worst single-run delta observed: +33%. At affected shapes the bias is large enough to be production-relevant for DeepSeek-V3-class workloads.

  ## Empirical characterization

  **Setup**:
  - NGC `nvcr.io/nvidia/tensorrt-llm/release:1.3.0rc15` (cute-dsl 4.5.0, flashinfer-python 0.6.11.post1, TRT-LLM 1.3.0rc15)
  - B200, sm100, single GPU; both implementations imported in the same Python process
  - DeepSeek-V3 config: `hidden=7168, intermediate=2048, num_experts=256, top_k=8`
  - Swept `EP ∈ {1, 8, 16, 32}` × `N ∈ {1, 2, 4, ..., 16384}` (powers of 2); CUDA-graph mode

  **Findings**:

  | Regime | Pattern |
  |---|---|
  | EP=1, EP=8 | Mostly within ±2% |
  | EP=16 / EP=32, N ∈ [1, 2048] | fi slower by 10-25% mean; worst single-run +33% |
  | EP=16 / EP=32, N ≥ 4096 | fi-faster (work-per-kernel dominates) |

  ## High-confidence findings

  These three findings together strongly localize the problem to autotune-time tactic ranking:

  **1. Tactic-pick is the dominant driver.** Force-tactic ablation — when fi is forced to use TRT-LLM's autotune-selected tactic — closes **77-100% of the gap** at affected cells. The remaining same-tactic residual is ~0-4%, consistent with measurement noise.

  **2. The good tactic exists in fi's tactic space.** Cherry-picking each cell's best run across 10 runs: median `gemm1_swiglu` Δ% is **+0.47%** and `gemm2_finalize` Δ% is **+0.51%**. fi's autotuner can reach near-parity — it just doesn't pick reliably.

  **3. The picks are bimodal between two tactic families.** At affected cells, fi splits ~50/50 between the `tile_size=128` family (near-parity timing) and the `tile_size=256` family (~13-16% slower). The two families form clean modes — fi std% at affected cells is 5-10%; TRT-LLM std% at the same cells is 0.3-1.5%. TRT-LLM locks consistently on one family per cell; fi flaps. The mean Δ% between the two families is **+13.85pp**, which closely matches the observed cell-mean bias magnitudes.

  ## Mechanisms tested and ruled out

  | Mechanism | Outcome |
  |---|---|
  | Cold-L2 (`use_cold_l2_cache` flag) | Re-sweep with flag set matched baseline |
  | Surrounding-kernel measurement noise | Refuted (Spearman −0.491 between noise-to-tactic-gap ratio and \|Δ%\|) |
  | Tactic enumeration / candidate space | Identical 4 candidates in identical order on both sides |
  | `fork_rng` device context | No CUDA random ops in the relevant block |
  | `inputs_pre_hook` algorithm | Swapping to TRT-LLM block-fill regressed 3 cells |
  | TuningConfig `dynamic_tensor_specs` structural alignment | Shifted biases around, did not shrink problem area |
  | Joint vs sequential tactic-space exploration | Eliminated flap variance; did not close mean bias; 3 cells regressed |

  Each was tested via a sweep with the variation applied.

  ## Remaining untested candidate

  The largest structural difference between the two autotuners is at the runner level:

  - **flashinfer**: ONE composite `TunableRunner` (`CuteDslFusedMoENvfp4Runner`) profiling the whole MoE pipeline end-to-end (`input_fp4_quantize → moe_sort → gemm1+swiglu → memset → gemm2+finalize`); picks a composite tactic tuple `(tile_size,
  gemm1_subtactic, gemm2_subtactic)`.
  - **TRT-LLM**: THREE separate runners (`Sm100BlockScaledContiguousGatherGroupedGemmActFusionRunner` for gemm1, `Sm100BlockScaledContiguousGroupedGemmFinalizeFusionRunner` for gemm2, `CuteDslFusedMoENvfp4Runner` for tile_size) profiled
  **independently** with isolated per-kernel synthetic inputs.

  **Hypothesis (untested)**: per-kernel-isolated measurement on TRT-LLM's side ranks tactics differently than fi's composite-pipeline measurement does. The bias may be a consequence of measuring whole-pipeline timing when the relevant kernel-local cost is what determines the optimal tactic.

  Validating this would require refactoring fi's autotuner integration to split the composite runner into per-kernel runners with their own synthetic-input setup and `TuningConfig`.

records.title: [Perf] qo_len=2 (MTP / spec-decode draft=1) dispatches to prefill kernel instead of decode kernel, 10× slower than FA on H20
records.body: ## Summary When serving an internal LLM Model with vLLM on H20 (SM90) using MTP / speculative decoding with `num_speculative_tokens = 1` (so the verify step has `qo_len = 2`), FlashInfer's attention wrapper dispatches to `PrefillWithKVCacheKernel` rather than the decode kernel. End-to-end attention latency is ~10× higher than the FLASH_ATTN backend under identical shapes, which we believe is because the prefill kernel is not tuned for the `qo_len ≪ kv_len` regime that spec-decode verify produces. ### decode kernel latency(flashinfer backend vs flash_attn backend) Since FlashInfer has no decode-phase kernel for MTP with m=2, cases like num_speculative_tokens=1 (M=2) on H20 (SM90) fall back to the prefill FA3 kernel, which uses a fixed M-tile of CTA_Q=128 served by 2 consumer warpgroups (each computing a 64-row m64nNk16 WGMMA tile). With only 2 valid query rows, one consumer warpgroup operates entirely on padding while the other is barely 2/64 utilized, so most of the tensor-core throughput is wasted — which explains the large performance gap. ### Question & Solution Are there any solutions for this? Or do you plan to develop customized kernels for this kind of scenario?

records.title: [Bug]Regression: `backend="cute-dsl"` MLA decode via API rejects `page_size=128`
records.body:
## Summary

  `tests/attention/test_cute_dsl_mla_decode.py::test_cute_dsl_mla_decode_via_api  now fails for `page_size=128` with:

  ```
  ValueError: Supported block_size are 32 and 64, got 128
```

  This appears to be a regression introduced between:

  - good/base: 56d537a106024eb25f4d4a186eadc226990a9185
  - bad/head: c802a05d9806a3d8ec72014f9cec4d67da0d5e8e

  The likely culprit is:

  - 0b755de7060980b6ced02359aac6921aef5418d2
  - PR #3355: MLA Decode Autotuning Across TRTLLM-Gen and CuTe Backends

  ## Failing Tests

  Examples:

  FAILED tests/attention/test_cute_dsl_mla_decode.py::test_cute_dsl_mla_decode_via_api[monolithic-128-512-4]
  FAILED tests/attention/test_cute_dsl_mla_decode.py::test_cute_dsl_mla_decode_via_api[monolithic-128-512-128]
  FAILED tests/attention/test_cute_dsl_mla_decode.py::test_cute_dsl_mla_decode_via_api[monolithic-64-128-1]
  FAILED tests/attention/test_cute_dsl_mla_decode.py::test_cute_dsl_mla_decode_via_api[monolithic-64-512-128]


  ## Root Cause Hypothesis (By  Codex)

  PR #3355 refactored trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla to share dispatch and autotuning logic between trtllm-gen and cute-dsl.

  As part of that refactor, the following validation is now executed before backend-specific runner selection:
```
  block_size = kv_cache.size(-2)
  if block_size != 32 and block_size != 64:
      raise ValueError(f"Supported block_size are 32 and 64, got {block_size}")
```
  This check appears to be trtllm-gen specific. However, it now also runs for explicit backend="cute-dsl" calls.

  The failing test uses:

  backend="cute-dsl"
  page_size=128

  Before #3355, the explicit cute-dsl path directly called cute_dsl_mla_decode, so page_size=128 was not rejected by the trtllm-gen block-size guard.

  ## Expected Behavior

  For backend="cute-dsl", page_size=128 should be validated by the cute-dsl compatibility checks, not rejected by the trtllm-gen-only block_size in {32, 64} restriction.

  ## Actual Behavior

  The public MLA API rejects the call before reaching the cute-dsl backend:

  ValueError: Supported block_size are 32 and 64, got 128

  ## Suggested Fix  (By  Codex)

  Make the block-size restriction backend-specific:

  - Keep block_size in (32, 64) as a hard error for backend="trtllm-gen".
  - Do not apply that restriction to explicit backend="cute-dsl".
  - For backend="auto", exclude trtllm-gen from candidate runners when block_size is unsupported, but still allow cute-dsl if its own compatibility check passes.

  Pseudo-structure:

  trtllm_gen_reason = None
  if block_size not in (32, 64):
      trtllm_gen_reason = (
          f"trtllm-gen supports block_size 32 and 64, got {block_size}"
      )

  if backend == "trtllm-gen" and trtllm_gen_reason is not None:
      raise ValueError(trtllm_gen_reason)

  runner_names = []
  if backend in ("auto", "trtllm-gen") and trtllm_gen_reason is None:
      runner_names.append("trtllm-gen")
  if backend in ("auto", "cute-dsl") and cute_dsl_reason is None:
      runner_names.append("cute-dsl")

  ## Additional Test Coverage

  The existing backend="cute-dsl" test already catches the explicit-backend regression.

  It may also be useful to add coverage for:

  backend="auto"
  page_size=128

  Expected behavior: auto should skip trtllm-gen and dispatch to cute-dsl if cute-dsl supports the configuration.

records.title: FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE IMA on B200 with SGLang RL rollout, correlated with t128x8x128 + schPd2x1x2x3 BMM kernel at effbs=1024
records.body:
## Summary

We are enabling a Miles RL rollout backend to use SGLang with the FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE backend for Qwen3-30B-A3B on B200. The initial SGLang hot-update layout issue was addressed in [sgl-project/sglang#25692](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25692). After that fix, the run can start and produce sane rollout metrics, but we still intermittently hit a CUDA illegal memory access in the FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE path.

After several repro and profiling runs, the strongest signal we have is that the failure correlates with a specific BF16 BMM kernel family selected at larger effective rollout batch size.

Important caveat: this is only the pattern we observed, not proof that this kernel family is inherently broken. We are filing this to ask for help interpreting the coredump and narrowing down whether this is a FlashInfer kernel issue, an SGLang integration issue, or an invalid input/workspace contract issue.

## Environment

- GPU: B200 / SM100
- Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B`
- Workload: Miles RL rollout with SGLang
- SGLang MoE backend: FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE
- SGLang patch: [sgl-project/sglang#25692](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25692)
- `flashinfer-python`: `0.6.11.post1`
- `flashinfer-cubin`: `0.6.11.post1`
- `flashinfer-jit-cache`: `0.6.11.post1+cu129`
- `torch`: `2.11.0+cu129`
- `sglang`: `0.5.13.dev20+gd9a0158` plus the PR patch above
- `sglang-kernel`: `0.4.2.post2+cu129`

## Workload Shape

We tested with response length capped at 1024 to get a faster repro. This is intentionally a stability repro, not a reward-quality run.

The key sweep was:

- `BATCH_SIZE=32`, `N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT=8`, effective batch = 256, `SGLANG_CUDA_GRAPH_MAX_BS=256`
- `BATCH_SIZE=64`, `N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT=8`, effective batch = 512, `SGLANG_CUDA_GRAPH_MAX_BS=512`
- `BATCH_SIZE=128`, `N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT=8`, effective batch = 1024, `SGLANG_CUDA_GRAPH_MAX_BS=1024`

Common settings:

```bash
FAULT_TOLERANCE=disabled
STEPS=3000
SKIP_EVAL=1
ROLLOUT_MAX_RESPONSE_LEN=1024
WANDB_MODE=online
```

## Observed Pattern

All runs used FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE + the SGLang PR #25692 patch.

### effbs=256, maxbs=256, len1024 (GOOD)

- Clean in the observed window.
- Profiler saw `schPd2x1x2x3` variants, but not the suspicious `t128x8x128 + schPd2x1x2x3` combo.

### effbs=512, maxbs=512, len1024 (GOOD)

- Profile collected; no conclusive IMA in that profile window.
- Profiler saw `t128x8x128` variants, but they were `schedS` variants, not `schPd2x1x2x3`.

### effbs=1024, maxbs=1024, len1024 (BAD!!)

- Reproduced CUDA illegal memory access.
- Lightweight CUDA coredump points to this BF16 BMM kernel family:

```text
bmm_Bfloat16_Bfloat16Bfloat16_Fp32_t128x8x128_s4_et128x8_m128x8x16_c1x1x1_16dp256b_rM_BN_transOut_schPd2x1x2x3_bN_rgTma_clmp_dynB_sm100f
```

Another rank/device saw:

```text
bmm_Bfloat16_Bfloat16Bfloat16_Fp32_t128x8x128_s5_et128x8_m128x8x16_c1x1x1_16dp256b_rM_BN_transOut_schPd2x1x2x3_bN_rgTma_clmp_dynB_sm100f
```

Both were launched as:

```text
<<<(16,32,1),(256,1,1)>>>
```

So the pattern we see is:

- `effbs=256`: no `t128x8x128 + schPd2x1x2x3` (GOOD)
- `effbs=512`: `t128x8x128` appears, but as `schedS` (GOOD)
- `effbs=1024`: IMA, and coredump lands on `t128x8x128 + schPd2x1x2x3` (BAD!!)

Again, this is a correlation from our runs, not proof that this kernel name is the root cause.

## Coredump Details

The coredump was generated with lightweight CUDA coredump enabled. The run reached rollout 2, then the SGLang workers became unavailable and the router returned `503 no_available_workers`.

The coredump decoded with `cuda-gdb target cudacore` shows:

```text
warning: Encountered unhandled device exception (30)
CUDA Exception: Device Unknown Exception
```

For one dump:

```text
[Current focus set to CUDA kernel 0, grid 2320505, cluster (13,7,0), block (13,7,0), thread (192,0,0), device 4, sm 0, warp 6, lane 0]

#0  0x0000787e6ff09cf0 in bmm_Bfloat16_Bfloat16Bfloat16_Fp32_t128x8x128_s4_et128x8_m128x8x16_c1x1x1_16dp256b_rM_BN_transOut_schPd2x1x2x3_bN_rgTma_clmp_dynB_sm100f<<<(16,32,1),(256,1,1)>>> ()

errorpc 0x787e6ff09b20 <...+14880>
```

For another dump:

```text
[Current focus set to CUDA kernel 0, grid 2320505, cluster (5,7,0), block (5,7,0), thread (192,0,0), device 5, sm 18, warp 7, lane 0]

#0  0x00007c1dcff04970 in bmm_Bfloat16_Bfloat16Bfloat16_Fp32_t128x8x128_s5_et128x8_m128x8x16_c1x1x1_16dp256b_rM_BN_transOut_schPd2x1x2x3_bN_rgTma_clmp_dynB_sm100f<<<(16,32,1),(256,1,1)>>> ()

errorpc 0x7c1dcff047a0 <...+15008>
```

There was also an active finalize kernel:

```text
moe::dev::finalize::finalizeKernel<moe::dev::finalize::KernelParams<cutlass::bfloat16_t, cutlass::bfloat16_t, 4, true> >
```

## Things We Tried / Ruled Down

- The original SGLang hot-update packed/canonical layout issue is fixed by [sgl-project/sglang#25692](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25692).
- Triton MoE backend works for the same broad workload, so the issue appears specific to FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE or its integration path.
- We tried several sync/profiling/coredump variants. The visible Python-side failure location can move because CUDA errors surface asynchronously, but coredump consistently gives us the BF16 BMM kernel family above.
- Pure shape mismatch was the first bug we fixed; this remaining issue happens after that fix.

## What We Need Help With

Could you help us interpret whether this points to:

1. A FlashInfer TRTLLM BF16 MoE kernel bug for the `t128x8x128 + schPd2x1x2x3 + BN_transOut` family on SM100.
2. An input/workspace contract issue in the SGLang FlashInfer integration, e.g. invalid routing/topk/workspace/packed-weight assumptions that only surface in this kernel variant.
3. A CUDA graph or workspace lifetime issue. Some runs use cuda graph, but the coredump points into the FlashInfer BMM kernel rather than Python-side graph replay machinery.

If there is a recommended way to collect more useful debug info, e.g. a FlashInfer-specific trace, kernel argument dump, or a way to decode which input pointer/workspace address caused the MMU/device exception, we can rerun with that instrumentation.

## Artifacts

We have lightweight CUDA coredumps and decoded `cuda-gdb target cudacore` text available and can share them privately if useful. The artifact set contains:

```text
umbriel-b200-077.19283.1779946774.nvcudmp
umbriel-b200-077.19283.1779946774.target-cudacore.txt
umbriel-b200-077.19284.1779946773.nvcudmp
umbriel-b200-077.19284.1779946773.target-cudacore.txt
driver.log
output.log
```
