records.title: import flashinfer.comm fails at import time when a co-loaded library matches "libcudart" (e.g. tilelang libcudart_stub.so) — find_loaded_library picks the non-runtime lib
records.body:
## Summary

`import flashinfer.comm` can fail at **import time** with `AttributeError: undefined symbol: cudaDeviceReset` when another package legitimately loaded in the same process provides a shared object whose filename contains `libcudart` but which is **not** the full CUDA runtime.

At import, `flashinfer/comm/cuda_ipc.py` constructs a module-level `CudaRTLibrary()` (line 194). With no explicit path, `CudaRTLibrary.__init__` calls `find_loaded_library("libcudart")`, which returns the **first** `/proc/self/maps` line containing the substring `libcudart`. Because `/proc/self/maps` is address-sorted, that's whichever `libcudart`-named mapping has the lowest base address — which is not necessarily the real CUDA runtime. If the selected library doesn't export `cudaDeviceReset`, `__init__` raises.

A concrete trigger is [`tilelang`](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang), which ships and loads `tilelang/lib/libcudart_stub.so` (a cudart shim that does not export `cudaDeviceReset`). `tilelang` and `flashinfer-python` are independent packages; both end up in the same process when a downstream framework (e.g. vLLM) imports both. This is legitimate usage — the user has no way to know one library's presence will break another's import.

## Minimal reproduction (arch-independent; verified on H100)

No special model/kernels needed — just three imports in a fresh process:

```bash
# flashinfer-python==0.6.12, tilelang==0.1.9, torch==2.11.0+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), Python 3.12
python3 -c "import torch; import tilelang; import flashinfer.comm"
```

Result:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File ".../flashinfer/comm/__init__.py", line 1, in <module>
    from .cuda_ipc import CudaRTLibrary, create_shared_buffer, free_shared_buffer
  File ".../flashinfer/comm/cuda_ipc.py", line 194, in <module>
    cudart = CudaRTLibrary()
  File ".../flashinfer/comm/cuda_ipc.py", line 134, in __init__
    f = getattr(self.lib, func.name)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.12/ctypes/__init__.py", line 392, in __getattr__
    func = self.__getitem__(name)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.12/ctypes/__init__.py", line 397, in __getitem__
    func = self._FuncPtr((name_or_ordinal, self))
AttributeError: .../tilelang/lib/libcudart_stub.so: undefined symbol: cudaDeviceReset
```

The failure is load-order dependent: it occurs when the non-runtime `libcudart`-named library maps at a lower address than the real `libcudart.so.13` (the case in a single process that imports `tilelang` before `flashinfer.comm`).

## Workaround (no code change)

Preloading the real CUDA runtime so it is the first `libcudart` match resolves it:

```bash
LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/cuda-13.0/lib64/libcudart.so.13 \
  python3 -c "import torch; import tilelang; import flashinfer.comm"   # imports cleanly
```

Verified on the same H100 environment.

## Suggested robustness improvement

Make `libcudart` resolution robust to other libraries that happen to share the name, so co-loading a `libcudart`-named shim doesn't break the import. Options:

- In `find_loaded_library` (or before accepting its result), select the `libcudart` mapping that actually provides the runtime API rather than the first substring match — e.g. skip candidates that don't resolve the symbols `CudaRTLibrary` needs (`cudaDeviceReset`, etc.), continuing the scan to the real runtime.
- Optionally prefer/allow an explicit `so_file` for the module-level `CudaRTLibrary()` (the constructor already accepts `so_file`), as vLLM's analogous `CudaRTLibrary` in `cuda_wrapper.py` does.

## Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| flashinfer-python | 0.6.12 |
| tilelang | 0.1.9 |
| torch | 2.11.0+cu130 |
| CUDA | 13.0 |
| Python | 3.12 |
| GPU | NVIDIA H100 (reproduces on any CUDA GPU; this is a host-side library-resolution issue, not arch-specific) |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 |

records.title: [Feature] b12x NVFP4 MoE can't serve Gemma-4 MoE on SM120/121: missing gelu_tanh activation + non-128-multiple intermediate_size (704)
records.body:
### Summary

The `blackwell_sm12x` (b12x) NVFP4 fused-MoE kernels cannot serve **Gemma-4 MoE** models
(`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`, `google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it`) on consumer/SoC Blackwell
(SM120 / SM121), for two independent reasons. The first I have a patch for; the second needs
the kernel owners. This is the last gap keeping native nvfp4-weight Gemma MoE off the DGX Spark.

Gemma-4 MoE config (relevant fields):
```
moe_intermediate_size = 704        # 128 * 5.5  -> NOT a multiple of 128
num_experts = 128, top_k = 8
hidden_activation = gelu_pytorch_tanh   # -> "gelu_tanh", gated (like SiLU/SwiGLU)
```

### Gap 1 — missing `gelu_tanh` activation (have a fix, happy to PR)

The micro-kernel supports only `silu` and `relu2`:
```python
# flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell_sm12x/moe_direct_micro_kernel.py
if activation not in {"silu", "relu2"}:
    raise ValueError(f"unsupported activation {activation!r}")
```
Gemma uses gated `gelu_tanh` (`gelu_pytorch_tanh(gate) * up`), so `flashinfer_b12x` rejects it
(`does not support MoEActivation.GELU_TANH`) and vLLM falls back to MARLIN (which emits null output
on SM121, cf. vllm#37030).

This mirrors the existing `relu2` addition (#3080) and is small. A working patch (validated *past
the activation gate* on a GB10 / SM121, CUDA 13):
- `moe_direct_micro_kernel.py`: accept `gelu_tanh`; `is_gated = activation in ("silu","gelu_tanh")`;
  add the math branch alongside silu at the activation site (~L2148):
  `g = 0.5*x*(1 + cute.math.tanh(0.7978845608*(x + 0.044715*x^3))); activated = g * up`
- `moe_w4a16_host.py`: add `"gelu_tanh"` to `_SUPPORTED_ACTIVATIONS`; `validate_activation` returns
  gated=True for it.
- `moe_dispatch.py`: the 4 `is_gated = activation == "silu"` sites -> include `"gelu_tanh"`.

I'm glad to open this as a PR if useful.

### Gap 2 — `intermediate_size` must be a multiple of 128 (needs the kernel owners)

```python
# moe_dispatch.py:398 (_get_weight_views)
if n % tile_n != 0:   # tile_n = 128
    raise ValueError(
        f"intermediate_size ({n}) must be a multiple of {tile_n} "
        f"for the SM120 MoE kernel's gate/up tile split.")
```
Gemma's `moe_intermediate_size = 704` is `128 * 5.5`. The 128-multiple assumption is baked through
the kernel — the gate/up tile-index split (above), `n % fc1_chunks` (`moe_direct_micro_kernel.py:480`),
and the 128-wide scale-factor swizzle blocks (`fc1_chunks_per_block = 16`). Serving Gemma MoE natively
needs the kernel to handle a non-128-multiple `n` (a **predicated final partial tile** across the TMA
descriptors, the MMA loop, the activation pairing, and the FP4 scale-factor layout) — i.e. split
gate/up into separate tile groups, each `ceil(n/128)` tiles with the last masked to `n % 128` rows.

This is the kind of generalization best done by the b12x kernel maintainers (it touches the core
tiling). Filing it here so it's tracked. (As an exact stop-gap on the serving side, zero-padding the
expert intermediate `704 -> 768` at weight-load is numerically identical — `act(0)*0 = 0` — at ~9%
extra FFN compute; that's what I'm using to serve today, but native non-128-multiple support is the
right fix.)

### Environment / repro

- GPU: NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), SM121, CUDA 13.0; also reproduces on SM120 (kernel is `blackwell_sm12x`).
- Reproduce: serve `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` (NVFP4 weights) via vLLM with the b12x MoE backend
  (`moe_backend=flashinfer_b12x`). Gap 1 raises the activation error; with gelu_tanh patched, Gap 2
  raises `intermediate_size (704) must be a multiple of 128`.

Related active b12x work: #3066, #3080, #3271, #3336 (W4A16), #3645 (per-token NVFP4), #3463 (MXFP8 grouped MoE).

records.title: Security Advisory: Self-Hosted Runner Risk (Skor: 20/100)
records.body:
## Security Advisory: Self-Hosted Runner Risk Tespit Edildi

Merhaba,

Bu repo'da **self-hosted GitHub Actions runner** kullanildigi ve **riskli trigger'larin** bulundugu tespit edilmistir.

### Tespit Edilen Sorunlar
- **Risk Skoru:** 20/100
- **Trigger'lar:** 4 workflow'da self-hosted runner var
- **Workflow'lar (4 adet):**
  - `nightly-release.yml`
  - `pr-test.yml`
  - `release-ci-docker.yml`
  - `release.yml`

### Oneriler
1. **Self-hosted runner** kullaniyorsaniz, runner'in guvenlik yamalarinin guncel oldugundan emin olun.
2. **Riskli trigger'lar** (`pull_request_target`, `issue_comment`, `workflow_run`, `repository_dispatch`) kullaniyorsaniz, ek guvenlik onlemleri alin:
   - `pull_request_target` icin: base branch'i checkout ederken PR koduyla calismayin
   - `issue_comment` icin: sadece yetkili kullanicilarin trigger'layabildiginden emin olun
   - `workflow_run` icin: calisma ortamini kistlayin
3. Runner erisimini **sadece guvenilir workflow'larla** sinirlandirin.
4. Runner'in ag erisimini kistlayin.
5. **Token'larinizi** sifreli sekilde (GitHub Secrets) saklayin.

Detayli dokuman: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions

---

*Bu mesaj, guvenlik amaciyla otomatik olarak gonderilmistir. Herkesin bilgisayari guvende olsun.*

records.title: [Bug] SM100 GDN prefill deadlock with non-null initial_state and long-tail varlen cu_seqlens
records.body:
## Problem

  `flashinfer.gdn_prefill.chunk_gated_delta_rule` can hang on Blackwell SM100+ for a long-tail varlen batch when `initial_state` is not `None`.

  The same input shape runs successfully when `initial_state=None`. The hang is also reproduced when `initial_state` is all zeros, so it does not seem to depend on non-zero state values. It appears tied to the SM100 GDN prefill path with a non-
  null initial state.

  ## Environment

  - GPU: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC
  - Driver: 580.82.07
  - CUDA: 13.0
  - Python: 3.12
  - PyTorch: 2.9.1+cu130
  - FlashInfer: 0.6.12、0.6.13rc2
  - API: `flashinfer.gdn_prefill.chunk_gated_delta_rule`

  ## Minimal Reproducer

  Run with:

  ```bash
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6 timeout -k 10s 90s python3 repro_gdn_prefill_hang.py --mode none
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6 timeout -k 10s 90s python3 repro_gdn_prefill_hang.py --mode zero
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6 timeout -k 10s 90s python3 repro_gdn_prefill_hang.py --mode random
  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=6 timeout -k 10s 90s python3 repro_gdn_prefill_hang.py --mode random-fp32
```
  Script:
```
  import argparse
  import os
  import time
  import torch

  os.environ.setdefault("FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK", "1")
  from flashinfer.gdn_prefill import chunk_gated_delta_rule

  def run(mode):
      torch.manual_seed(0)
      device = "cuda"

      lengths = [5994, 643, 642, 642, 642]
      total = sum(lengths)
      batch = len(lengths)
      h_qk, h_v, d = 8, 32, 128

      cu = [0]
      for x in lengths:
          cu.append(cu[-1] + x)
      cu_seqlens = torch.tensor(cu, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)

      q = torch.randn(total, h_qk, d, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      k = torch.randn(total, h_qk, d, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      v = torch.randn(total, h_v, d, device=device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      q = torch.nn.functional.normalize(q.float(), dim=-1).to(torch.bfloat16).contiguous()
      k = torch.nn.functional.normalize(k.float(), dim=-1).to(torch.bfloat16).contiguous()
      v = v.contiguous()

      g_log = torch.empty(total, h_v, device=device, dtype=torch.float32).uniform_(-0.08, 0.02)
      g = torch.exp(g_log).contiguous()
      beta = torch.rand(total, h_v, device=device, dtype=torch.float32).contiguous()

      state_shape = (batch, h_v, d, d)
      state_dtype = torch.float32 if mode == "random-fp32" else torch.bfloat16

      if mode == "none":
          initial_state = None
      elif mode == "zero":
          initial_state = torch.zeros(state_shape, device=device, dtype=state_dtype)
      else:
          initial_state = torch.randn(state_shape, device=device, dtype=state_dtype).contiguous()

      output_state = torch.empty(state_shape, device=device, dtype=state_dtype)

      print(f"mode={mode}, lengths={lengths}, initial_state={initial_state is not None}", flush=True)

      for i in range(10):
          t0 = time.perf_counter()
          out, st = chunk_gated_delta_rule(
              q=q,
              k=k,
              v=v,
              g=g,
              beta=beta,
              scale=None,
              initial_state=initial_state,
              output_final_state=True,
              output_state=output_state,
              cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
              use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=False,
          )
          torch.cuda.synchronize()
          print(f"iter={i+1}, ms={(time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000:.3f}", flush=True)

  if __name__ == "__main__":
      p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
      p.add_argument("--mode", choices=["none", "zero", "random", "random-fp32"], required=True)
      run(p.parse_args().mode)
```
  ## Observed Results

  ### initial_state=None

  This completes successfully:

  mode=none
  iter=1, ms=11297.355
  iter=2, ms=0.874
  iter=3, ms=0.323
  ...
  iter=10, ms=0.298
  exit_code=0

  ### initial_state=random bf16

  This hangs and times out:

  mode=random
  iter=1, ms=11938.687
  exit_code=124

  ### initial_state=random fp32

  This also hangs:

  mode=random-fp32
  iter=1, ms=12203.343
  iter=2, ms=0.998
  exit_code=124

  ### initial_state=zeros bf16

  This also hangs, even though zero initial state should be semantically close to initial_state=None:

  mode=zero
  iter=1, ms=12140.554
  iter=2, ms=0.997
  iter=3, ms=0.331
  ...
  iter=7, ms=0.303
  exit_code=124

  ## Control Cases

  Balanced varlen cases with similar total lengths did not reproduce the hang:

  total=8563, batch=5, lengths=[1713,1713,1713,1712,1712] -> OK
  total=12787, batch=5, balanced -> OK
  total=32553, batch=10, balanced -> OK

  The issue seems sensitive to long-tail cu_seqlens, e.g. [0, 5994, 6637, 7279, 7921, 8563].

  ## Expected Behavior

  The kernel should complete for long-tail varlen batches with a non-null initial_state, including all-zero initial state.

  At minimum, all-zero initial_state should behave consistently with initial_state=None.

  ## Current Workaround

  For batches where all prefix lengths are zero, passing initial_state=None avoids the hang.

  This is not a complete workaround for real prefix-cache hits, because those require a valid non-null initial state.

records.title: RFC: Adopt a Standard MegaMoE Kernel Integration API
records.body:
# MegaMoE Kernel Integration API

## Motivation

As we add MegaMoE support to FlashInfer, we need a standard interface between FlashInfer and MegaMoE kernels. Without one, each backend integrated into `moe_ep` would need to define its own preprocessing, workspace management, and kernel invocation interfaces.

We propose introducing a standardized **MegaMoE Kernel Integration API**.

## FlashInfer MegaMoE API

```
FlashInfer MoE EP Layer [Python]
           |
FlashInfer MegaMoE API [Python]
           |
MegaMoE Kernel Integration API [Python]
           |
       Mega Kernel [CUDA/CuteDSL/...]
```

## Design

A MegaMoE implementation consists of three components:

### 1. Data Preparation Utilities

- During initialization, there are functions that transform weights into formats required by the kernel. 
- During forward(), input tokens are quantized (typically from bf16) and placed into symm_buffer. It is recommended to fuse them into a single kernel (see [example](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a341fa109e569c8d265545adfca756f42451244/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/model.py#L529)).

### 2. Scratch Space (`symm_buffer`)

A symm_buff workspace containing prepared inputs and storage for intermediate kernel results.

### 3. Kernel Interface

The kernel operates on preprocessed inputs:

```python
mega_kernel(
    output_tensor,
    l1_weight,
    l2_weight,
    symm_buffer,
)
```

The integration API owns preprocessing and workspace management; the kernel focuses solely on computation.

## Example: DeepGEMM SM100 MegaMoE

DeepGEMM's SM100 MegaMoE implementation already follows this structure:

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `per_token_cast_to_fp8` | Activation quantization |
| `per_token_cast_to_fp4` | Weight quantization |
| `transform_sf_into_required_layout` | Scale tensor layout transformation |
| `get_symm_buffer_for_mega_moe` | Scratch-space allocation |
| `transform_weights_for_mega_moe` | Weight layout transformation |
| `fp8_fp4_mega_moe` | MegaMoE kernel |
| `_stage_mega_moe_inputs`* | quant+place input tokens into symm_buff |

*not a deepseek API, but needed for performance (see [example](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/7a341fa109e569c8d265545adfca756f42451244/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/model.py#L529)).

## Proposal

Adopt the existing DeepGEMM MegaMoE integration pattern as the standard **MegaMoE Kernel Integration API** for integrating new MegaMoE kernels into FlashInfer.

records.title: [Feature] Performant Blockwise 128x128 FP8 MoE Group Gemms for SM10x GPUs
records.body:
[Feature] Performant Blockwise 128x128 FP8 MoE Group Gemms for SM10x GPUs

Currently, SGLang is using DeepGemm kernels for Blockwise 128x128 FP8 MoE Group Gemms for SM10x GPUs, but the simulation shows that the kernels only achieve ~50% of the projection, and even just 30-50% in the Prefill phase (in 8k1k TP mapping).

The request is to have new Blockwise 128x128 FP8 MoE Group Gemms (or MoE) implementations that can push the performance to 80% of the projection.

Expected perf gain is: +14% for Ctx iter perf and +5% e2e perf for Qwen 3.5 on SM10x GPUs for TP setting.

My current guess is that DeepGemm kernels are more optimized for EP (and wideEP) settings but less optimized for TP settings. But ideally we want an implementation that is not slower than DeepGemm kernels for EP/wideEP setting, while being faster than DeepGemm kernels for TP setting.

The desired backend is cute-dsl, but it is also okay if this must be implemented with trtllm-gen backend.

records.title: [Bug] CuteDSL paged decode with `is_causal=False` uses padding KV lanes
records.body:
## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA B200, `sm_100`
- FlashInfer: `0.6.13rc2` and current `main` (`015f5973`)
- PyTorch: `2.9.1+cu128`
- CUDA driver: 580.126.09

## Description

`BatchDecodePagedCuteDSLWrapper` gives wrong output when `is_causal=False` and `seq_len` is not aligned to the 256-token sequence tile.
The non-causal path skips the boundary mask pass. KV lanes after `seq_len` remain in the score tile and enter the softmax denominator. With `q = 0`, attention should be uniform over valid KV tokens only, but the output is scaled as if padding lanes were valid.
The causal path is correct.

## Minimal Repro

```python
import torch
from flashinfer.cute_dsl.attention import BatchDecodePagedCuteDSLWrapper

D, page, H = 128, 16, 8
dev = torch.device("cuda")
dt = torch.bfloat16


def check(seq_len, is_causal):
    npages = (seq_len + page - 1) // page
    indptr = torch.tensor([0, npages], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    indices = torch.arange(npages, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    seq_lens = torch.tensor([seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)

    torch.manual_seed(1)
    k_cache = torch.randn(npages, page, H, D, device=dev, dtype=dt) * 0.1
    v_cache = torch.randn(npages, page, H, D, device=dev, dtype=dt) * 0.1
    q = torch.zeros(1, H, D, device=dev, dtype=dt)
    ref = v_cache.reshape(-1, H, D)[:seq_len].float().mean(0)

    wrapper = BatchDecodePagedCuteDSLWrapper(
        torch.empty(512 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev)
    )
    wrapper.plan(
        indptr,
        indices,
        seq_lens,
        num_qo_heads=H,
        num_kv_heads=H,
        head_dim=D,
        page_size=page,
        q_data_type=dt,
        kv_data_type=dt,
        sm_scale=1.0 / (D**0.5),
        reduction="none",
        kv_splits=1,
        q_len_per_req=1,
        is_causal=is_causal,
        max_kv_len=seq_len,
    )
    out = wrapper.run(q, k_cache, v_cache).reshape(H, D).float()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    ratio = (ref.abs().mean() / (out.abs().mean() + 1e-12)).item()
    max_abs = (out - ref).abs().max().item()
    print(is_causal, seq_len, ratio, max_abs)


for s in (16, 64, 128, 240, 256, 257, 512):
    check(s, is_causal=False)
for s in (16, 64, 128, 240, 256, 257, 512):
    check(s, is_causal=True)
```

## Observed

Before the fix:

```text
is_causal=False seq_len=  16  ref/out=16.000  max_abs=8.61e-02
is_causal=False seq_len=  64  ref/out= 4.000  max_abs=3.89e-02
is_causal=False seq_len= 128  ref/out= 2.000  max_abs=1.63e-02
is_causal=False seq_len= 240  ref/out= 1.067  max_abs=1.33e-03
is_causal=False seq_len= 256  ref/out= 1.000  max_abs=6.02e-05
is_causal=False seq_len= 257  ref/out= 1.940  max_abs=1.09e-02
is_causal=True  all tested seq_len values: ref/out=1.000
```

## Expected

`is_causal=False` should mask KV lanes where `key_pos >= seq_len`. All tested sequence lengths should have `ref/out` close to 1.0.

records.title: GLM-5.2: A Very Difficult to Reproduce Operator Anomaly
records.body:
# `fp4_quantize` returns scale tensors with potentially insufficient padding for downstream CUTLASS SwiGLU GEMM on B200

## Summary

When `fp4_quantize` is called with `is_sf_swizzled_layout=True` (the default), the returned scale factor tensor has padding aligned to 128 rows and 64 columns. However, the downstream flashinfer-cubin `bmm_E2m1_...swiGlu_dynB_sm100f` kernel (launched by sglang's `nvfp4_gemm_swiglu_nvfp4_quant`) requires the scale factor buffer to be padded to **`_round_up(M, 128)` rows and `_round_up(N_out // sf_vec_size, 4)` columns** in the swizzled layout. If the actual M dimension causes the tile coordinate to exceed the padded scale buffer, the TMA descriptor computes an out-of-bounds address, triggering a **Warp Illegal Address / MMU Fault (Xid 13)**.

## Environment

- **GPU**: NVIDIA B200 (SM100, 148 SMs)
- **CUDA**: 13.0
- **flashinfer**: 0.6.12
- **PyTorch**: 2.11.0+cu130
- **Model**: GLM-5.2-NVFP4 (`modelopt_fp4` quantization, NVFP4 block-scaled format, TP=8)
- **Downstream kernel**: CUTLASS DSL JIT `Sm100BlockScaledPersistentDenseGemmKernel` with SwiGLU fusion and TMA+LDGSTS loading

## Observed Behavior

During prefill with large M (e.g., 16K new tokens + 103K cached tokens), the kernel crashes:

```
dmesg:
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:70:00): 13, Graphics SM Warp Exception on (GPC 1, TPC 1, SM 1): MMU Fault
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:70:00): 13, Graphics Exception: ESR 0x5167b0=0x80f0017 0x5167b4=0x20 0x5167a8=0x1f81fb60 0x5167ac=0x1174

CUDA coredump:
CUDA Exception: Warp Illegal Address
The exception was triggered at PC 0x78605d165d30
  bmm_E2m1_E2m1E2m1_Fp32_..._swiGlu_dynB_sm100f<<<(4,16,1),(512,1,1)>>>
```

4 SMs across different GPCs report **identical fault virtual addresses** (`0x1f81fb60` / `0x1174`), confirming the same tile coordinate computes the same out-of-bounds TMA address.

## Reproduction

The crash occurs in production traffic with GLM-5.2-NVFP4. A minimal script with random weights and various M values (1 to 65536) does **not** reproduce the crash, suggesting the bug is input-data dependent — specific weight scale values combined with certain M dimensions cause the TMA address to exceed the allocated scale buffer bounds.

Call path:
```
sglang deepseek_v2._forward_shared_experts
  → FusedLinearMethod.forward
    → fp4_quantize()                    ← flashinfer (produces scale tensor)
    → nvfp4_gemm_swiglu_nvfp4_quant()   ← sglang 
      → bmm_E2m1_...swiGlu_dynB_sm100f  ← CRASH: TMA out-of-bounds
```

## Maybe Cause Analysis

The `_pad_scale_factors` function in `flashinfer/fp4_quantization.py` pads scale factors as:

```python
def _pad_scale_factors(unswizzled_sf, m, n, sf_vec_size=16):
    factor = sf_vec_size * 4  # = 64
    padded_row = ((m + 128 - 1) // 128) * 128
    padded_col = ((n + factor - 1) // factor) * factor  # Next multiple of 64
    ...
```

This produces a scale tensor of shape `[padded_row, padded_col // sf_vec_size]` in unswizzled layout.

After swizzling (`nvfp4_block_scale_interleave`), the layout is transformed. The downstream CUTLASS kernel then reads this swizzled scale tensor via TMA, using tile coordinates computed from the actual M/N of the GEMM problem. If the kernel's tile scheduler visits a tile whose scale coordinate falls outside the padded buffer (e.g., when `padded_col // sf_vec_size` is not a multiple of 4 after swizzling, or when M rounds up differently than expected), the TMA load hits an unmapped page → MMU Fault.

The key mismatch is:
1. `fp4_quantize` pads based on the **unswizzled** dimensions
2. The CUTLASS kernel expects the **swizzled** scale tensor to be padded to alignment requirements that may differ after the swizzle transform


## Related

- This issue is exposed by flashinfer's `nvfp4_gemm_swiglu_nvfp4_quant` , but the root cause is in the scale factor padding produced by `fp4_quantize`.
- The same kernel (`bmm_E2m1_...swiGlu_dynB_sm100f`) has crashed on two separate dates (2026-06-15 and 2026-06-24) with different request patterns, confirming it is a systematic alignment issue rather than a transient hardware fault.

# CUDA Coredump Analysis Report — cluster09-two-1 collective crash

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Pod** | `kis-qy-glm52-l3cache-nopd-cluster09-two-1` (namespace `kaic-kis`) |
| **Node** | `36.0.4.142` (hostNetwork; pod IP = node IP) |
| **Coredump dir** | `/tmp/crashdump/` |
| **Crash window** | 2026-07-06 20:40:31 ~ 20:41:07 CST (UTC+8) |
| **Corresponding pkl** | `/tmp/crashdump/36-0-4-142/crash_dump_2026-07-06_20-40-57.pkl` (12.8 MB) |
| **Analyzer** | in-pod `cuda-gdb` (CUDA 13.0, `/usr/local/cuda/bin/cuda-gdb`) |
| **Generated** | 2026-07-06 CST |

---

Similar issues occurred on B300, all pointing to this kernel

## TL;DR — root cause

**The actual fault is on GPU 3 (PCI 73:00.0), in the MoE expert FFN kernel
`bmm_E2m1_E2m1E2m1_Fp32_…_sm100f` — a 1.58-bit (E2M1 microscaling) batched matmul
with fused swiGLU and dynamic expert batching.** It raised **Warp Illegal Address**
on a **TMA-descriptor bulk load** (`LDG.E R5,desc[UR10][R14]`) at SM 49 / warp 8 / lane 0.

The other three coredumps (`.148/.149/.150`) are **collateral**, not independent
faults: their kernel — `flashinfer::trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce::oneshotAllreduceFusionKernel`
(the oneshot NVLink-C2C allreduce) — was **blocked in its flag-polling sync barrier**
(`errorpc = <unavailable>`, spinning on the `0x80000000` peer sentinel) waiting for
GPU 3, whose context had just died. They were dumped during teardown.

So: **one faulting GPU + one faulting kernel → 4 coredumps** (1 real + 3 collateral).

---

## 1. GPU device information

Node has **8 × NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC**, compute capability **sm_103 (CC 10.3)**, chip
`GB110GL-B`, 148 SMs each.

| GPU idx | PCI Bus:Dev | UUID (prefix) | role in this pod |
|--------:|:-----------|:--------------|:-----------------|
| 0 | 1a:00.0 | GPU-36dce934… | rank0 — allreduce (collateral) `.148` |
| 1 | 40:00.0 | GPU-4c2bfe6f… | rank1 — allreduce (collateral) `.149` |
| 2 | 62:00.0 | GPU-6d0efb14… | rank2 — allreduce (collateral) `.150` |
| **3** | **73:00.0** | **GPU-d4e78e52…** | **rank3 — bmm FAULT `.151` ⚠️** |
| 4–7 | 9a / bd / df / f0:00.0 | … | other pod/replica on the shared node |

Coredumps embed both `-arch sm_100` and `-arch sm_103` cubins → match the hardware
(the bmm kernel runs its `sm100f` cubin, forward-compatible on sm_103).

This pod uses **GPUs 0–3** (4 TP workers, ranks 0–3); the coredump suffixes
`.148/.149/.150/.151` are the worker host-PIDs, sharing timestamp `1783333733`
(the moment the 4 CUDA contexts were created at worker startup ≈ 18:28 CST, i.e.
the workers ran ~2h12m before crashing).

---

## 2. The four coredumps — fault vs. collateral

| Coredump | Written (CST) | GPU (dev/PCI) | Kernel | Exception | `errorpc` | SM/warp/lane | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.151` | **20:40:31.513** | **3 / 73:00.0** | `bmm_E2m1_…_sm100f` (MoE expert GEMM, 1.58-bit, fused swiGLU, dynB) | **Warp Illegal Address** | `0x771c072620a0` (≠ pc) | **49 / 8 / 0**, block (6,7,0), grid (8,8,1) | **ROOT FAULT ⚠️** |
| `.148` | 20:41:07.143 | 0 / 1a:00.0 | `flashinfer::trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce::oneshotAllreduceFusionKernel<4,bf16,true,float4>` | *(none — blocked)* | **`<unavailable>`** | 0 / 0 / 0, block (0,0,0), grid (1,4,1) | collateral |
| `.149` | 20:41:07.149 | 1 / 40:00.0 | same allreduce kernel | *(none — blocked)* | `<unavailable>` | 0 / 0 / 0 | collateral |
| `.150` | 20:41:07.151 | 2 / 62:00.0 | same allreduce kernel | *(none — blocked)* | `<unavailable>` | 0 / 0 / 0 | collateral |

**Why `.148/.149/.150` are collateral, not faults:**
- No `CUDA Exception` banner is emitted for them (cuda-gdb prints the banner only for
  the genuinely-faulting kernel; e.g. `.151` printed `CUDA Exception: Warp Illegal Address`).
- `errorpc = <unavailable>` — there is no faulting instruction.
- The instruction at their PC is a **spin loop**: a long run of
  `ISETP.EQ.OR P0,PT,R{8..19},-0x80000000,P0` — the allreduce's peer-flag polling
  barrier, checking whether every peer GPU has written the `0x80000000` sentinel.
  R8–R19 hold the (still-unset) peer flag values. They are **stuck waiting for GPU 3**.

**Timeline (consistent with bmm = root):**
`bmm fault on GPU3` (20:40:31) → `sglang crash handler writes pkl` (20:40:57, +26s) →
`remaining GPUs' spinning allreduce flushed during final teardown` (20:41:07, +10s).
Total teardown window ≈ 36 s.

---

## 3. Root fault — GPU 3, bmm TMA load (deep)

### Faulting instruction (.151)
```asm
*> 0x771c072620a0  bmm_…_sm100f+3488:   LDG.E R5, desc[UR10][R14.64]
   0x771c072620b0  …+3504:              BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x0
   0x771c072620c0  …+3520:              @P1 BRA 0x771c07262410
   0x771c072620d0  …+3536:              S2R R17,SR_CgaCtaId      ; cluster/CTA id
   0x771c072620e0  …+3552:              WARPSYNC.ALL
```
- `errorpc = 0x771c072620a0` (the LDG.E), `pc = 0x771c072663f0` (paused later in the
  kernel at +20720) — the split confirms a **real faulting instruction**.
- `LDG.E R5, desc[UR10][R14.64]` = an **extended global load through a TMA tensor
  descriptor** (`desc[UR10]`), base/offset `R14 = 0x22000000`. A bad/over-range
  descriptor → out-of-bounds global address → **Warp Illegal Address**.

### Key registers at fault (.151)
| Reg | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `R14` | `0x22000000` | TMA load base/desc offset |
| `UR10` | (descriptor reg) | TMA tensor descriptor |
| `R17` | `0x20` | `SR_CgaCtaId`-derived CTA index |
| `R5` | `0x0` | load destination (faulted → 0) |
| `pc` | `0x771c072663f0` | paused PC (kernel +20720) |
| `errorpc` | `0x771c072620a0` | faulting PC (kernel +3488) |

### Kernel meaning
`bmm_E2m1_E2m1E2m1_Fp32_Ab16_Bb16_Cb16_t128x16x512_s5_et128x16_m128x16x64_c1x1x1_rM_TN_transOut_schedS_biasFp32M_bN_ldgsts_ldgstsSf_rgTma_clmp_swiGlu_dynB_sm100f`
- `bmm` = **batched / grouped matmul** (MoE expert FFN)
- `E2m1` on A and B = **1.58-bit microscaling (MX) quantized** operands, Fp32 accumulate
- `dynB` = **dynamic/ragged expert batch** (variable token count per expert)
- `swiGlu` = fused swiGLU activation; `biasFp32M`; `TN` layout; `rgTma` + `ldgsts` =
  TMA bulk loads → shared memory
- `sm100f` cubin (runs on sm_103 B300, forward-compatible)

This is the **GLM-5.2 MoE expert FFN grouped-GEMM with 1.58-bit quantized weights,
fused swiGLU, dynamic expert load** — exactly the kernel that consumes the
MoE-routing/scatter output.

---

## 4. Lead: a corroborating (but NOT captured) MoE-routing assert

`strings` on `.151` contains an embedded assert message:
```
[CUDA_KERNEL_ASSERT] /pytorch/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Repeat.cu:20: ...
Assertion failed: `result_size == cumsum_ptr[size - 1]`:
Invalid input! In `repeat_interleave`, the `output_size` argument (%ld) must be the
same as the sum of the elements in the `repeats` tensor (%ld).
```

⚠️ **Caveat:** this string is embedded in the compiled binary's assert-message table;
its presence does **not** prove it fired. cuda-gdb captured a **Warp Illegal Address**
on the bmm TMA load, *not* a device assert (an assert would surface as
`CUDA Exception: Warp Assert` / `Device Assertion`, which was not reported).
So treat the Repeat.cu assert as a **plausible upstream trigger**, not a confirmed cause:
if the MoE routing/scatter (`repeat_interleave` over expert `repeats`) produced a
repeats-tensor whose cumsum ≠ output_size, the subsequent ragged `dynB` grouped-GEMM
would receive garbage tile offsets → exactly the OOB TMA descriptor load seen here.
**Confirm against the pkl / runtime logs** (Step "next" below) before claiming it.

---

## 5. ELF / static structure (Level 1)

- ELF64, `Machine: NVIDIA CUDA architecture`, `Type: CORE`, OS/ABI `<unknown: 33>` (CUDA core)
- 14676 section headers (large — many `.cudbg.elfimage.*` per loaded module)
- `readelf`, `strings`, `cuda-gdb`, `nvidia-smi`, `gdb`, `objdump` all present in-pod
- Notable symbol families present (loaded modules, not the fault):
  - `flashinfer::trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce::*` (NVLink-C2C oneshot allreduce) — the collateral kernel
  - NCCL collectives (`ncclDevKernel_AllGather/AllReduce/Reduce…`)
  - sglang `fused_metadata_copy_kernel`, `fused_metadata_copy_multi_kernel`
  - PyTorch `elementwise`/`reduce`/`vectorized` kernels, CUB `DeviceScan*`, `pow_*` (RoPE freq)

---

## 6. Summary & recommendations

**Root cause:** GPU 3 (PCI 73:00.0, UUID `GPU-d4e78e52-eff2-9e7a-3688-b077949c0107`)
faulted with **Warp Illegal Address** on a **TMA-descriptor bulk load** inside the
**1.58-bit MoE expert FFN grouped-GEMM** (`bmm_…_sm100f`, fused swiGLU, dynamic expert
batch) at SM 49 / warp 8. The other 3 ranks' oneshot NVLink allreduce was left spinning
in its sync barrier and was dumped as collateral during context teardown.

**Most likely mechanism (to confirm):** an out-of-bounds TMA tensor descriptor in the
ragged/dynamic MoE batch — i.e. a tile coordinate computed from a bad expert-token
offset. The `Repeat.cu:20 repeat_interleave` assert (cumsum ≠ output_size) is the
prime-suspect upstream trigger, but is **unverified** from this coredump alone.

**Next steps:**
1. **Parse the pkl** `crash_dump_2026-07-06_20-40-57.pkl` (the SGLang crash dump): dump
   `server_args`, the request/batch that was in flight, MoE expert-load distribution,
   and the Python/host stack — this is the artifact that can confirm/deny the
   `repeat_interleave` routing assert and identify the offending request/batch.
2. Check GPU 3 ECC / Xid / row-remapper events around 20:40 (`dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q`)
   to rule out a hardware (ECC/DBE) fault as the descriptor corruption source.
3. Cross-check whether this `bmm_…_sm100f` (sm100 cubin on sm_103) + `dynB` path is a
   known-bad combination for the installed FlashInfer/CUTLASS kernel build; consider
   forcing the sm_103 cubin or disabling `dynB`/TMA-descriptor path for MoE.
4. Since only GPU 3 faulted, also confirm GPU 3 health in isolation (run a targeted
   MoE stress kernel on GPU 3 alone) — if it reproduces, it's a kernel/data bug; if not
   and ECC errors appear, lean hardware.

**Key takeaway for triage:** do **not** treat all 4 coredumps as 4 independent GPU
faults. Only **GPU 3 / `.151` / the bmm kernel** needs root-causing; the allreduce
coredumps are expected fallout from a TP collective losing one member.

records.title: MiniMax M3 NVFP4 on sm12x: need support for SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE activation
records.body:
Running nvidia/MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 on 4x DGX Spark (sm12x) currently fails because of missing support for SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE activation in Flashinfer MoE backend.

If running on unmodified vLLM, it it fails one of the guards with:

```
(Worker_TP0 pid=136) ERROR 06-25 02:49:28 [multiproc_executor.py:898] NotImplementedError: No NvFp4 MoE backend supports the deployment configuration.
```

Or when forcing `--moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass`:

```
(Worker_TP0 pid=137) ERROR 06-25 19:52:59 [multiproc_executor.py:898] ValueError: Model sets swiglu_limit=7.0, but the explicitly requested moe_backend='flashinfer_cutlass' does not apply the SwiGLU clamp. Use 'flashinfer_trtllm' or 'flashinfer_cutlass' instead.
```

When vLLM guard is patched so it looks like in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py`:

```python
NVFP4_BACKENDS_WITH_CLAMP = {
    NvFp4MoeBackend.FLASHINFER_TRTLLM,
    NvFp4MoeBackend.FLASHINFER_CUTLASS,
}
```

Then vLLM fails with the following error:

```
ValueError: NvFp4 MoE backend 'FLASHINFER_CUTLASS' does not support the deployment configuration since kernel does not support MoEActivation.SWIGLUOAI_UNINTERLEAVE activation.
```

  - The job stopped before uploading remaining jit-cache wheels

  
  ## Preliminary Analysis

  The commits most likely to increase the AOT jit-cache size in this window are:

  1. f9546947 / #3395
      - Adds gen_sparse_mla_sm120_module() to default AOT.
      - Adds a new sparse_mla_sm120 JIT/AOT module.
  2. 5b300741 / #3576
      - Adds (512, 512) to default fa2_head_dim in flashinfer/aot.py.
      - This can generate many additional FA2 AOT modules for SM100+/SM120 CUDA 12.9 builds.
  3. 9dce62e0 / #3417
      - Does not add new AOT specs, but changes rmsnorm_silu codegen used by existing AOT modules.
  4. 49f2abfb / #3615
      - Changes topk.cuh. This does not add a new module, but may increase the existing topk.so.
      - This is the first observed failing commit, so it may have pushed an already-large wheel over the limit.

  ## Additional Notes

  The original dev20260617+cu129 artifact appears to have expired, so I could not inspect its exact wheel contents.

  A later locally downloaded dev20260629+cu129 wheel is not an exact match for the failing artifact, but it shows the package is well above the GitHub release limit when uncompressed:

  3338770046 bytes, 1026 files

  Largest modules in that later wheel include:

  fused_moe_103.so    ~294 MB
  fused_moe_100.so    ~279 MB
  topk.so             ~111 MB

  However, fused_moe_100.so and fused_moe_103.so appear to be existing CUTLASS fused MoE modules, not newly introduced in
  the c15ac84c..49f2abfb regression window. They are likely baseline contributors rather than the direct regression.

### `#3576` head_dim=512 AOT size contribution

  `#3576` adds `(512, 512)` to the default `fa2_head_dim` list in `flashinfer/aot.py`, so CUDA 12.9 SM100+/SM120 builds now
  precompile FA2 head_dim=512 variants.

  The original `dev20260617+cu129` artifact has expired, but inspecting a later `dev20260629+cu129` wheel shows the
  `head_dim_qk_512_head_dim_vo_512` modules alone account for about **326.4 MB uncompressed** across **64 `.so` files**:

  ```text
  192.7 MB    16 files    batch_prefill_with_kv_cache
  109.6 MB    16 files    single_prefill_with_kv_cache
   13.2 MB    16 files    batch_decode_with_kv_cache
   10.9 MB    16 files    single_decode_with_kv_cache
  ---------------------------------------------------
  326.4 MB    64 files    total head_dim=512 FA2 modules
```
  This makes #3576 a strong candidate for a large part of the jit-cache artifact growth. The size above is uncompressed size
  from unzip -l; the actual wheel upload limit applies to the compressed .whl, but this still shows the scale of the added
  AOT payload.


  ##  Possible mitigations:  (by  Codex)

  - Split flashinfer-jit-cache by CUDA architecture or module family.
  - Exclude less common AOT modules from the release wheel.
  - Gate head_dim=512 FA2 AOT coverage behind a smaller targeted config.
  - Keep oversized modules JIT-only instead of shipping them in the cache wheel.

records.body:
## Summary

  The GB200 unit test jobs are failing due to Slurm walltime timeout, not due to pytest assertion failures.

## Observed jobs:

  - [unit-test-gb200---cu129](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/350256652)
  - [unit-test-gb200---cu130](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/350256653)

  Both jobs hit:

```
  DUE TO TIME LIMIT
  srun: task 0: Killed
  ERROR: unit test completion marker was not written; the test process may have been killed or timed out.
```
  The JUnit summaries show completed tests passed:

  Summary: 244 succeeded, 0 failed   # job 350256652
  Summary: 245 succeeded, 0 failed   # job 350256653

  Missing / Incomplete Test Files

  For 350256653, the cleanest repro, 247 test files were launched, but only 245 JUnit XML files were produced. The two launched tests without matching XML were:
```
  tests/moe/test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe.py
  tests/utils/test_fp4_quantize.py
```
 ## Likely Root Cause (by Codex)

  The strongest root cause is a stale long-running test priority list after a file rename.

  Commit 378457c7 / PR #3635 split the long-running test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe.py into shards and added the long-running MoE files to LONG_RUNNING_TEST_PATTERNS in scripts/test_utils.sh, so they would be launched at the front of the parallel queue.

  That list currently contains:

  "test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe_routing_renormalize_fp4.py"
  "test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe_routing_renormalize_fp8.py"
  "test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe_routing_renormalize_bf16.py"
  "test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe_other.py"

  Then commit e1a828ea / PR #3730 renamed: tests/moe/test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe_other.py back to: tests/moe/test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe.py

  But scripts/test_utils.sh was not updated. As a result, test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe.py is no longer recognized as a long-running test and is not prioritized at the front of the queue.  In the failing logs, test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe.py starts late, around the middle/back half of the queue, and is still running when Slurm kills the job.

 ## Secondary Contributor

  tests/utils/test_fp4_quantize.py also appears to be a tailing long-running test. It was launched very late in both jobs and did not produce XML before timeout. This file has grown recently, notably around NVFP4 / CuTe DSL / 4over6 coverage, and now  appears large enough to be a walltime risk on GB200 full-suite jobs, especially when JIT/cache artifacts are unavailable.

  ## Additional Observation

  The logs also show missing prebuilt artifacts:
```
  ERROR: flashinfer-cubin wheel not found ...
  ERROR: flashinfer-jit-cache wheel not found ...
```
  This did not immediately fail the job, but it likely increases runtime by forcing more online JIT/download work, which makes the walltime issue worse.

##  Suggested Fix (by Codex)

  Update LONG_RUNNING_TEST_PATTERNS in scripts/test_utils.sh:
```
  LONG_RUNNING_TEST_PATTERNS=(
      "test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe_routing_renormalize_fp4.py"
      "test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe_routing_renormalize_fp8.py"
      "test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe_routing_renormalize_bf16.py"
      "test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe.py"
      "test_fp4_quantize.py"
      "test_trtllm_gen_attention_decode.py"
      "test_trtllm_gen_attention_decode_xqa.py"
      "test_decode_delta_rule.py"
  )
```
  Minimum required fix:
```
  - "test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe_other.py"
  + "test_trtllm_gen_fused_moe.py"
```
  Recommended additional fix:
```
  + "test_fp4_quantize.py"
```
  to avoid the second tailing test causing the same walltime failure.

records.title: aot.py never registers selective_state_update_sm100 — Mamba SSU op can't be AOT-cached on any Blackwell GPU (SM100/110/120/121)
records.body:
## Summary

`flashinfer.aot.gen_all_modules()` never registers `gen_selective_state_update_sm100_module` in the AOT/`flashinfer-jit-cache` build, but the runtime dispatcher always picks that exact module for any GPU with `sm_major >= 10`. As a result, **no AOT build can ever serve the Mamba `selective_state_update` op on any Blackwell-family GPU** (SM100/B100/B200, SM110, SM120, SM121/GB10) — it silently falls back to JIT, or raises `MissingJITCacheError` under `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1`.

## Where the mismatch is

Runtime dispatch, [`flashinfer/mamba/selective_state_update.py`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/mamba/selective_state_update.py):

```python
if sm_major >= 10:
    return gen_selective_state_update_sm100_module(*args).build_and_load()
elif sm_major >= 9:
    return gen_selective_state_update_sm90_module(*args).build_and_load()
else:
    return gen_selective_state_update_module(*args).build_and_load()
```

AOT registration, [`flashinfer/aot.py`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/flashinfer/aot.py) (`gen_all_modules`, inside the `add_misc` block):

```python
if has_sm80 or has_sm90 or has_sm100:
    ...
    gen_selective_state_update_module(...)        # default/Ampere path
if has_sm90 or has_sm100:
    ...
    gen_selective_state_update_sm90_module(...)    # sm90 path
# gen_selective_state_update_sm100_module is never called anywhere
```

`gen_selective_state_update_sm100_module` itself already declares `supported_major_versions=[10, 11, 12]` (`flashinfer/jit/mamba/selective_state_update.py`), matching the runtime's `sm_major >= 10` check — it's a real, working module, just never added to `gen_all_modules()`'s output.

## Impact

Any `flashinfer-jit-cache` wheel built for a Blackwell target (including consumer/edge SM120/SM121 parts like GB10/DGX Spark, not just datacenter SM100) will be missing the `selective_state_update_*_sm100` `.so` files. Frameworks that route Mamba/SSM layers through `flashinfer.mamba.selective_state_update` (e.g. vLLM's `flashinfer` SSU backend, used for NemotronH-style hybrid Mamba+attention models) get a silent JIT compile on first call in production, or a hard `MissingJITCacheError` for anyone building with `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1` to guarantee no-JIT serving.

## Fix

Add the missing registration, gated the same way the module declares its own arch support:

```python
if has_sm100 or has_sm110 or has_sm120 or has_sm121:
    for dtype_combo, dim, dstate, ntokens, cs_dtype, na_dtype in product(
        _ssu_dtype_combos,
        _ssu_dims,
        _ssu_dstates,
        _ssu_ntokens,
        _ssu_cu_seqlens_dtypes,
        _ssu_num_accepted_dtypes,
    ):
        jit_specs.append(
            gen_selective_state_update_sm100_module(
                *dtype_combo, dim, dstate, ntokens, cs_dtype, na_dtype
            )
        )
```

I have this fix applied and verified locally (confirmed an AOT-built `flashinfer-jit-cache` wheel now contains `selective_state_update_*_sm100` modules, and that `flashinfer.mamba.selective_state_update` loads one of them under `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1` without touching JIT, on an SM121a/GB10 device). Happy to open a PR with this change if useful.

## Repro

1. Build `flashinfer-jit-cache` for any Blackwell `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST` (e.g. `12.1a` for GB10) with `add_misc=True` (default).
2. Confirm no `selective_state_update_*_sm100` `.so` shows up under the built wheel's `jit_cache/`.
3. With that wheel installed and `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1`, call `flashinfer.mamba.selective_state_update(...)` on a Blackwell GPU → `MissingJITCacheError`.

## Environment

- flashinfer version: 0.6.13
- GPU: NVIDIA GB10 (SM121a, DGX Spark)
- Found while building a GB10-scoped `flashinfer-jit-cache` wheel for serving a NemotronH (hybrid Mamba+attention) MoE model via vLLM.

records.title: v0.6.14 release highlights draft
records.body:
### v0.6.14 Highlights

This release pushes FlashInfer's coverage onto Blackwell RTX PRO and DGX Spark silicon, lands the CuTe-DSL rewrite of the gated-delta-rule (GDN) kernels behind Qwen3.5/3.6, and makes those kernels production-ready inside vLLM.

**Gemma 4 and W4A16 on Blackwell RTX Pro and DGX Spark**

Blackwell SM12x parts (RTX PRO 6000, DGX Spark / GB10) previously trailed Blackwell GB200 NVL72 (and B300 SM103) on attention shape and quantization coverage. This release closes the gap for Gemma 4 and weight-only-quantized inference: head_dim=512 attention for Gemma 4's global layers now runs on SM120/121, the FMHAv2 prefill path gains head_dim=256/512 and sliding-window masking on SM120, the new mm_bf16_fp4 W4A16 GEMM is tuned for DGX Spark (completing W4A16 across both dense GEMM and MoE), and gated tanh-GELU brings Gemma 4 MoE onto the CUTLASS backend.


- #3576
- #3518
- #3597
- #3501


**GDN / gated delta rule: CuTe-DSL overhaul (Qwen3.5/3.6)**

The gated-delta-rule kernels behind the Qwen3.5/3.6 family were rewritten from CUTLASS C++ to CuTe-DSL ([megathread #3491](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3491)). The rewrite eliminates the C++ JIT compilation pain reported by customers and establishes the base for context-parallel delta-rule kernels — covering SM90 prefill and its context-parallel variant, SM120 prefill, and a ~20–25% GDN prefill speedup from mainloop efficiency work.


- #3477
- #3481
- #3479
- #3742


**GDN production-ready in vLLM**

Two gaps blocked GDN serving in vLLM ([#3602](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3602)); both are now resolved. GDN kernels are compilation batch-size agnostic, so a single compiled cubin is reused across batch shapes instead of recompiling on every new batch size at inference time, and a new BF16 state recovery/decode kernel writes SSM state into preallocated space to supply the MTP-compatible spec-decode path vLLM needs.


- #3649
- #3502


**DeepSeek-class sparse MLA on Blackwell, FP8 KV on Hopper**

New sparse-MLA paged-attention kernels extend the DeepSeek-V4 (d_qk=512) and DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.1 (d_qk=576) families onto SM120/121 through the existing flashinfer.mla APIs, with DSv4 coverage broadened to 8/16/32 head counts. On Hopper SM90, native FP8 KV cache support eliminates SGLang's per-layer cast workaround, saving an HBM round-trip per layer on DeepSeek-V3/V4 while staying bit-identical to the BF16 path.


- #3395
- #3545
- #3694

records.title: [RFC] Checkpoint lifecycle APIs for CUDA-graph-stable communication workspaces
records.body:
## Summary

We propose a small, uniform checkpoint lifecycle for FlashInfer communication workspaces:

```python
workspace.checkpoint_prepare()
# The workload orchestrator invokes cuda-checkpoint and CRIU.
workspace.checkpoint_restore(fresh_comm_backend)
```

The goal is to let workloads preserve captured CUDA graphs while checkpointing and restoring GPU state with `cuda-checkpoint`, including workloads that use NVLink and multi-node NVLink (MNNVL) communication.

## Motivation

We are extending [NVIDIA Dynamo Snapshot](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-dynamo-snapshot-fast-startup-for-inference-workloads-on-kubernetes/) beyond its current single-GPU path to multi-GPU and multi-node inference. This is important for frontier-scale MoE deployments, including DeepSeek-class models, where FlashInfer is increasingly the default communication backend in the serving configurations we are targeting.

The practical blocker is the interaction between CUDA graphs, CUDA VMM, and communication handles:

- FlashInfer owns peer-memory mappings used by NVLink and MNNVL communication workspaces.
- CUDA graphs capture graph-visible virtual addresses, so those addresses must remain unchanged across restore.
- The current [CUDA checkpointing API](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html) does not preserve and recreate the CUDA Fabric shareable-handle state used by these workspaces.
- Fully destroying and reallocating a workspace can change its virtual addresses, invalidating captured graphs.

We therefore need to separate the lifetime of a workspace's virtual-address reservation from the lifetime of its physical allocations and imported/exported communication handles.

## Proposed lifecycle

1. The workload initializes normally and captures its CUDA graphs.
2. The caller quiesces request and communication activity.
3. Every rank calls `checkpoint_prepare()`. The collective operation synchronizes the workspace, releases its physical backing and peer/fabric handles, and retains its graph-visible VA reservations.
4. The workload orchestrator invokes `cuda-checkpoint` and CRIU to capture the GPU and host process state.
5. The orchestrator restores the process with CRIU, then runs `cuda-checkpoint` restore and unlock.
6. Every rank calls `checkpoint_restore(fresh_comm_backend)`. The collective operation exchanges and recreates fresh handles, maps the new backing at the retained VAs, reinitializes protocol state, and fences before returning.
7. The workload can replay the CUDA graphs captured before checkpoint.

The proposed contract is:

- The public API lives on the high-level workspace that owns the communication protocol. Handle detach/reattach operations remain private implementation details.
- Both methods are collective and must be called by every rank in the same order.
- Restore receives a fresh communication backend with the same rank and world size so ranks can exchange newly created handles.
- Repeated successfully completed prepare or restore calls are idempotent no-ops.
- A failed transition is terminal for that workspace. There is no rollback or retry path; the worker should be restarted.
- Data operations are rejected while a workspace is detached.
- The lifecycle is supported only by FlashInfer-owned CUDA-VMM backing that can retain its address reservation. Workspaces backed by torch symmetric memory explicitly reject these methods because that allocator does not provide FlashInfer with the required stable-VA remap contract.

This keeps workload orchestration outside FlashInfer. Dynamo, vLLM, or SGLang can call these hooks as part of their existing quiesce/resume or sleep/wake flow, around the external CUDA/CRIU checkpoint operation.

## Implementation steps

1. **DEP MoE workloads:** These workloads need lifecycle support in both their all-reduce and MoE all-to-all communication paths.
   - [#3745](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3745) adds the stable-VA lifecycle for TRT-LLM and MNNVL all-reduce workspaces.
   - [#3727](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3727) adds the lifecycle for the MNNVL MoE all-to-all DEP/EP workspace.
2. **Tensor-parallel workloads:** [galletas1712/flashinfer#3](https://github.com/galletas1712/flashinfer/pull/3) adds the checkpointable symmetric all-gather needed by TP workloads, stacked on #3745.

## Validation plan

Before considering the lifecycle complete, we plan to validate:

- eager execution and replay of graphs captured before checkpoint
- repeated graph replay after restoring fresh physical handles at the original VAs
- multi-node MNNVL DEP/EP workloads and frontier MoE models
- single-node NVLink at TP2, TP4, and TP8
- end-to-end Dynamo Snapshot flows through both vLLM and SGLang

## Requested maintainer feedback

We would appreciate feedback on:

1. Whether `checkpoint_prepare()` / `checkpoint_restore(comm_backend)` is the right public surface and naming.
2. Whether the high-level-workspace/private-memory-core ownership boundary matches FlashInfer's preferred architecture.

records.title: [Bug] cuDNN FP8 MOE grouped matmul silently computes only the first expert group with backend 9.18–9.20 (SM120)
records.body:
## Summary

`flashinfer.grouped_mm.grouped_mm_fp8` (cuDNN backend) returns **silently wrong results** with cuDNN backend **9.18.0 – 9.20.0**: only the **first expert group** is computed; every group `e >= 1` of the output is left **zero**. `graph.check_support()` passes, no error or warning is raised. Fixed in cuDNN **9.21.0**.

The current version floor admits the broken versions: `_CUDNN_MOE_MIN_VERSION = 91800` (`flashinfer/grouped_mm/cudnn/core.py:48`) is used for `grouped_mm_fp8` (`flashinfer/grouped_mm/core.py:269`), and the test gate `requires_cudnn_moe` (`tests/grouped_mm/conftest.py:28`) is `>= 91800` as well.

**Blast radius:** `torch 2.11.0+cu130` pins `nvidia-cudnn-cu13==9.19.0.56` — i.e. a stock cu13 PyTorch environment gets exactly a broken version, and MoE FP8 grouped GEMM silently produces garbage for every expert but the first.

## Reproduction (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, SM120, CUDA 13, torch 2.11.0+cu130)

```python
import torch
from flashinfer.grouped_mm import grouped_mm_fp8

torch.manual_seed(42)
E, tpe, k, n = 4, 64, 256, 256
a = torch.randn(E * tpe, k, device="cuda").clamp(-1, 1).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
b = torch.randn(E, n, k, device="cuda").clamp(-1, 1).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
m_indptr = (torch.arange(E + 1, device="cuda") * tpe).to(torch.int32)
alpha = torch.tensor([1.0], dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")

out = grouped_mm_fp8(a, b, m_indptr, alpha=alpha, out_dtype=torch.bfloat16)

for e in range(E):
    s, t = e * tpe, (e + 1) * tpe
    ref = a[s:t].float() @ b[e].float().T
    ok = torch.isclose(out[s:t].float(), ref, atol=0.125, rtol=0.125).float().mean()
    zero = (out[s:t] == 0).float().mean()
    print(f"expert {e}: match={ok:.3f} zero-frac={zero:.3f}")
```

With cuDNN 9.19.0.56:

```
expert 0: match=1.000 zero-frac=0.004
expert 1: match=0.014 zero-frac=1.000
expert 2: match=0.010 zero-frac=1.000
expert 3: match=0.008 zero-frac=1.000
```

Same pattern for `float8_e5m2`, all shapes tried (`tpe ∈ {32..256}`, `k ∈ {256,512}`, `n ∈ {256,1024}`), with and without `alpha`. `pytest tests/grouped_mm/test_grouped_mm_fp8.py` → **58 failed** (everything with `num_experts > 1`).

## What rules out the wrapper

`grouped_mm_bf16` goes through the **same** `_run_cudnn_moe_grouped_gemm` / `_build_cudnn_moe_grouped_gemm_graph` code path (same `first_token_offset` construction, `flashinfer/grouped_mm/cudnn/core.py:248`) and is correct on every cuDNN version tested — `tests/grouped_mm/test_grouped_mm_bf16.py` = 46 passed on 9.19.0.56. Only the FP8 data types trip it, so the `first_token_offset`/graph semantics on the FlashInfer side are fine; the regression is inside the cuDNN backend's FP8 MOE kernels.

## cuDNN backend bisect (pip `nvidia-cudnn-cu13`, `tests/grouped_mm/test_grouped_mm_fp8.py`)

| cuDNN backend | result |
| --- | --- |
| 9.18.0.77 | 58 failed / 34 passed |
| 9.18.1.3 | 58 failed / 34 passed |
| 9.19.0.56 (torch 2.11 cu13 pin) | 58 failed / 34 passed |
| 9.19.1.2 | 58 failed / 34 passed |
| 9.20.0.48 | 58 failed / 34 passed |
| **9.21.0.82** | **92 passed** |
| 9.22.0.52 | 92 passed |
| 9.23.2.1 | 92 passed |

(The passing subset on broken versions is the `num_experts = 1` / empty-expert cases.)

Bonus datapoint: with 9.23.2.1 the whole `tests/grouped_mm/` directory is **305 passed** on SM120, including the `>= 9.21` block-scale MXFP8/FP4 suites.

## Scope caveat

Verified on **SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, CUDA 13)** only — I don't have SM90/SM100 hardware to check whether 9.18–9.20 mis-execute there too. bf16 vs fp8 discrimination above is from the same SM120 box.

## Proposed fix

Mirror the existing block-scale floor: add `_CUDNN_MOE_FP8_MIN_VERSION = 92100` and use it in `grouped_mm_fp8`'s runtime check (`flashinfer/grouped_mm/core.py:269`), plus a matching `requires_cudnn_moe_fp8` test gate, so the broken combination fails fast with an actionable error instead of silently corrupting MoE outputs. PR incoming.

records.title: [Bug] GDN sm_120a prefill fails with cudaErrorUnsupportedPtxVersion on CUDA-13.0 drivers: the TMA patch path reloads PTX through the driver JIT
records.body:
## Summary

The GDN sm_120a prefill path (`chunk_gated_delta_rule`) fails on any **CUDA 13.0 driver** with

```
cutlass.base_dsl.common.DSLCudaRuntimeError: cudaErrorUnsupportedPtxVersion (error code: 222)
```

at `flashinfer/gdn_kernels/delta_rule_dsl/custom_compile_cache.py` `_load_cuda_library`. On current main (`8fc7f079`), `pytest tests/gdn/test_prefill_delta_rule.py` = **2629 failed / 6 passed / 912 skipped** on an RTX PRO 6000 (SM120) with driver 580.159.03.

## Root cause

The sm_120a TMA patch path is the **only** CuTe-DSL consumer that round-trips through the **driver's PTX JIT**:

1. `_patch_sm120a_tma` extracts the compiled kernel's PTX text and rewrites the cluster-TMA instructions to their `shared::cta` forms (sm_120a has no cluster TMA).
2. `_install_patched_ptx_loader` then loads the **raw patched PTX text** via `cuLibraryLoadData(..., CU_JIT_TARGET=COMPUTE_120A)` — i.e. the *driver* must JIT the PTX.
3. Every `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 4.5.x build (4.5.0/4.5.1/4.5.2 — the full range `requirements.txt` admits with `>=4.5.0`) bundles **CUDA 13.1** and emits **`.version 9.1`** PTX. A CUDA-13.0 driver (580.xx series) cannot JIT PTX 9.1, hence error 222.

This is why only GDN fails while every other CuTe-DSL surface passes on the same box/driver (b12x fused MoE 142 passed, SM120 MXFP8 grouped GEMM 69 passed, unified MoE 99 passed today): the normal DSL pipeline materializes SASS through its own bundled toolchain and never asks the driver to JIT PTX.

No driver floor is documented — `requirements.txt` only pins `nvidia-cutlass-dsl>=4.5.0` — so a stock torch-2.11-cu130 + 580-driver machine (a common production setup, and driver updates are often not in the user's control on shared clusters) hits this on the very feature the v0.6.14 highlights lead with.

## Evidence (RTX PRO 6000, SM120, CUDA 13.0, driver 580.159.03, torch 2.11.0+cu130)

- Extracted the actual patched PTX from the failing path: header is `.version 9.1` / `.target sm_120a`.
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` 4.5.0, 4.5.1, 4.5.2 all report `DSLCudaVersion(major=13, minor=1)` — no 13.0-emitting release satisfies the `>=4.5.0` floor.
- Assembling that same patched PTX with a ptxas >= 13.1 (e.g. the 13.2 ptxas from the pip `nvidia/cu13` toolchain wheel) and loading the **cubin** through the identical `cuLibraryLoadData` call **succeeds on the 13.0 driver**, and the kernels run correctly:

| `tests/gdn/test_prefill_delta_rule.py` | result |
| --- | --- |
| main (`8fc7f079`), driver PTX JIT | 2629 failed / 6 passed / 912 skipped |
| with ptxas-assembly fix, same driver | **2635 passed / 0 failed / 912 skipped** |

## Proposed fix

In `_install_patched_ptx_loader`, assemble the patched PTX to a cubin with the first working `ptxas` (candidates: `FLASHINFER_PTXAS` env override, `PATH`, pip toolchain wheels `nvidia/cu1x/bin`, triton's bundled ptxas, `CUDA_HOME`; the assembly attempt itself is the version check) and hand `cuLibraryLoadData` SASS instead of PTX. Fall back to the current driver-JIT path with a diagnostic warning when no usable ptxas exists. PR incoming.

Found while validating current main on RTX PRO 6000 for the v0.6.14 SM12x release (#3783 follow-up in the proper venue this time). AI-assisted (Claude Code) under human direction; all numbers are from live runs on the real card.

records.title: [Bug] cudnn_batch_prefill_with_kv_cache: one-token Q batch stride silently corrupts every batch after the first when batch_offsets_q is not passed
records.body:
### Summary

`cudnn_batch_prefill_with_kv_cache` returns **silently wrong attention output for every batch after the first** whenever the caller does not pass `batch_offsets_q` - which is exactly how flashinfer's own trace suite calls it (`tests/trace/test_cudnn_batch_prefill_reference_correctness.py`, red on current main for its `B2` case).

### Root cause

The Q tensor descriptor in `flashinfer/cudnn/prefill.py` uses a **one-token batch stride**:

```python
cudnn_q = g.tensor(
    name="q",
    dim=(graph_b, h_qo, graph_s_qo, d_qk),
    stride=(h_qo * d_qk, h_stride, s_stride, d_stride),  # batch stride = ONE token
    ...
)
```

so batch `b`'s queries are read starting at token `b` instead of token `b * s_qo`. Batch 0 is coincidentally correct; every later batch computes attention over the wrong query rows and writes finite, plausible-looking garbage. The O descriptor right below does it correctly (`graph_s_qo * d_vo * h_qo`), which is what exposes this as an oversight rather than a convention.

The public wrapper path (`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(backend="cudnn")`) always supplies ragged offsets, and `set_ragged_offset` overrides the batch stride - which is why `tests/attention/test_cudnn_prefill.py` passes while the raw-function path is broken.

### Evidence (RTX PRO 6000, SM120, CUDA 13; reproduces identically with cuDNN backend 9.19.0.56 and 9.23.2.1, cudart 12 and 13)

- Failing config `B=2, Hq=8, Hk=2, D=128, PS=16, q_len=32, kv_len=64` (the trace test): per-batch max abs diff vs reference = `[0.0078, 1.7183]` - batch 0 perfect, batch 1 100% of tokens wrong from token 0.
- Independent arbitration: a hand-written torch reference (per-page gather + causal softmax) agrees with the trace template's reference on both batches (max 0.0039) and disagrees with the kernel on batch 1 - the references are right, the kernel path is wrong.
- Scales with batch: `B=3` gives `[0.0078, 1.7183, 1.5195]`. Not GQA-specific: `Hq=Hk=8` gives `[0.0039, 1.6133]`.
- Passing `batch_offsets_q`/`batch_offsets_o` heals it: `[0.0078, 0.0039]` - confirming the ragged-offset override is what protects the wrapper path.

### Fix

Use a full-sequence batch stride, mirroring the O descriptor: `stride=(graph_s_qo * s_stride, h_stride, s_stride, d_stride)` (using the tensor's own per-token stride also keeps non-contiguous `q` correct). With that one-line change on this machine: the trace file goes 1 failed / 1 passed -> 2 passed, `tests/attention/test_cudnn_prefill.py` + `test_cudnn_prefill_deepseek.py` stay green (384 passed), and the B3/GQA/MHA probes above all drop to <= 0.0078. PR incoming.

Also noting while reading the same function: the `q.dim() == 4` branch unpacks three values from a 4-D `q.stride()`, which raises ValueError if ever taken - the 4-D path looks untested.

### Environment

RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.11 cu130, flashinfer main 8fc7f079. Found during a systematic SM120 sweep of the trace suites; arbitration and fix verified on the same card.

records.title: [Bug] tests/utils full-directory run: sys.modules deletion in test_logging poisons enum identities - 630 cross-test failures that vanish in isolation
records.body:
### Summary

Running `pytest tests/utils` as a whole directory produces **630 failures** that do not reproduce for any file in isolation. The dominant error signature is self-contradictory type checks from the logits_processor pipeline, e.g.:

```
LegalizationError: Failed to legalize processor 1 (Softmax): Softmax can only be applied to LOGITS, got LOGITS
LegalizationError: Failed to legalize processor 1 (TopP): TopP can only be applied to PROBS, got PROBS
ValueError: ... (Sample): Sampling cannot be applied to PROBS
```

"can only be applied to LOGITS, got LOGITS" failing means the comparison is between **two different enum class objects with the same name** - i.e. some module in the directory run gets re-imported under a second identity, and enum members created against one copy fail equality against the other.

### Measured matrix (RTX PRO 6000, CUDA 13, flashinfer main 8fc7f079; deterministic across reruns)

| run | result |
| --- | --- |
| full `tests/utils` directory | 630 failed / 18280 passed (failures: test_logits_processor.py 591 = its entire body, test_sampling.py 18, test_quantization.py 16, test_logging.py 5) |
| each of those files standalone | all pass (591 / 1791 / 28 respectively) |
| `test_logging.py + test_logits_processor.py` (the alphabetical neighbors) | 611 passed - clean |
| front half (`activation, concat_mla, create_ipc_buffer, decorators, fp4_kv_quantization`) + `logits_processor` | 2515 passed - clean |
| back half (`fp4_kv_quantization, fp4_quantize, fp8_quantize, logging`) + `logits_processor` | logits_processor passes, but `test_logging.py` itself fails 4 cases, the process exits nonzero, and atexit produces `--- Logging error ---` spam from `flush_graph_dumps (atexit)` |

GPU memory peaked at ~19 GB during the full run, so this is not OOM pressure.

### Identified state mutation

`tests/utils/test_logging.py` fixtures and helpers delete `flashinfer.api_logging` from `sys.modules` to force re-imports under different `FLASHINFER_LOGLEVEL` values (lines ~59-81 and several `sys.modules.pop("flashinfer.api_logging", None)` sites). Any module re-imported after such a deletion (directly or transitively) acquires new class/enum identities; modules imported at pytest collection time keep the old ones. Which downstream file breaks then depends on collection/import interleaving across the whole directory - consistent with the pair being clean while the full directory explodes, and with the atexit logging errors (a second api_logging registers its own atexit/graph-dump state).

### Suggested direction

Either make the reload hygienic (snapshot and restore `sys.modules` and any registered atexit/graph-dump state in the fixture, or run the reload-dependent tests in a subprocess), or make the logits_processor type checks identity-robust. Happy to work on a fix if the owners of the api_logging/trace plumbing can confirm which direction is preferred - the subprocess isolation looks safest from here.

### Environment

RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.11 cu130, flashinfer main 8fc7f079. Found during a systematic SM120 sweep; the 630-failure explosion is fully reproducible.

records.title: [Bug] test_dcp_alltoall flaky under GPU load: alltoall launched on side streams without waiting for input fills on the current stream
records.body:
### Symptom

`tests/comm/test_dcp_alltoall.py::test_repeated_alltoall[cp2-3rounds]` and `[cp4-3rounds]` fail intermittently when the file runs as a suite on a loaded GPU, with exact-match assertions reporting 100% mismatched softmax stats (and, in instrumented runs, ~100% mismatched partial_o as well):

```
FAILED tests/comm/test_dcp_alltoall.py::test_repeated_alltoall[cp2-3rounds]
E   AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal!
E   Mismatched elements: 32 / 32 (100.0%)
```

Observed on main (bf92d49c), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), CUDA 13, torch 2.11.0+cu130, with a ~35-40% background GPU co-tenant. Base rate in that state: 3 of 6 full-file runs fail; the same tests pass when run in isolation, and the single-round `test_alltoall_correctness` cases have the same hazard but much smaller exposure, so they rarely trip.

### Root cause: missing cross-stream synchronization in the test, not a kernel bug

Both launch sites (`_run_single_gpu_alltoall` and `test_repeated_alltoall`) fill the inputs with `torch.randn(...)` on the current (default) stream, then launch `decode_cp_a2a_alltoall` on freshly created per-rank side streams without ordering them after the producing stream:

```python
streams = [torch.cuda.Stream() for _ in range(cp_size)]
for r in range(cp_size):
    with torch.cuda.stream(streams[r]):          # no wait_stream(current_stream)
        o, s = decode_cp_a2a_alltoall(all_po[r], all_ss[r], workspace, r, cp_size)
```

Under load, a rank's kernel can start before the default-stream fills complete and reads partially-written input buffers. The evidence matches this and nothing else I tried:

- Nondeterministic; the corrupted contribution belongs to whichever rank wins the race (I observed "everything received from rank 1 wrong" in one run and "everything from rank 0 wrong" in another).
- Wrong values are plausible randn-like floats, not zeros, not stale FIFO payloads, and not equal to any previous round's data.
- A/B with an instrumented standalone harness on the same box, same load: 6/12 runs fail without `wait_stream`, 12/12 pass with `streams[r].wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())` added and nothing else changed.
- With the two-line fix applied to the test file, 10/10 full-file pytest runs pass under the same load (stock: 3/6 failing).

The workspace/FIFO handshake itself looks fine: `initializeHelixWorkspace` runs on the default stream and is covered by the same ordering, and I found no misbehavior attributable to the kernel once the input ordering is fixed.

Other comm tests in the tree already do this correctly, e.g. `tests/comm/test_trtllm_moe_allreduce_fusion.py:209` (`s.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())` before entering the stream context), so this brings `test_dcp_alltoall.py` in line with the existing pattern.

### Fix

Add `streams[r].wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())` before the `with torch.cuda.stream(streams[r])` block at both launch sites. PR incoming.

### Environment

- flashinfer main @ bf92d49c, editable install
- NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation (SM120), driver 580, CUDA 13.0
- torch 2.11.0+cu130, python 3.10

records.title: [Bug] b12x fused MoE dynamic kernel overflows SM120 smem (118,784 B > 101,376) for intermediate_size >= 1024 — _compute_stages doesn't count fused down-GEMM buffers
records.body:
## Summary

The b12x fused MoE **dynamic** kernel (`blackwell_sm12x/moe_dynamic_kernel.py`, `MoEDynamicKernel`) fails to launch on SM120 with

```
Error: kernel '@kernels::@kernel_cutlass_kernel_flashinferfused_moecute_dslblackwell_sm12xmoe_dynamic_kernelMoEDynamicKernel_...' launch shared memory exceeds current GPU arch sm_120a allowed. Allocated: 118784 bytes. Max: 101376 bytes.
RuntimeError: CUDA Error: cudaErrorInvalidValue
```

for MoE shapes with `moe_intermediate_size >= 1024` (e.g. **Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4**: E=256, hidden=3072, inter=1024, topk=8). Smaller-intermediate MoEs (e.g. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4, inter=512) launch fine, which makes this look model-specific rather than what it is: **`_compute_stages` picks an AB pipeline stage count that does not account for all smem the fused MoE variant allocates.** The margin of error (~17.4 KB) happens to be absorbed at inter=512 and overflows at inter=1024.

In vLLM this makes `--moe-backend flashinfer_b12x` die at warmup (first large prefill batch → dynamic path) on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell for such models, while the same command works for the 35B. Reproduced identically on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q 96GB and RTX 5070 Ti (both SM120, 101,376 B smem/block).

## Environment

- GPUs: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120), RTX 5070 Ti (SM120)
- FlashInfer 0.6.13 as bundled in `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (vLLM `0.23.1rc1.dev714+g09663abde`, 2026-07-02); the two kernel files involved are byte-identical to the 0.6.12 build bundled with vLLM v0.24.0, so both versions are affected
- CUDA 13, driver 610.x
- Env: `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0f`, `FLASHINFER_FORCE_SM=120f`, `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1`

## Minimal repro

Launch-only test with random weights (output values irrelevant); runs in <2 GB VRAM:

```python
import torch
from flashinfer.fused_moe import b12x_fused_moe
from flashinfer.cute_dsl.utils import convert_sf_to_mma_layout

E, H, I, TOPK, M = 256, 3072, 1024, 8, 4096   # Qwen3.5-122B-A10B shapes; M large => dynamic path
dev = "cuda:0"

def make_sf(rows, cols, groups):
    m_pad = (rows + 127) // 128 * 128
    k_pad = ((cols // 16) + 3) // 4 * 4
    storage = torch.randint(100, 120, (groups * m_pad, k_pad), dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev)
    return convert_sf_to_mma_layout(storage.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn), m=rows, k=cols, num_groups=groups)

x = torch.randn(M, H, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
w1 = torch.randint(0, 255, (E, 2 * I, H // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev)
w2 = torch.randint(0, 255, (E, H, I // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev)
ids = torch.stack([torch.randperm(E, device=dev)[:TOPK] for _ in range(M)]).to(torch.int32)
scales = torch.softmax(torch.randn(M, TOPK, device=dev), dim=-1).float()
ones = lambda: torch.ones(E, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)

out = b12x_fused_moe(x, w1, make_sf(2 * I, H, E), w2, make_sf(H, I, E), ids, scales, E, TOPK,
                     w1_alpha=ones(), w2_alpha=ones(), fc2_input_scale=ones())
torch.cuda.synchronize()
print("LAUNCH OK", out.shape)
```

- As written (inter=1024): `cudaErrorInvalidValue`, kernel wants 118,784 B.
- With `I = 512` (Qwen3.6-35B shapes): `LAUNCH OK`.
- With `M = 16` (micro/static path instead of dynamic): `LAUNCH OK` at either shape.

## Root cause

In `MoEDynamicKernel._setup_attributes` (moe_dynamic_kernel.py):

```python
self.ab_stage, self.epi_stage = self._dense_cls._compute_stages(
    self.tile_shape_mnk, ..., self.smem_capacity, self.occupancy)
# ab_stage must divide k_tile_cnt evenly ...
k_tile_cnt = self._hidden_size // self.tile_shape_mnk[2]
while self.ab_stage > 1 and k_tile_cnt % self.ab_stage != 0:
    self.ab_stage -= 1
```

`self.smem_capacity = utils.get_smem_capacity_in_bytes("sm_120")` is correct (101,376), and `_compute_stages` (inherited from the **dense** GEMM kernel in `gemm/kernels/dense_blockscaled_gemm_sm120_b12x.py`) returns "the max that fits" — **but its accounting covers only the single-GEMM A/B/SF/epilogue buffers.** The fused MoE variant allocates additional smem on top (down-projection/second-GEMM + epilogue buffers whose footprint grows with `n` = intermediate_size). At (128,128,128) tiles, `_compute_stages` returns `ab_stage=3` for these shapes; the real allocation is then 118,784 B — 17,408 over the cap. At inter=512 the extra buffers are small enough that 3 stages still fit.

## Workarounds evaluated

- **`ab_stage` clamped to 2 → fits (≈100,352 B) and works end-to-end.** Verified by monkeypatching `_compute_stages` to `min(ret, 2)`: kernel launches, and a full vLLM serve of Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-NVFP4 with `--moe-backend flashinfer_b12x` at 128k context boots, passes NIAH 8/8 (incl. 120k depth sweep), 24/24 long-form generations with no degeneration, tool-calling and image inputs correct.
- Shrinking the tile instead does **not** work: overriding `_LEVEL_TILE_M` or `_LEVEL_TILE_N` to 64 fails in `_make_tma_atoms_and_tensors` (`cpasync.make_tiled_tma_atom` → `ValueError: Operation creation failed`), so stage count is the only available lever.
- Routing large batches to the static kernel (raising `B12X_DYNAMIC_STATIC_CUTOVER_PAIRS`) is memory-infeasible: the static workspace allocation scales with routed rows (12 GiB at 4096 tokens × topk 8).

## Suggested fix

Include the fused variant's extra smem consumers in the stage computation (or subtract them from the capacity passed to `_compute_stages`), so `ab_stage` reflects what the kernel actually allocates. A conservative interim fix would be to recompute the true total after `_setup_attributes` builds the staged layouts and decrement `ab_stage` until it fits — that turns a hard launch failure into a working (slightly less pipelined) kernel. Happy to test patches on both SM120 cards; the shapes above reproduce it deterministically.

Possibly related: #3683 (other intermediate_size-dependent b12x limits), #3170 (SM12x audit).

---

*Attribution: this bug was investigated and root-caused by Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic) working in Claude Code; the analysis, repro, and workaround were reviewed and validated by a human before filing.*
