records.title: [Bug] ~11% long-prefill regression on SM120 (RTX 5090) between 0.6.12 and 0.6.13, hybrid GDN model via vLLM
records.body:
### Summary

Upgrading FlashInfer **0.6.12 → 0.6.13** costs **~8–11% long-context prefill throughput** on **SM120 (RTX 5090)** with a hybrid GDN + attention MoE model served by vLLM. Decode is unaffected. The regression is isolated to the FlashInfer wheels: swapping *only* `flashinfer-python` / `flashinfer-cubin` / `flashinfer-jit-cache` between 0.6.12 and 0.6.13, with vLLM/torch/cutlass-dsl held constant, reproduces it in **both directions**.

The penalty scales with context length (≈0% at 4K, −8% at 64K, −11% at 131K), which points at the prefill attention path rather than kernel/backend selection.

### Environment

- GPU: **NVIDIA RTX 5090, 32 GB, SM120** (compute cap 12.0), driver 610.43.02, CUDA 13.0
- vLLM: `v0.24.0` (ships FI 0.6.12) and `v0.25.0` (ships FI 0.6.13), official `vllm/vllm-openai` images
- torch 2.11.0+cu130, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.2 — **identical across all runs**
- Model: `unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4-Fast` — MoE (256 experts, top-8), **hybrid: 30 GDN/linear-attn + 10 attention layers**, 256K context. compressed-tensors NVFP4 (W4A4) experts + FP8 attention.
- Attention backend: **FLASHINFER** (auto-selected). MoE: FLASHINFER_CUTLASS. GDN prefill: Triton/FLA.
- Env: `FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=12.0f`, `FLASHINFER_FORCE_SM=120f`

Serving flags: `--kv-cache-dtype=fp8 --max-model-len=262144 --max-num-batched-tokens=4096 --gpu-memory-utilization=0.92 --max-num-seqs=16 --enable-prefix-caching --moe-backend=auto`

### Reproduction

Measured with `vllm bench serve` (concurrency 1, `--random-output-len 128` so prefill dominates, 3 prompts). **prefill tok/s = prompt_tokens / mean_TTFT.**

**Stock images:**

| vLLM | FlashInfer | 4K | 16K | 64K | 131K |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v0.24.0 | 0.6.12 | 27,248 | 31,856 | **18,303** | **12,672** |
| v0.25.0 | 0.6.13 | 26,766 | 31,147 | **16,767** | **11,345** |
| nightly `0.25.1.dev37` | 0.6.13 | 26,742 | 31,428 | 16,844 | 11,369 |

**Isolating FlashInfer** — only the flashinfer wheels swapped (`pip install --no-deps --force-reinstall flashinfer-python==X flashinfer-cubin==X flashinfer-jit-cache==X`), everything else byte-identical:

| build | FlashInfer | prefill@131K | verdict |
|---|---|---:|---|
| vLLM 0.24.0 (stock) | 0.6.12 | **12,658** | good |
| vLLM 0.24.0 | **0.6.13** | **11,271** | **regressed** ← only FI changed |
| vLLM nightly 06-30 (stock) | 0.6.13 | **11,224** | regressed |
| vLLM nightly 06-30 | **0.6.12** | **12,581** | **recovered** ← only FI changed |
| vLLM 0.25.0 | **0.6.12** | **12,724** | recovered |

Decode is unaffected (aggregate output tok/s at 16 concurrent: 2,235 on 0.6.12 vs 2,198 on 0.6.13 — within noise).

### Ruled out

- **Not backend selection.** Both versions log the identical choices: `FLASHINFER` attention backend, `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` NvFp4 MoE backend, `Triton/FLA GDN prefill kernel (requested=auto, head_k_dim=128)`, and `attention block size 2096`. The vLLM engine-config diff between the two versions is three cosmetic lines.
- **Not the FP8-KV prefill repack** (#3485, `perf(attention): Speed up FP8 KV-cache prefill (FA2 BatchPrefill) by repacking K/V to BF16 in shared memory`). This was my first suspect since the config uses `--kv-cache-dtype=fp8`, but the regression **persists with BF16 KV** (`--kv-cache-dtype=auto`): 12,695 → 11,319, the same ~11%.
- **Not prefix caching.** Gap persists with `--no-enable-prefix-caching`: 12,658 → 11,013 (0.6.12) vs 11,224 → 10,005 (0.6.13).

### Possible culprits

I have not bisected inside the 0.6.12…0.6.13 range. From the [compare](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/compare/v0.6.12rc3...v0.6.13), the autotuner changes look like the most plausible candidates for a context-scaling prefill slowdown via worse tactic selection:

- #3367 `fix(autotuner): differentiate file cache entries by runner specific kernel parameters`
- #3396 `feat(autotuner): enable per-op autotune bypass for faster framework warmup`
- #3373 `Extend autotuner delay kernel length`

Happy to run further probes on this SM120 box (including a wheel-level bisect inside the range) if that's useful — I have the harness set up.

### Workaround

Pinning `flashinfer-python==0.6.12 flashinfer-cubin==0.6.12 flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.12` on top of vLLM 0.25.0 fully restores prefill throughput (12,724 tok/s @131K) with no other regressions (needle-in-haystack 8/8, no OOM under load).

records.title: check_cuda_arch() rejects SM 12.0 (Blackwell) due to string comparison
records.body:
**Bug**
`check_cuda_arch()` in `jit/core.py` raises `RuntimeError: FlashInfer requires GPUs with sm75 or higher` on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM 12.0 / compute capability 12.0).

The check compares compute capability as a string, so `"12"` is evaluated as less than `"75"` lexicographically.

**To reproduce**
```python
import flashinfer
# on any SM 12.x GPU (RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000, B200, etc.)
from flashinfer.jit.core import check_cuda_arch
check_cuda_arch()  # raises RuntimeError
```

**Environment**
- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM 12.0, compute_120)
- FlashInfer: 0.6.11.post2
- PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130
- CUDA: 13.0
- Driver: 580.159.03

**Expected behavior**
SM 12.0 should be recognized as >= SM 7.5.

**Suggested fix**
Compare as integers instead of strings, e.g.:
```python
major, minor = torch.cuda.get_device_capability()
if major < 7 or (major == 7 and minor < 5):
    raise RuntimeError(...)
```

**Workaround**
`VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` bypasses the FlashInfer sampler, but disables FlashInfer-accelerated sampling entirely.

records.title: cutlass fused_moe: silent fp4 omission when built with CUDA < 12.8
records.body:
## Summary

When the JIT toolchain is older than CUDA 12.8, `jit/fused_moe.py` drops `-DENABLE_FP4` (line 120 in 0.6.13) and the `fused_moe_90` module builds successfully without any fp4 support. The first fp4-dependent call then fails deep in runner construction:

```
RuntimeError: Check failed: (false) is false: Could not construct fused moe op with the
requested input combination Activation: bfloat16, Weight: uint8, Output: bfloat16
```

That message names a dtype combination that IS supported on a >= 12.8 build (`isWFP4A16Quant()` with `use_w4_group_scaling=True`), so it reads as a caller bug. Nothing tells the user the module was built without fp4 or that the toolkit version is the reason. Debugging this required reading `flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe_binding.cu` against the jit flag generation.

## Environment / repro

flashinfer-python 0.6.13, H100 (SM90), system nvcc 12.4 (driver 550), torch 2.11.0+cu129. Triggered through vLLM serving gpt-oss-20b W4A16-MXFP4 over `cutlass_fused_moe` (bf16 activations, uint8-packed fp4 weights, `use_w4_group_scaling=True`). The JIT build itself completes with no fp4-related diagnostics. Installing `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.13+cu129` and rerunning the identical workload works, isolating the build toolkit as the only variable.

## Requests

1. Fail loudly or warn at build/module-load time: if an op whose signature requires fp4 (`use_w4_group_scaling`, nvfp4 paths) is requested from a module built without `ENABLE_FP4`, raise with the actual cause ("built with CUDA 12.4; fp4 paths require a 12.8+ toolkit or flashinfer-jit-cache") instead of the generic construction ICHECK. Even just appending the build toolkit version to the existing ICHECK message would cut the debugging time to zero.
2. Expose the capability programmatically, e.g. `flashinfer.jit.has_fp4_support()` (prebuilt module available, or local toolkit >= 12.8). Frameworks selecting between MoE backends need this to gate fp4 paths before committing to a multi-minute JIT build; today the only options are probing private jit internals or trying and catching. Corresponding consumer-side issue in vLLM: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/48541.

If the 12.8 requirement is intended and documented, this is purely about the failure mode and the missing query, not about supporting fp4 on older toolkits.

AI assistance was used to root-cause this; I reviewed the analysis and can defend it.

records.title: [Bug] nvfp4 unified-MoE on SM100: cumulative cross-call state corruption after ~50 varied-shape calls in one process (device-side gather assert; victim config moves)
records.body:
## Summary

While enabling `tests/moe/test_unified_moe_fuzz.py` for CI, the fuzzer surfaced a **silent out-of-bounds device write** in the nvfp4 unified-MoE stack on SM100: an earlier fuzz config corrupts device memory, and a later config (`nvfp4_uniform_e16_k8_t3_h1536_i256_s46`) then trips a `vectorized_gather_kernel index out of bounds` device-side assert when the corrupted memory is consumed as gather indices. The failure is **deterministic** (2/2 accumulated runs stop at the same test id) but **state-dependent**: the "failing" config passes cleanly in isolation, so it is the victim, not the culprit.

This is the C3/C5 class from the release-quality plan (#3605) — the device-state probe is doing exactly what it was designed to do.

## Environment

- B200-class SM100 board, driver 595.71.05
- torch 2.9.1+cu130, CUDA 13.2 (JIT), cutlass-dsl 4.6.1
- flashinfer main @ `ce40d25a` (MegaMoE integration), JIT install
- Wired nvfp4 backends exercised by the run: `cute_dsl_nvfp4` + `trtllm_fp4_routed`

## Repro (deterministic, ~18 min on warm JIT cache)

```bash
FLASHINFER_UMOE_FUZZ=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<sm100-idx> \
  pytest tests/moe/test_unified_moe_fuzz.py -q -x
```

Result (identical across 2 runs):

```
1 failed, 50 passed in ~18 min
FAILED tests/moe/test_unified_moe_fuzz.py::test_unified_moe_fuzz[nvfp4_uniform_e16_k8_t3_h1536_i256_s46]
/pytorch/.../IndexKernelUtils.cu:16: vectorized_gather_kernel: Assertion `ind >= 0 && ind < ind_dim_size` failed
```

- The assert is reported asynchronously at the fuzzer's device-state `torch.cuda.synchronize()`.
- After the failure, the process ends with `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'c10::AcceleratorError'` during interpreter shutdown (a pending CUDA error escaping a destructor) → core dump. **This also root-causes the "whole-process abort" from the 2026-06-09 triage note** that originally motivated gating the fuzzer opt-in: it is not a separate Heisenbug, it is the natural downstream of any device-side-assert finding in an accumulated run.

Victim-not-culprit evidence:

```bash
FLASHINFER_UMOE_FUZZ=1 CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 \
  pytest "tests/moe/test_unified_moe_fuzz.py::test_unified_moe_fuzz[nvfp4_uniform_e16_k8_t3_h1536_i256_s46]" -q
# 1 passed
```

## Suggested next steps

1. Prefix-bisect the ~23 preceding configs (seeds 23–45; the suite is seed-deterministic, so any subset reproduces exactly) to find the minimal culprit→victim pair.
2. `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` on the narrowed pair to name the kernel doing the OOB write.
3. Suspect surfaces: cutedsl nvfp4 atomic scatter-add finalize; `trtllm_fp4_routed` workspace/routing buffers (small-token + large-topk regime: the victim config is 3 tokens, top_k=8, e16).

Found while preparing the PR that enables this fuzzer in CI (linked below).

records.title: [Bug] MoE EP unit/mock tests fail on sm86 CUDA13 nightly due to real arch validation
records.body:
### Summary

  The nightly `test-nightly-build` job fails on the CUDA 13.0 shard when running MoE EP unit/mock tests on the `sm86` runner. https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/29303176529/job/87009219403

  This does not look like a real MoE EP runtime regression. The failing tests are mock/factory tests, but they currently hit the real `validate_arch_for_backend()` gate, which correctly requires `sm_90+` for `nccl_ep` / `nixl_ep`.

  ### Failure

  Nightly workflow runs this job on an `sm86` runner:

  ```yaml
  # .github/workflows/nightly-release.yml
  runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, x64, gpu, sm86, on-demand]
```
  The failing path is:

  scripts/task_jit_run_tests_part1.sh
    -> bash tests/moe_ep/run_tests.sh unit

  Failures:
```
  FAILED tests/moe_ep/nixl_ep/test_fleet_mock.py::test_fleet_init_calls_update_memory_and_connect
  FAILED tests/moe_ep/nixl_ep/test_fleet_mock.py::test_handle_combine_requires_topk_weights
  FAILED tests/moe_ep/nixl_ep/test_fleet_mock.py::test_update_topology_diffs_ranks
  FAILED tests/moe_ep/test_layer_factory.py::test_factory_returns_split_for_string_backend
  FAILED tests/moe_ep/test_layer_factory.py::test_factory_returns_split_for_nvep_config
```
  Representative error:

  flashinfer.moe_ep.core.validation.common.MoEEpArchError:
  nixl_ep requires sm_90+, host has sm_86

  and:

  flashinfer.moe_ep.core.validation.common.MoEEpArchError:
  nccl_ep requires sm_90+, host has sm_86

  ### Root Cause (By Codex)

  validate_arch_for_backend() correctly rejects pre-Hopper GPUs:

  cc = _device_capability()
  if cc < (9, 0):
      raise MoEEpArchError(f"{backend} requires sm_90+, host has sm_{cc[0]}{cc[1]}")

  This is expected for real nccl_ep / nixl_ep runtime usage.

  However, the failing tests are not real runtime/multirank/correctness tests:

  - tests/moe_ep/nixl_ep/test_fleet_mock.py uses a fake nixl_ep.Buffer and is intended to verify Buffer call sequencing / argument marshaling.
  - tests/moe_ep/test_layer_factory.py verifies that MoEEpLayer(...) routes to MoEEpSplitLayer.

  These tests currently only skip CUDA < 13, but do not skip or mock the sm_90+ arch gate. On CUDA 13 + sm86, the CUDA version check passes and the tests reach the real arch validation.

  The most directly related recent commit is:

  ce40d25a feat: MegaMoE Kernel integration in moe_ep (#3852)

  It added tests/moe_ep/test_layer_factory.py and moved split-layer initialization through the new validation path. The older NIXL mock tests already had an incomplete skip helper from af979cc9 that checked CUDA version but not compute capability.

  ### Expected Behavior

  unit + mock (no multirank) tests should not require Hopper/Blackwell hardware unless the test is explicitly validating runtime arch support.

  The real arch validation should still be tested by dedicated validation tests, e.g.:

  python -m pytest -v tests/moe_ep/test_arch_and_build.py::test_validate_arch_rejects_pre_hopper

  ### Proposed Fix (By Codex)

  Prefer mocking the arch validation in mock/factory tests instead of skipping all sm < 90 runs.

  Reason: these tests validate mock Buffer behavior and factory routing, not real backend hardware support. Skipping on sm80/sm86 would make CI green but lose useful unit coverage.

  Suggested changes:

  1. In tests/moe_ep/nixl_ep/test_fleet_mock.py, patch the backend module-local validation function in patched_loader:

  mock.patch.object(fleet, "validate_arch_for_backend", return_value=None)

  2. In tests/moe_ep/test_layer_factory.py, wrap the split MoEEpLayer(...) construction with:

  with mock.patch(
      "flashinfer.moe_ep.modes.split_layer.validate_arch_for_backend",
      return_value=None,
  ):
      ...

  This keeps the production sm_90+ gate intact while allowing mock/factory unit tests to run on sm80/sm86 CI.

  ### Acceptance Criteria

  - tests/moe_ep/test_arch_and_build.py::test_validate_arch_rejects_pre_hopper still passes.
  - tests/moe_ep/nixl_ep/test_fleet_mock.py no longer fails on CUDA13 + sm86 due to MoEEpArchError.
  - tests/moe_ep/test_layer_factory.py no longer fails on CUDA13 + sm86 due to MoEEpArchError.
  - Real multirank/correctness/smoke tests still require appropriate Hopper+ / Blackwell runners or skip via markers.

records.title: SM103 serving hang caused by TRTLLM_GEN_BMM artifact regeneration in #3708 (batched_gemm-dd6d23e-721ae60, 0.6.14): FP4 batched-GEMM clusters stuck in mbarrier phase wait
records.body:
## Summary

During sustained serving of Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4 (MoE, TP4, `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` via sglang) on GB300 (SM103), a TRTLLM_GEN_BMM kernel from the flashinfer-cubin 0.6.14 artifact intermittently never completes: a few thread-block clusters remain stuck in an mbarrier phase-wait loop after the rest of the grid has finished. The affected rank never reaches the next TP allreduce, peer ranks wait indefinitely in `ncclDevKernel_AllReduce`, and the NCCL watchdog eventually aborts the serving group.

**We attribute this regression to #3708 — specifically to the regenerated TRTLLM_GEN_BMM artifact it ships (`batched_gemm-dd6d23e-721ae60`), not to its host-side code changes.** The isolation is three-layered:

1. **Version window**: 0.6.13 (artifact `896b90b`) does not reproduce; 0.6.14 (artifact `dd6d23e-721ae60`) reproduces in 9 of 10 runs. The only changes to this artifact and its launch path in that window are #3708 and #3588.
2. **#3588 (PDL wiring) excluded**: forcing `device_support_pdl` to False (verified at runtime) still hangs.
3. **#3708 split-tested**: keeping flashinfer 0.6.14 fully intact — including #3708's host-side selection changes in `csrc/trtllm_batched_gemm_runner.cu` / `KernelRunner.h` — and substituting only the artifact contents with the previous generation (`batched_gemm-91e0ba0-da44fdf`, forcing a runtime JIT rebuild against its metainfo) eliminates the hang. The host half of #3708 is therefore exonerated; the artifact half is the trigger.

GPU core dumps of all four TP ranks, captured while wedged, are available.

## Environment

- GB300 (SM103), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.11.0+cu130
- sglang, disaggregated prefill, TP4, `moe-runner-backend: flashinfer_trtllm`
- flashinfer trio 0.6.14 (`flashinfer_python` / `flashinfer-cubin` / `flashinfer-jit-cache`); also reproduces with the wheels shipped in public sglang cu13 nightly images (20260711 and later)
- Workload: multi-turn 256k-context serving; token-per-expert counts vary per batch (dynamic-batch BMM variants)

## Evidence (from the core dumps)

Kernels resident on each GPU at capture time (3+ minutes after the last completed batch; all scheduler threads blocked on their next stream sync):

| rank | resident kernel | state |
|---|---|---|
| 0, 1, 3 | `ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_bf16_RING_LL`, grid (32,1,1)×(544,1,1) | waiting for peer |
| 2 | `bmm_Bfloat16_E2m1E2m1_Fp32_Ab16_Bb16tokFp32_t128x128x256_s6_et128x128_m256x128x64_c2x1x1_rM_TN_transOut_schPd2x1x2x3_biasFp32M_bN_rgTma_clmp_dynB_sm100f`, grid (32,1631,1)×(384,1,1), cluster dim (2,1,1) | stuck |

Residual state of the stuck kernel: 10 of 52,192 blocks (5 cluster pairs) still resident, the rest completed:

```
  BlockIdx To BlockIdx Count   State
*  (2,0,0)     (3,0,0)     2 running
   (0,1,0)     (1,1,0)     2 running
  (20,1,0)    (21,1,0)     2 running
  (16,2,0)    (17,2,0)     2 running
  (24,3,0)    (25,3,0)     2 running
```

All warps of the inspected block are in the same wait loop (SASS at `$pc`):

```
=> @!P0 NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680
   @!P0 SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64 P0[R5+URZ+0x33890],R3
   @!P0 BRA  <back to the poll>
```

The mbarrier phase never advances. With the NCCL watchdog enabled this surfaces as `Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: ... OpType=ALLREDUCE ... 600000ms` on the waiting ranks. Onset is intermittent: minutes to about 45 minutes of sustained serving (observed across roughly 30 occurrences; about one run in eight completes without hanging).

## Isolation experiments

Single-variable substitutions; same image, config, and hardware for every row. "Hang rate" counts full sustained-serving runs (about 4,300 prefill batches each when they complete).

| flashinfer trio | TRTLLM_GEN_BMM artifact in use | PDL | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.6.12 | `batched_gemm-91e0ba0-da44fdf` | default | 0 hangs in 20+ runs |
| 0.6.13 | `batched_gemm-91e0ba0-896b90b` | default | 0 hangs in 2 runs |
| 0.6.14 | `batched_gemm-dd6d23e-721ae60` | default (on) | hang in 9 of 10 runs |
| 0.6.14 | `batched_gemm-dd6d23e-721ae60` | forced off (`device_support_pdl` patched to False, verified at runtime) | hang in 1 of 2 runs — **PDL is not the trigger** |
| 0.6.14 | **`batched_gemm-91e0ba0-da44fdf` (substituted)** | default (on) | **0 hangs in 2 runs** |

Notes on the substitution row, since it is the load-bearing one:

- The prebuilt `fused_moe` modules in `flashinfer-jit-cache` (which carry a build-time artifact path) were removed, forcing a runtime JIT rebuild; the new artifact directory was deleted from `flashinfer-cubin` so any residual reference would fail loudly rather than silently fall back.
- Verified post-hoc: the rebuilt module's compile flags point at the old artifact's include directory, its binary contains none of the 504 kernel names that exist only in the new metainfo, and no runtime re-download of the new artifact occurred.
- The stuck kernel's name exists in both artifact generations with different cubin SHA-256, so the substituted runs exercise the same-named kernel compiled from the older generation.

## Root-cause attribution

**The regression entered with #3708's regeneration of the TRTLLM_GEN_BMM artifact (`91e0ba0-896b90b` → `dd6d23e-721ae60`), shipped in 0.6.14.** Since the artifact is a pregenerated cubin package, the defective change itself lives in the kernel-generator side that produced `dd6d23e`; within the flashinfer repo, #3708 is the terminal attribution. Supporting chronology:

- #3153 (May) bumped the artifact `91e0ba0-da44fdf` → `91e0ba0-896b90b`. That bump was reverted on `release-v0.6.12` (15886abd) but kept on main, so 0.6.13 ships `896b90b` — and 0.6.13 does **not** reproduce this hang. The `896b90b` generation is healthy; the break is specific to the `dd6d23e-721ae60` regeneration.
- #3708's host-side bias config selection changes (`csrc/trtllm_batched_gemm_runner.cu`, `KernelRunner.h`) are exonerated by the substitution experiment, which ran them unchanged against the older artifact with no hangs.

## Reproduction

Runnable recipes for this serving setup are in NVIDIA/InferenceMAX#117 (`benchmarks/multi_node/srt-slurm-recipes/sglang/qwen3.5/gb300-fp4/agentic/`). The hang reproduces on the disaggregated TP4↔TP4 agentic points (e.g. `disagg-gb300-1p1d-tp4-tp4-c64-mtp-convaware-jid2214439.yaml`, 2×GB300 nodes) with flashinfer 0.6.14 obtained either way:

- run the recipe image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260709-074bb928` and pip-install the trio at 0.6.14 (`flashinfer_python==0.6.14` from PyPI, `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.14` from https://flashinfer.ai/whl, `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.14` from https://flashinfer.ai/whl/cu130), or
- use any 20260711-or-later cu13 nightly image (ships 0.6.14 natively).

Dataset is public (`semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126-256k` on HF). Keep `--mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer` as in the recipes. Expected within minutes to about 45 minutes of sustained load: prefill batch lines stop, then the NCCL watchdog fires ALLREDUCE timeouts on the peer ranks. The 0.6.12 or 0.6.13 trios, aggregated (non-disaggregated) serving, or `no_buffer` do not reproduce it.

## Suggested change

- **Short term**: revert the TRTLLM_GEN_BMM artifact pointer to the previous generation (`91e0ba0-896b90b`, as shipped in 0.6.13) on main and the next release, following the precedent of the `release-v0.6.12` revert (15886abd). Our isolation shows both the `da44fdf` and `896b90b` generations run clean under the exact load that wedges `dd6d23e-721ae60`, and no host-side change is needed.
- **Root fix**: locate the defect in the generator that produced `dd6d23e-721ae60` — the failure mode is a cluster-pair mbarrier wait that never satisfies (TMA transaction/arrival accounting) in the dynamic-batch bias variants — and regenerate. We can turn around validation of candidate artifacts on the serving reproducer quickly; core dumps and cuda-gdb transcripts are available on request.

records.title: [RFC] Oracle #8 for the quality fuzzers: device-memory canaries (red zones + asset snapshots + scattered sentinels) — the OOB-write class that passes all 7 existing oracles
records.body:
## Motivation: the 7-oracle kit has a demonstrated blind spot

#3957 survived every oracle the quality fuzzers run today (numeric-vs-reference, NaN, determinism CRC, output-poison, tactic sweep, autotune-ON, device-state probe): a kernel that computes the **right answer** into its own output while **writing out of bounds elsewhere** passes all seven. The corruption only became visible ~45 configs later, when the stray writes happened to land on another backend's long-lived gather-index tensors — by then the failing test id pointed at an innocent victim, and the 2026-06-09 triage had already once written the whole thing off as an unexplained "whole-process abort".

During the #3957 hunt we prototyped a **device-memory canary probe** (384 checksummed sentinel tensors interleaved with freed gaps, verified after every config at native speed) — it bracketed the writer to a single config **on its first run**, where compute-sanitizer was unusable (~65× slowdown on CuteDSL workloads because every freshly-JIT'd cubin gets SASS-instrumented; and under the default caching allocator memcheck is structurally blind to intra-pool OOB anyway, since the whole segment is one valid allocation).

Proposal: promote this from a one-off debug script into **oracle #8 of the shared quality-fuzzer kit** (#3605), as an upgrade of the existing device-state probe.

## Design: three complementary pieces

| Piece | Mechanism | Catches | Character |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Red zones** | Allocate fuzzer-owned output buffers with guard margins filled with a known pattern; verify after each call | Near-boundary overruns: tile overhang, padding write-through, cluster-padding CTAs (the #3957 class fires exactly here — the epilogue wrote at `out[token, N]` ≡ one row past the slice) | **Deterministic**, names the overrun buffer |
| **Asset snapshots** | Checksum known long-lived device tensors (e.g. `_TRTLLM_PERMUTE_CACHE` index tensors) after each config | "Victim-class" corruption of persistent state — the exact #3957 manifestation | **Deterministic** for known assets |
| **Scattered canaries** | N seeded sentinel tensors interleaved with freed gaps across the pool; verify after each config | Wild pool-relative writes with no predictable victim | **Probabilistic** (density = knob); a net, not a proof of absence |

Honest scope note: stray addresses that are truly random 64-bit values hit unmapped VA and fault on their own — canaries add nothing there. Their value is precisely the observed dominant class: **pool-relative** bad addresses (`base + wrong offset`, stale pointers), which land in mapped memory and corrupt silently. #3957 ran 45+ configs without a single fault — that class is real and otherwise invisible.

## Rollout

1. Shared helper `tests/test_helpers/device_canary.py` (sibling of `fuzz_ledger.py`, same one-concept-for-all-fuzzers pattern): `arm(density)`, `verify(tag)`, plus a pytest-plugin wrapper for whole-file bracketing runs.
2. Wire into the unified MoE fuzzer and the scaled-GEMM fuzzer (#3539, now merged) as an **upgrade of check #7** (device-state probe) — not a new checklist item for reviewers.
3. **Default-ON in the fuzzers only** (not the general test suite): cost is ~50 MB + a few ms of device reductions per config; canaries have no legitimate writers, and verification happens after synchronize, outside any CUDA-graph capture (guard with `is_current_stream_capturing`). General-suite adoption can be revisited once SNR is proven.
4. Document the probabilistic nature and the density knob; on a trip, the deterministic follow-up is per-phase verification (the #3957 hunt's per-tactic monkeypatch localized the writer to a single `(runner, tactic)`).

## Prior art

- `compute-sanitizer --padding` (cudaMalloc-granularity red zones) — same concept, ~65× cost on JIT-heavy workloads; this proposal is the always-on cheap version.
- ASan redzones on the host side.
- Validation case: #3957 (first-run bracket) — any implementation must be able to catch it before the fix lands, and stays as the regression example after.

Refs: #3605 (release-quality plan), #3957 (motivating bug + live validation), #3958 (MoE fuzzer enablement; the debug knobs used in the hunt), #3539 (GEMM fuzzer, merged).

records.title: [BUG] Prefill kernel Qwen3.5 high concurrency
records.body:
Problem description:
Using vllm 0.21.0 with model Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B and structured outputs, and under high concurrency (around 1K) we noticed a hang on H100.
In version 0.21.0, you will notice the hang around 5 to 20 minutes while I also tested 0.25.0 and the hang shows up after 8 to 9 hours.
For debugging purposes, I recommend using vllm 0.21.0 that will show the hang faster.
The workaround for now is using triton kernel for the prefill: ```--gdn-prefill-backend triton```

Steps to reproduce the error:
Build the docker image, and inside the image run:
```bash repro_flashinfer_gdn_hang.sh```

To run with the workaround, use:
```GDN_PREFILL_BACKEND=triton bash repro_flashinfer_gdn_hang.sh```

Dockerfile
```
FROM vllm/vllm-openai:v0.21.0

# Optional debug tooling for capturing the stuck GPU kernel with cuda-gdb.
# The minimal repro only needs the base image above; this layer is for triage.
RUN set -eux; \
    apt-get update; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends gdb curl; \
    CUDA_DIR="$(readlink -f /usr/local/cuda)"; \
    CUDA_SUFFIX="$(basename "$CUDA_DIR" | sed 's/^cuda-//' | cut -d. -f1-2 | tr '.' '-')"; \
    if apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends "cuda-gdb-${CUDA_SUFFIX}"; then \
        echo "installed cuda-gdb-${CUDA_SUFFIX}"; \
    else \
        apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nvidia-cuda-gdb || true; \
    fi; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

ENV PATH="/usr/local/cuda/bin:${PATH}"

WORKDIR /repro
COPY . /repro/
RUN chmod +x /repro/repro_flashinfer_gdn_hang.sh /repro/zombie_repro_generic.py

# Example:
#   docker build -t flashinfer-gdn-repro .
#   docker run --gpus all --rm -it \
#     -e HF_TOKEN=$HF_TOKEN \
#     -v $PWD/logs:/repro/logs \
#     flashinfer-gdn-repro \
#     bash repro_flashinfer_gdn_hang.sh
```

**Copy these files inside the docker container and run the script**

[repro_flashinfer_gdn_hang.sh](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30064700/repro_flashinfer_gdn_hang.sh)
[response_format_generic.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30064701/response_format_generic.json)
[system_prompt_generic.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30064702/system_prompt_generic.txt)
[zombie_repro_generic.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30064699/zombie_repro_generic.py)

TLDR:

* Stuck kernel: cutlass::device_kernel<flat::kernel::FlatKernelTmaWarpSpecializedDeltaRule<...>>
* GPU: H100 sm_90, kernel stays Active with ~100% util / ~125W
* Mitigation: vLLM --gdn-prefill-backend triton avoids FlashInfer prefill; validated stable 2h

records.title: [Bug]`test_bmm_fp8.py` regression: cuDNN tuple tactic can be replayed on cuBLAS runner after #3707
records.body:
## Summary

Found unit-test error in https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/365155065/raw `tests/gemm/test_bmm_fp8.py` started failing with:
```
    TypeError: '>=' not supported between instances of 'tuple' and 'int'
    /workspace/flashinfer/flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py:214
```
This appears to be a regression introduced by #3707 (b35396c1 Yanqinz/autotuner tactic).#3707 changed cuDNN GEMM tactics from integer plan indices to structured (engine_id, knob_items) tuples, but the autotuner cache still stores runner_id as an index relative to the runner list used during the original tuning call. When the same cached cuDNN entry is reused from a later call whose runner list has a different ordering, the tuple tactic can be dispatched to a non-cuDNN runner.

## Failure
Observed in:  tests/gemm/test_bmm_fp8.py
Failure snippet:
```
    E   TypeError: '>=' not supported between instances of 'tuple' and 'int'
    E   /workspace/flashinfer/flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py:214
```
    The failing line is in the cuBLAS FP8 BMM runner: 
    if tactic >= 0:
    This runner expects an integer tactic, but receives a tuple.

## Suspected Cause (By Codex)
After #3707, CudnnFp8GemmRunner.get_valid_tactics() returns tuple tactics via:
```
    return _cudnn_graph_engine_knob_tactics(graph)
```
The autotuner stores cache entries as:
```
    self.profiling_cache[cache_key] = (runner_id, tactic, p)
```
where runner_id is only meaningful for the runner list used during that specific choose_one() call.

A likely sequence is:

    1. backend="cudnn" tunes bmm_fp8; runner list is [CudnnFp8GemmRunner], so cached value stores runner_id=0 and
       tactic=(engine_id, knob_items).
    2. Later backend="auto" runs for the same shape/profile. For FP8 e5m2 cases, CUTLASS is excluded, so runner list can be
       [CublasFp8GemmRunner, CudnnFp8GemmRunner].
    3. search_cache() finds the cuDNN cache key, but returns stale runner_id=0.
    4. Current runners[0] is cuBLAS, so cuBLAS receives the cuDNN tuple tactic and fails at tactic >= 0.

Before #3707, this was masked because cuDNN tactics were integer plan indices.

## Expected Behavior
A cached tactic should only be replayed on the same runner implementation it was tuned for. cuDNN tuple tactics should never be passed to cuBLAS/CUTLASS integer-tactic runners.

## Proposed Fix (By Codex)
Primary fix:
    - Do not store list-relative runner_id in profiling_cache.
    - Since search_cache() already iterates over the current runners, cache values can store only (tactic, profile), and on hit return the current loop index for the matched runner.

    For file configs:

    - If a stored runner_name is not present in the current runner list, skip that config instead of falling back to index 0.

Additional guard:
    - Integer-only runners such as CublasFp8GemmRunner can defensively reject non-int tactics and fall back to -1, but the cache semantics fix should be the main change.

cc: @aleozlx @yanqinz2

records.title: [Bug] FA2 CUDA-graph no-split plans launch padded CTAs over uninitialized scheduler entries
records.body:
## Description

FA2 tensor-core decode can launch CUDA-graph blocks beyond the scheduler entries initialized by the planner when all of these hold:

- `enable_cuda_graph=True`
- `disable_split_kv=True`
- tensor-core FA2 path
- a uniform decode query length

The scheduler constructs entries only for real request, query-tile, and KV-tile work, then pads `padded_batch_size` with the split-KV occupancy target. Since split-KV is disabled, the planner neither initializes the padded scheduler tail nor creates `block_valid_mask`. The FA2 kernel uses `padded_batch_size` directly as grid-x.

The same mechanics remain on current main at `71d31b5a23a3c0394edb36330dec1ce2a0def365`:

- [One-token decode passes `uniform_q_len=0`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/71d31b5a23a3c0394edb36330dec1ce2a0def365/flashinfer/decode.py#L1215-L1241)
- [The scheduler creates real entries and then pads grid-x](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/71d31b5a23a3c0394edb36330dec1ce2a0def365/include/flashinfer/attention/scheduler.cuh#L621-L680)
- [Validity storage is allocated only for split-KV](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/71d31b5a23a3c0394edb36330dec1ce2a0def365/include/flashinfer/attention/scheduler.cuh#L855-L878)
- [The kernel launches `padded_batch_size` blocks in grid-x](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/71d31b5a23a3c0394edb36330dec1ce2a0def365/include/flashinfer/attention/prefill.cuh#L4150-L4172)

## Reproduction and evidence

Tested on an H100 80GB SXM5 with 132 SMs, batch size 2, 16 query heads, 2 KV heads, head dimension 128, page size 1, one query row per request, and split-KV disabled.

The planner returned grid-x 132 although it initialized only two scheduler entries. Filling the page-locked integer workspace with `0xA5` before planning left the first tail entries at `0xA5A5A5A5`. The poisoned plan was inspected and intentionally not launched.

With a controlled zeroed tail, Nsight captured grid `(132, 1, 2)`, or 264 CTAs, while the exact initialized grid is `(2, 1, 2)`, or 4 CTAs. This demonstrates redundant execution. Reused nonzero workspace contents create a conditional stale-index correctness risk; this report does not claim unconditional output corruption.

For a uniform decode query length, the exact graph-stable grid is:

`batch_size * ceil((q_len_per_request * num_qo_heads / num_kv_heads) / cta_tile_q)`

## Expected behavior

A no-split CUDA-graph plan must not launch blocks whose scheduler entries were never initialized. When query length is a checked graph invariant, the planner can use the exact initialized grid. Ragged and split-KV paths should retain their current behavior.

## Proposed fixes

- Root planner fix: [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4794](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4794)
- Guarded integration fix for SGLang's pinned FlashInfer release: [sgl-project/sglang#36785](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36785)

records.title: v0.6.15 release highlights draft
records.body:
### v0.6.15 Highlights

This release ships **Expert Parallelism (`moe_ep`) in the default install** and extends the **TRTLLM-GEN MoE** stack for large-model serving. It broadens **Blackwell** model coverage — Gemma 4 / MiniMax-M3 MoE on consumer / DGX-Spark SM12x, DeepSeek-class MLA decode on B300, and context-parallel GDN on SM120 — and adds **Video Sparse Attention** plus **CUDA-graph-safe FP8 all-reduce fusion** for distributed inference.

**Unified MoE API with Expert Parallelism (Experimental API to try!)**

FlashInfer's unified MoE compute API is now wired into **expert parallelism**. A new `flashinfer.moe_ep.MoEEpLayer` runs one MoE layer split across ranks as **dispatch → per-expert grouped GEMM → combine**, over pluggable transport (**NCCL-EP** via `nccl.ep`/`nccl4py`, and **NIXL-EP**). The expert GEMM reuses the unified `flashinfer.fused_moe.MoELayer` as a pure per-expert grouped GEMM — routing lives in dispatch/combine. `moe_ep` is part of the **default install** (CUDA 13+), with vLLM-facing APIs and checkpoint-safe MoE all-to-all graph VAs. This EP API is also the integration surface for **MegaMoE** kernels in upcoming releases — try it out and let us know how it works for you.

- #3686
- #3821
- #3813
- #3727
- #3591

**Gemma 4 and MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 MoE now run on Blackwell SM12x**

Gemma 4 and MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 MoE now run on **Blackwell SM12x** (consumer / DGX Spark), enabled by two new NVFP4 MoE activation functions — **gelu_tanh** and **swiglu_oai** — added to the SM12x MoE path.

- #3744
- #3737

**TRTLLM-GEN MoE adds shared experts, DeepSeek-V4 routing, and low-latency FP8**

TRTLLM-GEN MoE gains shared-expert fusion for FP8 paths, hash-based DeepSeek-V4 routing (`hash_topk`), and a fused FP8 blockwise megakernel that cuts latency for small batches (BS ≤ 8).

- #2625
- #3561
- #3424

**Video Sparse Attention and DeepSeek MLA decode on Blackwell B300**

Video Sparse Attention (VSA) is now integrated into the block-sparse attention API, bringing efficient long-context attention for video diffusion models to FlashInfer. DeepSeek-class MLA decode extends onto **Blackwell B300 (SM103)** with cluster-aware CUTLASS `split_kv`, and CuTe-DSL GQA decode adds sliding-window and attention-sink masking for newer attention variants.

- #3250
- #3888
- #3794

**Linear attention: context-parallel GDN on SM120 and faster KDA decode**

Gated delta-rule (GDN) linear attention adds **SM120 context-parallel delta rule** support, extending the CuTe-DSL GDN rewrite from 0.6.14 onto Blackwell SM120 prefill, alongside SM90 context-parallel prefill optimizations. KDA recurrent-decode kernels are also optimized for lower decode latency.

- #3659
- #3788
- #3766

**Distributed comm: FP8 fusion and CUDA-graph checkpoint restore**

Dynamic per-token FP8 quantization fuses into allreduce + residual + RMSNorm (TRT-LLM and MNNVL backends, CUDA-graph safe). All-reduce workspaces support `checkpoint_prepare` / `checkpoint_restore` so physical backing can be released and remapped at stable VAs across serving checkpoints.

records.title: GB300 (SM103): enable_flashinfer_autotune triggers cudaErrorNotPermitted during CUDA-graph capture for NVFP4 MoE
records.body:
## Summary

On **GB300** (Blackwell-Ultra, SM103, `compute_cap 10.3`), enabling
`enable_flashinfer_autotune` for **NVFP4 block-scale MoE** models makes vLLM engine
startup crash at **CUDA-graph capture** with:

```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted
```
(`cudaErrorNotPermitted`), raised from `torch.cuda.graph(...).capture_end()`.

Importantly, the **FlashInfer autotune sweep itself completes cleanly**
(`[Autotuner]: Autotuning process ends`) — the crash happens *afterwards*, during
CUDA-graph capture. This is therefore distinct from #3197 (illegal-memory access
*during* the `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` sweep), which appears resolved in 0.6.14.

## Environment

- FlashInfer **0.6.14**
- vLLM **0.24.0**
- GPU: **NVIDIA GB300** (SM103 / `compute_cap 10.3`), single GPU, TP=1
- `quantization=modelopt_fp4`, `enable_flashinfer_autotune=true`
- container run as root

## Reproduce (dummy weights are sufficient)

```bash
vllm bench throughput \
  --model=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 \
  --load-format=dummy --quantization=modelopt_fp4 --tensor-parallel-size=1 \
  --num-prompts=128 --input-len=256 --output-len=256 --max-model-len=2048 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization=0.9 --trust-remote-code \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": true}'
```

## Observed

The FP4 autotune sweep finishes, then during
`Capturing CUDA graphs (mixed prefill-decode, PIECEWISE)` it dies deterministically at
~graph 26/51:

```
[Autotuner]: Autotuning process ends
Capturing CUDA graphs (mixed prefill-decode, PIECEWISE):  51%|#####     | 26/51
...
  File ".../torch/cuda/graphs.py", line 169, in capture_end
    super().capture_end()
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

Reproduced 2/2 with the crash at the same graph index.

## What isolates it (A/B)

| condition | result |
|---|---|
| GB300, autotune **ON** | **crash** at CUDA-graph capture |
| GB300, autotune **OFF** | clean, runs to completion |
| B300 (also SM103 / cap 10.3), autotune **ON** | clean |
| MoE backend | **backend-independent** — `moe_backend=flashinfer_trtllm` crashes on `Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4`; `moe_backend=flashinfer_cutlass` crashes on `Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4` |

So the failure is **GB300-specific, autotune-gated, and not tied to a single MoE backend**
— an autotuned tactic selected on GB300 appears not to be CUDA-graph-capture-safe. B300
(same SM103 compute capability) is unaffected, so a compute-capability gate is insufficient;
it is specific to GB300.

## Notes

- Related predecessor: #3197 (illegal-memory during the same FP4-MoE autotune sweep) — that
  one no longer reproduces in 0.6.14; this graph-capture crash is a separate, later failure.
- Workaround today: keep `enable_flashinfer_autotune` disabled on GB300.
- The `nvidia/...-NVFP4` checkpoints may be gated on Hugging Face; any NVFP4 block-scale-MoE
  checkpoint that selects a FlashInfer MoE backend on GB300 should exhibit the same path
  (dummy weights are enough — no real weights needed to trigger the crash).

records.title: RFC: JIT/AOT package KPIs
records.body:
## Context

This is a smaller RFC carved out of the broader design-doc PR in #3654. The goal is to get signoff on the top-level KPIs first, before continuing to refine the longer implementation/design document.

FlashInfer has three related runtime artifact paths:

- `flashinfer-python`: core package, runtime JIT source generation/compilation, and on-demand cubin downloads where needed.
- `flashinfer-jit-cache`: optional package containing prebuilt JIT shared libraries for covered specializations.
- `flashinfer-cubin`: optional package containing pre-downloaded cubin/header artifacts for cubin-backed paths.

The main tradeoff is between package/image size, workload coverage, and startup/warmup overhead. This issue proposes the KPI set we should optimize and report over time.

One concrete starting constraint: GitHub Releases currently requires each release asset to be under 2 GiB, even though GitHub does not limit the total size of a release or release bandwidth. Since FlashInfer wheels are distributed through GitHub Releases, keeping each wheel below that per-asset ceiling is an immediate packaging requirement and one of the reasons this KPI discussion began. See GitHub's release storage and bandwidth quotas: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/about-releases#storage-and-bandwidth-quotas

## Decision Requested

Do we agree that these are the right high-level KPIs for the JIT/AOT packaging strategy?

| KPI | What good looks like | Measurement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Package size | Wheels remain practical for image builds/pulls, stay under GitHub Releases' per-asset limit, and grow predictably as kernels are added | Wheel size by package (`flashinfer-python`, `flashinfer-jit-cache`, `flashinfer-cubin`), CUDA index, and architecture set; distance to the 2 GiB GitHub Releases per-asset limit; optionally image-size delta and bytes by API/artifact family |
| Model/workload coverage with all packages installed | A representative workload suite runs with zero runtime JIT and zero runtime artifact downloads when `flashinfer-jit-cache` and `flashinfer-cubin` are installed | Missing `JitSpec.name` count and missing cubin/header count with `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1` and `FLASHINFER_NO_DOWNLOAD=1`; target 0 for the agreed workload matrix |
| JIT/download overhead when optional packages are absent | Cold compile/download overhead is bounded and understandable for users who install only `flashinfer-python` or a partial package set | Cold first-call or warmup latency per representative API/module, broken down into runtime compile time vs. cubin download time, across agreed package/cache scenarios |

Detailed functional requirements still matter, but should be tracked separately as engineering checks. Examples: version mismatches fail early, shared caches are race-safe, logs identify whether the first call hit AOT/local JIT/runtime compile/download, and disable-JIT/no-download modes fail fast.

## Proposed Measurement Shape

For workload coverage:

1. Install `flashinfer-python`, `flashinfer-jit-cache`, and `flashinfer-cubin` in an isolated environment.
2. Run the representative workload suite outside the source checkout.
3. Set:

```bash
export FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1
export FLASHINFER_NO_DOWNLOAD=1
export FLASHINFER_JIT_CACHE_REPORT_FILE=/tmp/flashinfer_jit_cache_report.json
```

4. Report missing `JitSpec.name` values and missing cubin/header artifacts, grouped by model, framework path, backend, dtype, KV cache dtype, head dimension, page size, CUDA version, and GPU architecture where available.

For cold-start/warmup overhead, measure at least:

| Scenario | Packages | Cache state | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Core only, true cold | `flashinfer-python` | empty JIT cache and empty cubin cache | downloads/JIT allowed |
| Core plus cubin | `flashinfer-python`, `flashinfer-cubin` | empty JIT cache | isolates JIT overhead when cubins are local |
| Core plus JIT cache | `flashinfer-python`, `flashinfer-jit-cache` | empty cubin cache | isolates cubin/download overhead when JIT `.so` coverage exists |
| Fully prebuilt/offline | all three packages | empty user cache | `FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1`, `FLASHINFER_NO_DOWNLOAD=1` |
| Warm cache restart | `flashinfer-python` only | runtime cache already populated at same `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE` | validates persisted runtime-cache reuse |

For each scenario, report import time, model/engine initialization time, explicit FlashInfer warmup time, first-token/first-request latency, repeated steady-state latency, runtime JIT build count, cubin download count, and failure mode.

## Signoff Questions

- Are the three proposed KPIs the right top-level set?
- What representative model/workload matrix should define coverage for vLLM, SGLang, and direct FlashInfer use?
- Beyond the hard 2 GiB GitHub Releases per-asset ceiling, what package-size or image-size budgets should we use initially?
- What cold-start, engine-start, first-token, or warmup latency budgets should we use initially?
- Which results should be release-blocking CI gates versus advisory/nightly reports?
- Should customer-owned/workload-pruned AOT wheels be treated as part of the KPI plan now, or tracked as a follow-up deliverable?

## Out of Scope for This RFC

- Final design for custom/pruned AOT package generation.
- Full implementation details for trace-to-manifest workflows.
- Exhaustive per-API coverage enumeration.
- Detailed UX/logging requirements beyond what is needed to measure the KPIs above.

## References

- Broader draft/design doc: #3654
- Reviewer feedback in #3654 suggested splitting high-level KPIs from detailed engineering requirements and focusing first on package size, model/workload coverage, and JIT time when optional packages are not installed.

records.title: [Bug] SM90 CUTLASS FP8 grouped-GEMM MoE: WARP_ILLEGAL_INSTR_PARAM at UTMALDG.2D — invalid TMA descriptor, race-like, strongly aggravated by CUDA graphs
records.body:
Summary

Serving nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8 with vLLM 0.17.1 on 2× H200 NVL (TP=2), the FlashInfer CUTLASS SM90 FP8 grouped-GEMM MoE kernel crashes the GPU with CUDBG_EXCEPTION_WARP_ILLEGAL_INSTR_PARAM (27).

Disassembly at the faulting PC shows the exception is raised by a TMA bulk load consuming a TMA descriptor:

0x7fc8359d56b0:  UTMALDG.2D desc[UR22][UR4][UR10]     <-- faulting instruction (exception PC)

i.e. the TMA descriptor (TensorMap) was invalid at consumption time. In this ptr-array/grouped kernel the tensormaps are maintained in a device-side workspace and updated per group, so an invalid descriptor here points at the tensormap workspace being stale, mid-update, or overwritten when the load issues — consistent with a race between MoE metadata/descriptor preparation and kernel execution.

The crash reproduces across eager and torch.compile modes, two different nodes, and both TP ranks, always in the same kernel; in two independent captures (live cuda-gdb and a GPU coredump from a separate run) the faulting PC was byte-identical (0x7fc8359d56b0).

Crash latency depends dramatically on launch timing, which is the classic signature of a race window:

Configuration | Time to crash -- | -- torch.compile + cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | ~15 s (first or second request) torch.compile + cudagraph_mode=NONE | no crash observed in limited testing

A plausible mechanism consistent with all observations: with vLLM's async scheduling (step N+1 prepared while step N executes) and especially with CUDA-graph replay (same workspace addresses reused every step, minimal launch gaps), the grouped-GEMM tensormap workspace for the next invocation can be written while the previous invocation's kernel is still consuming it. Serializing launches (CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1) narrows the window to near-zero; graph replay widens it to near-certainty.

Faulting kernel

Demangled (abbreviated):

cutlass::device_kernel<cutlass::gemm::kernel::GemmUniversal<
  cutlass::gemm::GroupProblemShape<cute::tuple<long,long,long>>,
  CollectiveMma<MainloopSm90ArrayTmaGmmaWarpSpecialized<10, ...>,
                KernelPtrArrayTmaWarpSpecializedCooperativeFP8FastAccum, ...
                float_e4m3_t A/B, TiledMMA<SM90_GMMA MMA_64x32x32_F32E4M3E4M3_SS_TN>,
                SM90_TMA_LOAD / SM90_TMA_LOAD_MULTICAST>,
  CollectiveEpilogue<Sm90PtrArrayTmaWarpSpecialized<1,1,16,false,false,2>,
                     bfloat16_t output, LinearCombination, SM90_TMA_STORE>>>

Launch config at crash: grid (2,66,1), cluster dim (2,1,1), block (384,1,1). Exception at device 0, SM 0, warp 3, lane 0, PC 0x7fc8359d56b0 (kernel+25520).

Disassembly around the faulting PC

kernel+25456:  UIADD3 UR12, UR19, 0x28000, UR12
kernel+25472:  LOP3.LUT R3, R3, R6, RZ, 0x3c, !PT
...
kernel+25520:  UTMALDG.2D desc[UR22][UR4][UR10]        <-- FAULT (WARP_ILLEGAL_INSTR_PARAM)
...
kernel+25616:  LEA R3, R19.reuse, UR19, 0x3
kernel+25632:  BSSY B1, 0x7fc8359d5790
kernel+25648:  SHF.L.U32 R2, R0, 0x1f, RZ
kernel+25664:  LEA R8, R19, UR19, 0x4
kernel+25680:  @P0 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.A1T0 RZ[UR19+0x34538], RZ

The surrounding block is the TMA producer path (mbarrier arrive-with-transaction, uniform-register descriptor/buffer addressing), all based off the same uniform registers loaded from the per-group metadata.

Environment

  • Model: nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8 (ModelOpt FP8 checkpoint)
  • vLLM: 0.17.1 (V1 engine, async scheduling enabled)
  • FlashInfer: 0.6.4
  • MoE backend selected by vLLM: FLASHINFER_CUTLASS (candidates listed at startup: AITER, FLASHINFER_TRTLLM, FLASHINFER_CUTLASS, DEEPGEMM, TRITON, MARLIN)
  • GPUs: 2× NVIDIA H200 NVL (SM90), TP=2, disable_custom_all_reduce=True
  • dtype: bf16 activations, FP8 E4M3 weights, kv_cache_dtype=fp8_e4m3
  • PyTorch: 2.10.0+cu128

Reproduction

  1. vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8 -tp 2 (defaults select the FLASHINFER_CUTLASS FP8 MoE backend; CUDA graphs FULL_AND_PIECEWISE by default)
  2. Send ordinary chat-completion traffic (agentic workload, ~1–2 concurrent requests, prompts ~1–2k tokens, generation a few hundred tokens)
  3. GPU fault within the first one or two requests (~15 s of inference)

CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered) but the device-level exception and PC are identical whenever captured.

MODEL_PATH="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8" VLLM_PORT=8000 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 TORCH_LOGS="+dynamo,+inductor,+graph_breaks,+dynamic" python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \ --model "${MODEL}" \ --port "${VLLM_PORT}" \ --host "localhost" \ --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ --max-model-len 32768 \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 \ --enable-chunked-prefill \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 256 \ --disable-custom-all-reduce \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --trust-remote-code \ --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}' & VLLM_PID=$! echo "vLLM PID: ${VLLM_PID}"

records.title: Refactor Batch MLA Wrapper and Backends

Refactor Batch MLA into an operation-owned private package while preserving the existing public `flashinfer.mla` API and compatibility bindings.
- Move Batch MLA orchestration into `flashinfer/mla/_batch_mla/`, with `_core.py` and `_planning.py` owning the public adapters and planning lifecycle.

records.title: [Perf][Bug] v0.6.15 autotuner: O(n^2) hash-collision in `_find_nearest_profile` lru_cache ## Summary
records.body:
## Description
In 0.6.15, every eager call through `AutoTuner.choose_one` with a per-call `TuningConfig` (e.g. `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla`) builds a cache key that hashes identically to all previous keys but never compares equal. The `@lru_cache` on `AutoTuner._find_nearest_profile` degenerates into one collision chain: each call linearly scans all prior entries with `__eq__`, so host overhead grows O(n^2) with call count


Measured (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, SGLang, 4x GB300, TP4, DSA, ~74k-token prefills, concurrency 8):
| flashinfer | c=8 mean TPOT | total throughput |
|---|---|---|
| 0.6.14 | 12.60 ms | 132k tok/s |
| 0.6.15 | **29.53 ms** | **62.9k tok/s** |

## Root cause
1. `_build_mla_decode_tuning_config` (`mla/_core.py`) creates a fresh `TuningConfig` per
   call, with fresh closures in `DynamicTensorSpec.tensor_initializers`.
2. `DynamicTensorSpec.__hash__` skips `tensor_initializers` (its own
   `# FIXME: currently not hashing tensor_initializers`) and hashes
   `id(map_to_tuning_buckets)`; the dataclass-generated `__eq__` compares all fields,
   including the fresh closures, so two calls' configs never compare equal.
3. New in 0.6.15: `make_bucket_mapper` gained `@lru_cache`, so it returns the same mapper
   object every call, and same-shape configs now all hash identically. (In 0.6.14 it
   returned a fresh closure, so hashes differed, keys scattered, and lookups stayed O(1).)
Identical hash + never equal means one dict bucket, an O(n) `__eq__` scan per call, O(n^2)
overall.

records.title: nvfp4-KV: strided scale-factor / paged-data tensors silently corrupt fa2/XQA output (no error)
records.body:
### Environment

```
GPU: RTX 5090 (SM120, 32 GB) | driver 595.71.05, CUDA 13.2
flashinfer-python 0.6.13 | torch 2.11.0
```

### The problem

The fa2 prefill and XQA decode nvfp4-KV paths take the KV scale-factor tensors as raw-pointer additional tensors and don't validate contiguity. Passing strided views (in our case, views sliced out of a packed `[data | scale]` per-row cache layout) produces:

- strided **scale factors** → NaN output (stride garbage decoded as e4m3 scales)
- strided **data** with contiguous scales → deterministically wrong output, cos 0.927 vs 0.947 for the correct result - close enough to look plausible, which is the dangerous part

There's already an ICHECK that k and v strides match each other (`TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(paged_k_cache.stride(i), paged_v_cache.stride(i))`) but nothing requires the strides to be dense, and the sf tensors get no stride checks at all.

### Ask

ICHECK contiguity on the sf tensors and the packed data at the ffi boundary so this fails loudly. Stride support would be nicer but the silent wrong-answer mode is the actual problem. Small standalone repro available (quantize with `nvfp4_quantize_paged_kv_cache`, re-slice as strided views, compare `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper.run` output against a bf16 reference).

Unrelated but positive: the SM120 XQA nvfp4 path checks out numerically end to end once inputs are contiguous - bf16 KV gives cos 1.00000 vs reference at 8K context, and we have it running under vLLM at 245K-token context on a 5090 (vllm-project/vllm#49011).

records.title: [Bug] SM120 fused-MoE gemm1 tactic profiling followed by illegal instruction
records.body:
## Environment

- 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition (SM120), tensor parallel size 2
- CUDA toolkit 13.3; FlashInfer runtime metadata reports CUDA 13.0 and cuBLAS 13.6.0
- `flashinfer-python==0.6.15.dev20260718`, `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.15.dev20260718`
- FlashInfer `nightly-v0.6.15-20260718` (`82784bb112c32bb38e4d7ee171eab4855ad4f91a`)
- vLLM `0.23.1rc1.dev1263+gc233d90aa.d20260718.cu133`
- Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`
- MoE backend `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP8`

## Reproduction

Start vLLM with FlashInfer autotuning enabled:

```text
--tensor-parallel-size 2
--max-num-batched-tokens 4096
--speculative-config {"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}
--enable-flashinfer-autotune
--attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4
--kernel-config.moe_backend flashinfer_cutlass
```

## Observed behavior

During mixed-token warmup, the autotuner completes six `sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4` entries and then begins fused-MoE tactic profiling:

```text
[AutoTuner]: Tuning sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4: 6/6
[AutoTuner]: Tuning trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1: 0/21
Error: Failed to initialize the TMA descriptor 715
...
[Autotuner]: Skipped 20 unsupported tactic(s) for trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1
[AutoTuner]: Tuning trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1: 1/21
```

The next tensor allocation inside the tuner fails:

```text
flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py:634 in cutlass_fused_moe
  _, gemm_tactic_1 = tuner.choose_one(...)
flashinfer/autotuner/autotuner.py:1589 in choose_one
flashinfer/autotuner/autotuner.py:2104 in _prepare_input_tensors
flashinfer/autotuner/initializers.py:69 in _rand_scaled
  torch.rand(...)
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered
```

CUDA errors can be reported asynchronously, so this identifies where the error surfaced, not the faulting launch. The failure reproduced on at least three consecutive fresh-cache starts. The tuner cache written by a failed start contains the six sparse-MLA entries and no fused-MoE selection.

## Control

With both fused-MoE operation names passed to this autotune context through `skip_ops`, a fresh-cache startup completed sparse-MLA tuning, all 1,064 vLLM warmup cases, CUDA-graph capture, and serving requests. The resulting cache contained 24 sparse-MLA configurations. The log contained no fused-MoE tuning attempt, TMA descriptor failure, or illegal-instruction error.

```text
trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1
trtllm::fused_moe::gemm2
```

Only `gemm1` appears in the failing log; no independent `gemm2` failure was observed.

## Additional context

The failing module is `get_cutlass_fused_moe_module("120")`. The tested nightly contains #3614, which addresses the MXFP8-weight/MXFP8-activation profiler path; this case uses MXFP4 weights and MXFP8 activations.

## Expected behavior

Tactic profiling should not leave the CUDA context unusable.

records.title: [Bug]: Cascade state merging returns NaN when all input states are empty
records.body:
## Observed behavior

FlashInfer represents an empty attention state as zero V with logsumexp equal to negative infinity. Merging two such states currently produces NaN for both the attention output and logsumexp.

This affects `merge_state`, `merge_state_in_place`, and reductions using `state_t::merge`, including `merge_states` and persistent attention reductions.

## Reproduction

The official trace reference reproduces the failure:

```python
import torch
from flashinfer.trace.templates.cascade import merge_state_trace

v_a = torch.zeros((1, 1, 64), dtype=torch.float16)
v_b = torch.zeros_like(v_a)
s_a = torch.full((1, 1), -torch.inf, dtype=torch.float32)
s_b = torch.full_like(s_a, -torch.inf)

v, s = merge_state_trace.reference(v_a, s_a, v_b, s_b)

print(torch.isnan(v).any().item())  # True
print(torch.isnan(s).any().item())  # True
```

The merge formula evaluates:

```text
s_a = s_b = -inf
s_max = max(s_a, s_b) = -inf
exp2(s_a - s_max) = exp2(-inf - -inf) = NaN
```

## Expected behavior

The union of empty attention states should remain empty:

```text
merge((0, -inf), (0, -inf)) = (0, -inf)
```

This matches the existing behavior for zero input index sets.

## Impact and scope

An empty or fully masked partition can contaminate subsequent cascade reductions with NaN. Finite-state and single-empty merges are unaffected.

## Success criteria

- `merge_state` and `merge_state_in_place` preserve the empty state.
- Both `merge_states` launch strategies preserve the empty state.
- `state_t::merge` does not evaluate `-inf - -inf`.
- Existing finite-state behavior remains unchanged.

records.title: [Bug]: bmm_fp8 accepts scales that do not match its tensorwide contract
records.body:
## Observed behavior

`flashinfer.bmm_fp8` accepts `A_scale` and `B_scale` tensors with arbitrary shapes, dtypes, and devices even though its interchangeable backends expose tensorwide float32 scale semantics.

For example, a per-row scale is not rejected before cuBLAS dispatch:

```python
A_scale = torch.ones((batch, m, 1), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
B_scale = torch.ones((), dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")

flashinfer.bmm_fp8(
    A, B, A_scale, B_scale, torch.bfloat16, backend="cublas"
)
```

## Backend contracts

| Backend | Scale interpretation |
|---|---|
| cuBLASLt | Default tensorwide FP32 scalar |
| cuDNN | FP32 tensor shaped `(1, 1, 1)` |
| SM100 CUTLASS | Scalar-broadcast epilogue |
| SM120 CUTLASS | Can reach groupwise internals, conflicting with `auto` |
| Public `bmm_fp8` contract | One FP32 CUDA value per operand |

Because `backend="auto"` may choose any compatible runner, `bmm_fp8` needs to enforce their common tensorwide-scalar contract. Groupwise scaling belongs to `gemm_fp8_nt_groupwise`.

Non-float32 scale storage can additionally reach FFI casts to `float*`.

## Expected behavior

Each scale should:

- contain exactly one value;
- have dtype `torch.float32`;
- be on the same CUDA device as its operand.

## Impact and scope

Non-scalar scales can be interpreted as tensorwide values, producing backend-dependent or silently incorrect results. Existing callers using float32 CUDA scalars are unaffected.

`mm_fp8` is a separate TensorRT-LLM API and is outside this issue.

## Success criteria

- Invalid shape, dtype, and device combinations fail before dispatch.
- FFI boundaries validate scale tensors before `float*` casts.
- Valid scalar behavior remains unchanged across all backends.
- Documentation distinguishes tensorwide and groupwise APIs.

records.title: [Bug]: Legacy CUDA RMSNorm quantization clips E5M2 output to the E4M3 range
records.body:
## Observed behavior

With the legacy CUDA norm backend, `rmsnorm_quant` and `fused_add_rmsnorm_quant` clamp E5M2 output to ±448, the E4M3 finite range.

E5M2 supports finite values through ±57344, so representable results between 448 and 57344 are silently reduced to 448.

This affects `FLASHINFER_USE_CUDA_NORM=1` and fallback use when the CuTe DSL implementation is unavailable.

## Reproduction

```python
import torch
import flashinfer

x = torch.ones(1, 128, dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda")
weight = torch.full((128,), 1024.0, dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda")
out = torch.empty_like(x, dtype=torch.float8_e5m2)

flashinfer.rmsnorm_quant(out, x, weight, 1.0, enable_pdl=False)
print(out[0, 0].float())
```

For these inputs, RMS normalization produces approximately 1024:

| Output type | Finite maximum | Input to clamp | Previous output | Expected output |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| E4M3 | 448 | 1024 | 448 | 448 |
| E5M2 | 57344 | 1024 | 448 | 1024 |

```text
previous = clamp(1024, -448, 448) = 448
expected = clamp(1024, -57344, 57344) = 1024
```

## Root cause

Both legacy CUDA kernels use a hard-coded ±448 clamp even though the output type is available as a template parameter.

## Scope

Affected:

- Legacy CUDA `rmsnorm_quant`
- Legacy CUDA `fused_add_rmsnorm_quant`
- E5M2 results above 448

Not affected:

- E4M3 output
- INT8
- The default CuTe implementation

## Success criteria

- Both kernels select the limit from the output FP8 type.
- E4M3 continues to saturate at 448.
- E5M2 preserves representable values above 448.
- Both APIs and formats receive regression coverage.

records.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Pro cold multi-process fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90 JIT cache race can make the CUDA loader fail
records.body:
## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA H100 80 GB HBM3 (SM90), eight GPUs on one node for the operator reproduction
- Driver: 580.105.08
- CUDA: 13.0 (`torch==2.11.0+cu130`)
- FlashInfer: `flashinfer-python==0.6.13`, `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.13`
- Consumer: vLLM `v0.25.1` (`752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34`)
- Model which exposed it: `nvidia/DeepSeek-V4-Pro-NVFP4`

## Summary

DeepSeek-V4-Pro exposed this during vLLM startup: when several GPU workers call
`fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90` for the same warmup shape against an empty, shared TensorRT-LLM
DeepGEMM JIT cache, they concurrently compile and publish the same cubin. The race can make the
runtime's CUDA driver-library load sequence terminate with:

```text
CUDA error: invalid argument
```

This is a cold-cache multi-process race, not an unsupported GEMM shape or an incompatible weight
scale layout. The exact same tensors pass on all eight H100s when each worker has a separate
`TRTLLM_DG_CACHE_DIR`. A local patch serializes each cache-key build, validates compiler output and
cache artifacts, and propagates publication failures. With the FlashInfer wrapper genuinely
rebuilt from that source, one cold shared-cache run produced exactly one inner compilation and all
eight H100 workers returned the known-good result.

The issue first appeared in a captured vLLM launch because eight ranks reached the same
DeepSeek-V4-Pro warmup projection together; that launch never became ready even though the
accepted operator arguments were valid. A separate cold launch with the stock compiler and the
same default selector completed successfully, confirming that the race is timing-dependent. A
full two-node/16-H100 TP16 server using the final patch also completed mixed-token warmup, CUDA
graph capture, and coherent requests with the FlashInfer selector enabled.

## Minimal reproduction

Save this as `repro.py`:

```python
import os

local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
if os.environ.get("PER_RANK_CACHE") == "1":
    os.environ["TRTLLM_DG_CACHE_DIR"] += f"-{local_rank}"

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from flashinfer.gemm import fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90
from flashinfer.testing.utils import per_block_cast_to_fp8

torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)
torch.manual_seed(0)

# DeepSeek-V4-Pro fused_wqa_wkv at the mandatory mixed-token warmup.
M, N, K = 16, 2048, 7168
a = torch.randn(M, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
w = torch.randn(N, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
wq, ws = per_block_cast_to_fp8(w)

out = fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90(a, wq, None, ws)
torch.cuda.synchronize()

w_dequant = wq.float() * ws.repeat_interleave(128, 0).repeat_interleave(128, 1)
ref = a.float() @ w_dequant.T
cosine = F.cosine_similarity(ref.flatten(), out.float().flatten(), dim=0)
relative_l1 = (ref - out.float()).abs().mean() / ref.abs().mean()
print(
    f"rank={local_rank} scale={ws.shape, ws.dtype, ws.stride(), ws.is_contiguous()} "
    f"PASS cosine={cosine.item():.8f} relative_l1={relative_l1.item():.8f}",
    flush=True,
)
```

Run eight workers with one new shared cache directory:

```bash
export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1
export TRTLLM_DG_CACHE_DIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/flashinfer-shared.XXXXXX)"
torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=8 repro.py
```

Observed in Slurm job `5313278`:

```text
rank=7 mode=block A=(16, 7168):torch.bfloat16 B=(2048, 7168):torch.float8_e4m3fn
scale=((16, 56), torch.float32, (56, 1), True)
CUDA error: invalid argument
EXIT=1
```

The race is timing-dependent. In the same cold-cache shape sweep some configurations completed
while others failed, including the exact `M=16, N=2048, K=7168` configuration above.

As a control, give each worker its own new cache:

```bash
export TRTLLM_DG_CACHE_DIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/flashinfer-isolated.XXXXXX)"
PER_RANK_CACHE=1 torchrun --standalone --nproc-per-node=8 repro.py
```

All eight workers pass. The result on every GPU was:

```text
scale=((16, 56), torch.float32, (56, 1), True)
PASS cosine=0.99966240 relative_l1=0.02618705
EXIT=0
```

The BF16-weight form of the same operator also changed from `CUDA error: invalid argument` with a
cold shared cache to eight passes with isolated caches. This rules out checkpoint quantization and
the 128x128 weight-scale path as necessary causes.

## Root cause

The embedded TensorRT-LLM DeepGEMM compiler in
`csrc/nv_internal/tensorrt_llm/deep_gemm/compiler.cuh` does the following:

1. checks the process-local/runtime and filesystem cache;
2. on a miss, immediately starts NVCC, with no inter-process lock;
3. tries to rename its temporary cubin to the shared cache-key path, but catches and logs a rename
   failure and continues; and
4. creates a runtime which reads that path.

The NVCC branch calls `pclose()` but discards its return status. It does not verify that the
temporary cubin exists and is nonempty before publishing it. `Runtime::isPathValid()` in
`runtime.cuh` only checks that the cubin path exists, so a directory or zero-byte file is accepted;
`Runtime::getKernel()` then enters a `CHECK_CUDA`-wrapped driver sequence beginning with
`cuLibraryLoadData()`. That wrapper is the only source of the observed bare error, but it does not
print which individual driver call failed.

This explains all three A/B observations:

- shared cold cache: concurrent identical builds, intermittent CUDA loader failure;
- separate cache per worker: no competing build, eight passes;
- patched shared cold cache: exactly one build plus seven cache rechecks, with eight correct
  results.

It also disproves an initial layout hypothesis. vLLM's DeepGEMM weight post-processing left this
Hopper 128x128 scale tensor at shape `[16, 56]`, stride `(56, 1)`, FP32, contiguous. Calling
`.contiguous()` did not change the failure; separating the JIT caches did.

## Suggested fix

Serialize a cold build per cache key and recheck the cache after acquiring the lock. Treat a
failed NVCC process, missing or empty cubin, and failed cache publication as errors instead of
publishing or loading an invalid artifact.

The local patch does five things:

1. takes a POSIX advisory lock at `<cache-key>.lock`;
2. rechecks `RuntimeCache` after taking the lock;
3. validates `pclose()` plus the temporary cubin before rename;
4. removes the temporary tree and rethrows a publication/rename failure; and
5. requires the cached cubin to be a regular, nonempty file before treating it as valid.

An initial header-overlay run appeared to pass, but audit showed that the packaged AOT
`fp8_blockscale_gemm_90.so` still contained the stock compiler: JIT debug printed eight inner
compiles, not one. That result is withdrawn as patch evidence. The corrected after arm made the
AOT wrapper unreachable, rebuilt it from the mounted candidate source, and used one new shared
cache. It recorded exactly one `Compiling JIT runtime` line; all eight workers returned
`cosine=0.99966240`, `relative_l1=0.02618705`, and the command exited 0 in 1m29.664s.

The final production patch then passed a complete stock-vLLM 0.25.1 DeepSeek-V4-Pro server test on two nodes and
16 H100s. All ranks selected `FlashInferFp8DeepGEMMDynamicBlockScaledKernel`, the packaged AOT
wrapper was hidden so the mounted source was rebuilt, and the server completed mixed-token warmup
and normal CUDA graph capture. `/v1/models` returned HTTP 200; temperature-0 requests returned
Paris, Tokyo, `22`, Rayleigh scattering, and Earth's axial tilt correctly.

Three cache-hardening tests also passed simultaneously on two eight-H100 nodes:

- a seeded zero-byte cubin was rejected and rebuilt exactly once per node; all eight consumers per
  node returned the exact known-good result and each final cubin was 34,024 bytes;
- a forced NVCC failure returned nonzero and published no final cubin, then a normal retry against
  the same cache compiled once and passed on all eight workers per node; and
- a deliberately seeded directory at the final cubin path made publication fail and propagate;
  after removing only that obstacle, the same lock and cache recovered with one compile and eight
  correct consumers per node.

A CPU-only process-contention unit test now exercises the real C++ lock and cache-artifact
predicate without CUDA headers, NVCC, a GPU, or a tensor result. From an independent Linux checkout
of the published branch, both tests passed. Mutation checks confirmed that removing the lock or
its destructor cleanup makes the contention test fail.

Tested v0.6.13 commit: `c92c24cc9d53b572fae80d4f7b51f5213f4cdb99`. The forward-port fix and
unit test are published on
[`mikekg:fix/trtllm-deepgemm-jit-cache-lock`](https://github.com/mikekg/flashinfer/tree/fix/trtllm-deepgemm-jit-cache-lock)
at commit `cae9be97550adb666ea09ea7a218b13e918eba49`.

## Workarounds

- For the direct FlashInfer operator, a separate `TRTLLM_DG_CACHE_DIR` per worker avoids the race
  but duplicates compilation and cache storage.
- In vLLM 0.25.1, `VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER=0` removes this FlashInfer candidate and
  uses vLLM's pure DeepGEMM kernel. It does not dequantize the model or change its NVFP4 MoE
  kernels.

records.title: [bug] cuDNN grouped_mm_bf16 requires backend version >= 92100, found 91900 on b300
records.body:
## Summary
Found this issue in FlashInfer CI. 
## CI metadata
- Test case: `tests/grouped_mm/test_grouped_mm_fp8.py, tests/grouped_mm/test_grouped_mm_bf16.py`
- Pipeline URL: https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/pipelines/5864558
- Job name(s):  unit_test_b300: 
- Branch: `main`
- Environment: `B300` / `cu129`

## Failed Jobs
- [unit_test_b300[cu129]](https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/367420335)


## Failure
```text
RuntimeError: cuDNN grouped_mm_bf16 requires backend version >= 92100, found 91900.
```

## Likely root cause
https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3797
flashinfer/flashinfer/grouped_mm/cudnn/core.py
```python
_CUDNN_MOE_MIN_VERSION = 92100  # 9.21.0
```
but in flashinfer/tests/grouped_mm/conftest.py
```python
requires_cudnn_moe = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not CUDNN_AVAILABLE or CUDNN_BACKEND_VERSION < 91800 or not CUDNN_HAS_MOE_API,
    reason="cuDNN MOE requires backend >= 9.18.0 and a frontend exposing moe_grouped_matmul_mode",
)
``` 

### Suggest fix

1.  Update requires_cudnn_moe 

```python
requires_cudnn_moe = pytest.mark.skipif(
    not CUDNN_AVAILABLE or CUDNN_BACKEND_VERSION < 92100or not CUDNN_HAS_MOE_API,
    reason="cuDNN MOE requires backend >= 9.21.0 and a frontend exposing moe_grouped_matmul_mode",
)
``` 

2.   **Or** upgrade the cudnn version, as now these files are skipped in cuda12.9 and cuda13.0 because of cudnn is lower. 

flashinfer/scripts/setup_test_env.sh
```shell
# Override nvidia-cudnn if specified
if [ -n "${CUDNN_VERSION:-}" ]; then
  CUDA_MAJOR=$(python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda.split('.')[0])" 2>/dev/null || echo "12")
  if [ "$CUDA_MAJOR" = "13" ]; then
    CUDNN_PKG="nvidia-cudnn-cu13==${CUDNN_VERSION}"
  else
    CUDNN_PKG="nvidia-cudnn-cu12==${CUDNN_VERSION}"
  fi
  echo "========================================"
  echo "Overriding nvidia-cudnn with: ${CUDNN_PKG}"
  echo "========================================"
  pip install --upgrade "${CUDNN_PKG}"
  echo "nvidia-cudnn override complete."
  echo ""
fi
``` 
flashinfer/ci/setup_python.env
```shell
# Uncomment to override nvidia-cudnn version (e.g. to get backend >= 9.21.0 for grouped_mm):
# CUDNN_VERSION=
```

- pipeline #https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/pipelines/58425817, unit_test_b300: [cu130]
- pipeline #https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/pipelines/58260687, unit_test_b300: [cu130]

records.title: [Bug] mxfp8/deepseekfp8 unified-MoE (trtllm_fp8_block): marginal numeric failures + a solo-config core dump on SM100 (pre-existing on main, surfaced by the fuzzer)
records.body:
Found while validating #4086 on a B200-class SM100 (main @ `6104afe3`). Two distinct symptoms on the recently-added mxfp8/deepseekfp8 unified-MoE paths, both reproducing on **unpatched main** (the #4086 guards touch only CuteDSL nvfp4 kernels — different backend):

**1. Marginal tolerance failures (16 configs, backend `trtllm_fp8_block`)** in the accumulated fuzzer sweep (`FLASHINFER_UMOE_FUZZ=1 FLASHINFER_UMOE_FUZZ_SEED=100`): e.g.
```
trtllm_fp8_block mxfp8_FL_Renormalize_uniform_e32_k4_t127_h3072_i1024_s100: 74/390144 elems exceed tol (rtol=0.85 atol=0.00141; max|diff|=0.002881)
trtllm_fp8_block mxfp8_RenormalizeNaive_imbalanced_e16_k4_t256_h2048_i1024_s900013: 110/524288 elems exceed tol (atol=0.00138; max|diff|=0.002357)
```
Hair's-breadth exceedances (tens of elems out of ~500K, ~1.7-2x atol) that appear/disappear between runs — consistent with autotune-winner nondeterminism flipping marginal cases, i.e. either a tolerance-calibration gap in the new mxfp8 reference/tolerances or a genuinely marginal tactic. Full list of 16 ids available in the #4086 validation logs.

**2. A solo-config core dump**: `FLASHINFER_UMOE_FUZZ=1 FLASHINFER_UMOE_FUZZ_ONLY_SEED=900013 pytest tests/moe/test_unified_moe_fuzz.py` on unpatched main ends in `Aborted (core dumped)` — a single curated mxfp8 config, no accumulation needed. Needs its own triage (assert-class in the fp8-block path? — the same exit-abort decoding as #3957 applies: any device assert poisons the context and terminates at interpreter shutdown).

Both are independent of #3957/#4086 and belong to the owners of the mxfp8/deepseekfp8 unified-MoE integration (#4026-era). The fuzzer had been opt-in until #3958, so these paths had never been swept before.
