```text
GPU1    NODE     X      128-255 1               N/A
```

### Bug description

Summary. The fa2 attention kernels initialize the online-softmax running max m to -math::inf, where math::inf is a finite value of 5e4 (include/flashinfer/math.cuh:33 on main; :32 on the 0.6.12 tag). When every real logit in a row falls below that sentinel, m = max(m, rowmax) stays clamped at -5e4, every exp2() term underflows to zero, and the kernel silently returns a zero vector for that row. No error, no NaN — just a wrong answer.

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/4b964ec4e147cf06a39e08b08c43188859df2652/include/flashinfer/math.cuh#L33

How we hit it. A bf16 GQA model we serve produces degenerate repetitive text on longer generations with the flashinfer backend, while --attention-backend triton on an identical build is correct. The model has massive activations in its final attention layer, with |q|max ≈ 448 and |k|max ≈ 1880 driving raw pre-sm_scale QK logits down to -2.45e5. One head has a row whose logits are all large negative — that head's output is exactly zero on every decode step, corrupting the final hidden state.

Massive activations of this kind are not exotic; any model without QK-norm can develop them, so we expect this to affect other deployments silently.

Mechanism (real numbers, head_dim = 128, sm_scale = 0.088388, so sm_scale_log2 = 0.1275):

m_prev  = -5e4                                     // prefill.cuh:901, initial sentinel
rowmax  = -2.45e5                                  // real logits, all below the sentinel
m       = max(-5e4, -2.45e5) = -5e4                 // clamped, never moves
o_scale = exp2((m_prev - m) * sm_scale_log2) = 1
s_frag  = exp2((-2.45e5 + 5e4) * 0.1275) = 0        // every term underflows
d       = 1.0                                       // stays at its init value (prefill.cuh:901)
o_frag  = 0

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/4b964ec4e147cf06a39e08b08c43188859df2652/include/flashinfer/attention/prefill.cuh#L896-L905

o_frag is already zero and d is still 1.0 before the epilogue runs, so the output is a zero vector regardless of which branch OutputTransform takes.

Note on the sentinel comparison. variant_helper.cuh:86 does float d_rcp = (m != -math::inf) ? math::ptx_rcp(d) : 0.f; — it uses "m still equals the sentinel" as the test for "this row was fully masked". That test also misfires here, but as shown above it is not what produces the zeros: the underflow in update_mdo_states already did. Replacing the equality test with an explicit "row fully masked" flag would therefore not fix this bug — the sentinel value itself has to move.

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/4b964ec4e147cf06a39e08b08c43188859df2652/include/flashinfer/attention/variant_helper.cuh#L85-L89

A second, nastier variant of the same root cause. KTraits::MaskFillValue is also -math::inf = -5e4 (prefill.cuh:339/345, and AttentionUpdater::fill_value at hopper/attention_updater.cuh:168). If a row contains both masked/padding positions and real logits below -5e4, the masked positions become the row maximum and receive softmax weight ≈ 1. The output then degenerates into an average of the V rows at masked positions — a non-zero garbage value rather than a clean zero, which is considerably harder to notice. We observed exact zeros only because the corresponding V entries happened to be zero.

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/4b964ec4e147cf06a39e08b08c43188859df2652/include/flashinfer/attention/prefill.cuh#L339-L347

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/4b964ec4e147cf06a39e08b08c43188859df2652/include/flashinfer/attention/hopper/attention_updater.cuh#L167-L168

Threshold is in the raw (pre-sm_scale) domain for fa2. In prefill.cuh the scale is applied inside exp2 (prefill.cuh:1577) and m is only multiplied by sm_scale_log2 later in finalize_m (prefill.cuh:1754), so m holds unscaled logits throughout and the breakpoint is a sm_scale-independent raw -5e4. This matches our measured breakpoint exactly: scaled -4450 at sm_scale = 0.088388 → raw -5.03e4.

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/4b964ec4e147cf06a39e08b08c43188859df2652/include/flashinfer/attention/prefill.cuh#L1576-L1585

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/4b964ec4e147cf06a39e08b08c43188859df2652/include/flashinfer/attention/prefill.cuh#L1753-L1757

Inconsistency between the two paths. decode.cuh:94-99 applies s[j] *= variant.sm_scale_log2 before comparing against -math::inf, so on that path the sentinel lives in the scaled domain and the effective raw threshold becomes -5e4 / (sm_scale * log2e) instead. The same named constant serves as a sentinel in two different domains. This explains an otherwise confusing observation in our sweeps: at sm_scale = 1.0 the breakpoint moved to roughly -3.47e4 rather than staying at -5e4.

https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/4b964ec4e147cf06a39e08b08c43188859df2652/include/flashinfer/attention/decode.cuh#L93-L95

Expected behavior. A row of finite, well-ordered logits should produce a correct softmax-weighted output regardless of its absolute magnitude. -2.45e5 is far inside fp32 range and the row has an unambiguous argmax (top1/top2 gap = 4545, vs ~0.003 fp32 resolution at that magnitude).

Affected paths. fa2 prefill and fa2 tensor-core decode (which reuses the prefill kernel). fa3 appears immune: hopper/attention_updater.cuh:185 initializes row_max from the real scores via reduce_max</*init=*/true> and finalize has no sentinel comparison. We could not verify this by running, since fa3 is unavailable on sm120.


### Minimal reproduction

```python
# Requires only flashinfer + torch. No model weights.
# Sweeps the row-max of an all-negative logit row across the -5e4 sentinel.
import torch
import flashinfer

dev = "cuda"
D, HQ, HKV, KV = 128, 16, 1, 64   # head_dim / qo heads / kv heads / kv len

def run(level: float):
    """Build q/k so every raw logit (q·k, before sm_scale) == `level`,
    except key 0 which is an unambiguous argmax at `level + 5000`."""
    q = torch.full((1, HQ, D), 1.0, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
    k = torch.full((KV, HKV, D), level / D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
    k[0].fill_((level + 5000.0) / D)
    v = torch.randn(KV, HKV, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)

    o = flashinfer.single_prefill_with_kv_cache(q, k, v, causal=False, backend="fa2")

    # fp32 reference; sdpa's default scale 1/sqrt(D) matches flashinfer's default sm_scale
    ref = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(
        q.transpose(0, 1).unsqueeze(0).float(),
        k.transpose(0, 1).unsqueeze(0).float().expand(1, HQ, KV, D),
        v.transpose(0, 1).unsqueeze(0).float().expand(1, HQ, KV, D),
    ).squeeze(0).transpose(0, 1)

    rel = (o.float() - ref).norm() / ref.norm()
    print(f"raw row-max = {level + 5000:>11.0f}   rel_l2 = {rel:.5f}   |out| = {o.float().norm():.4f}")

for level in [-1e4, -3e4, -5e4, -6e4, -1e5, -2.45e5]:
    run(level)

Expected: rows whose maximum stays above raw -5e4 are accurate (rel_l2 ~ 1e-3); once the row maximum drops below -5e4, rel_l2 jumps to 1.0 and |out| becomes exactly 0. Running with backend="fa2" on an sm90 machine should reproduce identically; backend="fa3" should not.
```

### Error messages / logs

```text
raw row-max =       -5000   rel_l2 = 0.00000   |out| = 42.4961
raw row-max =      -25000   rel_l2 = 0.00000   |out| = 46.9097
raw row-max =      -45000   rel_l2 = 0.00000   |out| = 50.0367
raw row-max =      -55000   rel_l2 = 1.00000   |out| = 0.0000
raw row-max =      -95000   rel_l2 = 1.00000   |out| = 0.0000
raw row-max =     -240000   rel_l2 = 1.00000   |out| = 0.0000

No exception is raised and no warning is emitted — this is a silent numerical failure. That is the main hazard: short prompts are correct under both backends, so the bug survives casual smoke tests. It only becomes visible in longer generations, where the per-step error accumulates.
```

### Additional context

_No response_

records.title: [Performance] SM120 NVFP4 paged causal prefill is ~1.7-1.8x slower than FP8
records.body:
## Summary

On SM120, FlashInfer's paged causal prefill with BF16 queries and an NVFP4 KV cache is about **1.7-1.8x slower than the matched FP8 KV-cache path** in our vLLM workload.

NVFP4 decode is faster than FP8 as expected for a bandwidth-bound workload, so the regression appears localized to the compute-heavy causal prefill path.

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA RTX PRO 5000 Blackwell (SM120)
- CUDA: 12.9
- PyTorch: 2.10.0+cu129
- FlashInfer: 0.6.15
- KV layout: HND
- Query dtype: BF16 at the model boundary (quantized as required by the selected path)
- KV formats compared:
  - NVFP4 packed data with per-16-element FP8 scale factors
  - FP8 KV cache
- Integration: vLLM FlashInfer backend

## Matched profile results

The two traces contain some disjoint startup/warmup regions, so the table below compares the same 48 causal paged-prefill calls.

| KV cache | Calls | Total | Mean per call |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NVFP4 | 48 | 145.81 ms | 3.04 ms |
| FP8 | 48 | 84.03 ms | 1.75 ms |

**NVFP4 / FP8 prefill ratio: 1.74x**

For context, in the same workload:

| Operation | NVFP4 | FP8 | Observation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Decode | 9.63 us | 12.35 us | NVFP4 is about 22% faster |
| KV append | 8.39 us | 3.01 us | NVFP4 is slower, but only about 7 ms total |
| Matched CUTLASS segment | 93.61 ms | 96.69 ms | Similar |
| All matched kernels | 297.73 ms | 238.45 ms | Prefill explains most of the gap |

The end-to-end capacity test also shows the tradeoff: NVFP4 avoids preemption and admits more concurrent requests, but wall time is worse because prefill is slower.

## Current hypothesis

The current SM120 FA2 NVFP4 prefill path appears to consume packed FP4 KV through an unpack/convert/scale sequence before the BF16-oriented QK MMA. In causal prefill, QK is compute-heavy and the reduced KV memory traffic does not offset that extra conversion work.

This is a hypothesis based on the kernel path and profile behavior, not yet a complete instruction-level Nsight Compute proof.

An A4Q-style path could avoid this cost by quantizing Q and using native block-scaled FP4 QK MMA (`use_nvf4_qk`-style dispatch), while retaining the packed NVFP4 KV representation.

## Questions

1. Is this performance behavior expected for the current SM120 NVFP4 paged-prefill implementation?
2. Is an A4Q/native block-scaled FP4 QK path planned for upstream FlashInfer?
3. Would maintainers accept a contribution wiring Q quantization and block-scaled FP4 MMA into the paged causal prefill path?
4. Are there existing benchmarks or recommended kernel parameters for comparing NVFP4 and FP8 prefill fairly on SM120?

## Related work

- vLLM tracking issue with the serving-level measurements: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/50416
- NVFP4 KV support for prefill/batch attention: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3097
- SM120/121 NVFP4 paged-prefill extensions: https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3684

I can provide the Nsight Systems JSON traces and a reduced benchmark case if that would help with kernel-level investigation.

records.title: test_proxy_split_k_heuristic fails on high-SM GPUs (fp4 split-K)
records.body:
`tests/msa_ops/test_proxy_fp4.py::test_proxy_split_k_heuristic` fails on GPUs where the fp4 split-K optimum diverges from the test's hard-coded `ceil(2*sm/8)`.

Observed on RTX 5090 (sm120, 170 SMs): `_proxy_split_k_fp4(8, 512, dev)` returns **40**, test asserts **43**.

```
E   AssertionError: assert 40 == -((-2 * 170) // 8)
tests/msa_ops/test_proxy_fp4.py:456: AssertionError
```

**Root cause — test only, not a kernel bug.** The assertion uses the closed form `ceil(2*sm/8)`, but `_proxy_split_k_fp4` delegates to the `_split_k_makespan_argmin` model, which caps at one CTA wave and breaks ties to the smaller split. The closed form ignores wave / KV-tile quantization, so it is off (typically by one) on most SM counts; sm120 CI is just where it first ran. The kernel and heuristic behavior are correct.

**Fix:** assert against the model itself rather than a closed form, keeping the check independent of the runtime SM count.

records.title: v0.6.16 release highlights draft
records.body:
### v0.6.16 Highlights

This release delivers the **MegaMoE kernels** promised for expert parallelism in 0.6.15 and extends **Blackwell** model coverage — MiniMax-M3 sparse attention on Blackwell RTX and DGX Spark, and a unified MoE API that now executes per-tensor FP8, block-scale FP8, and B12x NVFP4/W4A16 — plus distributed serving under **Confidential Computing** with multicast-free all-reduce fusion. Under the hood, an on-disk JIT cache for CuTe-DSL kernels cuts cold-start compilation and shrinks the install.

**MegaMoE kernels land in expert parallelism (`moe_ep`)**

The `MoEEpLayer` now unifies the split and **mega** execution paths under one entry point and adds three mega backends — `deep_gemm_mega` (FP8/FP4), `nvfp4_cutedsl`, and `mxfp8_cutedsl` — each fusing expert-parallel communication with the local MoE in a single symmetric-memory kernel (Blackwell SM100+, NVSHMEM). In a microbenchmark, on a GB200 node (EP=4, DeepSeek-V3-like geometry) the tuned CuTeDSL NVFP4 backend with in-register FP4 combine reaches up to **1.89× the throughput of `deep_gemm_mega`** at 8192 tokens/rank. NIXL-EP transport gaps and combine deadlocks blocking the vLLM Fleet/Handle adapters are also closed.

- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3852
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3980
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4075
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4139

**MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA) on Blackwell RTX and DGX Spark**

MiniMax-M3's MSA — a proxy/top-k indexer plus sparse prefill, decode, and combine — now runs on **Blackwell RTX and DGX Spark (SM120/121)** GPUs. The tensor-core kernels are rebuilt on SM12x warp-level `mma.sync`, top-k and combine are rewritten in CuTe-DSL, and an optional NVFP4 indexer is available, with prefill/decode accepting FP8 or NVFP4 KV (paged or flat). New APIs live under `flashinfer.msa_ops`.

- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3655

**XQA decode adds sliding-window, attention sinks, and ragged Q for speculative decode**

The XQA decode kernel — used on Blackwell RTX and DGX Spark (SM120/121) for models with attention sinks — expands coverage for sliding-window attention and ragged Q, across causal and non-causal draft-block mask modes and combinations of them. Ragged Q lets each request in a batch verify a different number of draft tokens, and sliding-window masking is now computed per draft-token row, making the kernel useful for speculative-decoding workloads across models on SM120/121.

- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4137

**Unified MoE API reaches parity with the legacy FP8 and NVFP4 paths**

The unified `MoELayer` API continues to expand quantization formats to reach parity with legacy flat APIs: **TRTLLM per-tensor FP8** (SM100/SM103, with Llama4 routing-scale-on-input), **DeepSeek FP8 and MXFP8 block-scale** (SM100/SM103), and **SM120/SM121 B12x** NVFP4 and W4A16 backends. In-kernel routing (`FromLogits`) is now wired through the unified API and fuzzer, so precomputed and in-kernel routing share one path with CUDA-graph and autotuning coverage.

- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4091
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4026
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3983
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3892

**Confidential Computing: multicast-free all-reduce fusion and FP8 AllReduce**

The TRT-LLM AllReduce-fusion workspace now allocates a **multicast-free IPC workspace** when NVIDIA Confidential Computing is detected (`is_confidential_compute()`, overridable via `FLASHINFER_CONFIDENTIAL_COMPUTE`), so one-shot Lamport and two-shot sync fusion run under CC where `cuMulticast` setup otherwise fails. Separately, a new `flashinfer.comm.quantized_all_reduce()` halves AllReduce transfer volume by quantizing activations to FP8 before P2P transfer over symmetric memory (SM90+, NVSwitch).

- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3993
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3759

**Faster JIT cold-start and smaller install**

CuTe-DSL kernels now persist to an on-disk cache (`JitSpec` gains a `JitSpecCuteDsl` backend) and reload via JITLink in about **3–30 ms** instead of recompiling in every new process; `mm_fp4` autotuning additionally compiles tactics in parallel and reuses the shared disk cache, cutting autotune wall time. Pruning architecture gencode that dispatch can never load removes roughly **1.6 GB** of installed size from the CUDA-13 aarch64 JIT-cache wheel.

- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3874
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4029
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3947
- https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4073

records.title: [BUG] FP16_QK_REDUCTION path does not compile, and decodes QK logits with a value cast instead of a bit cast
records.body:
### Description In `include/flashinfer/attention/prefill.cuh`, the `FP16_QK_REDUCTION` path (`DTypeQKAccum = __half`) converts the QK accumulator fragment back to `float` with: ```cpp // include/flashinfer/attention/prefill.cuh:1400 logits = std::bit_cast(fp16_ieee_to_fp32_value(s_frag[mma_q][mma_kv][reg_id])); ``` `fp16_ieee_to_fp32_value` is declared in `include/flashinfer/fp16.h:48` as: ```cpp static constexpr float fp16_ieee_to_fp32_value(uint16_t h) ``` It expects the IEEE half **bit pattern** in a `uint16_t`. But the argument passed is a `__half`, and nothing bit-casts it. What happens instead is `__half`'s implicit conversion operator to `unsigned short` (`cuda_fp16.hpp`): ```cpp __CUDA_HOSTDEVICE__ operator unsigned short() const { return __half2ushort_rz(*this); } ``` `__half2ushort_rz` is a saturating round-toward-zero **numeric value** conversion (`cvt.rzi.u16.f16` on device), not a reinterpret. So the bit pattern handed to the decoder is the *integer value* of the half, not its bits. Note also that the outer `std::bit_cast` is a no-op — `fp16_ieee_to_fp32_value` already returns `float`. It gives the line the appearance of doing a bit-level conversion while the actual bit-level step is missing. ### Impact This corrupts essentially every logit, not just edge cases: - Any **negative** half saturates to `0x0000` and decodes to `+0.0f`. This includes the `-inf` softmax mask sentinel (`KTraits::MaskFillValue`, `KTraits::getNegInf()`). - Any **positive** half is truncated to its integer part, which is then interpreted as a half bit pattern, producing a tiny subnormal (`+1.0` -> `5.96e-08`, `+10.0` -> `5.96e-07`). - Sweeping all 65536 half bit patterns: **Among 63,490 non-NaN half patterns, 63,489 decode incorrectly; only `+0.0` matches bit-for-bit.** The failure is **silent**. The symmetric write-back a few lines later is correct: ```cpp // :1415 s_frag[mma_q][mma_kv][reg_id] = std::bit_cast(fp16_ieee_from_fp32_value(logitsTransformed)); ``` (`fp16_ieee_from_fp32_value` returns `uint16_t`, so `std::bit_cast` is right.) The fragment therefore stays well-formed and no NaN or assert appears. Because masked positions become `0.0` instead of `-inf`, they receive uniform softmax weight, so the row degenerates to `lse == log2(kv_len)` and `output == mean(V)`. ### The path does not even compile on current main Before the numeric bug can be reached at all, the path fails to build. On `main` with `-DFP16_QK_REDUCTION_SUPPORTED` and a `boost/math/ccmath` include path, `nvcc` rejects `include/flashinfer/attention/variant_helper.cuh:86`: ```cpp // AttentionVariantBase::OutputTransform float d_rcp = (m != -math::inf) ? math::ptx_rcp(d) : 0.f; ``` `m` has type `T_M&`, which is `DTypeQKAccum` — `__half` on this path — while `-math::inf` is a `float`. The comparison is ambiguous, since `__half` converts to `float` and `float` converts to `__half`, and CUDA supplies `operator!=` overloads for `__half`, `__half2`, `__nv_bfloat16` and `__nv_bfloat162`: ``` variant_helper.cuh(86): error: no operator "!=" matches these operands ... note #3326-D: function "operator==(const __half2 &, const __half2 &)" does not match because argument #1 does not match parameter ... note #3326-D: function "operator==(const __nv_bfloat16 &, const __nv_bfloat16 &)" does not match because argument #1 does not match parameter ... note #3328-D: built-in operator==(, ) does not match because argument #1 does not match parameter 1 error detected in the compilation of ".../single_prefill_..._f16qk_True/single_prefill_kernel_mask_1.cu" ``` So `FP16_QK_REDUCTION` currently has **two independent latent defects**: this compile error, and the value-cast bug above that it hides. Neither can be observed without first supplying the define by hand. One subtlety worth flagging for whoever fixes the compile error: `math::inf` is the **finite** sentinel `5e4`, not an infinity. Widening `m` to `float` compiles but is wrong — the `__half` mask fill value is `fp16_ieee_from_fp32_value(-math::inf)` = `0xFA1A` = `-49984.0f`, which compares unequal to `-50000.0f`, so a fully-masked row would be treated as live and take `math::ptx_rcp(d)` with `d == 0`. Comparing in the accumulator type instead (`static_cast(-math::inf)`) is both unambiguous and correct, and is the identity for `T_M = float`. ### Why this has gone unnoticed The path appears to be unreachable from a stock build: - The line was introduced verbatim by #962 ("Fix compilation with FP16_QK_REDUCTION enabled.", commit `3a695603`), which also added `fp16.h`. `git log -L1398,1402:include/flashinfer/attention/prefill.cuh` shows it as the most recent change to that region. That PR's goal was making the path **compile**, and with the implicit `operator unsigned short()` available it compiled cleanly — which is exactly why the value cast went unnoticed. The no-op outer `std::bit_cast` reinforces the impression that the bit-level conversion was handled. - `FP16_QK_REDUCTION_SUPPORTED` is referenced **only inside `prefill.cuh` itself** (lines 30, 329, 343, 1398, 1406, 1412). Nothing in the workflows, build files, or JIT flag lists defines it. - Without the define, the `static_assert` at `:1405` (and `:342`) hard-fails the build when `DTypeQKAccum` is `__half`, so requesting fp16 QK reduction cannot silently fall through. - Enabling it requires both `-DFP16_QK_REDUCTION_SUPPORTED` and a `boost/math/ccmath` include path (per the `static_assert` message). So as far as I can tell no CI job compiles this path, which means neither defect has ever been exercised. The two layers corroborate that directly: a path that does not compile cannot have been built by anything, and a numeric bug sitting behind a compile error cannot have been observed by anyone. The history fits too. `prefill.cuh:1400` and `fp16.h` both arrived in #962 ("Fix compilation with FP16_QK_REDUCTION enabled.", `3a695603`) — a PR whose goal was to make this path *compile*. It did compile at the time, which is exactly why the value cast was never examined numerically; and the path has since rotted back into not compiling, without anything noticing. Impact on current users is likely nil, but `use_fp16_qk_reduction` is part of the public API surface, and this would ship broken the moment the define is wired up. ### Reproduction The mechanism is deterministic and provable on the host, with no GPU. This program contrasts the correct bit-cast decode against the value-cast decode that `:1400` actually performs (emulating `__half2ushort_rz` per its definition in `cuda_fp16.hpp`):
g++ -std=c++20 proof.cpp -o proof && ./proof ``` half value bits correct(bit) buggy(value) verdict -inf (softmax mask sentinel, KTraits::MaskFillValue) 0xFC00 -inf 0 DIVERGES -10.0 (typical masked/low logit) 0xC900 -10 0 DIVERGES -1.0 0xBC00 -1 0 DIVERGES -0.125 0xB000 -0.125 0 DIVERGES smallest negative subnormal 0x8001 -5.96046e-08 0 DIVERGES -0.0 0x8000 -0 0 DIVERGES +0.0 0x0000 0 0 ok +1.0 0x3C00 1 5.96046e-08 DIVERGES +10.0 (positive: value cast truncates to 10 -> decodes as 5.96e-07) 0x4900 10 5.96046e-07 DIVERGES +inf 0x7C00 inf -nan DIVERGES exhaustive sweep over all non-NaN half bit patterns: diverging patterns : 63489 negative patterns : 31745 negative patterns diverging : 31745 (all of them) ``` (full source attached / see linked PR)
I have also observed this on hardware, on an H200 (sm90), with `-DFP16_QK_REDUCTION_SUPPORTED -std=c++20` plus a `boost/math/ccmath` shim. Because of the compile error above, getting the kernel to build at all required fixing `variant_helper.cuh:86` first; with only that compile fix in place and `prefill.cuh:1400` left as-is, prefill cases returned `lse == log2(64)` exactly with `output == mean(V)` — the signature of an all-zero `s_frag` entering the softmax, matching the prediction above. The same harness on the same build with `use_fp16_qk_reduction=False` was correct, so the only variable was the fp16 accumulator. With both fixes applied, the same cases track an fp64 reference to within fp16 accumulation error (e.g. logits `-512/-256` -> `lse = -27.656` vs reference `-27.644`; sign-mixed `+512/-256` -> `70.312` vs `70.289`; all-positive `+51200` -> `6537.249` vs `6534.892`), and the fp16 and fp32 paths produce bit-identical output on identical inputs. ### Suggested fix Two one-line changes, one per defect. `prefill.cuh:1400` — reinterpret the bits, matching the direction already used by the write-back at `:1415` and by `KTraits::getNegInf()` at `:333`: ```cpp logits = fp16_ieee_to_fp32_value(std::bit_cast(s_frag[mma_q][mma_kv][reg_id])); ``` `variant_helper.cuh:86` — compare in the accumulator type, which is unambiguous and, per the note above, the only variant that stays correct for the finite sentinel (and is the identity when `T_M` is `float`): ```cpp float d_rcp = (m != static_cast(-math::inf)) ? math::ptx_rcp(d) : 0.f; ``` `` is already available via `fp16.h`. Happy to open a PR — I have both changes built and passing on an H200 (sm90). Separately, it may be worth deciding whether this path should be built by CI or removed. Two independent defects accumulating unnoticed suggests that an unbuilt, untested code path behind a manual define is not carrying its maintenance cost.

records.title: [Bug] FA2 prefill never validates head_dim: values not a multiple of 64 give an illegal memory access, values not a multiple of 16 silently return wrong results
records.body:
## Summary

FlashInfer's FA2 prefill path accepts any `head_dim` at the Python level,
JIT-compiles a module for it, and then misbehaves in one of two ways depending on
the value. Nothing rejects it, at any layer.

* `head_dim` a multiple of 16 but not of 64 (80, 96, 112, 144, 160, 176 …) →
  **`CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`**.
* `head_dim` not a multiple of 16 (72, 136 …) → the call **returns normally with
  wrong results**, no error anywhere.

Neither case needs a non-default argument: three tensors and `causal=True`.

Why it is worth your time: **`head_dim=96` is Phi-3-mini's head dimension**
(3072/32), and `head_dim=80` is in the Phi-2 generation, so the faulting class is
reachable from a real model. #455 was a user hitting `head_dim=96` with Phi-3-mini
through SGLang; on that (2024-era decode) path it produced a clean dispatch error.
On today's FA2 prefill path the same head dim is a memory fault instead. The
silently-wrong class needs nothing exotic at all — just a head dim that is not a
multiple of 16.

## Reproducer

```python
import torch
import flashinfer

dev = torch.device("cuda:0")
head_dim = 96          # 96 -> illegal memory access.  72 -> returns wrong results.  64/128 -> fine.

q = torch.randn(128, 8, head_dim, dtype=torch.float16, device=dev)
k = torch.randn(256, 8, head_dim, dtype=torch.float16, device=dev)
v = torch.randn(256, 8, head_dim, dtype=torch.float16, device=dev)

o = flashinfer.single_prefill_with_kv_cache(q, k, v, causal=True)
torch.cuda.synchronize()

# fp32 reference
s = torch.einsum("ihd,jhd->hij", q.float(), k.float()) / head_dim**0.5
i = torch.arange(q.shape[0], device=dev)[:, None]
j = torch.arange(k.shape[0], device=dev)[None, :]
s = s.masked_fill(~(j <= i + (k.shape[0] - q.shape[0])), float("-inf"))
ref = torch.einsum("hij,jhd->ihd", s.softmax(-1), v.float())
print(head_dim, (o.float() - ref).abs().max().item() / ref.abs().max().item())
```

Expected outcomes, qualitatively:

* `head_dim = 96` (also 80, 112): raises before it prints. With
  `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` the error is attributed to the prefill kernel launch —
  `RuntimeError: Check failed: (status == cudaSuccess) is false:
  SinglePrefillWithKVCache kernel launch failed, error: an illegal memory access was
  encountered`. Without it, it surfaces later at the next synchronisation as
  `torch.AcceleratorError`, which is what makes it hard to trace back to `head_dim`
  in an application.
* `head_dim = 72` (also 136): prints a relative error of order 100 rather than the
  ~1e-3 you get at 64 or 128. I am deliberately not promising an exact figure for
  *this* snippet: the numbers I measured came from my own harness (a naive fp32
  reference with explicit GQA broadcast and bottom-right causal alignment), where it
  was `max_abs = 203.7` / `max_rel_to_peak = 242.1` at head_dim 72 and
  `max_rel_to_peak = 284.7` at 136, against ~3e-4 at 64/128. The snippet is the
  minimal form of the same comparison; treat its magnitude as "enormous", not as a
  number to match.
* `head_dim = 64` or `128`: prints ~3e-4.

## Measured surface

`head_dim` swept in steps of 8, one fresh process per case (a CUDA illegal access
poisons the context, so an in-process loop manufactures fake failures after the
first real one), `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, fp16 Q/K/V, `backend="fa2"`.

**This sweep is partial.** 28 head dims (8 … 224, step 8) have been measured on the
single-request path so far; the rest of the range and the full batch-path rows are
still running. The table is evidence for the three regimes; it is **not** a complete
residue-class map and I would not want it read as one.

`single_prefill_with_kv_cache(q, k, v, causal=True)`, `qo_len=128`, `kv_len=256`:

| head_dim | outcome |
|---|---|
| 8 | the JIT compile itself fails (`ninja: build failed`) |
| 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56 | `E1` |
| **64** | **ok** — matches fp32 reference, ~3e-4 |
| **72** | **WRONG — returns successfully, rel. error 242** |
| **80, 88, 96, 104, 112, 120** | **IMA** |
| **128** | **ok** — ~3e-4 |
| **136** | **WRONG — returns successfully, rel. error 285** |
| **144, 152, 160, 168, 176, 184** | **IMA** |
| 192, 200, 208, 216, 224 | `E1` at this shape |

`IMA` = illegal memory access. `E1` = `FlashInfer Internal Error: Invalid
configuration : NUM_MMA_Q=… please create an issue`. The `E1` at 192+ is
shape-dependent tile configuration, not this bug — head_dim 192 does run correctly at
other shapes (e.g. `qo_len=1, kv_len=8192` with `disable_split_kv=True`).

Independently, on `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper` with
`plan(..., disable_split_kv=True)`, over 4 shape variants each
(`(qo_len, kv_len, num_qo_heads)` = `(128,256,8)`, `(1,8192,8)`, `(2048,2048,8)`,
`(128,256,32)`): head_dim **80, 96, 112 → illegal memory access in 12 of 12 cases**;
head_dim **64, 128 → ok in 8 of 8**, matching the reference. Together with the
single-request path that is **24 of 24** faulting cases for those three head dims,
and the outcome does not depend on shape.

What the measurements and the source agree on: the outcome is decided by
`D = floor(head_dim / 16)`. `D % 4 != 0` → out-of-bounds access. `D % 4 == 0` → the
kernel runs, but is correct only if `head_dim` is *exactly* `16*D`. `D < 4` → `E1`.

### Paged batch prefill: predicted, not yet measured

`page_produce_kv` and `page_produce_kv_on_the_fly` carry the identical offset
arithmetic (line numbers below), so I expect
`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper` to behave exactly like the ragged wrapper:
shielded by the split-KV merge kernel by default, faulting with
`disable_split_kv=True`. **I have not measured the paged path** — that is a source
reading, not a result.

## Root cause

`HEAD_DIM_QK` arrives as a template parameter and is immediately turned into a tile
count by **integer division** (`include/flashinfer/attention/prefill.cuh:2479`, and
`:4096` / `:4296` for the batch entry points):

```c++
constexpr uint32_t NUM_MMA_D_QK = HEAD_DIM_QK / 16;
constexpr uint32_t NUM_MMA_D_VO = HEAD_DIM_VO / 16;
```

and `KernelTraits` then *redefines* the head dim from that count (`:252-253`):

```c++
static constexpr uint32_t HEAD_DIM_QK = NUM_MMA_D_QK * 16;
```

### Regime 1 — `head_dim % 16 != 0` → silent truncation

`head_dim = 72` becomes `NUM_MMA_D_QK = 4`, i.e. the kernel is built for head_dim
**64**, while the tensors it is handed still have 72 elements per row and the output
tensor is still 72 wide. It attends over the first 64 channels, writes 64 of the 72
output columns, and leaves the remaining 8 columns of every row at whatever the
freshly-allocated output buffer contained. No error is raised at any layer.

This is the class I would prioritise: the caller gets numbers back, and they are
wrong.

For what it is worth, the `% 16` half of the invariant *is* enforced elsewhere in the
tree — `csrc/page.cu:199` has `TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(head_dim % 16, 0);`. Prefill has no
equivalent in C++ or Python; `csrc/single_prefill.cu:41` reads
`unsigned int head_dim_qk = q.size(2);` and checks nothing.

### Regime 2 — `head_dim % 64 != 0` → out-of-bounds shared memory access

The staging loops walk a swizzled shared-memory offset column-by-column and then
subtract exactly one row width to return to the row start. The column loop is bounded
by another integer division, so it only reaches the row end when the tile count is a
multiple of 4 — i.e. when `head_dim` is a multiple of **64**. `load_q_global_smem`:

```c++
for (uint32_t mma_do = 0; mma_do < KTraits::NUM_MMA_D_QK / 4; ++mma_do) {   // :931
  q_smem->template load_128b_async<...>(q_smem_offset_w, q_ptr, ...);
  q_smem_offset_w = q_smem->template advance_offset_by_column<8>(q_smem_offset_w, mma_do);
  q_ptr += 8 * upcast_size<DTypeQ>();
}
q_smem_offset_w =
    q_smem->template advance_offset_by_row<4, UPCAST_STRIDE_Q>(q_smem_offset_w)
    - 2 * KTraits::NUM_MMA_D_QK;                                            // :938-940
```

Offsets are counted in 16-byte `b128_t` units (`permuted_smem.cuh:74-125`) and
`advance_offset_by_column<8>` is `offset + 8`. With `D = NUM_MMA_D_QK` and fp16,
`UPCAST_STRIDE_Q = head_dim/8 = 2*D`, so the loop advances the column offset by
`8 * floor(D/4)` while the row step subtracts `2*D`. Those cancel **iff `D % 4 == 0`,
i.e. `head_dim % 64 == 0`**. At `head_dim = 96` (`D = 6`) the loop advances 8 and the
code subtracts 12, so the offset drifts −4 units per row group instead of returning to
the row start, and accesses computed from it leave the buffer.

The same `loop-then-subtract-a-full-row` pattern, with the same assumption, appears in
five places:

| function | loop bound | backtrack |
|---|---|---|
| `load_q_global_smem` | `prefill.cuh:931` | `:938-940` |
| `produce_kv` (ragged) | `:483` | `:495-496` |
| `page_produce_kv` (paged) | `:555` | `:567-569` |
| `page_produce_kv_on_the_fly` | `:639` | `:650-651` |
| `write_o_reg_gmem` | `:2006` | `:2014-2015` |

All three FA2 prefill kernels (`SinglePrefillWithKVCacheKernel:2448`,
`BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheKernel:2682`,
`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheKernel:4057`) go through these.

Two further observations:

1. **The invariant is already asserted in this very file**, only on paths the default
   configuration never instantiates:
   `static_assert(KTraits::NUM_MMA_D_QK % 4 == 0, "NUM_MMA_D_QK must be a multiple of
   4")` at `prefill.cuh:955`, `:991` and `:1278` — inside
   `q_smem_inplace_apply_rotary`, `q_smem_inplace_apply_rotary_with_pos` and
   `compute_qk_fp4_rope`. With `pos_encoding_mode="NONE"` none of them is compiled, so
   nothing stops the loader that violates the same invariant from building.
2. **`backend="auto"` actively routes these head dims into the affected kernel.**
   `determine_attention_backend` (`flashinfer/utils.py:571-576`) consults
   `is_fa3_prefill_head_dim_supported` (`:452` — `{64,128,256}` ∪ `{(192,128)}`) and,
   when it fails, returns `"fa2"`. There is no FA2-side counterpart to that predicate,
   so `head_dim=96` ends up in FA2 *because* FA3 declined it.

### Why the batch default path looks fine

`BatchPrefillWith{Ragged,Paged}KVCacheWrapper` reach the same kernel, but with
split-KV enabled the merge step (`VariableLengthMergeStates`,
`attention/cascade.cuh:687`, wrapped in `DISPATCH_HEAD_DIM` — `utils.cuh:194`, which
instantiates only `{64,128,256,512}`) rejects the head dim first, so you get a clean
`Unsupported head_dim: 96`. Pass the documented `plan(..., disable_split_kv=True)` and
the fault returns. The guard that exists lives in a kernel only some paths call.

## `compute-sanitizer`

memcheck localises regime 2, and the controls come back clean — which is what makes
the record quotable (`--report-api-errors no --check-api-memory-access no`; without
those, library-init API noise buries everything):

```
========= Invalid __shared__ read of size 16 bytes
=========     at void flashinfer::SinglePrefillWithKVCacheKernel<
                 flashinfer::KernelTraits<(flashinfer::MaskMode)1, 128u, 2u, 4u,
                 6u, 6u, 4u, 1u, (flashinfer::PosEncodingMode)0,
                 __half, __half, __half, float, int,
                 flashinfer::DefaultAttention<0,0,0,0>>, Params>(T2)+0x55e0
=========     by thread (31,3,0) in block (0,0,1)
=========     Access to 0xc420 is out of bounds
```

```
head_dim=96,  single_prefill      -> 48 errors, all "Invalid __shared__ read of size 16 bytes"
head_dim=64,  single_prefill      ->  0 errors      (control)
head_dim=96,  ragged, no split-KV -> 16 errors, same signature
head_dim=128, ragged, no split-KV ->  0 errors      (control)
```

`NUM_MMA_D_QK = NUM_MMA_D_VO = 6` in that mangled name is `head_dim = 96`, and 16
bytes is exactly one `b128_t` — the unit the swizzled offsets above are counted in.

Caveat: I did not map the SASS offset `+0x55e0` back to a source line (the module is
built without `-lineinfo`), so the sanitizer establishes *an* out-of-bounds shared
access in this kernel; the arithmetic above is what identifies the offset-drift family
as the mechanism, and **which of the five sites emits this particular access is not
proven.**

## Suggested resolution (your call)

* **Reject early.** Give FA2 prefill the counterpart of
  `is_fa3_prefill_head_dim_supported` and check `head_dim_qk` / `head_dim_vo` at the
  top of `single_prefill_with_kv_cache` and in `plan()`, before JIT compilation. For
  fp16 the predicate the kernel actually implements is `head_dim % 64 == 0` (fp8 KV
  would need `% 128` by the same arithmetic, since the loop divisor becomes
  `8 / sizeof(DTypeKV) == 8` — that is inference; I did not measure fp8). That is
  strictly better than today in every regime: the illegal access becomes an actionable
  error, the silent wrong answer becomes an actionable error, the `Invalid
  configuration … please create an issue` becomes an actionable error, and the user
  stops paying a 1–2 minute JIT compile before each failure.
* **Or support them**, by making the five loops iterate to the row end with a
  partial-tile tail. Note that this also has to fix the truncation in
  `NUM_MMA_D = HEAD_DIM / 16`, not just the offset drift.

If "reject" is the answer, I am happy to send that patch — it is small and the test
matrix above already exists. The only thing I would need from you is which predicate
should be authoritative.

Related but not a duplicate: #3176 / #3467 are the same class of defect in the same
function (an unvalidated Python-level input reaching the kernel) for `custom_mask`
rather than `head_dim`.

## What I am not claiming

* Not that upstream intends to support head_dim 72/80/96/112 — the evidence says the
  opposite. The report is that the failure mode is a fault or a wrong number instead
  of a rejection.
* **Not that the illegal access corrupts other allocations.** I looked for that
  specifically: sentinel guard regions around Q/K/V and (on the batch path, via
  `run(out=...)`) around the output, plus allocator-adjacency canaries around the
  output on the `single_prefill` path — 4 shape variants × 3 bad head dims × 2 code
  paths, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, one process each. Every regime-2 case faulted;
  **no case was observed in which such a call returned successfully and memory outside
  the tensors had been modified**, and every 64/128 control ran with zero guard
  violations. What the sanitizer reports is an out-of-bounds *read* of shared memory,
  which is consistent with that. Once the fault fires the CUDA context is dead, so the
  guards cannot be read back for the failing cases — the claim is "no out-of-tensor
  corruption observed", not "impossible".
* The regime-1 wrongness is *inside* the output tensor (columns the kernel never
  writes), not corruption of neighbouring memory — guard regions were clean there too.
* The sweep is partial: 28 head dims, single-request path, plus 5 head dims × 4 shapes
  on the ragged batch path. The regime boundaries are consistent across everything
  measured and follow from the source arithmetic, but I have not enumerated the whole
  range yet.
* The paged path is a source reading, not a measurement.
* fp8 / NVFP4 KV, FA3, and `head_dim_qk != head_dim_vo` combinations were not probed.

## Environment

FlashInfer `main` @ `668a1ba1ca86432c79f6adad37ecfce8d06ec083` (0.6.17), built from
source, JIT only, on an H200 (sm90), CUDA 13.0, driver 580.65.06,
torch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.13. One fresh process per measurement.

records.title: [Feature]: Support per-token NVFP4 activation scales in dense `mm_fp4`
records.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

vLLM recently added `--quantization nvfp4_per_token`, which quantizes BF16 expert weights to NVFP4 at load time and uses dynamic per-token activation scales https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48538.

This is currently MoE-only because FlashInfer’s fused-MoE kernels accept `per_token_scale`, while dense [mm_fp4](https://docs.flashinfer.ai/generated/flashinfer.gemm.mm_fp4.html) only exposes a scalar `alpha`. The quantizer already returns everything needed:

```python
a_fp4, a_sf, per_token_scale = nvfp4_quantize(
    a,
    1.0 / (448.0 * 6.0),
    per_token_activation=True,
)
```

Per-token support has also landed for the CuTe DSL MoE path in https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3645. This request is for the dense-GEMM equivalent.

### Requested outcome

Could one or more Blackwell dense NVFP4 backends behind `mm_fp4` accept the `[M]` FP32 `per_token_scale` returned by `nvfp4_quantize`?

For example:

```python
out = mm_fp4(
    a_fp4,
```

records.title: [Bug] sm12x MoE CuTe-DSL kernels are never disk-cached — cute.compile hardcodes no_cache=True, so every fresh engine re-pays 15–40 s MLIR compiles per kernel shape
records.body:
## Summary

The Blackwell sm12x fused-MoE path compiles all of its CuTe-DSL kernels through explicit
`cute.compile(...)`, which unconditionally disables the DSL's file cache. The only caching
layer is three in-process Python dicts, so **every engine start re-pays the full MLIR JIT
cost for every kernel specialization it touches** — measured at **~40 s** for the dynamic
kernel's first hit and **~15–18 s per small-`m` micro-kernel specialization**. In a serving
context (vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`) these compiles land mid-request and freeze
the whole engine (vllm#47458: ~17.5 s stop-the-world stalls, all in-flight requests frozen
including mid-decode).

`CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` / `CUTE_DSL_DISABLE_FILE_CACHING` have no effect on this path — the
gate that would consult them is short-circuited before they are read.

## Environment

- flashinfer 0.6.12, 0.6.13, and **0.6.15.post1** (all verified; `moe_dispatch.py` cache
  structure unchanged across them)
- nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0 and **4.6.0** (both verified)
- SM120: RTX 5070 Ti (×2, TP/PP), RTX 5090 (unsharded), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell — reproduced
  on all three in the vllm#47458 thread
- Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4` via vLLM `--moe-backend=flashinfer_b12x`

## Mechanism (exact code paths)

1. **The DSL hardcodes `no_cache=True` for explicit compiles.**
   `CompileCallable._compile` sets `kwargs["no_cache"] = True` unconditionally:
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.5.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:604-605`
   - nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.0: `base_dsl/compiler.py:1319`

2. **The file cache is gated behind `if not no_cache`** — both the load and the dump —
   so the env vars are never even consulted for explicit compiles:
   - 4.5.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:1645` (load), `:1736` (dump)
   - 4.6.0: `base_dsl/dsl.py:2004` (load), `:2105` (dump); in-memory `jit_cache` lookups
     likewise skipped under `no_cache` at `:2012`, `:2293`

3. **The sm12x MoE dispatch only ever compiles through `cute.compile`,** with plain
   in-process dicts on top — nothing reaches disk:
   - 0.6.12/0.6.13: `blackwell_sm12x/moe_dispatch.py:676/912/1675` (compile sites);
     `_STATIC/_MICRO/_DYNAMIC_KERNEL_CACHE`
   - 0.6.15.post1: compile sites at `:697/:942/:1723`; caches at `:486/:733/:1524`

4. Compounding factor (tracked separately as #3836): the micro-kernel `cache_key`
   includes both `m` and `workspace.max_rows` (0.6.15.post1 `moe_dispatch.py:770-791`,
   fields at `:774`/`:778`), so workspace growth invalidates already-compiled small-batch
   entries even *within* a process lifetime. With no disk layer underneath, each
   invalidation is a full 15 s+ recompile, not a reload.

## Verification

Behavioral check from the vllm#47458 thread (credit @waynehacking8, on 0.6.12 / DSL 4.5.0):

- `cute.compile` of a trivial `@cute.jit` function leaves `CUTE_DSL_CACHE_DIR` **empty**.
- Calling the same jit function **directly** (implicit compile path) writes
  `cute_dsl_<hash>.mlir`, and a fresh process then logs `JIT cache hit IN-FILE`.
- Only the implicit direct-call path caches; flashinfer's MoE dispatch never uses it.

Source-level re-verification on 0.6.15.post1 / DSL 4.6.0 (2026-08-02, inside the
`vllm/vllm-openai` nightly image): every line cite in the Mechanism section above was
confirmed against the installed packages — the hardcoded `no_cache=True`, the
`if not no_cache` gates around both file-cache load and dump, the three `cute.compile`
sites, the three in-process dicts, and `m`/`max_rows` still present in the micro-kernel
cache key.

Measured first-hit compile costs (RTX PRO 6000, synthetic MoE E=32/topk=4 driving
`B12xMoEWrapper.run` exactly as vLLM's `FlashInferB12xExperts` does):

| kernel path | first hit | subsequent (same key) |
|---|---|---|
| dynamic (m-independent key) | ~40 s | 1–3 ms |
| micro m=1 | 14.9 s | ms |
| micro m=2 | 15.2 s | ms |
| micro m=64 | 18.3 s | ms |

Production symptom: vllm#47458 — py-spy captured 16 consecutive samples over 8.35 s pinned
in `b12x_fused_moe (flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/b12x_moe.py:166)` during a live
~17.5 s engine-wide stall; `perf` showed `_cutlass_ir.cpython-312.so` frames present only
during stalls.

## Why this deserves a disk layer even after #3836

#3836 stops *rekeying* (recompiles within one process). But serving engines restart —
deploys, config changes, crash recovery, autoscaling — and each fresh process re-pays the
entire compile set: ~40 s dynamic + 15–18 s per small-shape class. For a model like
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B this is 1–2 minutes of mid-serving stalls per engine lifetime that a
disk cache would reduce to milliseconds. The artifacts are deterministic products of
(kernel source, shape/config tuple, DSL version, arch) — exactly what file caches are for.

## Suggested fix directions

Either would resolve it; the first is contained entirely in flashinfer:

1. **flashinfer grows its own disk layer for sm12x MoE kernels**: serialize the compiled
   artifact keyed by the existing `cache_key` tuples + flashinfer version +
   nvidia-cutlass-dsl version + SM arch, under `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_DIR` (or a new env),
   loading into `_STATIC/_MICRO/_DYNAMIC_KERNEL_CACHE` on miss. The DSL's own
   `compile_and_cache` machinery demonstrates the artifact is serializable (the implicit
   path already writes/reads `.mlir` + compiled objects).
2. **Upstream: nvidia-cutlass-dsl honors its file cache under explicit `cute.compile`**
   (stop hardcoding `no_cache=True`, or add an opt-in kwarg flashinfer can pass).

A third, cheaper-but-partial option is an official warm-up API (the attempt in
vllm#47599 was closed unmerged): it moves the cost to boot but still re-pays it every
process start, and needs the largest-workspace-first ordering to avoid #3836 rekeying —
a disk cache composes with, rather than replaces, that.

## Cross-references

- vllm#47458 — serving-stall report this splits from (mechanism established in-thread by
  @waynehacking8; py-spy confirmation by me)
- flashinfer#3836 — the workspace-rekeying half (open)
- vllm#47599 — warm-up mitigation PR (closed, unmerged)
- flashinfer#3807 — earlier sm12x smem-overflow issue in the same dispatch (fixed)

records.title: [Bug] `test_quantized_allreduce_scale_groups` flakes with TCPStore `EADDRINUSE` when run under `mpirun -np 4`
records.body:
## Summary

  `tests/comm/test_quantized_allreduce.py::test_quantized_allreduce_scale_groups` failed in CI with:
  Failed job: https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/382853443

  ```text
  torch.distributed.DistNetworkError: The server socket has failed to listen on any local network address.
  port: 52078, useIpv6: false, code: -98, name: EADDRINUSE, message: address already in use
```
  This looks like a test harness / launch-mode issue rather than a quantized allreduce kernel correctness failure.

  The file appears to be run under an outer mpirun -np 4, while the test itself already creates its own distributed workers  via torch.multiprocessing.spawn. That can launch multiple pytest parent processes concurrently, each running the same test and choosing random TCPStore ports, which makes port collision possible.

  ## Failure Log

  The failing command was:
```
  timeout --kill-after=300s 7200s mpirun -np 4 pytest --continue-on-collection-errors --junitxml=/tmp/junit/
  tests_comm_test_quantized_allreduce.py.4173784547.xml "tests/comm/test_quantized_allreduce.py"
```
  The pytest session header appeared multiple times, consistent with multiple pytest parents launched by mpirun:

  tests/comm/test_quantized_allreduce.py ============================= test session starts ==============================
  platform linux -- Python 3.12.13, pytest-9.0.3, pluggy-1.6.0
  rootdir: /workspace/flashinfer
  configfile: pytest.ini
  collected 3 items

  Failure:

  FAILED tests/comm/test_quantized_allreduce.py::test_quantized_allreduce_scale_groups

  torch.multiprocessing.spawn.ProcessRaisedException:

  -- Process 0 terminated with the following error:
    File "/workspace/flashinfer/tests/comm/test_quantized_allreduce.py", line 118, in run_scale_group_sweep
      device, group = setup(rank, world_size, port)

    File "/workspace/flashinfer/tests/comm/test_quantized_allreduce.py", line 66, in setup
      dist.init_process_group(...)

  torch.distributed.DistNetworkError:
  The server socket has failed to listen on any local network address.
  port: 52078, useIpv6: false, code: -98, name: EADDRINUSE, message: address already in use

  Captured stderr:

  torch/multiprocessing/spawn.py:165] Terminating process 23383 via signal SIGTERM
  torch/multiprocessing/spawn.py:165] Terminating process 23384 via signal SIGTERM
  torch/multiprocessing/spawn.py:165] Terminating process 23385 via signal SIGTERM

  ## Why This Looks Like a Harness Issue

  tests/comm/test_quantized_allreduce.py already owns distributed process creation:

  port = random.randint(30000, 60000)
  world_size = _supported_world_size()
  mp.spawn(run_scale_group_sweep, args=(world_size, port), nprocs=world_size, join=True)

  But the multi-GPU comm script runs it under:

  mpirun -np 4 pytest tests/comm/test_quantized_allreduce.py

  So the effective process shape becomes:

  mpirun -np 4
    -> 4 pytest parent processes
         -> each parent runs test_quantized_allreduce_scale_groups
              -> each parent calls mp.spawn(...)
                   -> each spawned rank tries to init TCPStore

  This multiplies the intended workload and can race/collide on randomly selected ports.

  ## Expected Behavior

  tests/comm/test_quantized_allreduce.py should run once with plain pytest, letting its internal mp.spawn create the distributed workers:

  pytest tests/comm/test_quantized_allreduce.py -v

  ## Suggested Fix (By Codex)

  Move tests/comm/test_quantized_allreduce.py out of the mpirun-based TEST_FILES list in scripts/
  task_test_multi_gpu_comm_kernels.sh.

  Keep MPI-style tests such as tests/comm/test_allreduce_unified_api.py under mpirun, but run test_quantized_allreduce.py separately without PYTEST_COMMAND_PREFIX.

  Alternative: make test_quantized_allreduce.py detect OMPI_COMM_WORLD_RANK and only execute on MPI rank 0, but running it as plain pytest is cleaner because the file already manages its own distributed workers.

records.title: [Feature]: DCP-aware interface and behaviour for `trtllm_mha` to support DCP + Spec
records.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

We are adding DCP (decode context parallelism) + speculative decoding for GQA models in SGLang
(sgl-project/sglang#32795, sgl-project/sglang#32858), which requires

1. Strided KV ownership. Local key `c` on rank `r` = global pos `c * cp_world + r`. Kernel sees only this rank’s shard + local page table / `seq_lens`
2. Support `return_lse`
3. Global causal masking via `causal_seqs` + `cp_world` + `cp_rank`

What we'd want is roughly what #4178 did for MLA: `cp_world`, `cp_rank`, and a
`causal_seqlens_kv_global` carrying the global per-request KV length, with the
per-row bound worked out inside the kernel.  

See  [DCP design document ](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1pjBSID0palpuI7rx8Ck7Z0BcyzBXAgnkDrf9uQg0uqU/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.9w6mfr2kxls6) or our [blog](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-27-kimi-k3-day0-support/#decode-context-parallelism:~:text=next%20part%20covers.-,Decode%3A%20context%20parallelism,-Decode%20is%20where) for more details on how KV is sharded across ranks

Longer note: For DCP (non-spec), we currently shard the token dimension
round-robin — local key `c` on rank `r` is global position `c*cp_world + r` —
and build a compacted page table plus rank-local `seq_lens` host-side, so the
kernel never sees the striding. `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` already
returns the partial LSE we need for the cross-rank merge, and plain DCP decode
works today. However it breaks at `q_len_per_req > 1`, which is what we need for spec decode. With
`L` draft tokens, query row `j` of request `i` should see local keys up to `floor((S_i + j - r) / cp_world) + 1`. That steps by one every `cp_world` rows, so it isn't the affine `seq_len - L + j + 1` the kernel derives internally, and no single `seq_lens` value per request expresses it. We can't precompute it host-side either without a per-row length tensor, which breaks our CUDA graph static buffers.

### Requested outcome

Add DCP + Spec support for `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` (or other cutedsl MHA backends ?)

SM100 (B200, GB200), SM103 (B300, GB300)

records.title: Question: Should split-KV batch_prefill_tmp_v workspace use sizeof_dtype_o instead of sizeof(float)?
records.body:
Hi, I noticed a possible inconsistency in the FA2 batch prefill planner around the split-KV temporary output workspace.

In `PrefillPlanImpl`, the function accepts a `sizeof_dtype_o` argument:

```cpp
bool enable_cuda_graph, uint32_t sizeof_dtype_o, ...
```

but the argument is currently unused:

```cpp
(void)sizeof_dtype_o;
```

When split-KV is enabled, the temporary output buffer `batch_prefill_tmp_v` is allocated with `sizeof(float)`:

```cpp
plan_info.v_offset = float_allocator.aligned_alloc_offset(
    num_qo_heads * padded_batch_size * cta_tile_q * head_dim_vo * sizeof(float),
    16,
    "batch_prefill_tmp_v");
```

However, at run time this buffer is interpreted as `DTypeO*`:

```cpp
tmp_v = GetPtrFromBaseOffset<DTypeO>(float_buffer_ptr, plan_info.v_offset);
```

and the prefill kernel writes partial outputs through `params.o = tmp_v`, where `params.o` is also `DTypeO*`.

So I wanted to ask whether the `sizeof(float)` allocation is intentional here.

My understanding is that `tmp_s` / LSE should be float, but `tmp_v` represents partial output values and should probably be sized according to `DTypeO`, i.e. using `sizeof_dtype_o`. With the current code, fp16/bf16 output appears to over-allocate the `tmp_v` workspace by 2x. This is probably safe from a correctness perspective for current fp16/bf16 paths, but it makes the workspace size larger than necessary and seems inconsistent with the existing `sizeof_dtype_o` parameter.

Would it make sense to change this allocation to:

```cpp
num_qo_heads * padded_batch_size * cta_tile_q * head_dim_vo * sizeof_dtype_o
```

and pass `sizeof(DTypeO)` from `csrc/batch_prefill.cu` instead of the current hardcoded `/*sizeof_dtype_o=*/2`?

Thanks!

### Bug description

# SM120 sparse MLA dsv4 decode: missing kernel instance for (num_heads=32, topk=256) crashes DSPark drafts

**flashinfer-python**: 0.6.16.post1 (also reproduced on 0.6.15.post1 and 0.6.13)
**Hardware**: NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark, compute capability 12.1 / SM121a), CUDA 13.0, aarch64

## Problem

`trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4` crashes for decode with num_tokens<=64 when `num_heads=32, topk=256`:

```
tvm.error.InternalError: Check failed: num_tokens > 64 (7 vs. 64) :
Decode (num_tokens <= 64) must go through sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv3_2
or sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4; got num_tokens=7
```

(also, for num_tokens>64 the same shape hits: `Unsupported sparse-MLA prefill configuration: model=DSV4 num_heads=32 topk=256 page_block_size=64`)

## Root cause

`_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH` in `flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120.py` only instantiates
topk ∈ {128, 512, 1024}:

```python
_DECODE_DSV4_DISPATCH = frozenset({
    (8, 128), (8, 512), (8, 1024),
    (16, 128), (16, 512), (16, 1024),
    (32, 128), (32, 512), (32, 1024),
    (64, 128), (64, 512), (64, 1024),
    (128, 128), (128, 512), (128, 1024),
})
```

`(32, 256)` is missing. The kernel instances are precompiled per (num_heads, topk):
adding the tuple to the python set alone changes the error to
`decode-dsv4 launch failed (unsupported shape or kernel error)`, i.e. no compiled
instance exists for the shape.

## Impact

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731's **DSPark draft attention uses topk=256 with num_heads=32**
(at TP=2), so DSPark warmup crashes on sm120. Workaround applied in vLLM:
pad indices from 256 to 512 before the call (verified numerically safe — the
kernel masks strictly by `topk_length`, padded entries are ignored).

Also checked: upstream `main` branch (fetched 2026-08-04) has the same missing `(32, 256)`.

## Repro (synthetic)

```python
import torch
from flashinfer.mla._core import trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4

q = torch.randn(7, 1, 32, 512, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
kv = torch.zeros(8, 1, 64, 584, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
idx = torch.randint(0, 8, (7, 256), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
ws = torch.empty(64*1024*1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
out = torch.empty(7, 32, 512, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
lens = torch.full((7,), 256, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
seq = torch.full((7,), 100, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
trtllm_batch_decode_sparse_mla_dsv4(
    query=q, swa_kv_cache=kv, workspace_buffer=ws, sparse_indices=idx,
    out=out, bmm1_scale=1.0, seq_lens=seq, swa_topk_lens=lens)
# -> Check failed: num_tokens > 64 (7 vs. 64)
```

With `num_heads=32, topk=128` or `512` the same call succeeds.

## Suggestion

Add the `(32, 256)` instance (and consider whether DSV4 drafts can produce other
topk values, e.g. 256 with num_heads=16/64 at other TP sizes) to the sm120 dsv4
decode instantiation set. Also consider a graceful fallback instead of the hard
assert when a shape is outside the instantiation set and num_tokens<=64.

### Bug description

Despite larger power-of-two page sizes intending to be supported, for page sizes > 128, `trtllm_batch_context_with_kv_cache` fails to produce correct outputs, appearing to attend only to the first 4096 and last page of tokens:
```
device=NVIDIA B200 sm=10.0 qo_heads=32 kv_heads=2 head_dim=256

page_len x seqlen (head_dim=256), cos vs SDPA:
page\\seq |   1024 |   2048 |   4096 |   6144 |   8192 |   8864 |  12288 |  16384
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
      128 | ok 1.000 | ok 1.000 | ok 1.000 | ok 1.000 | ok 1.000 | ok 1.000 | ok 1.000 | ok 1.000
      256 | ok 1.000 | ok 1.000 | ok 1.000 | XX 0.979 | XX 0.902 | XX 0.931 | XX 0.965 | XX 0.937
```

Unfortunately, the kernel is closed-source, which makes additional debugging difficult. Attaching simple repro.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from flashinfer.prefill import get_trtllm_gen_fmha_module
from flashinfer.utils import get_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_bytes

DEVICE = torch.device("cuda:0")
DTYPE = torch.bfloat16
NUM_QO_HEADS = 32
NUM_KV_HEADS = 2
PAGE_LENS = [128, 256]
COSINE_PASS = 0.99


def _reference(q: torch.Tensor, k: torch.Tensor, v: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    # q: [S, Hq, D]; k/v: [S, Hkv, D]. Causal GQA attention in fp32.
    qh = q.permute(1, 0, 2).unsqueeze(0).float()  # [1, Hq, S, D]
    kh = k.permute(1, 0, 2).unsqueeze(0).float()  # [1, Hkv, S, D]
    vh = v.permute(1, 0, 2).unsqueeze(0).float()
    out = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(qh, kh, vh, is_causal=True, enable_gqa=True)
    return out[0].permute(1, 0, 2).contiguous()  # [S, Hq, D]


def _trtllm_paged(
    module: object,
    q: torch.Tensor,
    k: torch.Tensor,
    v: torch.Tensor,
    page_len: int,
    workspace: torch.Tensor,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    seqlen, hq, head_dim = q.shape
    hkv = k.shape[1]
    num_pages = (seqlen + page_len - 1) // page_len

    k_nhd = torch.zeros(
        num_pages, page_len, hkv, head_dim, dtype=q.dtype, device=DEVICE
    )
    v_nhd = torch.zeros_like(k_nhd)
    for t in range(seqlen):
        k_nhd[t // page_len, t % page_len] = k[t]
        v_nhd[t // page_len, t % page_len] = v[t]
    k_hnd = k_nhd.permute(0, 2, 1, 3).contiguous()
    v_hnd = v_nhd.permute(0, 2, 1, 3).contiguous()

    block_tables = torch.arange(num_pages, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE).view(1, -1)
    kv_lens = torch.tensor([seqlen], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
    qo_indptr = torch.tensor([0, seqlen], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
    kv_indptr = torch.tensor([0, num_pages], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
    num_sms = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(DEVICE).multi_processor_count
    sm_scale = 1.0 / (head_dim**0.5)
    out = torch.empty_like(q)

    kv_counter = torch.zeros(
        get_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_bytes(1, hq, num_sms),
        dtype=torch.uint8,
        device=DEVICE,
    )

    module.trtllm_paged_attention_context(  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        out,
        None,
        q,
        k_hnd,
        v_hnd,
        workspace,
        kv_counter,
        block_tables,
        kv_lens,
        seqlen,  # max_qo_len
        seqlen,  # max_kv_len
        sm_scale,  # bmm1_scale
        1.0,  # bmm2_scale
        -1,  # o_sf_scale
        -1,  # o_sf_vec_scale
        0,  # o_sf_start_index
        1,  # batch_size
        -1,  # window_left
        qo_indptr,
        kv_indptr,
        num_sms,
        False,  # enable_pdl
        workspace.numel() * workspace.dtype.itemsize,  # workspace_size
        None,  # sinks
        None,  # key_block_scales
        None,  # value_block_scales
        None,  # skip_softmax_threshold_scale_factor
        True,  # uses_shared_paged_kv_idx
        True,  # is_causal
        None,  # lse
        0,  # lse_stride_tokens
        0,  # lse_stride_heads
    )
    return out


def _measure(
    module: object, page_len: int, seqlen: int, head_dim: int, workspace: torch.Tensor
) -> float:
    q = torch.randn(seqlen, NUM_QO_HEADS, head_dim, dtype=DTYPE, device=DEVICE) * 0.5
    k = torch.randn(seqlen, NUM_KV_HEADS, head_dim, dtype=DTYPE, device=DEVICE) * 0.5
    v = torch.randn(seqlen, NUM_KV_HEADS, head_dim, dtype=DTYPE, device=DEVICE) * 0.5
    ref = _reference(q, k, v)
    out = _trtllm_paged(module, q, k, v, page_len, workspace)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return F.cosine_similarity(
        out.float().flatten(), ref.flatten(), dim=0, eps=1e-8
    ).item()


def main() -> None:
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(DEVICE)
    print(
        f"device={props.name} sm={props.major}.{props.minor} "
        f"qo_heads={NUM_QO_HEADS} kv_heads={NUM_KV_HEADS} head_dim=256",
        flush=True,
    )
    module = get_trtllm_gen_fmha_module()
    workspace = torch.empty(256 * 1024 * 1024 // 4, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)

    seqlens = [1024, 2048, 4096, 6144, 8192, 8864, 12288, 16384]
    print("\npage_len x seqlen (head_dim=256), cos vs SDPA:", flush=True)
    print(f"{'page\\\\seq':>9} | " + " | ".join(f"{s:>6}" for s in seqlens), flush=True)
    print("-" * (12 + 9 * len(seqlens)), flush=True)
    for page_len in PAGE_LENS:
        cells = []
        for seqlen in seqlens:
            cos = _measure(module, page_len, seqlen, 256, workspace)
            cells.append(("ok " if cos >= COSINE_PASS else "XX ") + f"{cos:.3f}")
        print(f"{page_len:>9} | " + " | ".join(f"{c:>6}" for c in cells), flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

records.title: [Bug] CUDA 13/aarch64 JIT-cache package lacks SM107/10.7a coverage
records.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

On aarch64 SM107 hardware, FlashInfer’s prebuilt JIT-cache package fails when running the BF16 paged-MLA specialization used by Kimi K3 (head_dim_ckv=512, head_dim_kpe=64):

  `Failed to run MLA, error: no kernel image is available for execution on the device`

The CUDA 13/aarch64 JIT-cache release matrix omits 10.7a, although SM107 source-build support was added in PR #4122. This affected flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.16rc5+cu130, and the 0.6.16.post1 release workflow still omitted 10.7a.

As a control, we removed flashinfer-jit-cache, set FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.7a, and source-JIT compiled the same operator with FlashInfer 0.6.16.post1. It passed numerical validation and completed two-node TP8 Kimi K3 serving with full GSM8K accuracy. This indicates a JIT-cache release-coverage issue rather than an operator-correctness issue.

### Requested outcome

Please add SM107/10.7a coverage to the CUDA 13/aarch64 JIT-cache release workflow and publish a matching flashinfer-jit-cache package containing an executable image for this paged-MLA specialization.

Possibly also add an SM107 regression test confirming that the published package can execute BF16 paged MLA without uninstalling the JIT cache or triggering a local source build.

### Target hardware

Future architecture

### Inference engine

SGLang

### Affected model or model family

Kimi K3

### Workload and configuration

BF16 paged-MLA specialization used by Kimi K3 (head_dim_ckv=512, head_dim_kpe=64)

### Current workaround

pip uninstall -y flashinfer-jit-cache
export FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.7a

Then run with flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post1, allowing FlashInfer to source-JIT and cache the paged-MLA kernel locally.

records.title: [Feature] MLA decode: add fold_sq to trtllm-gen so one backend is fast at all context lengths
records.body:
## TL;DR

All numbers below are attention TP8, DCP off.

On SM100, MLA decode has two backends: `trtllm-gen` and `cute-dsl`. Neither is faster in all cases. `trtllm-gen` wins at `q=1` (plain decode) and at short context. `cute-dsl` wins at `q>1` (MTP/spec verify) above a context threshold (~100k for bf16 q=8, ~200k for fp8). A framework must fix one backend at launch (it goes into the CUDA graphs), and `backend="auto"` + the autotuner cannot pick by context length. We ask for `fold_sq` in `trtllm-gen` so a single backend is fast at every context length.

## What we see

On SM100 (B200/B300), neither MLA decode backend is faster in all cases:

- `q=1` (plain decode): `trtllm-gen` always faster.
- `q>1` (MTP/spec verify): `cute-dsl` faster above a context threshold (~100k for bf16 q=8, ~200k for fp8), `trtllm-gen` below it.

Example, TP8, µs/call (trtllm-gen | cute-dsl), decode backend the only variable (lower is faster):

| q | 131k | 500k | 1000k |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (bf16) | 94 / 122 | 143 / 177 | 254 / 331 |
| 8 (bf16) | 201 / 124 | 717 / 193 | 1413 / 359 |
| 8 (fp8) | 103 / 124 | 343 / 123 | 667 / 168 |

Reason: `cute-dsl` folds the `q` verify tokens into the MMA tile (`fold_sq`), so it reads the KV once and stays flat in context. `trtllm-gen` re-reads KV per query row, so it grows as O(ctx·q). End-to-end in SGLang (Kimi-K3, q=8, 900k, 8×B300): decode throughput 98 → 197 tok/s.

## Why the autotuner doesn't help

`backend="auto"` builds both runners, but it cannot pick by context length:
- It tunes at one fixed context (`profile_seq_len`) and sweeps the batch dim, not context ([`mla/_core.py` L2152](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.6.15.post1/flashinfer/mla/_core.py#L2152), [L2198](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/v0.6.15.post1/flashinfer/mla/_core.py#L2198)).
- It profiles only inside `flashinfer.autotune(True)`; otherwise it returns `trtllm-gen` with no measurement.

A launch-time choice does not work either. The best backend depends on the run-time context length. An operator does not know that length at launch. One deployment serves many context lengths, and the context of a single sequence grows during decode. So no fixed choice is right for every request. The operator cannot pick the best backend, and SGLang cannot pick it for them, because the backend goes into the CUDA graphs and cannot change per request or per step.

## Why it hurts (MTP)

Without DCP, MTP mixes `q=1` and long-context `q>1` steps and wants one backend for both. No single backend wins: `trtllm-gen` is faster at `q=1`, `cute-dsl` is faster at long-context `q>1`. The backend is fixed at launch (it goes into the CUDA graphs), so the framework must eat a regression on one regime.

## Request

Add `fold_sq` to the `trtllm-gen` MLA decode kernel (fold `seq_q` into MMA-M, as `cute-dsl` does). It stays best at `q=1` and becomes flat in context at `q>1`, so `trtllm-gen` wins or ties at every context length. A framework can then standardize on one backend with no context-length trade-off.

## Reproduction

flashinfer `0.6.15.post1`, one B300 (SM100). The script sweeps the isolated MLA decode call for both backends and prints the table above (TP8 / H=12, q=1 and q=8, bf16 and fp8, ctx 131k/500k/1000k), µs per call.

<details><summary>repro.py</summary>

```python
import torch, flashinfer

dev = "cuda"
KV_LORA, ROPE, NOPE, HDQK, PAGE = 512, 64, 128, 576, 64
H = 12  # query heads per rank at TP8 (1 KV head, MQA)
torch.manual_seed(0)

def counter_buf(h):
    import flashinfer.utils as fu
    try:
        n = int(fu.get_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_bytes(dev, h, 1))
        return torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev)
    except Exception:
        return None

def make_kv(kv_len, dt):
    npp = (kv_len + PAGE - 1) // PAGE
    if npp % 2:
        npp += 1
    kv = torch.randn(npp, PAGE, HDQK, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(dt)
    bt = torch.arange(npp, device=dev, dtype=torch.int32).view(1, npp)
    sl = torch.full((1,), kv_len, device=dev, dtype=torch.int32)
    ws = torch.zeros(512 * 1024 * 1024, device=dev, dtype=torch.uint8)
    return kv, bt, sl, ws

def bench(kv, bt, sl, kv_len, q, backend, ws, dt):
    query = torch.randn(1, q, H, HDQK, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16).to(dt)
    kw = dict(query=query, kv_cache=kv, workspace_buffer=ws,
              qk_nope_head_dim=NOPE, kv_lora_rank=KV_LORA, qk_rope_head_dim=ROPE,
              block_tables=bt, seq_lens=sl, max_seq_len=kv_len,
              bmm1_scale=1 / (192 ** 0.5), bmm2_scale=1.0)
    if backend == "trtllm-gen":
        kw.update(backend="trtllm-gen", enable_pdl=True,
                  multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer=counter_buf(H))
    else:
        kw.update(backend=backend)
    f = flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla
    try:
        for _ in range(8):
            f(**kw)
    except Exception:
        return None
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    s, e = torch.cuda.Event(True), torch.cuda.Event(True)
    s.record()
    for _ in range(30):
        f(**kw)
    e.record()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    return s.elapsed_time(e) / 30 * 1000  # us/call

print("dtype,q,ctx,trtllm_us,cutedsl_us")
for dt, tag in [(torch.bfloat16, "bf16"), (torch.float8_e4m3fn, "fp8")]:
    for q in [1, 8]:
        for kv_len in [131072, 500000, 1000000]:
            kv, bt, sl, ws = make_kv(kv_len, dt)
            tr = bench(kv, bt, sl, kv_len, q, "trtllm-gen", ws, dt)
            cd = bench(kv, bt, sl, kv_len, q, "cute-dsl", ws, dt)
            print(f"{tag},{q},{kv_len},{tr and round(tr,1)},{cd and round(cd,1)}", flush=True)
            del kv, bt, sl, ws
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
```

</details>

Happy to share the wider sweep (TP1/TP4/TP16, all q, more contexts) and nsys captures.

records.title: bmm_fp8 shared workspace growth frees storage referenced by captured CUDA graphs → Xid 31 MMU fault / silent corruption at replay
records.body:
## Summary

The shared fp8 GEMM workspace (`_get_cache_buf("bmm_fp8_workspace", 32MB)`) is grown by **freeing and reallocating** — `workspace.resize_(workspace_size)` in the cuDNN execute paths, and entry replacement in `_get_cache_buf` itself. A CUDA graph captured before the growth holds the old device address as a baked kernel argument (a value, not a reference), so after the growth every previously captured graph replays through a dangling pointer:

- if the freed VA gets unmapped → **GPU MMU fault at first replay**: `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure`, dmesg `Xid 31: MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS HUBCLIENT_FE FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_WRITE`, fault address = freed workspace base + fixed offset;
- if the freed block is reused by another allocation → **silent memory corruption** (no error at all).

Present in v0.6.13 through current `main` (8 `resize_(workspace_size)` sites in `gemm/gemm_base.py` at v0.6.14; 10 on main including `gemm/gemm_bf16_fp4_cudnn.py:271,334`), plus the `_get_cache_buf` growth path in `utils.py`.

## Environment where hit in production

FlashInfer 0.6.13/0.6.14 · vLLM 0.26.0 (`bmm_fp8(backend="auto")`, FULL+PIECEWISE cudagraphs) · torch 2.11 cu130 · cuDNN 9.19 · 8× RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120), TP8 · FP8 per-tensor checkpoint (`nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1_5-FP8`). Crash rate at this config: 5/5.

## Root-cause chain (verified by instrumentation)

1. All three fp8 runners (cutlass / cublas / cudnn) share ONE growable 32 MiB buffer per device, cached for process lifetime (`utils.py::_get_cache_buf`; handed to runners in `fp8_gemm_sm100`).
2. Only the cuDNN execute paths grow it: `execute_cudnn_gemm_fp8_graph` computes the selected plan's workspace demand at execute time and calls `workspace.resize_()` (v0.6.14 `gemm_base.py:3108-3110`; override-shape twin at `:3249-3253`). `resize_` to a larger size reallocates and frees the old storage.
3. The autotuner never grows the real buffer during tuning: the workspace input is a wildcard (`ConstraintSpec(5, 0, ...)`, `gemm_base.py:1077`), so all profiling `resize_` calls hit synthesized throwaway tensors.
4. With `backend="auto"`, every pre-capture eager execution runs cutlass (tuner cache-miss fallback = `runners[0]`) or cublas — which structurally cannot grow the buffer (`CUBLASLT_MATMUL_PREF_MAX_WORKSPACE_BYTES = numel`, `bmm_fp8.cuh:202`). The first execution of an oversized tuned cuDNN plan against the *real* buffer therefore lands in the middle of the caller's capture sequence (observed at 8–75% of vLLM's capture sweep, in the eager warmup between captures, where `is_current_stream_capturing()` is False).
5. Observed trigger on cuDNN 9.19: engine `eng0` sits at plan indices 0 and 8 at *every* shape under `policy=ALL` and demands exactly **33,554,688 bytes = DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_SIZE + 256** — any tuned pick of it forces the growth.

Instrumented run (TP rank 0): workspace created at `0x7efb42000000` → **56 graph nodes captured with that pointer baked** (24 cublas + 32 cudnn) → `resize_` frees it mid-sequence, new buffer at `0x7efb2e000000` → 658 more nodes on the new pointer → first replay → ULF. The historical fault-address invariant (`…700000` low bits across machines/driver branches r580+r595) is the freed buffer's base + 0x700000.

## Why existing mitigations don't close it

- #4165 gates cuDNN out of sm12x `auto` (when override_shape is unavailable) — masks this SKU family, leaves the defect live wherever cuDNN participates (sm_100/103).
- #3707 (engine/knob tactics, 0.6.16) removes the bucket-index→exact-shape plan remap that *amplifies* the trigger, but any legitimately tuned plan needing > current buffer still fires the unsafe growth.
- Forced single backends dodge it structurally (cublas: C++ workspace clamp; cudnn-only: buffer grows in pre-capture eager runs) — which is exactly why only `auto` crashes and why the bug looked nondeterministic.

## Minimal repro

Two single-GPU tests (seconds, no model, CI-safe — they detect the use-after-free as corruption/pointer-invalidation instead of relying on the fault): capture a graph holding the buffer's pointer → grow through the stock entry points (`_get_cache_buf`; `_cudnn_gemm_fp8` with a plan whose workspace demand exceeds the buffer) → replay / assert. Both fail on v0.6.14 and current main, and are included in the fix PR.

## Proposed fix

Grow by **retiring** the old tensor into a keep-alive registry instead of freeing it (growth is monotone per buffer, so retention is bounded to a handful of buffers). PR incoming. Natural follow-ups (separate PRs): constrain cuDNN plan selection to the buffer budget via `cudnn-frontend`'s `deselect_workspace_greater_than` (mirrors the cublas contract), and/or a VA-stable growable workspace via CUDA VMM (`cuMemAddressReserve` + `cuMemMap`), both validated locally.
