records.author: aleozlx

records.title: [KDA] Unify flashinfer.recurrent_kda API
records.body:
## Context

Status as of 2026-08-12 on FlashInfer `main`.

FlashInfer currently has **two decorated functions named `recurrent_kda`** with divergent signatures and opposite backend-selection policies. That split landed across recent CAKE/KDA PRs and is already affecting how new kernels are proposed (e.g. packed serving-native decode).

This is a **design / tracking** issue, not a correctness bug in any one kernel. Related CAKE progress is tracked in [#4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254); this issue is specifically about the **public Python API contract**.

## Current public surface (main)

| Import path | Defined in | `@flashinfer_api` | Notable kwargs | Routing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flashinfer.recurrent_kda` | `flashinfer/kda.py` | yes (`recurrent_kda_trace`) | `seq_order`, `prefill_workspace` | Eligible ordinary **prefill** → frozen FlashKDA (`_run_flash_kda_prefill`). Otherwise → `run_recurrent_kda` via raw `_run_recurrent_kda` (**bypasses** decorated `kda_decode.recurrent_kda`; **does not pass `backend=`**, so default `backend="cute-dsl"` applies). For decode/spec that means **CuTe DSL only** — exported FlashKDA decode is selected only when `backend="cake"`, which this path never sets |
| `flashinfer.kda_decode.recurrent_kda` | `flashinfer/kda_decode.py` | yes (same trace template) | `backend: "cute-dsl" \| "cake"` (default `"cute-dsl"`) | No frozen-prefill dispatch; always `run_recurrent_kda(backend=…)`. Callable with `T>1`, but does **not** auto-select frozen prefill (docstring focuses on T=1 decode shapes). Default `cute-dsl` → CuTe DSL decode. `backend="cake"` → strict exported FlashKDA decode (raises when no matching export; no CuTe fallback) |
| `flashinfer.fused_kda_decode` | `flashinfer/kda_decode.py` | yes (`fused_kda_decode_trace`) | packed QKV + conv + RMSNorm | Separate Kimi K3 fused op |
| `flashinfer.RecurrentKDAPrefillWorkspace` | `flashinfer/kda_prefill.py` | n/a (type) | graph-capture workspace | Top-level export |

Top-level `__init__.py` exports:

- `recurrent_kda` from **`kda`** (not `kda_decode`)
- `fused_kda_decode` from `kda_decode`
- `RecurrentKDAPrefillWorkspace` from `kda_prefill`

`flashinfer.kda.recurrent_kda` works via submodule import but `flashinfer.kda` itself is **not** re-exported from the package root — only the `recurrent_kda` symbol is.

`flashinfer.kda_kernels` also re-exports both noun aliases (`recurrent_kda`, `fused_kda_decode`) and `run_*` backends, which blurs public vs internal.

Docs are split across three pages: `docs/api/kda.rst`, `kda_decode.rst`, `kda_prefill.rst`. Today `kda_decode.rst` documents both `recurrent_kda` and `fused_kda_decode` (not fused-only).

**In-repo usage today:** Prefill tests/benchmarks use the top-level / `kda` facade. Decode paths — including Cake export tests **and** the main CuTe DSL correctness suite `tests/kda/test_recurrent_kda.py`, plus decode benchmarks — import **`flashinfer.kda_decode.recurrent_kda`**, not the top-level symbol. fi_trace examples also call the decode facade. The split affects Cake *and* CuTe callers, not Cake-only.

## How we got here

| PR / issue | Effect on API |
|---|---|
| #4262 | Introduced phase-neutral `flashinfer.kda.recurrent_kda` and switched the top-level export to it; automatic frozen **prefill** dispatch |
| #4279 | Added `backend="cake"` to **`kda_decode.recurrent_kda`** and the `run_recurrent_kda` backend — updating the older decode facade, not the new top-level one |
| #4243 | Added `fused_kda_decode` (reasonable separate op: conv + recurrence + norm) |
| #4313 / #4314 | SM100-family kernel sharing around the same timeframe (facade split adjacent, not the root cause) |
| #4182 (open) | Indexed paging / dispatch heuristics; continues editing the decode path without consolidating facades |
| #4417 (open) | Proposes `flashinfer.kda_kernels.packed_kda_decode_cute.run_packed_kda_decode_cute` (submodule; not yet on main) — a third entrypoint convention |
| #4378 (open) | Cake serving-native packed decode backend (separate packed track from #4417; also not yet on main) |

## Concrete problems

1. **Duplicate canonical name.** Two `@flashinfer_api` wrappers share the name `recurrent_kda` and the same trace template, but are not equivalent. Top-level decode also **bypasses** the decode facade and calls `_run_recurrent_kda` directly.
2. **Trace registry collision.** Both facades register in `_TRACE_REGISTRY` under the same label `'recurrent_kda'` (same `name_prefix`; module path differs). `tests/trace/test_fi_trace_template_consistency.py` imports `flashinfer.kda_decode` (and importing the package can also register the top-level facade). fi_trace e2e tests/examples still exercise only `kda_decode.recurrent_kda` — top-level `fi_api` strings remain untested. Prefill-only kwargs (`seq_order`, `prefill_workspace`, etc.) are also absent from `recurrent_kda_trace`.
3. **Opposite backend policy.** Prefill selects frozen kernels *implicitly* on the top-level API (separate `_run_flash_kda_prefill` path — **not** `backend="cake"`). Decode selects exported FlashKDA only via *explicit* `backend="cake"` on the decode facade (strict; raises on unsupported shapes). Default `cute-dsl` decode is CuTe DSL. Top-level callers cannot request Cake decode today because they never pass `backend=`.
4. **Discoverability.** `flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` does not exist today. Users following top-level docs cannot opt into strict Cake decode without knowing to import the submodule.
5. **Docs / traces lag the facade.** Prefill-only kwargs are not modeled in `recurrent_kda_trace`; the template is still tagged `stage:decode`. Three Sphinx pages describe pieces of one recurrent API; `kda_decode.rst` still autosummarizes `recurrent_kda`.
6. **Risk of further fragmentation.** New specialized kernels (packed QKV, etc.) lack a stated rule for “public op vs internal backend,” so each PR invents a pattern (#4417 CuTe packed submodule `run_*`, #4378 Cake packed).

## Non-goals

- Do **not** merge `fused_kda_decode` into `recurrent_kda` — different serving contract (packed QKV + conv + RMSNorm; different return type).
- Do **not** require open kernel PRs to refactor all of KDA; they should either follow the target facade pattern or stay explicitly internal.
- Do **not** change numerical contracts of existing CuTe / Cake kernels in the unification PR.

## Proposed target (backwards-compatible)

### Canonical API

**One** public recurrent entrypoint:

```python
flashinfer.recurrent_kda(..., backend="auto", ...)
# alias: flashinfer.kda.recurrent_kda
```

Suggested `backend` semantics (defaults preserve today’s top-level behavior):

| `backend` | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `"auto"` (default) | Current top-level policy: eligible ordinary prefill → frozen FlashKDA; otherwise → today's `run_recurrent_kda` default (`backend="cute-dsl"` → CuTe DSL decode/spec) |
| `"cute-dsl"` | Preserve today's decode-facade default: CuTe DSL decode/spec only; **no** frozen-prefill dispatch and **no** Cake decode selection |
| `"cake"` | Strict exported FlashKDA where a contract exists (decode T=1..6 and/or eligible prefill); **raise** on unsupported shapes — no silent fallback. Unification must wire **both** prefill and decode strict paths explicitly (different eligibility predicates / code paths today) |

Keep `seq_order` / `prefill_workspace` on this facade only.

### Compatibility shims

1. **`flashinfer.kda_decode.recurrent_kda`** becomes a thin wrapper that forwards to `flashinfer.kda.recurrent_kda`:
   - **Required:** map omitted `backend` → `"cute-dsl"` (not `"auto"`), to preserve current decode-facade behavior on eligible multi-token inputs. Mapping to `"auto"` would silently switch those callers onto frozen FlashKDA **prefill**.
   - Accept and forward `backend="cake"` unchanged.
   - Optionally accept `seq_order` / `prefill_workspace` by forwarding (additive; no break).
   - Emit `DeprecationWarning` pointing at `flashinfer.recurrent_kda` (soft; keep for ≥1 minor release).
2. **Top-level `flashinfer.recurrent_kda`**: add optional `backend="auto"` with default `"auto"` → **no behavior change** for existing callers. Prefer one internal dispatcher (stop bypassing a second decorated wrapper) so tracing/logging stay consistent.
3. **`flashinfer.fused_kda_decode`**: unchanged.
4. **`flashinfer.kda_kernels.run_*`**: document as **backends only**; prefer removing noun aliases (`recurrent_kda` / `fused_kda_decode`) from `kda_kernels.__all__` in a follow-up, or keep them as deprecated aliases to the public facades.

### Docs / traces

- Single “start here” page for recurrent KDA (`docs/api/kda.rst`); `kda_decode.rst` focuses on `fused_kda_decode` + compatibility note for the old `recurrent_kda` import; `kda_prefill.rst` remains workspace/contract detail.
- Extend `recurrent_kda_trace` for `backend`, `seq_order`, `prefill_workspace` (or mark prefill-only fields optional), retag stage appropriately, and resolve the duplicate registry label so top-level vs decode-shim traces are distinguishable (or intentionally collapsed after the shim).
- Point decode benches/tests (CuTe + Cake) and fi_trace examples at the canonical facade once `backend="cake"` works there.

### Rule for new kernels (immediate guidance)

Until unification lands, new KDA work should do **one** of:

1. **Public op:** noun-form facade (`@flashinfer_api` + trace + top-level/docs export); `run_*` stays in `kda_kernels` as backend; **or**
2. **Internal/experimental:** do **not** add to public `__all__` / top-level; state that clearly in the PR.

Do **not** introduce a third public convention such as “only `kda_kernels.run_foo` / `kda_kernels.<submod>.run_foo` is the product API.”

Packed serving-native decode (different tensor contract from separated Q/K/V) may remain a **separate** public op (e.g. `packed_recurrent_kda_decode`) rather than being forced into `recurrent_kda`, as long as it follows (1).

## Suggested implementation sequence

| Step | Scope | Compatibility |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add `backend=` to `flashinfer.kda.recurrent_kda` with default `"auto"`; wire Cake decode **and** frozen-prefill eligibility through it explicitly; consolidate internal dispatch | Additive |
| 2 | Make `kda_decode.recurrent_kda` forward with omitted→`"cute-dsl"` + deprecate; update docs/trace/registry | Soft deprecation |
| 3 | Retarget decode benchmarks, `test_recurrent_kda.py`, Cake export tests, and fi_trace to the canonical facade | Test-only (touches many call sites) |
| 4 | Tighten `kda_kernels` exports if desired (noun-alias cleanup) | Cleanup |

## Why this is backwards compatible

- Existing `flashinfer.recurrent_kda(...)` calls keep working (`backend` defaults to `"auto"` = today’s routing: implicit frozen prefill when eligible, else CuTe decode).
- Existing `flashinfer.kda_decode.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cake")` keeps working via forwarding shim; omitted `backend` stays `"cute-dsl"` (CuTe decode).
- Existing `fused_kda_decode` / workspace APIs unchanged.
- No forced migration in the first release; warnings guide callers toward one import path.

## Related

- [#4254](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/4254) — CAKE kernel tracker (includes KDA prefill/decode and packed draft #4378)
- #4262, #4279, #4313, #4314 — facade / Cake split / SM100 sharing
- #4243 — fused Kimi K3 decode
- #4182 — CuTe indexed paging / dispatch (open)
- #4417 — CuTe packed decode via `packed_kda_decode_cute.run_packed_kda_decode_cute` (open; needs clear public-vs-internal guidance)
- #4378 — Cake packed serving-native decode (open)

records.title: [Feature]: Define empty KV attention semantics for output and LSE
records.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

Problem: 

DCP computes attention with glocal Q and local KV, then combines the partial output w/ LSE. In the local attention, effective KV for a query row can be empty because:
* The rank holds empty KV: `kv_len == 0`
* local KV exists, but causal or explicit masking excludes every key for that query

For online-softmax merging to treat the empty attention result as a neutral element, it requires LSE = -inf, and, ideally, output = 0.

### Requested outcome

For every query head whose effective attention set is empty:

  LSE MUST be -inf.
  Output SHOULD be zero.

This should apply consistently to attention APIs that return LSE, particularly MLA decode and prefill backends.

Hardware-independent

records.body:
### Before submitting

### Problem

CP combines partial attention w/ LSE. Depending on the backend, the LSE may be represented in natural-log or base-2 form.

Requiring the caller to infer the convention from the selected backend is fragile, and majority backend currently return natural-log, i.e. FlashAttention | FlashMLA etc.

Allow callers to explicitly select the base of returned LSE values. i.e.

  out, lse = trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(

records.title: [Regression][SM100/SM103] TRTLLM NVFP4 MoE emits NaNs in v0.6.16.post4/v0.6.17 (v0.6.16rc4 passes)
records.body:
## Summary

TRTLLM-Gen per-token NVFP4 MoE produces NaNs on Blackwell with FlashInfer `0.6.16.post4` and `0.6.17`, while the same SGLang checkout and workload pass with `0.6.15.post1` and `0.6.16rc4`.

The measured version boundary is **v0.6.16rc4 PASS -> v0.6.16.post4 FAIL**. I did not directly run rc5. Source/tag containment makes **v0.6.16rc5 the inferred first affected release**: [#4252 / `c4053a28`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4252) first appears in rc5 and changes the pinned TRTLLM BMM artifact as well as the advertised FP4 tile set. The same underlying change is [#4180 / `a34a735b`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4180) on the v0.6.17 line.

## Environment

```text
Hardware: 8x NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103, 267.7 GiB, 148 SMs); server uses 4 GPUs (TP4/EP4)
Driver: 590.48.01
Container: lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260812-c7c03ec5
amd64 digest: sha256:e948f2d4adb7d3ca8336d855f667ab26ab27bc7515702336e3c6f7093121bf23
OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, Linux 6.8.0-137-generic, glibc 2.39
Python: 3.12.3
PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
CUDA: 13.0 (nvcc 13.0.88)
NCCL: 2.29.7
cuDNN frontend/backend: 1.27.0 / 9.20.0
FlashInfer 0.6.17 commit: a0a6b019b9b27d49d209f85d028a1ae5a9b347d7
FlashInfer packages: flashinfer-python==0.6.17, flashinfer-cubin==0.6.17,
                     flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.17+cu130
SGLang: 3f3002d4a88d964f2f19ef501755f994cd5d25cc
Model: Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8
Backend / quantization: flashinfer_trtllm / nvfp4_online
```

The full output of `python3 -m flashinfer.collect_env` is available on request. The container image declares stale `FLASHINFER_VERSION=0.6.15.post1`; package metadata, `flashinfer.__version__`, `flashinfer show-config`, and `collect_env` all confirmed the aligned runtime packages shown above.

## Reproduction

The model requires Hugging Face authentication. Install SGLang first, then replace all three FlashInfer packages together. Repeat with `VERSION=0.6.16rc4`, `0.6.16.post4`, and `0.6.17` using a fresh server process and cache directory.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zianglih/sglang.git
cd sglang
git checkout 3f3002d4a88d964f2f19ef501755f994cd5d25cc
python3 -m pip install -e python

VERSION=0.6.17
python3 -m pip uninstall -y \
  flashinfer-python flashinfer-cubin flashinfer-jit-cache
rm -rf /root/.cache/flashinfer
python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps \
  "flashinfer-python==${VERSION}"
python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps \
  --index-url https://flashinfer.ai/whl \
  "flashinfer-cubin==${VERSION}"
python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps \
  --index-url https://flashinfer.ai/whl/cu130 \
  "flashinfer-jit-cache==${VERSION}+cu130"
python3 -m pip check
python3 -m flashinfer show-config

cd test
SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=true \
python3 registered/backends/test_flashinfer_nvfp4_online_moe_backend.py \
  TestFlashinferTrtllmGenMoeBackendNvFp4Online.test_gsm8k -f
```

The registered test launches:

```text
sglang serve \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 \
  --tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 \
  --quantization nvfp4_online \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7
```

with:

```text
FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6=1
FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6_ERR_MODE=MSE
FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6_ERR_USE_FAST_MATH=1
FLASHINFER_NVFP4_4OVER6_E4M3_USE_256=1
SGLANG_FP4_IGNORED_LAYERS=shared_expert,model.layers.40,model.layers.41,model.layers.42,model.layers.43,model.layers.44,model.layers.45,model.layers.46,model.layers.47
SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=False
SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=true
```

The evaluation is 200 GSM8K examples, 128 client threads, completion API, `max_tokens=512`. SGLang automatically logs `--disable-shared-experts-fusion is automatically set`; shared-expert fusion is not active.

## Confirmed package-only bisect

The SGLang SHA, image, model, arguments, environment, hardware, and full workload were held constant:

| Aligned FlashInfer trio | Result | GSM8K score | Latency | Throughput | First observed failure |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `0.6.15.post1` | PASS | `0.960` | `4.2688 s` | `6747.30 tok/s` | none |
| `0.6.16rc4` | PASS | `0.945` | `4.7273 s` | `6153.64 tok/s` | none |
| `0.6.16.post4` | FAIL | `0.000` | `147.96 s` | n/a | pure prefill, `M=1792`; NaNs on all four ranks |
| `0.6.17` | FAIL | `0.000` | n/a | n/a | first concurrent prefill; reduced trace reaches `M=896`; NaNs on all four ranks |

This brackets the measured runtime regression after `0.6.16rc4`. Source/tag inspection points to rc5 as the first line carrying the corresponding artifact/launcher update, but rc5 itself has not yet been executed.

## Independent B200 reproduction

The same registered test independently reproduces the first-`M=896`, all-rank NaN symptom on four NVIDIA B200 GPUs (SM100):

- SGLang: `8531fe0a8ca4e3b6d92b4134be399aaac261c636`
- Driver: `580.126.09`
- PyTorch: `2.13.0+cu130`
- Aligned FlashInfer trio: `0.6.17` / `0.6.17` / `0.6.17+cu130`
- Job: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/31607763933/job/94151038518

The first `M=896` prefill logs `Assertion 'NaN detected! sampler: next_token_logits' failed.` on all four ranks and GSM8K score `0.000`. The later CUDA abort/coredumps are downstream effects and are not separately root-caused here.

## Control matrix on 0.6.17 / B300

| Single change | Scope | Result |
|---|---|---|
| default | 1 example, 1 thread, `max_tokens=512` | PASS |
| default | full 200/128/512 | FAIL, score `0.000` |
| `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph` | full 200/128/512 | FAIL |
| Triton attention + page size 64 | full 200/128/512 | FAIL |
| `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` | reduced concurrent run | FAIL |
| deferred finalize disabled | reduced concurrent run | FAIL |
| `SGLANG_TRTLLM_MOE_PDL_MAX_TOKENS=0` | reduced concurrent run | FAIL |
| `--enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion` | full 200/128/512 | FAIL |
| `SGLANG_FORCE_COARSE_WAR_BARRIER=1` | full 200/128/512 | FAIL |
| `--disable-flashinfer-autotune` | full 200/128/512 | FAIL |
| force exact `[128,19]` through `M=16384`, v0.6.17 cubins | full 200/128/512, prefill graph disabled | PASS: score `0.955`, no non-finite marker or async assertion |
| same `[128,19]`, substitute the exact same-name v0.6.15 FC1+FC2 cubins | 24 requests / 24 threads / `max_tokens=1`, prefill graph disabled | PASS |
| force `[192,1]`, v0.6.17 cubins | startup autotune, `M=4096` | FAIL: non-finite finalized MoE output on all ranks; serving later hits async device assertions |
| force `[192,3]`, v0.6.17 cubins | startup autotune, `M=4096` | FAIL identically |
| device sync at FP4 entry; stream sync after routing, FC1, explicit quantization, or FC2 | reduced eager run, one probe per run | FAIL at every boundary |
| `--disable-overlap-schedule` | full 200/128/512 | PASS, score `0.955` |
| `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | full 200/128/512 | PASS, score `0.940` |

Attention and prefill CUDA graph capture are not required. PDL, routed-vs-FromLogits dispatch, deferred finalize, FlashInfer all-reduce fusion, and SGLang's coarse WAR barrier are insufficient explanations. The forced tile-192 tactics become non-finite during FlashInfer's startup autotune, before serving requests, so SGLang request concurrency/overlap is not required to reproduce the kernel defect. Serialization can still mask the default serving failure.

## Artifact and tactic evidence

| Release line | `TRTLLM_GEN_BMM` | Manifest checksum |
|---|---|---|
| `0.6.15.post1`, `0.6.16rc4` | `b368d003.../batched_gemm-da58956-b4ac80e/` | `d0178cd4...` |
| `0.6.16rc5`, `0.6.16.post4`, `0.6.17` | `5988e15c.../batched_gemm-3d40263-3e19f0a/` | `b19ed6c8...` |

The old manifest has 2,516 configs and the new one has 3,418. All 2,516 old function names remain, but every corresponding cubin SHA changes; 902 configs are added. The same change adds FP4 `tile_N=192` to fallback enumeration.

The first-nonfinite probe narrows the runtime boundary further. On the failing concurrent run, layer 0 receives finite BF16 input, block scales, per-token scales, and router logits, while the finalized BF16 tensor returned from `flashinfer::trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe` is non-finite on all four ranks. The corrupt MoE invocation is the aggregated batch (`M=15605` in that trace), not the nearby scheduler line that reports 896 new tokens.

Capture-aware synchronization probes also ran on every rank: `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` at FP4 FFI entry and `cudaStreamSynchronize()` after routing, FC1, explicit BF16-to-NVFP4 quantization, and FC2. Every variant still returned non-finite output. This rules out a simple missing completion edge between those high-level stages or unfinished work already enqueued before the call; it does not identify corruption inside a compound BMM stage.

The v0.6.17 tile-192 tactics are the Cartesian product below:

| Tactic | FC1 raw config | FC2 raw config | Shape-valid for `I=768` | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `[192,0]` | 521 (`u2`, 2-CTA) | 779 (`u2`, 1-CTA) | no | rejected as an invalid tactic |
| `[192,1]` | 521 (`u2`, 2-CTA) | 787 (non-`u2`, 1-CTA) | yes | non-finite |
| `[192,2]` | 529 (non-`u2`, 2-CTA) | 779 (`u2`, 1-CTA) | no | not runnable for this shape |
| `[192,3]` | 529 (non-`u2`, 2-CTA) | 787 (non-`u2`, 1-CTA) | yes | non-finite |

Both shape-valid tile-192 tactics fail during the real `M=4096` dummy-model forward used by startup autotuning. They use different FC1 cubins but share FC2 raw config 787. In contrast, forced tile-128 `[128,19]` stays finite and passes the full 200-example test with score `0.955` using the v0.6.17 cubins; substituting its exact same-name v0.6.15 FC1+FC2 pair also stays finite in the reduced crash reproducer. The old artifact has no tile-192 cubins to substitute directly.

## Root-cause status

Confirmed:

- This is a FlashInfer-version-dependent regression: package-only replacement flips pass/fail on identical SGLang code.
- Layer 0 enters FlashInfer FP4 MoE with finite inputs/scales/router data and returns non-finite BF16 output.
- The release/source boundary and available runtime tactics both change at the #4252/#4180 artifact update.
- Both shape-valid tile-192 tactics fail before serving starts; tile-128 `[128,19]` passes the full correctness test.

Strong working hypothesis, not yet a final root cause:

- a correctness defect in the newly exposed tile-192 TRTLLM_GEN BMM path;
- FC2 raw config 787 or its tile-192 integration contract is the strongest common-variable localization, because both valid tactics share that FC2 while changing FC1. A finalized-output probe does not yet prove FC2 is the first internal tensor to become non-finite.

Relevant prior context, not the regression's introduction:

- [#3971](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/3971) reports an artifact-only TRTLLM BMM regression where disabling PDL did not help and substituting the old artifact did.
- [#3973](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3973) refreshed cubins to fix a 2-CTA hang before the passing `0.6.15.post1` artifact.
- [#3991](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3991) is an older, still-open 2-CTA filtering proposal. Both tile-192 FC1 choices are 2-CTA, so filtering those kernels plus suppressing the now-empty tile-192 family would avoid this path, but it does not identify the generator-side defect.

## Current upstream status

As of current main [`2d132e68`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/commit/2d132e68c9c70e17efa2a0c81c56508ba2cf421d), the shipped pin remains `5988e15c.../batched_gemm-3d40263-3e19f0a/`, and NVFP4 tile 192 remains advertised. I found no merged post-0.6.17 change targeting this path.

Open [#4281](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4281) (head `e85337e0`) refactors BMM dispatch and repins to `d2659297.../batched_gemm-4868e72-cacd555`. It is not in main and has not been tested with this reproducer. Its exact tile-192 FC1/FC2 function names remain but both cubins are rebuilt, so it is a valuable A/B, not an evidenced fix.

## Expected behavior

TRTLLM NVFP4 MoE outputs should remain finite and the unchanged end-to-end test should retain its `>0.90` GSM8K score across the dependency update.

## Requested help

1. Is tile-192 FC2 raw config 787 known to have an SM100/SM103 per-token-NVFP4 correctness issue?
2. Is the new artifact in #4281 intended to address this path?
3. Can maintainers provide a fixed artifact or a supported way to suppress tile 192 so fallback selects a valid tile-128/256 tactic?

Verified mitigations are pinning the aligned trio to `0.6.15.post1` / tested `0.6.16rc4`, forcing valid tile-128 tactic `[128,19]` (full score `0.955`), or using SGLang `--disable-overlap-schedule`. `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` is diagnostic only.

Linked SGLang integration issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/34629

No exact duplicate was found for this version/shape/NaN regression. #3971/#3973/#3991 are the closest artifact/2-CTA context but report or address an older hang.

records.title: NVCC JIT cache can reuse stale same-version binaries after reinstall
records.body:
# Issue draft: NVCC JIT cache can reuse stale same-version binaries after reinstall

**Title**: NVCC JIT cache can reuse stale same-version binaries after reinstall

**Body**:

## Summary

FlashInfer's nvcc JIT cache (under `~/.cache/flashinfer/`) is validated by Ninja's
file **mtime** scan alone. When a wheel is reinstalled at the *same version* (e.g.
`pip install --force-reinstall flashinfer==0.6.12`), the wheel's source files may
carry **older mtimes** than the previously compiled artifacts. Ninja then treats the
stale `.so`/`.o` as up-to-date and reuses them even though the C++/CUDA source bytes
changed, producing a module linked from a mix of old and new objects.

## Repro (GB10 / sm_121a)

1. Install `flashinfer-python==0.6.12`, run SGLang to build `fused_moe_120.so` (7/10).
2. Reinstall the same wheel (8/12). Ninja decides 5 of 65 objects are stale and
   relinks a *partially stale* `fused_moe_120.so`.
3. `flashinfer.fused_moe.cutlass_fused_moe` (bf16 and fp4) **deadlocks at launch**:
   GPU utilization ~5%, scheduler stuck in epoll/futex, watchdog 300s timeout.
4. `rm -rf ~/.cache/flashinfer/0.6.12` + full rebuild fixes it.

## Evidence

- `cuobjdump` shows `fused_moe_120.so` contains `sm_121a` code, so arch is not the issue.
- `ninja -n` in the module dir reports 5 files that *would* rebuild — i.e. Ninja
  itself knows the artifacts are out of date, yet `build_and_load()`'s fast path
  (mtime-only) reused the stale `.so` before Ninja ever ran.
- Logs: `fused_moe_120.so` mtime unchanged across the failing run; SGLang scheduler
  watchdog 300s timeout with no GPU kernel active.

## Related but different

- #3634 (parallel-compile OOM): different symptom; this issue is correctness (stale
  artifact reuse), not resource exhaustion.
- #3579 (`ninja -t restat`): addresses *spurious full rebuilds*; this issue addresses
  *missing rebuilds* after a same-version reinstall.

## Proposed fix

See the PR: add a content/ABI build fingerprint (`meta.json`) to each nvcc module;
wipe and rebuild when it mismatches, so a same-version reinstall with different bytes
(and older mtimes) can never reuse stale artifacts.

### Bug description

## Problem

`BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper.run()` supports both MLA decode and paged
prefill. However, its current Trace Apply definition describes decode.

As a result, a registered `mla_paged_decode_*` solution can also be invoked for
a paged-prefill call. A decode solution may interpret the total query-token
count as the request batch size, causing incorrect indexing or an illegal
memory access.

## Expected behavior

A decode solution should only be applied when the installed plan is compatible
with the decode definition:

- `causal == False`
- every request has exactly one query token
- the live query count matches the planned query count

Causal, multi-token, mismatched, or unknown calls should conservatively use
native FlashInfer.

I have a tested patch implementing invocation-time template dispatch and this
conservative fallback policy.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
## Reproduction

- SGLang 0.5.17
- DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat
- H100 NVL
- an `mla_paged_decode_h16_ckv512_kpe64_ps1` Trace Apply solution

The solution survives the initial request wave. A later prefix-cached request
enters `prefill_wrapper_paged.run()`, where Trace Apply invokes the decode
solution and its Triton launch fails with an illegal memory access.

With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, the first failure is localized to the staged
decode candidate called from SGLang's paged-prefill path.
```

records.title: [Bug]SM90 push FP8 contract tests read missing source-tree files in isolated /tmp test dir
records.body:
## Summary

  Nightly package tests are failing with `FileNotFoundError` in the new SM90 push FP8 MoE contract tests.
  https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/31661197699/job/94517179743

  The failure appears to be a test/env regression rather than missing kernel sources in the repo. `scripts/
  task_test_nightly_build.sh` intentionally runs tests from an isolated `/tmp/flashinfer-nightly-tests.*` directory after copying only `tests/` and `pytest.ini`, but `tests/moe_ep/test_sm90_push_fp8_gemm_contract.py` reads private kernel sources  by constructing a source-tree path relative to `__file__`.

  ## Failure

  Example:

  ```text
  FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
  '/tmp/flashinfer-nightly-tests.gYsvaN/flashinfer/moe_ep/kernel_src/sm90/push_style_megamoe/src/fp8_gemm/
  fp8_moe_scheduler.cuh'
```
  Also fails for:
```
  /tmp/flashinfer-nightly-tests.gYsvaN/flashinfer/moe_ep/kernel_src/sm90/push_style_megamoe/src/fp8_gemm/fp8_moe_binding.cu
``
  Failing tests include:
``` tests/moe_ep/test_sm90_push_fp8_gemm_contract.py::test_private_fp8_host_headers_resolve_deep_gemm_symbols
  tests/moe_ep/test_sm90_push_fp8_gemm_contract.py::test_private_fp8_runtime_shapes_require_complete_scale_blocks
```
  ## Root Cause Hypothesis

  test_sm90_push_fp8_gemm_contract.py defines:

  _FP8_SOURCE_DIR = (
      Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
      / "flashinfer"
      / "moe_ep"
      / "kernel_src"
      / "sm90"
      / "push_style_megamoe"
      / "src"
      / "fp8_gemm"
  )

  In normal source-tree test runs, this works.   In nightly package tests, scripts/task_test_nightly_build.sh does:

  TEST_RUN_DIR="$(mktemp -d /tmp/flashinfer-nightly-tests.XXXXXX)"
  cp -a "${SOURCE_WORKSPACE}/tests" "${TEST_RUN_DIR}/"
  cp -a "${SOURCE_WORKSPACE}/pytest.ini" "${TEST_RUN_DIR}/"
  (cd "${TEST_RUN_DIR}" && bash "${SOURCE_WORKSPACE}/scripts/task_jit_run_tests_part${TEST_SHARD}.sh")

  So the isolated test dir contains tests/, but not flashinfer/moe_ep/kernel_src/.... Any test that resolves private kernel sources from Path(__file__).parents[2] will fail.

  ## Likely Regressing PR

  Likely introduced by:

  #4069 / f9b13ef1 feat(moe_ep): add SM90 push FP8 mega-MoE backend for Hopper

  That PR added:

  - tests/moe_ep/test_sm90_push_fp8_gemm_contract.py
  - flashinfer/moe_ep/kernel_src/sm90/push_style_megamoe/src/fp8_gemm/*
  - package-data entries for the SM90 push sources

  The nightly isolation behavior itself appears older and intentional.

  ## Suggested Fix (By Codex)

  One of:

  1. Update the contract tests to read packaged resources via
     importlib.resources.files("flashinfer.moe_ep.kernel_src.sm90.push_style_megamoe") instead of assuming a source checkout  exists next to tests/.
  2. Mark source-tree-only contract checks to skip when the source tree is unavailable.
  3. Split source-tree contract tests from installed-package tests, and keep package-resource checks in the nightly package test path.

  tests/moe_ep/test_sm90_push_fp8_packaging.py already has package-resource style checks, so aligning the contract tests with that pattern may be the cleanest fix.

records.title: [Bug][create-release] ARM64 cu129 flashinfer-jit-cache wheel exceeds the 2 GiB GitHub Release asset limit
records.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and did not find a solution or an existing report.

### Bug description

[Nightly Release #347](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/31661197699) produced an oversized ARM64 CUDA 12.9 JIT-cache wheel.

The package-size report measured:
- Current size: 2194.6 MB
- Hard limit: 2048 MB / 2 GiB
- Excess: 146.6 MB
- Change from [baseline](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/31451899040): +300.8 MB (+15.9%)

GitHub Release assets must be smaller than 2 GiB. Therefore this wheel cannot be published through `gh release upload`, which prevents a complete nightly release. Expected behavior is that every release wheel stays below the GitHub Release per-asset limit, or that the package is split/published through a compatible channel.


### Minimal reproduction

1. Check out the nightly head:
```python
   git clone --recursive https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer.git
   cd flashinfer
   git checkout 8f9ad2000db7fa9970b397086296b0c6e6461b02
```

2. Run the JIT-cache build with the nightly ARM64 CUDA 12.9 configuration:
```python
   export CUDA_MAJOR=12
   export CUDA_MINOR=9
   export FLASHINFER_LOCAL_VERSION=cu129
   export FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="7.5 8.0 8.9 9.0a 10.0a 10.3a 12.0f 12.1a"

   docker run --rm \
     -v "$PWD:/workspace" \
     -w /workspace \
     -e CUDA_VERSION=12.9 \
     -e CUDA_MAJOR \
     -e CUDA_MINOR \
     -e FLASHINFER_LOCAL_VERSION \
     -e ARCH=aarch64 \
     -e FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST \
     pytorch/manylinuxaarch64-builder:cuda12.9 \
     bash /workspace/scripts/build_flashinfer_jit_cache_whl.sh
```
3. Measure the generated wheel:
```python
   ls -lh flashinfer-jit-cache/dist/*.whl
```
The resulting cu129/aarch64 wheel is ~2194.6 MB, exceeding the 2 GiB GitHub Release asset limit. Uploading it with `gh release upload` is expected to fail with a size-limit validation error.

### Root-cause evidence

**Primary cause:** 
- [PR #3684](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3684) (tip merge of Nightly 347) extended nightly/release FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST with 12.1a (SM121) only for ARM64 CUDA 12.9 and 13.0. x86_64 lists and CUDA 12.8 are unchanged. The JIT-cache wheel therefore packages an extra full set of SM121 kernels on the two aarch64 variants that regress.

**Secondary / partial contributors:**
- [PR #4318](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4318) / [PR #4069](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4069): plausible for some tracked .so growth (e.g. fused_moe, topk), but cannot explain the ARM64-only multi-hundred-MB jump.
- [PR #4457](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4457): Docker CI tag bump may add shared rebuild noise on the order of the x86 same-CUDA delta (~35–45 MB), not the ARM64-extra bulk.

records.title: CAKE kernel candidates for MiniMax-H3 on B300 and RTX 5090
records.body:
# CAKE kernel candidates for MiniMax-H3 on B300 and RTX 5090

Thank you for inviting customized kernel challenges in the CAKE tracker. We have
a MiniMax-H3 FL2VA runtime based on Sol Engine and SGLang and would like to ask
whether any of the standalone kernels below would be useful CAKE challenges.

These are independent candidates rather than a request for the CAKE team to
implement all of them. We will take care of Sol Engine/SGLang integration,
collectives, quantized checkpoints, calibration, end-to-end validation, and
deployment.

The two targets are:

- NVIDIA B300 / SM103a, with Ulysses SP1/SP2/SP4/SP8;
- NVIDIA RTX 5090 / SM120, quantized execution and SP1 only.

## B300 / SM103a candidates

Common H3 dimensions:

- hidden size: 5,376
- heads: 56
- head dimension: 128
- attention inner dimension: 7,168
- FFN dimension: 14,336
- supported Ulysses degree `P`: 1, 2, 4, or 8
- heads per rank after all-to-all: `56 / P` = 56, 28, 14, or 7
- non-causal packed-varlen attention
- batch size: 1

For B300, we are interested in separate shape specializations for SP1, SP2,
SP4, and SP8.

Nominal `M` values for our main 768p duration buckets are:

| Duration | Global packed rows `T` | SP1 `M` | SP2 `M` | SP4 `M` | SP8 `M` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 s | 33,472 | 33,472 | 16,736 | 8,368 | 4,184 |
| 5 s | 38,592 | 38,592 | 19,296 | 9,648 | 4,824 |
| 6 s | 48,768 | 48,768 | 24,384 | 12,192 | 6,096 |
| 8 s | 58,944 | 58,944 | 29,472 | 14,736 | 7,368 |
| 10 s | 74,240 | 74,240 | 37,120 | 18,560 | 9,280 |
| 15 s | 109,952 | 109,952 | 54,976 | 27,488 | 13,744 |

Prompt length makes `M` slightly dynamic, so kernels need tail handling around
these values. We can provide exact tensor traces and a PyTorch reference for each
operator below.

## 1. Fused BF16 pre-attention kernel — highest priority

Reference operation:

```text
x [M, 5376]
  -> RMSNorm
  -> indexed AdaLN scale/shift
  -> BF16 QKV GEMM [M, 5376] x [5376, 21504]
  -> Q/K RMSNorm over D=128
  -> 3-D RoPE on Q/K
  -> destination-major BF16 QKV
       [P, M, 56/P, 3, 128]
```

The output is only a send buffer; NCCL all-to-all is outside the kernel. The goal
is to avoid writing normalized x, modulated x, ordinary QKV, normalized Q/K, and
RoPE Q/K to HBM. `P` may be implemented as four compile-time specializations
instead of one dynamic kernel if that produces better code.

## 2. Fused low-precision pre-attention kernels

Same operation and output layout as kernel 1, with two independent variants:

```text
A. MXFP8/FP8 QKV GEMM
   -> BF16 Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE
   -> destination-major E4M3 QKV + scales

B. NVFP4 W4A4 QKV GEMM
   -> BF16 Q/K RMSNorm + RoPE
   -> destination-major NVFP4 QKV + block scales
```

An additional NVFP4-GEMM-to-E4M3-output variant is useful if the matching NVFP4
attention kernel is not accurate enough.

We will provide prepacked weights and scale tensors. The kernel does not need to
create or calibrate quantized weights.

## 3. Packed-varlen FlashAttention-4 kernels

Input after our existing Ulysses all-to-all:

```text
Q/K/V: [T, 56/P, 128]
cu_seqlens: int32
causal: false
output: BF16 [T, 56/P, 128]
```

Nominal `T` centers are 33,472, 38,592, 48,768, 58,944, 74,240, and
109,952. Requested standalone variants:

```text
A. BF16 FA4
B. E4M3 FP8 FA4 with explicit descales
C. experimental block-scaled NVFP4 FA4
```

For C, we would be interested in a genuine low-precision Tensor Core implementation
rather than NVFP4 storage followed by BF16 matmuls. Softmax remains FP32. It would
be helpful to report the actual QK and PV MMA dtypes separately; a hybrid
NVFP4-QK / FP8-or-BF16-PV candidate would also be useful.

## 4. Direct-layout attention output projection

Reference operation:

```text
inverse-Ulysses receive layout [P, M, 56/P, 128]
  -> read without a standalone unpack/transpose
  -> O GEMM [M, 7168] x [7168, 5376]
  -> indexed gate * output + residual
  -> BF16 [M, 5376]
```

Requested GEMM variants: BF16, MXFP8/FP8, and NVFP4 W4A4. The collective itself
is outside the kernel.

## 5. Fused RMSNorm + AdaLN + FC1 + SwiGLU

Reference operation:

```text
x [M, 5376]
  -> RMSNorm
  -> indexed AdaLN scale/shift
  -> FC1 [M, 5376] x [5376, 28672]
  -> split gate/up
  -> SiLU(gate) * up
  -> BF16 [M, 14336]
```

Requested GEMM variants: BF16, MXFP8/FP8, and NVFP4 W4A4.

## 6. Persistent full MLP candidate

Reference operation:

```text
RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN
  -> FC1 [M, 5376] x [5376, 28672]
  -> SwiGLU
  -> FC2 [M, 14336] x [14336, 5376]
  -> indexed gate * output + residual
  -> BF16 [M, 5376]
```

Requested variants: BF16, MXFP8/FP8, and NVFP4 W4A4. This is only worth keeping
if it beats kernel 5 plus a tuned standalone FC2 GEMM; CAKE does not need to solve
that scheduling decision outside the kernel benchmark.

## 7. Quantize-and-pack helper kernels

These are useful fallbacks when the GEMM epilogue cannot write the communication
layout directly:

```text
BF16 Q/K/V [M, 56, 128]
  -> destination-major E4M3 + scales [P, M, 56/P, 3, 128]

BF16 Q/K/V [M, 56, 128]
  -> destination-major NVFP4 + block scales [P, M, 56/P, 3, 128]
```

Quantization and relayout should happen in one HBM pass.

## RTX 5090 / SM120 quantized SP1 candidates

If CAKE currently supports SM120, we would also appreciate considering a smaller
set of single-GPU kernels for the quantized H3 FL2VA path on RTX 5090. This target
uses SP1 only, so there is no Ulysses layout or collective in these kernels.

For SP1, `M = T`; the nominal M values are 33,472, 38,592, 48,768, 58,944,
74,240, and 109,952 for 4/5/6/8/10/15 seconds. We are interested in two quantized
GEMM formats:

- W8A8 E4M3 FP8;
- NVIDIA-compatible block-scaled NVFP4 W4A4.

BF16 is used as the numerical reference but does not need a separately tuned 5090
kernel in this request.

### 5090-K1. Quantized fused pre-attention

```text
x [M, 5376]
  -> RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN
  -> FP8 or NVFP4 QKV GEMM [M, 5376] x [5376, 21504]
  -> BF16 Q/K RMSNorm + 3-D RoPE
  -> Q/K/V [M, 56, 128]
```

Useful output variants would be BF16, E4M3 plus scales, and NVFP4 plus block
scales, so that we can connect the best one to the corresponding attention path.

### 5090-K2. Quantized packed-varlen FA4

```text
Q/K/V [T, 56, 128]
cu_seqlens: int32
causal: false
output: BF16 [T, 56, 128]
```

The requested candidates are E4M3 FP8 FA4 and experimental block-scaled NVFP4
FA4. Softmax should remain FP32. For the NVFP4 candidate, it would be helpful to
report the QK and PV MMA dtypes separately and include a hybrid NVFP4-QK /
FP8-or-BF16-PV result if it is more accurate or faster.

### 5090-K3. Quantized attention output projection

```text
attention output [M, 7168]
  -> FP8 or NVFP4 O GEMM [M, 7168] x [7168, 5376]
  -> indexed gate * output + residual
  -> BF16 [M, 5376]
```

### 5090-K4. Quantized FC1 + SwiGLU

```text
x [M, 5376]
  -> RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN
  -> FP8 or NVFP4 FC1 [M, 5376] x [5376, 28672]
  -> SwiGLU
  -> BF16 [M, 14336]
```

### 5090-K5. Quantized persistent full MLP candidate

```text
RMSNorm + indexed AdaLN
  -> FP8 or NVFP4 FC1
  -> SwiGLU
  -> FP8 or NVFP4 FC2 [M, 14336] x [14336, 5376]
  -> indexed gate * output + residual
  -> BF16 [M, 5376]
```

As with the B300 candidates, this full MLP would only be useful if it outperforms
the fused FC1 + SwiGLU kernel followed by a tuned standalone FC2 kernel. We will
provide prepacked quantized weights and scales; weight conversion and calibration
are not part of the kernel request.

For RTX 5090, our preferred starting point would be **5090-K4 NVFP4 FC1 +
SwiGLU**, followed by 5090-K1 and the FP8/NVFP4 attention candidates.

## Integration

For any selected candidate, a FlashInfer-compatible kernel implementation and
basic benchmark results would be very helpful. We will handle the Sol
Engine/SGLang integration and end-to-end evaluation.

records.title: trtllm-gen MLA: numCtasZ (= batch size) still unguarded against the gridDim.z limit (65535), and the failed cuLaunchKernelEx only fprintf's — output silently left unwritten (cf. #3125)
records.body:
## Context

#3125 correctly diagnosed this in April and the maintainer direction there was "just raise an error" — but that was never implemented and the issue was closed. As of flashinfer 0.6.17:

- `include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh:516` still computes `int numCtasZ = params.mBatchSize;` with no cap, and `:388` passes it to `cuLaunchKernelEx` as `gridDim.z`.
- `include/flashinfer/trtllm/common.h:44-50` — `cuErrCheck_` **only `fprintf`s and returns** when `cuLaunchKernelEx` fails. A launch-configuration error is not a sticky context error, so nothing downstream notices either.

CUDA's `gridDim.z` maximum is 65535, so any caller with a pseudo-batch of ≥ 65536 gets a failed launch whose only symptom is one stderr line — and an **unwritten output tensor**.

## Fresh evidence (end-to-end, from the sglang side)

sgl-project/sglang#34947 just hit this in production-shaped usage: sglang's DSA `prefill=trtllm` path reuses the decode kernel and flattens every query token into its own batch entry, so a single unchunked extend > 65535 tokens drives `mBatchSize` past the limit. Measured on SM100 / B200:

- Exact onset: **65535 works, 65536 does not** (one-token bisection).
- A sentinel-filled `out` tensor comes back **100 % untouched**; no Python exception is raised.
- torch-profiler shows **0 of `num_layers` attention kernels** — the model returns garbage and the benchmark reports a **falsely fast** number (the broken 131072-token prefill is "1.80x faster" than the correct 65535-token one because all attention work silently disappears).

## Minimal reproducer (flashinfer only, no sglang, ~30 s)

```python
import sys, torch, flashinfer

B = int(sys.argv[1])                       # pseudo-batch == number of query tokens
NH, TOPK, KVL, ROPE, HD = 16, 2048, 512, 64, 576
PAGE, PAGES, SENT = 64, 8192, -31337.0

kv  = torch.zeros(PAGES, 1, PAGE, HD, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda")
ws  = torch.empty(256 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
q   = torch.zeros(B, 1, NH, HD, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda")
bt  = torch.zeros(B, 1, TOPK, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
sl  = torch.full((B,), TOPK, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
out = torch.full((B, 1, NH, KVL), SENT, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")

flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla(
    query=q, kv_cache=kv, workspace_buffer=ws,
    qk_nope_head_dim=KVL, kv_lora_rank=KVL, qk_rope_head_dim=ROPE,
    block_tables=bt, seq_lens=sl, max_seq_len=TOPK,
    sparse_mla_top_k=TOPK, out=out, bmm1_scale=1.0, backend="trtllm-gen",
)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(f"B={B} out_untouched={(out == SENT).all().item()}")
```

`B=65535` → `out_untouched=False`; `B=65536` → `out_untouched=True`, one `CUDA Error: CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE ... fmhaKernels.cuh 388` line on stderr, no exception.

## Ask

1. Guard the launch: `FLASHINFER_CHECK(numCtasZ <= 65535, ...)` (or split into multiple launches / use a free grid dimension), so the failure is loud instead of silent.
2. Make `cuErrCheck` propagate (throw) rather than `fprintf`-and-return — at minimum at launch sites — so no trtllm-gen launch failure can ever leave the output tensor uninitialized again.

Happy to send a PR for (1) if maintainers agree on the preferred shape.

records.title: [sm120][dsv4] Sparse MLA decode-form calls with non-instantiated topk silently fall through to the prefill orchestrator
records.body:
### Environment

FlashInfer 0.6.17, `_sparse_mla_sm120` JIT kernel family, GB10 (SM 12.1). Caller: vLLM `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` backend, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 with DSpark speculative decoding (2× DGX Spark, TP=2).

### Problem

The SM120 sparse-MLA decode kernels are instantiated for a fixed set of `(num_heads, topk)` pairs with `page_block_size=64` (in 0.6.17: topk ∈ {128, 512, 1024}). A call that is *semantically decode* (num_tokens ≤ 64) but carries a non-member topk does not fail dispatch — it **silently falls through to the varlen prefill orchestrator**, which then asserts:

```
num_tokens > 64 ... Decode ... must go through sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv3_2 or sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4
```

For a 5-token speculative-decode call this message is maximally confusing: the caller *is* trying to reach the decode kernels; the library routed it away because of an unrelated shape parameter, and reports the failure in terms of token count. We lost most of a day to this exact message before finding the dispatch tables (`_decode_dsv4_dispatchable` in `flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120.py`).

We're aware #4380 (merged) consolidates top-k 192/256 support, which removes the *specific* gap that bit us (DSpark non-causal width) on future releases — thank you! This issue is about the failure mode itself, which remains for any shape outside whatever the instantiated set is.

### Suggested fix

When a decode-form call (num_tokens ≤ 64) fails to match a decode instantiation, raise at dispatch time naming the actual mismatch, e.g.:

```
No SM120 sparse-MLA decode kernel for (num_q_heads=64, topk=256, page_block_size=64);
available topk: {128, 192, 256, 512, 1024}. Prefill fallback is invalid for q_len <= 64.
```

A `supported_sparse_mla_sm120_configs()` query API would additionally let callers validate at init instead of first-request time (vLLM now does an init-time check along these lines, see vllm-project/vllm#51538).

records.title: [Feature]: Kimi K3 TP12 kernels for saturated decode on GB300 NVL72
records.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

Hi CAKE team! We are testing TP12 as a Kimi K3 decode configuration on a GB300 NVL72 rack and would like to check whether the uncovered shapes below fit the kind of problems CAKE wants to take on.

The target is the high-throughput decode regime: we increase decode batch size until the GB300 reaches its throughput saturation region. The relevant `B` is therefore empirical and depends on the complete runtime, sequence lengths, and memory footprint; it is not fixed in this request. The relevant operating range is the part of the batch sweep where aggregate decode throughput approaches its plateau.

## GB300 platform topology

![GB300 compute-tray connectivity](https://docs.nvidia.com/enterprise-reference-architectures/nvl72-ai-factory/latest/_images/nvl72-ai-factory-03.png)

Source: [NVIDIA GB300 NVL Compute Tray](https://docs.nvidia.com/enterprise-reference-architectures/nvl72-ai-factory/latest/components.html#nvidia-gb300-nvl-compute-tray)

## Why TP12 exposes different shapes

Relevant Kimi K3 dimensions are:

```text
layers                         93
KDA / Gated-MLA layers         69 / 24
hidden size                    7168
KDA heads                      96
KDA head dimension             128
KDA convolution width          4
TP degree                      12
local KDA heads                8
routed latent width            3584
experts / selected experts     896 / 16
```

Our reading of the current public work is summarized below. Please correct us if any of these shapes are already covered on SM103a.

| Area | Public coverage we found | Shape left by TP12 |
|---|---|---|
| Full fused KDA decode | local heads 12/24/32/48/96 | `H=8, D=128` |
| Packed CAKE KDA (#4378) | `T=1, H=12, D=128`, post-convolution | `H=8`; throughput-scale batches |
| AlphaMoE router (#4339) | up to 512 experts, softmax-style routing | 896 experts with K3 sigmoid routing |
| K3 LatentMoE fused tail | TP8 and TP16 | TP12 |

### Requested outcome

We would be interested in any of the following independent kernel candidates. The full KDA decode shape is the main candidate; the other two can be considered separately.

## Shape A: full KDA decode with eight local heads

This is the main candidate. K3 runs this operation in 69 layers, so it remains important even when the GPU is driven by a large active batch.

The operation boundary we use is:

```text
packed projected input       BF16 [B, 3072]       # 3 * H * D
convolution state            BF16 [slots, 3072, 3]
recurrent state              BF16 [slots, 8, 128, 128]
state index                  INT32 [B]
raw output gate              BF16 [B, 8, 128]

width-4 causal convolution
  -> SiLU
  -> recurrent KDA update
  -> output gate + RMSNorm
  -> BF16 [1, B, 8, 128]
```

The relevant shape is `H=8, D=128, T=1` across the batch sweep where aggregate decode throughput approaches saturation on SM103a.

Indexed states, changing batch size, and CUDA Graph execution are part of the serving path. We are happy to adapt our integration to whichever ABI is most natural for CAKE or FlashInfer.

## Shape B: K3 routing in the throughput-saturated decode regime

This is a smaller, independent candidate. The routing rule differs from the currently published AlphaMoE router:

```text
logits                      FP32 [M, 896]
expert correction bias      FP32 [896]
selected experts            16

scores = sigmoid(logits)
ids = topk(scores + correction_bias, 16)
weights = gather(scores, ids)
weights = weights / reduce_sum(weights)

output weights              FP32 [M, 16]
output ids                  INT32 [M, 16]
```

The bias participates in selection but not in the returned weights. `M` follows the decode batch sweep through the throughput saturation region. This candidate is behind the KDA shape in priority.

## Optional: TP12 LatentMoE tail

There is also a TP12 gap in the fused LatentMoE tail. For our decode setup, we would first measure whether this remains worthwhile around the throughput saturation region.

The mathematical boundary is:

```text
routed_partial              BF16 [M, 3584] per TP rank
shared_partial              BF16 [M, 7168] per TP rank

latent = RMSNorm(AllReduce12(routed_partial))
output = latent @ up_weight.T + AllReduce12(shared_partial)
```

The unusual part of TP12 is that 7168 is not divisible by 12. If communication-aware multi-GPU kernels are currently of interest to CAKE, this could be considered separately.

### Target hardware

SM103 (B300, GB300)

### Inference engine

SGLang

### Affected model or model family

Kimi K3 - https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3/raw/main/config.json

records.title: [Bug] Sampling kernel hangs on sm_86 (A16/GA107) — GPU 100% + worker spin after JIT compile, only under TP=4 + MTP
records.body:
## Summary

On NVIDIA A16 (sm_86 / GA107, ~10 SMs per GPU, PCIe-only, no FP8 tensor cores) with tensor-parallel size 4, the FlashInfer top-k/top-p sampler hangs on the **first sampling call**: the sampling `.so` JIT-compiles successfully, then the GPU stays pinned at 100% and the worker main thread spins at ~85% user-mode CPU indefinitely.

Key points:
- The hang reproduces **only under TP=4 with MTP (multi-token prediction / speculative) sampling**.
- A single-process, small-batch call to `top_k_top_p_sampling_from_logits` does **not** reproduce it.
- **Attention is not the problem** — disabling only the FlashInfer sampler (while keeping the FlashInfer attention backend) makes the exact same model start and run fine.

## Environment

- GPUs: 4× NVIDIA A16 (sm_86, GA107, ~10 SMs each, PCIe-only, no FP8 TC), TP=4
- vLLM 0.27.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130
- `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=fork`
- flashinfer-python 0.6.16.post3, **flashinfer-cubin removed** (to force the JIT path)
- nvcc 13.3, CUDA 13, 44-core CPU, 62 GiB RAM

## Reproduction

1. GPTQ model, TP=4, no `flashinfer-cubin` installed, `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER` unset.
2. Start the engine.

Timeline:

| Time | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 15:16 → 15:17:49 | `sampling.so` JIT compiles successfully |
| 15:17:49 onward | GPU 100% sustained; worker main thread ~85% user-space spin, 15+ minutes |

Runtime evidence captured from the live hang:
- All 4× A16 GPUs at `utilization = 100%` (continuous over 30 s).
- Worker main thread at ~85% user-mode CPU spin.

## What's ruled out (attention is NOT the problem)

With everything else identical, setting only `VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0` — which falls back to the PyTorch-native sampler while **keeping the FlashInfer attention backend** — makes the same GPTQ model start successfully (init ~41 s).

Therefore the hang is isolated to the FlashInfer **sampling** path, not attention.

## Only TP=4 + MTP triggers it

- A single-process, small-batch call to `top_k_top_p_sampling_from_logits` completes fine on the same sm_86 GPU.
- The hang appears only in the real engine path, i.e. TP=4 + MTP speculative sampling.
- The exact kernel that hangs is not yet pinned down. Candidates: `top_p_sampling_from_probs`, `top_k_sampling_from_probs`, or the MTP multi-step sampling path (not `top_k_top_p_sampling_from_logits`, which works standalone).

## Workaround

```
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0
```

Verified with both GPTQ (no cubin) and FP8 models. The native sampler is also functionally more complete here (supports `processed` logprobs), and sampling is <1% of end-to-end runtime.

## Additional context

- Separately, on the same box, with a mismatched `flashinfer-cubin 0.6.13` present, the 4 forked workers deadlock on `sampling.lock` during JIT — only `tmp/sampling.lock` exists under the cache and `build.ninja` is never written. This matches the known fork + `fcntl.flock` pattern (cf. xorbitsai PR#5130, sglang#19583). Reported separately.
- `flashinfer-cubin 0.6.16.post3` cu130 wheels are not available from `flashinfer.ai/whl/cu130`, so the "restore cubin" route is currently not usable; JIT is the only path.

### Bug description On SM120 the CUTLASS FP4 GEMM asks for a workspace larger than the shared scratch buffer `mm_fp4` gives it, for the batch sizes that dominate decoding. Every such call therefore takes the fallback branch in `csrc/fp4_gemm_cutlass_sm120.cu`, which allocates a private workspace, launches the kernel asynchronously against it, and lets the tensor go out of scope immediately. The result is a 34 MiB device allocation and free on the model's hot path, once per NVFP4 linear layer per forward pass, including inside CUDA graph capture. `flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py` hands every `mm_fp4` call a fixed 32 MiB buffer: ```python DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_SIZE = 32 * 1024 * 1024 ... workspace_buffer = _get_cache_buf("mm_fp4_workspace", DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_SIZE, a.device) ``` `csrc/fp4_gemm_cutlass_sm120.cu` then compares that against what the kernel needs: ```cpp int64_t const required_workspace_size = gemmRunner.getWorkspaceSize(m, n, k, batch_count); int64_t const provided_workspace_size = workspace_buffer.numel() * get_element_size(workspace_buffer); ... if (provided_workspace_size < required_workspace_size) { Tensor new_workspace = alloc_tensor({required_workspace_size}, DLDataType{kDLInt, 8, 1}, mat1.device()); runKernel(new_workspace.data_ptr()); } else { runKernel(workspace_buffer.data_ptr()); } ``` ### Measurement Hardware is an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (sm120), driver 595.71.05, CUDA 13.0.2, torch 2.11.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.6.14. The shapes below are the NVFP4 linear layers of a ModelOpt-quantized 27B model (hidden 5120, ffn 17408, so the fused gate/up projection is 5120 → 34816). Driving `mm_fp4(..., backend="cutlass")` once per shape and reading the torch allocator peak across the call, with the output tensor subtracted: ``` mm_fp4 shared workspace = 32 MiB [5120 -> 34816] M= 1 transient= 34.00 MiB <== per-call alloc [5120 -> 34816] M= 8 transient= 34.00 MiB <== per-call alloc [5120 -> 34816] M= 16 transient= 34.00 MiB <== per-call alloc [5120 -> 34816] M= 24 transient= 34.00 MiB <== per-call alloc [5120 -> 34816] M= 48 transient= 34.00 MiB <== per-call alloc [5120 -> 34816] M= 128 transient= 34.88 MiB <== per-call alloc [5120 -> 34816] M= 256 transient= 34.00 MiB <== per-call alloc [5120 -> 34816] M= 384 transient= 0.00 MiB [17408 -> 5120] M= 1 transient= 0.00 MiB ``` The fallback fires for every M from 1 to 256 and stops at 384. That range is exactly the decode regime: a server with `--max-num-seqs 24` runs every decode step at M ≤ 24, so all 64 of this model's fused gate/up projections take the fallback on every step, about 2.2 GiB of allocate-and-free churn per decode iteration. ### Why this is worth fixing beyond the allocator traffic 1. **It puts a device allocation inside CUDA graph capture.** vLLM captures decode graphs at batch sizes 1 through 48 on this model, all of which are inside the affected range. Each capture allocates a 34 MiB workspace from the graph's private memory pool and frees it before the capture ends, so the pool permanently reserves memory for a buffer no longer nominally live, and the replayed kernel writes through a pointer whose block the allocator has since handed to something else within that pool. 2. **`getWorkspaceSize` returns the maximum over every config, not the config being run.** `getWorkspaceSizeImpl` loops over `getConfigs()` and takes `std::max`, so the requirement reported for a shape is the worst tactic's, which makes the 32 MiB buffer inadequate more often than the selected kernel actually requires. 3. **The memo table is not thread-safe.** `getWorkspaceSize` caches into a function-local `static std::unordered_map` with no lock, so two threads calling FP4 GEMMs on different shapes can corrupt it. ### What we observed downstream > **Edit (after filing).** Raising the shared workspace so the fallback is never taken does **not** fix the crash described in this section: the patched build wedged after 15 minutes against 16.5 minutes unpatched. The two are separate problems. The allocation defect above is measured and stands; the crash below is recorded only as the symptom that led us here. Serving this checkpoint under vLLM v0.26.0 and v0.27.1 with CUDA graphs enabled, the engine dies after 16 to 22 minutes of sustained batch load with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`, occasionally `cudaErrorMisalignedAddress`, and sometimes wedges with the GPU pinned at 100% and no Xid. `dmesg` records MMU faults at wild addresses (`faulted @ 0x4_00000000`, `0xf_00001000`, type `FAULT_PDE`). The same model quantized to FP8 on the same box, same image and same attention backend logged 10,282 completions over 35 hours with none of this. `--enforce-eager` reduces the rate roughly tenfold without eliminating it. We swept the GEMM itself for memory-safety problems and found none: every real layer shape, every M from 1 to 8192, all 32 SM120 CUTLASS FP4 tactics, under `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` with `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1`, produced zero invalid accesses, with both a zeroed and a randomly poisoned workspace. That set of runs would not have caught this defect, because disabling the caching allocator turns every free into a synchronizing `cudaFree`, which is what makes the fallback path harmless. ### Minimal reproduction ```python import torch from flashinfer import mm_fp4, nvfp4_quantize, SfLayout from flashinfer.gemm.gemm_base import DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_SIZE K, N = 5120, 34816 # fused gate/up projection of a 27B model print(f"mm_fp4 shared workspace = {DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_SIZE // 2**20} MiB") b = torch.randn(N, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.02 b_gs = (448 * 6) / b.float().abs().nan_to_num().max() b_fp4, b_sf = nvfp4_quantize(b, b_gs, sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_128x4, do_shuffle=False) del b for m in (1, 8, 24, 48, 128, 256, 384, 512): a = torch.randn(m, K, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) a_gs = (448 * 6) / a.float().abs().nan_to_num().max() a_fp4, a_sf = nvfp4_quantize(a, a_gs, sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_128x4, do_shuffle=False) alpha = 1.0 / (a_gs * b_gs) out = torch.empty(m, N, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) mm_fp4(a_fp4, b_fp4.T, a_sf, b_sf.T, alpha, torch.bfloat16, out=out, backend="cutlass") torch.cuda.synchronize() base = torch.cuda.memory_allocated() torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats() mm_fp4(a_fp4, b_fp4.T, a_sf, b_sf.T, alpha, torch.bfloat16, out=out, backend="cutlass") torch.cuda.synchronize() extra = (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() - base) / 2**20 print(f"M={m:>4} transient device alloc = {extra:6.2f} MiB" f"{' <== per-call workspace' if extra > 1 else ''}") ``` On an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell this prints: ``` mm_fp4 shared workspace = 32 MiB M= 1 transient device alloc = 34.00 MiB <== per-call workspace M= 8 transient device alloc = 34.00 MiB <== per-call workspace M= 24 transient device alloc = 34.00 MiB <== per-call workspace M= 48 transient device alloc = 34.00 MiB <== per-call workspace M= 128 transient device alloc = 34.00 MiB <== per-call workspace M= 256 transient device alloc = 34.00 MiB <== per-call workspace M= 384 transient device alloc = 0.00 MiB M= 512 transient device alloc = 0.00 MiB ``` ### Suggested fix Size the shared buffer so the fallback is never taken. The smallest version, which we are running now: ```python MM_FP4_WORKSPACE_SIZE = 256 * 1024 * 1024 # or query getWorkspaceSize ... workspace_buffer = _get_cache_buf("mm_fp4_workspace", MM_FP4_WORKSPACE_SIZE, a.device) ``` `_get_cache_buf` already grows a cached buffer when the request exceeds it, so exposing `getWorkspaceSize` to Python and passing the real requirement would be strictly better than any constant. Failing either, the C++ fallback should keep its private workspace in a per-device cache that outlives the launch rather than a scoped `Tensor`. Happy to test a fix on this hardware; the measurement above is scripted and takes under a minute.

records.body:
We benchmarked `BlockSparseAttentionWrapper(backend="vsa_blackwell")` from
`flashinfer-python==0.6.16.post2` against an FA4-lineage CuTe-DSL block-sparse
forward (`flash_attn.cute` BSA — the kernel family credited in your
`blk128/flash_fwd_sm100.py` header) on one GB200 (SM100). Two findings:
`vsa_blackwell` sustains ~60% of the FA4 kernel's throughput on identical
block masks, and its CPU-side `plan()` costs 1.3–2.7 ms per mask. Please take
a look at optimizing this backend. Results and repros below.

Context: we develop FastVideo/VSA (the workload integrated in #3250). VSA
masks are data-dependent and change every layer × step, so both findings sit
on its critical path.

**Setup (identical for both kernels):** batch 1, 12 heads, head_dim 128, bf16,
non-causal, kv_len = q_len; seq 4096–65536 × sparsity {0–90%}; seeded per-head
boolean block masks with identical selected-token sets for both kernels
(block-size note below); one sparse-aware FLOP formula
(`4·h·d·q_len·selected_blocks·block_tokens`); `triton.testing.do_bench`
(warmup=5, rep=20); `run()` timed alone, `plan()` timed separately. torch
2.12.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, triton 3.7.0, driver 580.159.04. Outputs of both
kernels sit at the bf16 rounding floor vs an fp32 masked-SDPA reference in
every cell, so this is purely a throughput comparison.

**Block-size note.** The two kernels take sparsity masks at different
granularities: `vsa_blackwell` at 128×128 blocks (R=C=128), the FA4-lineage
kernel at 256-token tiles — on SM100 it rejects Q-side block sizes below 256
(verified), so 256 is its finest selection granularity. Masks are generated
once at VSA's 256-token tile granularity and expanded 2×2
(`repeat_interleave`) into the 128×128 block mask fed to `vsa_blackwell`, so
both kernels attend exactly the same tokens in every cell and the shared FLOP
count makes the TFLOP/s directly comparable.

**Finding 1 — flat ~950 TFLOP/s ceiling.** Achieved throughput is 887–961
TFLOP/s in every cell at seq ≥ 8192, essentially independent of sequence
length and sparsity — the FA4-lineage kernel sustains 1130–1620 on the same
masks (1.25–1.71× faster, median 1.60×):

| seq | sparsity | vsa_blackwell run / TFLOP/s | FA4-lineage CuTe BSA / TFLOP/s | time ratio | plan() ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16384 | dense | 1.810 ms / 911 | 1.186 ms / 1390 | 1.53× | 2.11 |
| 32768 | dense | 6.946 ms / 950 | 4.130 ms / 1597 | 1.68× | 2.22 |
| 65536 | dense | 28.030 ms / 941 | 17.695 ms / 1491 | 1.58× | 2.43 |
| 32768 | 90% (89.8) | 0.737 ms / 909 | 0.591 ms / 1133 | 1.25× | 2.21 |
| 49152 | 80% (80.2) | 3.076 ms / 955 | 1.955 ms / 1503 | 1.57× | 2.44 |
| 65536 | 90% (89.8) | 3.022 ms / 887 | 1.886 ms / 1421 | 1.60× | 2.24 |

Sparsity = fraction of 256-token KV tiles not attended per query tile;
keep = round((1−s)·NB) of NB tiles, self tile always kept — e.g. 90% at
seq 32768 is keep 13/128 = 89.8% exact (in parentheses). Per-cell keep
counts and `actual_sparsity` are in the harness JSON.

Below seq 8192 the comparison inverts: `vsa_blackwell` is faster there than
the FA4 wrapper stack.

**Finding 2 — `plan()` CPU cost on mask-per-call workloads.** With a boolean
`block_mask`, `plan()` costs 1.3–2.7 ms of CPU at seq ≥ 8192 (scales with
mask area; ~0.3 ms at 4096). VSA masks change every layer × step, so
mask-per-call deployments pay plan+run per call — at 32768/90% that is
2.2 ms plan + 0.74 ms run.

**Minimal repro** (single GPU, ~30 s, flashinfer-only deps):

```python
import time, torch
from triton.testing import do_bench
from flashinfer.sparse import BlockSparseAttentionWrapper

S, H, D, R = 32768, 12, 128, 128
NB = S // R
torch.manual_seed(42)
q = torch.randn(S, H, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
k, v = torch.randn_like(q), torch.randn_like(q)

g = torch.Generator("cpu").manual_seed(0)
keep = NB // 10  # ~90% sparse; keep = NB for dense
idx = torch.topk(torch.rand(H, NB, NB, generator=g), keep, -1).indices
mask = torch.zeros(H, NB, NB, dtype=torch.bool).scatter_(-1, idx, True).cuda()

w = BlockSparseAttentionWrapper(
    torch.empty(128 << 20, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"),
    backend="vsa_blackwell")

def plan():
    w.plan(None, None, M=S, N=S, R=R, C=R, num_qo_heads=H, num_kv_heads=H,
           head_dim=D, block_mask=mask,
           q_data_type=torch.bfloat16, o_data_type=torch.bfloat16)

plan()  # first call includes JIT
torch.cuda.synchronize()
t0 = time.perf_counter(); plan(); torch.cuda.synchronize()
print(f"plan (steady): {(time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1e3:.2f} ms CPU")
ms = do_bench(lambda: w.run(q, k, v), warmup=5, rep=20)
flops = 4 * H * D * S * keep * R  # QK^T + PV over selected blocks only
print(f"run: {ms:.3f} ms   {flops / ms * 1e-9:.0f} TFLOP/s")
```

Expected on GB200: ~909 TFLOP/s run, ~2.2 ms plan. The FA4-lineage arm on the
identical mask: ~1133 TFLOP/s all-inclusive.

**Full grid harness** (both arms, identical masks/FLOPs, fp32 parity + bf16
floor per cell, plan/run split, markdown table + JSON output):
`bench_vsa_blackwell.py`:
https://gist.github.com/SolitaryThinker/90a1d1447929fc38dc509c1852e76532
The flashinfer arm needs only `flashinfer-python` + torch + triton; the FA4
arm runs when its deps (`fastvideo_kernel`, `quack`, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl`) are
importable and is skipped otherwise. `--quick` runs a 4-cell subset in ~1 min.

We can PR the harness into `flashinfer/benchmarks`, and can test candidate
branches on GB200. cc authors of #3250 / #4355 / #4397.

records.title: quack-kernels==0.6.4 hard-pins nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2, conflicting with downstream projects using CuTe DSL 4.7.0
records.body:
## Summary
quack-kernels==0.6.4 currently declares a hard dependency on nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2:
This creates a dependency conflict for downstream projects that already require a newer CuTe DSL version, for example  nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.0.

  In our CI, installing quack-kernels==0.6.4 into an environment that already has CuTe DSL 4.7.0 causes pip to downgrade CuTe DSL packages to 4.6.2. Later, when the downstream project is reinstalled, pip upgrades some CuTe DSL packages back to 4.7.0,   leaving an inconsistent mixed environment such as:
```
  nvidia-cutlass-dsl              4.7.0
  nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-base    4.7.0
  nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-core    4.7.0
  nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu12    4.7.0
  nvidia-cutlass-dsl-libs-cu13    4.6.2
  quack-kernels                   0.6.4
```
  This environment is not valid for either dependency set and can lead to CuTe DSL compiler failures, e.g. internal DSL errors  during cute-to-nvvm.

 ## Expected Behavior
  quack-kernels should either:

  - support nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.0, if compatible, or
  - declare a less restrictive version range if possible, or
  - provide a newer release compatible with CuTe DSL 4.7.x.

 ## Actual Behavior
  quack-kernels==0.6.4 forces nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2, which makes it difficult to install alongside downstream projects  that require nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.0.

 ## Request
  Could quack-kernels publish a release compatible with nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.7.0, or relax the dependency pin if 4.7.x is supported?

records.title: [Tracking][SM100] CuTe DSL W4A16 MoE implementation and follow-ups
records.body:
## Scope

@humansand

Track implementation and follow-up work for the SM100-family CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE path with BF16 activations (`quant_mode="w4a16"`). #4249 captured the original B200 W4A16 feature request; this issue consolidates the implementation, integration, and related follow-ups.

This tracker is limited to work with explicit W4A16 scope. General CuTe DSL / NVFP4 infrastructure and activation quantization are omitted unless they directly enable or modify this path.

Status last verified: 2026-08-22. Checked items are merged or concluded; unchecked items remain open.

## Tracked contract

- **Hardware:** SM100-family CuTe DSL path; validation in the linked PRs covers B200/SM100 and B300/SM103 where documented.
- **Precision:** BF16 activations and block-scaled NVFP4 weights.
- **Path:** `cute_dsl_fused_moe_nvfp4` / `CuteDslMoEWrapper`, including eager and CUDA graph execution plus fused and deterministic finalize modes.
- **Out of scope:** dense W4A16 GEMM implementation, SM12x/b12x kernels, and the TRT-LLM MoE backend. Related SM100 dense work is linked below for context.

## Shared foundations

- [x] #3976 — `feat(moe): add deterministic CuTe DSL NVFP4 finalize mode` — Adds the reusable deterministic `moe_unpermute` path that #4048 explicitly builds on.
- [x] #4192 — `fix(moe): serialize CuTe DSL autotune replay` — Fixes a shared CuTe DSL MoE runner deadlock hazard during selected-tactic replay; this is not W4A16-specific, but applies to the runner reused by W4A16.

## Core implementation

- [x] #4048 — `feat(moe): support BF16 activations in CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE` — Adds the explicit W4A16 mode, dedicated online NVFP4-to-BF16 weight decode and kernels, runner/API integration, autotuning, fused and deterministic finalize, PDL/CUDA graph support, tests, and B200 evidence.

## Direct follow-ups

- [x] #4394 — `feat(moe): support GeGLU and SiTU in W4A16` — Adds GeGLU-tanh and SiTU, including parameter plumbing and autotune/compiled-kernel cache identities.
- [x] #4558 — `fix(moe): release W4A16 CuTe DSL scratch workspaces` — Removes per-runner scratch retention that can cause multi-GiB serving memory retention/OOMs while preserving eager allocator reuse and CUDA graph ownership. Open draft.
- [x] #4540 — `perf(moe): fold W4A16 SiTU reciprocals` — Replaces trace-time per-element divisions with FP32-rounded reciprocal multiplies and adds controlled B200 evidence. Open.
- [ ] #4366 — `feat(moe): support input-side router weights in CuTe DSL W4A4/W4A16 MoE` — Adds opt-in pre-FC2 router-weight placement for cross-stack numerical alignment. Open.
- [ ] #4678 — `perf(moe): prune score-routing compilation from moe_utils` — Uses source-owned post-topK wrappers to prune unreachable score-routing compilation from the shared SM10x CuTe DSL W4A4/W4A16 `moe_utils` JIT while retaining the existing routing/permutation kernels. Fresh B200 cold first-run wall time drops from 244.03 s to 121.28 s for W4A4 and from 245.19 s to 120.99 s for W4A16; open draft, built on merged #4082.

## SGLang integration

- [ ] [sgl-project/sglang#35120](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35120) — `feat: add FlashInfer CuTe DSL NVFP4 W4A16 mode` — Adds opt-in W4A16 dispatch through `CuteDslMoEWrapper(quant_mode="w4a16")`, supports no-A2A and FlashInfer A2A on SM100/SM103, and adds online-quantized Nemotron-3 plus serialized ModelOpt Qwen3 coverage. Open draft; depends on FlashInfer #4048, #4394, and #4558.

## Related dense W4A16 work

- [x] #4466 — `feat: sm100 cute_dsl w4a16 gemm` — Adds a dedicated SM100/SM103 CuTe DSL dense BF16-by-NVFP4 kernel, architecture-specific weight preparation and dispatch, and autotuning. The implementation adapts the W4A16 MoE TCGen05/dequantization design and tactic family while retaining a separate dense ABI and scheduler. #3597 established the earlier public dense API and cuDNN/SM12x foundation. Merged.

- [ ] #4686 — `perf(gemm): optimize CuTe DSL W4A16 dense GEMM` — Compiles the SM100/SM103 kernel at O3 and expands all 15 structural tactics across both raster directions. Controlled B300/SM103 A/B/A measured `1.029759x` geometric-mean speedup across the #4466 shape matrix (`0.996866x`–`1.060623x`). Open.

## Concluded experiment

- [x] #4424 — `perf(moe): persist SM100 CuTe DSL kernels to disk cache` — Evaluates persistent disk caching for W4A4 and W4A16. Closed without merge; measurements and design tradeoffs are documented in the PR.

## Related issue

- #4249 — Original B200 W4A16 feature request, closed after the core implementation landed in #4048.

records.title: [Bug] CuTe-DSL BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper output mismatch on B300 and GB300 with FP8
records.body:
## Summary

`BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper` produces reproducible output mismatches for the `cute-dsl` backend against `trtllm-native` on B300 and GB300 for DeepSeek-R1 FP8 cases with randomized actual sequence lengths. The mismatch reproduced in both benchmark runs on every completed tested commit from `e9fb62b` through `f9b13ef`.

## Affected cases

| GPU | Page size | Batch size | Mismatched elements |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| B300 | 32 | 64 | 89 / 4,194,304 |
| B300 | 64 | 64 | 68 / 4,194,304 |
| GB300 | 32 | 64 | 67 / 4,194,304 |
| GB300 | 64 | 16 | 1 / 1,048,576 |
| GB300 | 64 | 64 | 58 / 4,194,304 |

## Error signature

```text
Backend cute-dsl output mismatch
```

## Reproduction

```bash
python3 flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper --backends trtllm-native fa2 fa3 cutlass cute-dsl --page_size 32 --batch_size 64 --s_qo 1 --s_kv 8192 --num_qo_heads 128 --num_kv_heads 128 --head_dim_ckv 512 --head_dim_kpe 64 --random_actual_seq_len -vv --refcheck --q_dtype fp8_e4m3 --kv_dtype fp8_e4m3 --generate_repro_command --case_tag DeepSeek-R1
python3 flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper --backends trtllm-native fa2 fa3 cutlass cute-dsl --page_size 64 --batch_size 16 --s_qo 1 --s_kv 8192 --num_qo_heads 128 --num_kv_heads 128 --head_dim_ckv 512 --head_dim_kpe 64 --random_actual_seq_len -vv --refcheck --q_dtype fp8_e4m3 --kv_dtype fp8_e4m3 --generate_repro_command --case_tag DeepSeek-R1
python3 flashinfer_benchmark.py --routine BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper --backends trtllm-native fa2 fa3 cutlass cute-dsl --page_size 64 --batch_size 64 --s_qo 1 --s_kv 8192 --num_qo_heads 128 --num_kv_heads 128 --head_dim_ckv 512 --head_dim_kpe 64 --random_actual_seq_len -vv --refcheck --q_dtype fp8_e4m3 --kv_dtype fp8_e4m3 --generate_repro_command --case_tag DeepSeek-R1
```

## Expected behavior

The `cute-dsl` result should satisfy the benchmark refcheck against `trtllm-native`.

## Actual behavior

The benchmark reports the mismatch signature above consistently on both GPU families.

## CI evidence

- B300: https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/395570745
- GB300: https://nv/flashinfer-ci/-/jobs/395570744
