records.title: [Feature] Add MiniMax-M3 speculative sparse decode for SM100/SM103
records.body:
## Request

Add an SM100/SM103 FlashInfer kernel for MiniMax-M3 speculative sparse decode, using vLLM's [`minimax_m3_sparse_attn_decode`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/866fea2b9900bf49d552c205d2eaac4716fb63ac/vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/ops/sparse_attn.py#L600-L722) as the semantic and performance baseline.

FlashInfer only needs to replace sparse attention after the existing indexer produces `topk_idx`.

## Required contract

- Each speculative query token has an independent sparse selection: `topk_idx[Hkv, total_q, 16]`. Adjacent tokens' rows may differ and must not be shared or unioned.
- Support GQA, causal/ragged lengths, arbitrary and prefix-shared physical pages, and contexts with fewer than 16 valid pages.
- Support BF16 query/output and packed FP8 E4M3 KV with explicit K/V scales and token stride 256.
- Be CUDA-graph safe as page tables, lengths, and sparse indices change in place.
- No KV gather, per-step allocation, host synchronization, or device-to-host metadata copy in steady state.

## Target configuration

- B300 (SM103), TP1 `Hq/Hkv=64/4` and TP4 `16/1`
- Head dim 128, page size 128, sparse top-k 16
- Query lengths 2–8 (primary: 4 = target token + 3 EAGLE3 drafts)
- Contexts 8K, 100K, and 200K; batches 16–256 as memory permits
- Maximum model length 262K, CUDA graphs and prefix caching enabled

## Acceptance

Match the Triton reference for independent per-token sparse rows, ragged/non-aligned lengths, short contexts, permuted/shared block tables, packed FP8 KV, TP1/TP4, and CUDA-graph replay. Benchmark the complete FlashInfer call—including metadata preparation or query quantization—against the complete Triton wrapper.

Reference implementation: [`sparse_attn.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/866fea2b9900bf49d552c205d2eaac4716fb63ac/vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/ops/sparse_attn.py)
records.author: xinli-sw

records.title: [Tracking] Kimi-K3-NVFP4 end-to-end kernel support
records.body:
## Goal

Track end-to-end FlashInfer kernel support for [`nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4) on B200/B300, with vLLM integration that does not require the checkpoint's compatibility patch.

Kimi-K3 is a 93-layer hybrid model with 69 KDA layers, 24 MLA layers, Attention Residuals (AttnRes), Stable LatentMoE, and a multimodal vision tower. The checkpoint uses mixed `NVFP4` experts and `FP8_PB_WO` attention projections.

## Kernel coverage checklist

### Text model

- [ ] **KDA prefill:** chunked KDA with width-4 causal convolution, SiLU, state checkpointing/paging, and CUDA Graph support.
- [x] **KDA decode primitive:** fused convolution + recurrent KDA + gated RMSNorm for production head shapes (#4243).
- [ ] **KDA serving coverage:** indexed/paged states, packed inputs, B200/B300 dispatch and performance across TP shapes (#4182, #3885, #4417, #4483).
- [ ] **MLA prefill/decode:** BF16 I/O, FP8 KV cache, query quantization, packed low-head/variable-Q decode, CUDA Graphs and prefix caching (#4178).
- [ ] **AttnRes:** graph-safe fused block-residual accumulation/normalization for `attn_res_block_size=12`, including the final output AttnRes path.
- [ ] **K3 router:** FP32 `[M, 896]` sigmoid routing with correction bias, top-16 selection, renormalized weights, and reusable graph-safe workspace. The current AlphaMoE router in #4339 supports only `E <= 512` and softmax-style selected weights.
- [ ] **Stable LatentMoE:** fused `7168 -> 3584` routed projection/norm, 896 routed experts + 2 shared experts, and `3584 -> 7168` output/tail with TP/EP communication.
- [ ] **NVFP4 SiTU experts:** group-size-16 NVFP4 experts with SiTU (`beta=4`, `linear_beta=25`) and correct scale handling across TRTLLM-GEN/CUTLASS/CuTe DSL backends (#4180, #4009, #4460).
- [ ] **Mixed projection GEMMs:** serialized 128x128 per-block `FP8_PB_WO` KDA/MLA projections, fused-projection padding/trim, and absorbed-MLA weight preparation without runtime dequantization patches.

### FP8 GEMM inventory

The checkpoint's `hf_quant_config.json` marks 16 KDA/MLA projection target names as `FP8_PB_WO`. Track optimized kernels for the logical GEMMs below; fused names are alternate serving layouts rather than additional model math.

| Area | Manifest modules | Global logical shape(s), `K -> N` | Layers |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| KDA Q/K/V | `q_proj`, `k_proj`, `v_proj` | `7168 -> 12288` each | 69 |
| KDA output gate | `g_proj` | `7168 -> 12288` | 69 |
| KDA decay/beta path | `f_a_proj`, `f_b_proj`, `b_proj` | `7168 -> 128`, `128 -> 12288`, `7168 -> 96` | 69 |
| KDA fused input | `fused_qkvg_proj`, `in_proj_qkvgfab` | `7168 -> 49152`; `7168 -> 49376` before TP padding/trim | 69 |
| MLA query | `q_a_proj`, `q_b_proj` | `7168 -> 1536`, `1536 -> 18432` | 24 |
| MLA latent KV | `kv_a_proj_with_mqa`, `kv_b_proj` | `7168 -> 576`, `512 -> 24576` | 24 |
| MLA fused input | `fused_qkv_a_proj`, `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` | fused Q-A + latent-KV-A/MQA outputs; honor TP-local padding and split points | 24 |
| MLA output gate | `g_proj` | `7168 -> 12288` | 24 |
| Attention output | `o_proj` | `12288 -> 7168` | 93 |

Required FP8 GEMM coverage:

- [ ] BF16 input/output with serialized FP8 E4M3 weights and 128x128 block scales, including UE8M0 requantization/layout preparation.
- [ ] Both prefill (`M = tokens`) and decode (`M = active sequences`) regimes, including small-M latency and throughput-saturated batches.
- [ ] TP1 and TP8 row/column-parallel shapes; TP-local output sizes that are not multiples of 128 must use deterministic zero-padding and trim before fused-output splitting.
- [ ] Fused KDA/MLA projections and their unfused equivalents produce matching results, with arbitrary valid TP-local strides.
- [ ] MLA decode weight absorption consumes the serialized 2D block-scale layout without retaining a dequantized FP32/BF16 weight copy in the steady-state path.
- [ ] Query/input quantization, scale conversion, workspace reuse, and kernel selection are CUDA Graph safe with no per-step allocation or host synchronization.
- [ ] DeepGEMM and non-DeepGEMM/FlashInfer fallback paths have correctness parity and explicit dispatch tests; unsupported shapes must not silently run an unintended slow path.
- [ ] Benchmarks cover every unique `(M, N, K)` family above on B200 and B300 and report complete-call time, including activation quantization and scale/layout preparation.

### Multimodal path

- [ ] Vision patch embedding (`14x14` Conv2D), 27-layer ViT attention/MLP, 2x2 spatial merge + temporal pooling, and PatchMergerV2 projection (`1024 -> 7168`).
- [ ] Variable image/video token counts under CUDA Graph-compatible serving, with parity to the reference vision implementation.

## Reference configuration

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Hardware | B200 / B300 (SM100 / SM103) |
| Initial serving target | TP8, `modelopt_mixed`, `flashinfer_trtllm` MoE |
| Hidden size / layers | 7168 / 93 |
| KDA | 69 layers, 96 heads, head dim 128, conv width 4 |
| MLA | 24 layers, `q_lora_rank=1536`, `kv_lora_rank=512` |
| MoE | 896 routed experts, top-16, 2 shared experts, latent width 3584 |
| Quantization | NVFP4 experts (group size 16), FP8 per-block attention projections, FP8 KV |
| Context | 1,048,576 architectural maximum; 196,608 validated TP8 baseline |

TP12 saturated-decode shape gaps are tracked separately in #4542.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Text-only and multimodal outputs match the reference implementation within dtype-appropriate tolerances.
- [ ] Prefill, decode, CUDA Graph replay, prefix caching, ragged batches, and changing cache/state indices are covered by tests.
- [ ] A public benchmark reports complete-call latency/throughput for each major kernel family on B200 and B300, including metadata preparation and quantization overhead.
- [ ] The published `nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4` checkpoint serves through upstream vLLM with FlashInfer backends and no repository-provided `sitecustomize.py` compatibility patch.

## References

- Model/checkpoint: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4
- Existing KDA tracker/API work: #4254, #4483
- Kimi-K3 TP12 follow-up: #4542
- vLLM mixed FP8 dispatch: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50617
- vLLM fused projections: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52406
- vLLM NVFP4 SiTU scale fix: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52405

records.title: [Bug] SM107 TRT-LLM Gen SiTU MXFP4 tile-64/128/256 tactics return NaNs or incompletely write output
records.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and did not find a solution or an existing report.

### Environment

```text
Python: 3.12.3
  torch.version.cuda: 13.5
  flashinfer.__version__: 0.6.18

  Loaded module:
    fused_moe_trtllm_sm107

  Relevant module flags:
    -DTLLM_RUBIN_FEATURES
    -gencode=arch=compute_100f,code=sm_100f

  SGLang source commit:
    c20aceeb88d65cd4815551d8e2a75f7a1988ed72

  FLASHINFER_NO_DOWNLOAD=1
  No FLASHINFER_CUBINS_REPOSITORY, FLASHINFER_CUBIN_DIR,
  FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST, or artifact override was set.
  `enable_pdl` was not explicitly supplied, so FlashInfer used its default.
  Each tactic was tested in a fresh process with isolated caches.
```

### Bug description

On SM107, FlashInfer’s native TRT-LLM Gen SiTU MXFP4 MoE module advertises larger-tile tactics that produce non-finite values or fail to write the complete output. This initially appeared during concurrent Kimi K3 serving: 30/32 requests emitted token ID 0 (`!`) from the first generated token, while serialized FlashInfer and Marlin controls remained correct.

The failure was reduced to a direct call to `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe`, bypassing SGLang’s scheduler and MoE integration. Inputs, weights, guards, package identity, module identity, and caches were verified unchanged. Each tactic ran twice in a fresh process.

At `M=3392`, the exhaustive matrix produced:
  - Tile 32: 25/25 passed and were bit-identical to the finite reference.
  - Tile 64: 12/12 produced non-finite/all-NaN output.
  - Tile 128: 24/24 produced non-finite output; 22 were deterministic all-NaN, while configurations 6 and 27 were nondeterministic.
  - Tile 256: 2/2 performed incomplete, nondeterministic output writes, leaving portions of the initialized sentinel unchanged.

The 38 failing tile-64/128/256 tactics are the tactics advertised for the 4096-token tuning bucket. That bucket advertises no tile-32 fallback. The boundary is externally visible: the normal path is correct through `M=3584`, while `M=3585` enters the 4096 bucket and becomes non-finite.

Expected behavior: every tactic returned by FlashInfer’s tactic enumeration must completely write finite output and satisfy the same numerical comparison as the passing tile-32 controls. Unsafe tactics should not be advertised or selected.

No CUDA exception, OOM, guard corruption, or input mutation is observed; the API returns successfully with silently corrupt output.

`enable_pdl` was not explicitly supplied, so these runs used FlashInfer’s default. Tile-32 and earlier M8/M128 controls pass with that same default, excluding PDL alone, but a larger-tile `enable_pdl=False` comparison has not yet been run.

### Minimal reproduction

```python
On an SM107 GPU, call FlashInfer’s public trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe API directly with deterministic synthetic inputs using this operator configuration:

  tokens (M):               3392
  hidden size:              3584
  intermediate size:         384
  experts:                   896
  top_k:                      16
  activation dtype:          MXFP8
  weight dtype/layout:       MXFP4, Major-K
  activation function:       SiTU
  tune_max_num_tokens:       4096

Execute the same inputs and weights twice, changing only the selected [tile_N, config] tactic:

  [32, 0]  -> finite, deterministic, fully written output
  [64, 0]  -> call returns successfully, but every output element is NaN

The failing output has shape [3392, 3584], so all 12,156,928 BF16 elements are NaN. Inputs and weights remain unchanged, and output guard regions remain intact. This reproduces through the public FlashInfer API without model weights, an inference server, or distributed execution.
```

records.title: [Feature] Fuse LSE correction into DCP A2A
records.body:
## Motivation

SGLang uses FlashInfer's MNNVL DCP A2A operator to exchange partial attention outputs and LSE values across context-parallel ranks. The current API returns the peer-stacked tensors, after which SGLang launches a separate kernel to apply the LSE correction:

```python
recv_o, recv_stats = decode_cp_a2a_alltoall(
    partial_o,
    softmax_stats,
    workspace,
    cp_rank,
    cp_size,
)
output = lse_reduce(recv_o, recv_stats[..., 0])
```

Could FlashInfer provide a fused A2A + LSE-reduction operation that directly returns the corrected attention output?

## Proposed Interface

```python
output = decode_cp_a2a_lse_reduce(
    partial_o,            # [..., cp_size, head_dim], fp16/bf16
    partial_lse,          # [..., cp_size], fp32
    workspace,
    cp_rank,
    cp_size,
    is_lse_base_on_e=False,
    enable_pdl=None,
)
```

## Expected behavior

- Perform the same MNNVL exchange as `decode_cp_a2a_alltoall`.
- Apply the exact LSE-weighted reduction over contributions from all CP ranks.
- Return `output` with shape `[..., head_dim]`, with the CP dimension removed.
- Support both base-2 LSE, used by FlashInfer MLA, and natural-log LSE.
- Remain compatible with CUDA graph capture and replay.
- Ideally avoid materializing peer-stacked receive tensors and launching a separate correction kernel.

For inputs shaped as follows:

```text
partial_o:   [batch, local_heads, cp_size, head_dim]
partial_lse: [batch, local_heads, cp_size]
```

the result should have shape:

```text
output:      [batch, local_heads, head_dim]
```

## Reference validation

The fused result should match the current A2A followed by an explicit LSE reduction:

```python
softmax_stats = torch.zeros(
    *partial_lse.shape, 2, dtype=torch.float32, device=partial_lse.device
)
softmax_stats[..., 0] = partial_lse

recv_o, recv_stats = decode_cp_a2a_alltoall(
    partial_o,
    softmax_stats,
    workspace,
    cp_rank,
    cp_size,
)

recv_lse = recv_stats[..., 0]
lse_max = recv_lse.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
weights = (
    torch.exp(recv_lse - lse_max)
    if is_lse_base_on_e
    else torch.exp2(recv_lse - lse_max)
)
expected = (
    (recv_o.float() * weights.unsqueeze(-1)).sum(dim=-2)
    / weights.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
).to(partial_o.dtype)

actual = decode_cp_a2a_lse_reduce(
    partial_o,
    partial_lse,
    workspace,
    cp_rank,
    cp_size,
    is_lse_base_on_e=is_lse_base_on_e,
)

torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=1e-2, atol=1e-3)
```

records.title: [Bug] BF16 GDN decode rejects naturally aligned A_log and dt_bias views
records.body:
# BF16 GDN decode rejects naturally aligned `A_log` and `dt_bias` views

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA B30Z (SM103)
- PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130
- CUDA: 13.0
- FlashInfer: 0.6.14; reproduced against current `main`
- SGLang: 0.5.17.dev36

## Problem

The BF16-state GDN decode wrappers pass `assumed_align=32` for `A_log` and
`dt_bias`. Contiguous tensor views with a nonzero storage offset are valid
inputs and retain their scalar dtype alignment, but need not begin at a
32-byte boundary. CuTe rejects such inputs before launching the kernel.

For example, a float32 `A_log` view at storage offset one has `data_ptr() % 32
== 4`, and a bfloat16 `dt_bias` view has `data_ptr() % 32 == 2`:

```python
A_log = torch.randn(HV + 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)[1:]
dt_bias = torch.randn(HV + 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)[1:]

# Both are contiguous, but gated_delta_rule_decode_pretranspose(...) raises:
# RuntimeError: Tensor data pointer is not aligned to 32 bytes.
```

This occurs in SGLang when model parameter slices are passed to FlashInfer's
native BF16 GDN decode path, including during CUDA graph capture.

## Expected behavior

The kernel should accept these naturally aligned views. `A_log` and `dt_bias`
are loaded elementwise, so their descriptors only require their scalar dtype
alignment.

## Proposed fix

Use 4-byte alignment for float32 `A_log` and `dt_bias.element_size()` for
`dt_bias` at the three BF16 GDN compile sites. A regression test compares
misaligned views against allocation-aligned clones and requires bit-identical
output and state.

On B30Z, the patched native FlashInfer kernel passes for both views and clones;
their results are bit-identical. This does not switch backend, disable CUDA
graphs, copy the parameters, or change precision.

records.title: [Bug] trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe: fallback tactic returns non-finite outputs with per_token_scale at large num_tokens (SM103)
records.body:
## Summary

`trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` with `per_token_scale` (per-token NVFP4 activation scaling) produces **non-finite outputs** when it runs on the fallback tactic (tactic `-1`, i.e. no autotune cache entry for the bucket) and `num_tokens` is large. With identical weights, routing, and inputs:

| config | result |
|---|---|
| fallback tactic, `per_token_scale`, num_tokens=8064 | **~0.7–13% of output elements NaN/Inf** (count varies run to run) |
| fallback tactic, static activation scale (`per_token_scale=None`), same everything | clean, cosine 0.973 vs bf16 reference |
| autotuned tactic, `per_token_scale`, same everything | clean, cosine 0.973 vs bf16 reference |

An untuned tactic may be slow, but should never be wrong. In serving this shows up as `NaN detected in logits` on real prefill batches whenever the extend-shaped warmup pass didn't run.

Additional observations:

- `num_tokens <= 5120` is clean; `>= 6144` is broken (threshold between 5120 and 6144 at these shapes).
- `enable_pdl` True/False does not matter.
- The non-finite count varies run to run at fixed seed, and grows to **~60–80%** of the output if free GPU memory is pre-filled with NaN bytes before the call — consistent with the fallback config reading memory it shouldn't (uninitialized workspace or an out-of-bounds/garbage read of the per-token scales).
- Quantizer backend for the activations (`cuda` vs `cute-dsl`) does not matter; routing skew does not matter.

Possibly related: #4190 reports the *perf* side of the same regime (default tactic at >=8k tokens on this op, autotuned tactic fine); this issue is the correctness side with `per_token_scale`.

## Environment

- flashinfer 0.6.16.post4 (also reproduced on 0.6.17): `flashinfer-python` + `flashinfer-cubin` wheels
- 1× NVIDIA GB300 (SM103), driver 580.159.03
- torch 2.11.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, aarch64

## Repro

Single GPU, only torch + flashinfer. Shapes are a production MoE per-TP-rank slice: hidden=6144, intermediate=768, 256 experts, top_k=6, gated silu; num_tokens=8064 is a real chunked-prefill batch.

```
$ python repro_trtllm_fp4_routed_moe_nan.py
UNTUNED per-token scales: non-finite = 4865152/49545216, cosine vs bf16 ref = nan
UNTUNED static act scale: non-finite = 0/49545216, cosine vs bf16 ref = 0.9730
TUNED   per-token scales: non-finite = 0/49545216, cosine vs bf16 ref = 0.9731
```

<details>
<summary>repro_trtllm_fp4_routed_moe_nan.py</summary>

```python
"""trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe: the untuned fallback tactic produces
non-finite outputs when per_token_scale is used and num_tokens is large (>= ~6k).

Single GPU (tested on GB300 / SM103). Depends only on torch + flashinfer.

Shapes are the per-TP-rank MoE of a production model (hidden=6144,
intermediate=768, 256 experts, top_k=6, gated silu). num_tokens=8064 is a real
chunked-prefill batch size.

Expected output (buggy):
    UNTUNED per-token scales      : non-finite = <large>/49545216   <-- BUG
    UNTUNED static act scale      : non-finite = 0/49545216, cos ~0.97
    TUNED   per-token scales      : non-finite = 0/49545216, cos ~0.97

i.e. with identical weights/routing/inputs, only the (fallback tactic,
per_token_scale) combination is broken; the autotuned tactic and the
static-activation-scale fallback are both fine. The non-finite count varies
run to run. enable_pdl True/False does not matter. num_tokens <= 5120 is
clean; >= 6144 is not.
"""

import torch

from flashinfer import SfLayout, nvfp4_block_scale_interleave, nvfp4_quantize
from flashinfer.autotuner import autotune
from flashinfer.fused_moe import trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe
from flashinfer.fused_moe.core import (
    _maybe_get_cached_w3_w1_permute_indices,
    get_w2_permute_indices_with_cache,
)

torch.manual_seed(0)
DEV = "cuda"
E, D, F, TOPK = 256, 6144, 768, 6
T = 8064
FP4_MAX, E4M3_MAX = 6.0, 448.0
EPILOGUE_TILE_M = 128


def quant_weight(w: torch.Tensor):
    """(rows, D) bf16 -> (packed fp4 uint8, linear e4m3 block sf, global dequant scale)."""
    gs = (FP4_MAX * E4M3_MAX) / w.abs().amax().float()
    data, sf = nvfp4_quantize(w, gs.reshape(1), sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_linear, do_shuffle=False)
    return data, sf, 1.0 / gs


def main() -> None:
    # Random experts: rows [0:F] = up (w3), rows [F:2F] = gate (w1).
    w13 = torch.randn(E, 2 * F, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEV) * 0.02
    w2 = torch.randn(E, D, F, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEV) * 0.02

    w13_q = torch.empty(E, 2 * F, D // 2, dtype=torch.uint8, device=DEV)
    w13_sf = torch.empty(E, 2 * F, D // 16, dtype=torch.uint8, device=DEV)
    w2_q = torch.empty(E, D, F // 2, dtype=torch.uint8, device=DEV)
    w2_sf = torch.empty(E, D, F // 16, dtype=torch.uint8, device=DEV)
    g1_alphas = torch.empty(E, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEV)
    g2_alphas = torch.empty(E, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEV)
    for e in range(E):
        w13_q[e], sf, g1_alphas[e] = quant_weight(w13[e])
        w13_sf[e] = sf.view(torch.uint8).reshape(2 * F, D // 16)
        w2_q[e], sf, g2_alphas[e] = quant_weight(w2[e])
        w2_sf[e] = sf.view(torch.uint8).reshape(D, F // 16)

    # Shuffle weights + interleave block scales for the trtllm-gen kernel.
    cache: dict = {}
    w13_shuf = torch.empty_like(w13_q)
    w2_shuf = torch.empty_like(w2_q)
    w13_sf_shuf = torch.empty(E, 2 * F * (D // 16), dtype=torch.uint8, device=DEV)
    w2_sf_shuf = torch.empty(E, D * (F // 16), dtype=torch.uint8, device=DEV)
    for e in range(E):
        pi = _maybe_get_cached_w3_w1_permute_indices(
            cache, w13_q[e], EPILOGUE_TILE_M, is_gated_act_gemm=True
        )
        w13_shuf[e] = w13_q[e][pi.to(DEV)]
        pi = _maybe_get_cached_w3_w1_permute_indices(
            cache, w13_sf[e], EPILOGUE_TILE_M, num_elts_per_sf=16, is_gated_act_gemm=True
        )
        w13_sf_shuf[e] = nvfp4_block_scale_interleave(w13_sf[e][pi.to(DEV)].contiguous()).flatten()
        pi = get_w2_permute_indices_with_cache(cache, w2_q[e], EPILOGUE_TILE_M)
        w2_shuf[e] = w2_q[e][pi.to(DEV)]
        pi = get_w2_permute_indices_with_cache(
            cache, w2_sf[e], EPILOGUE_TILE_M, num_elts_per_sf=16
        )
        w2_sf_shuf[e] = nvfp4_block_scale_interleave(w2_sf[e][pi.to(DEV)].contiguous()).flatten()
    w13_sf_shuf = w13_sf_shuf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).reshape(E, 2 * F, D // 16)
    w2_sf_shuf = w2_sf_shuf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).reshape(E, D, F // 16)

    x = torch.randn(T, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEV)

    # Routing: random experts, softmax weights, packed as (expert_id << 16) | bf16 weight bits.
    topk_ids = torch.stack([torch.randperm(E, device=DEV)[:TOPK] for _ in range(T)]).int()
    topk_weights = torch.softmax(torch.randn(T, TOPK, device=DEV), dim=-1)
    packed = (topk_ids.to(torch.int32) << 16) | (
        topk_weights.to(torch.bfloat16).view(torch.int16).to(torch.int32) & 0xFFFF
    )

    # bf16 reference from the unquantized tensors: sum_k w_k * (silu(gate) * up) @ w2.
    ref = torch.zeros(T, D, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEV)
    for k in range(TOPK):
        we = topk_ids[:, k].long()
        up = torch.einsum("td,tfd->tf", x, w13[we, :F])
        gate = torch.einsum("td,tfd->tf", x, w13[we, F:])
        h = torch.nn.functional.silu(gate) * up
        ref += topk_weights[:, k, None] * torch.einsum("tf,tdf->td", h, w2[we]).float()

    def quant_act(per_token: bool):
        if per_token:
            gs_inv = torch.full(
                (1,), 1.0 / (E4M3_MAX * FP4_MAX), dtype=torch.float32, device=DEV
            )
            x_q, x_sf, pts = nvfp4_quantize(
                x, gs_inv, sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_linear, per_token_activation=True
            )
            # per-token path: activation global scale is folded into per_token_scale
            o1c, o1g, o2 = g1_alphas, g1_alphas, g2_alphas
        else:
            act_gs = ((E4M3_MAX * FP4_MAX) / x.abs().amax().float()).reshape(1)
            x_q, x_sf = nvfp4_quantize(x, act_gs, sfLayout=SfLayout.layout_linear)
            pts = None
            o1g = (g1_alphas / act_gs).contiguous()
            o1c, o2 = o1g.clone(), g2_alphas
        return x_q.reshape(T, D // 2), x_sf.view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).reshape(T, D // 16), pts, o1c, o1g, o2

    def run(per_token: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
        x_q, x_sf, pts, o1c, o1g, o2 = quant_act(per_token)
        return trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe(
            topk_ids=packed,
            routing_bias=None,
            hidden_states=x_q,
            hidden_states_scale=x_sf,
            gemm1_weights=w13_shuf,
            gemm1_weights_scale=w13_sf_shuf,
            gemm1_bias=None,
            gemm1_alpha=None,
            gemm1_beta=None,
            gemm1_clamp_limit=None,
            gemm2_weights=w2_shuf,
            gemm2_weights_scale=w2_sf_shuf,
            gemm2_bias=None,
            output1_scale_scalar=o1c,
            output1_scale_gate_scalar=o1g,
            output2_scale_scalar=o2,
            per_token_scale=pts,
            num_experts=E,
            top_k=TOPK,
            n_group=0,
            topk_group=0,
            intermediate_size=F,
            local_expert_offset=0,
            local_num_experts=E,
            routed_scaling_factor=None,
            routing_method_type=1,
            do_finalize=True,
            tune_max_num_tokens=8192,
        )[0]

    def report(name: str, out: torch.Tensor) -> None:
        bad = (~torch.isfinite(out)).sum().item()
        cos = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(
            out.float().flatten(), ref.flatten(), dim=0
        ).item()
        print(f"{name}: non-finite = {bad}/{out.numel()}, cosine vs bf16 ref = {cos:.4f}")

    report("UNTUNED per-token scales", run(per_token=True))  # <-- BUG: non-finite
    report("UNTUNED static act scale", run(per_token=False))  # control: clean
    with torch.inference_mode(), autotune(True):
        run(per_token=True)
    report("TUNED   per-token scales", run(per_token=True))  # clean


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

</details>

-Robot

### Bug description

During normal serving of DeepSeek-V4-Flash (DSpark) on SM120/GB10 with
speculative/decode traffic, the engine logs this warning for every decode step
that uses an `extra_dense_topk` budget the boot-time autotuning pass did not
physically run:

```
No tuned config covers sparse_mla_sm120_decode_dsv4 input_shapes=((58, 32, 512), (58, 128), (58, 32, 18, 512), (58, 32, 18), (58, 32, 512), (58, 32), (58,), (32,), (58, 1024), (58,)); falling back to runner=SparseMlaDecodeV3Runner tactic=-1.
```

The request still completes (the fallback is correct), but this lands on the
heuristic partition for the whole CUDA-graph-replay shape. On an idle GPU we
measured the difference between the heuristic and the best tuned `cpb` for the
steady-state replay shape to be large (see below).

We inspected `_decode_dsv4_tuning_config()` (also `_decode_dsv3_2_tuning_config()`)
in `flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120.py` on current `main` and it looks like the
**num_tokens axis is the only `DynamicTensorSpec`**, while the dense/extra-topk
axis appears only as part of the *shape* — i.e. matched exactly, never bucketed.
If that reading is correct, then any dense value the tuning pass doesn't happen
to run is a guaranteed cache miss → heuristic, by construction. File is attached
for a maintainer to confirm in one read — this is not an expertise claim, just a
pointer to what we believe we observed; happy to be corrected.

### Minimal reproduction

The following needs only an importable flashinfer (no GPU, no specific model) to
show the bucket structure. On main today:

```python
from flashinfer.mla._sparse_mla_sm120 import (
    _decode_dsv4_tuning_config, _decode_dsv4_num_token_buckets,
)
cfg = _decode_dsv4_tuning_config()
print("dynamic_tensor_specs:", [(s.input_idx, s.dim_idx) for s in cfg.dynamic_tensor_specs])
print("token buckets:", _decode_dsv4_num_token_buckets())
# => Only token-axis specs; NO DynamicTensorSpec covers the dense/extra dimension
#    of the final tensors, so cache lookup matches that axis exactly.
#    A dense value absent from the boot tuning pass therefore cannot be a hit.
```

Kernel A/B (idle GPU, only where an SM120 box is handy) — this exact shape is a
steady-state CUDA-graph replay in DeepSeek-V4-Flash Decode, not an outlier:

```text
shape T=12 topk=128 dense=8192: heuristic 656.97 µs  vs  best-tuned 360.50 µs  (+82.2%)
```

A copy of the microbench tool that produced this is available on request if useful
(no repo dependency).

### Error messages / logs

The warning above emits on every uncovered decode step. Boot-time count: all
observed production `(T, topk, dense)` shapes were uncovered. The served-shape
census and warning frequency were mined from the engine log.

### Additional context

- Same code exists in the current upstream `main` (`flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120.py`,
  `_decode_dsv4_tuning_config`) and in the deployed DSPark fork; believed
  inherited.
- As an interim workaround the deployment merges 24 autotuner-generated configs
  for dense ∈ {256,1024,2048,8192} into the cache at boot
  (https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark-2x-DGX-Spark/issues/83) — that removes the
  warning and recovers the perf, but it's not a library fix.
- #2958 (custom tuning buckets) and autotuner v2 discussions (#3861/#3920) appear
  related in spirit; this report is specifically the missing dense-axis bucket in
  the sparse-MLA decode config.

Thanks for reading — happy to provide the raw logs or rerun anything on request,
but no deep flashinfer background on our side, so a maintainer confirming or
correcting the interpretation would be most valuable.

records.title: [Bug] NVFP4 grouped-BMM hang on SM103 (0.6.8.post1): BMM warps parked in tcgen05 guardrail trap "unallocated_columns_being_dealloced", PDL finalize kernel spins forever
records.body:
## Summary

On a pipeline-parallel vLLM serving deployment running an NVFP4 MoE model, the rank-0 GPU wedged at 100% utilization with the host thread blocked in `cudaDeviceSynchronize`. Attaching cuda-gdb shows the trtllm-gen NVFP4 grouped BMM (`bmm_Bfloat16_E2m1E2m1_..._sm100f`) with warps parked inside the ptxas-injected guardrail handler `$__internal_2_$__cuda_sm10x_tcgen05_guardrail_trap_unallocated_columns_being_dealloced`, while the co-scheduled MoE finalize kernel (`finalizeKernelVecLoad`) spins at a PDL `griddepcontrol.wait` (`ACQBULK`) that can never be satisfied. This is the same root-cause family as #4032 and #3971; this report adds a fully captured 0.6.8.post1 datapoint with debugger evidence.

## Environment

- GPU: SM103 (B300-class, 148 SMs; nvidia-smi reports the marketing name "NVIDIA H800", `compute_cap` = 10.3)
- Driver 580.126.20, CUDA 13.0
- torch 2.11.0+cu130
- vLLM 0.21.0-based serving stack (custom build, vllm commit gad7125a43), PP=4
- flashinfer-python 0.6.8.post1 / flashinfer-cubin 0.6.8.post1 / flashinfer-jit-cache 0.6.8.post1+cu130
- Model: GLM-class NVFP4 MoE (per-token FP4 block-scale MoE via trtllm-gen BMM + fused finalize)

## Symptoms

- GPU 0 util pinned at 100%; rank-0 worker's main thread spinning in libcuda's `cuCtxSynchronize_v2` poll loop (100% CPU); pipeline peers idle.
- No fresh Xid for this incident. (Historical note: earlier runs of the same stack produced Xid 31 MMU faults, `FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ`, on three different GPUs.)

## cuda-gdb evidence

Two kernels resident on device 0:

| grid | kernel | state |
|---|---|---|
| 5220464 | `bmm_Bfloat16_E2m1E2m1_Fp32_bA16_bB16_t128x128x256u2_s6_et128x128_m256x128x64_c2x1x1_16dp256b_rM_TN_transOut_schPd2x1x2x3_biasFp32M_bN_rgTma_clmp_dynB_sm100f`, grid (48,766,1) x (384,1,1), cluster dim (2,1,1) | warps executing `$__internal_2_$__cuda_sm10x_tcgen05_guardrail_trap_unallocated_columns_being_dealloced` (observed in block (4,0,0), cluster (2,0,0)) |
| 5220465 | `moe::dev::finalize::finalizeKernelVecLoad<KernelParams<bf16,bf16,4,true>>`, grid (8192,1,1) x (256,1,1) | every warp on all 148 SMs parked at the same PC (+0x1050), zero divergence |

Offline disassembly of the sm_103a cubin of `finalizeKernelVecLoad` (from `flashinfer_jit_cache`'s `fused_moe_trtllm_sm100.so`) shows the parked PC (+0x1050) is `ACQBULK` — `griddepcontrol.wait` (programmatic dependent launch): the finalize grid waits for the preceding BMM grid to release/complete. With the BMM's warps trapped in the TMEM guardrail handler, the BMM grid never completes, so `ACQBULK` is never satisfied, all SMs spin, and `cudaDeviceSynchronize` never returns.

Host backtrace of the blocked thread: `cudaDeviceSynchronize` → `cuCtxSynchronize_v2` (libcuda poll loop at 100% CPU).

## Relation to existing reports

- #4032: same trap (`unallocated_columns_being_dealloced`); reporter saw the hang on 0.6.8.post1, fixed by 0.6.13, re-introduced in 0.6.14. Our capture independently confirms the 0.6.8.post1 manifestation and completes the causal chain (guardrail trap → PDL finalize spin → host sync hang).
- #3971: same BMM artifact family on SM103/GB300 with the mbarrier phase-wait manifestation, bisected to the 0.6.14 artifact regeneration (#3708, `batched_gemm-dd6d23e-721ae60`).

## Reproduction conditions (new datapoint)

In our deployment the hang has only ever occurred **when an LMCache server process co-runs on the same 4 GPUs** (LMCache L1 tier 1600 GB host RAM, `--max-gpu-workers 4`, its own CUDA contexts + KV-transfer kernels/DMA on GPUs 0–3, sharing SMs with the vLLM workers). Sustained runs of the same model/serving stack **without** the LMCache server have never reproduced it. This is consistent with #4032's "doesn't reproduce offline" and #3971's "minutes to ~45 min of sustained serving" — the defect seems to need production-like timing/shape perturbation to fire. Plausible coupling channels: (a) higher prefix-cache hit rates change per-batch per-expert token distributions (empty/tiny expert groups exercising the dynB tail-CTA path), (b) cross-process SM timesharing perturbs the timing of the tcgen05 alloc spin / cluster scheduling window, exposing the race.

## Workaround datapoint: device sync before the op fully avoids the hang

Inserting `torch.cuda.synchronize()` immediately before this fused NVFP4 MoE op (before the grouped-BMM launch) has, so far, completely eliminated the hang in the same LMCache co-run deployment that previously reproduced it. Our reading of why this works:

- The sync drains **all** in-context streams (LMCache KV-transfer streams, comm streams, and any still-resident finalize grids from the previous MoE layer — each finalize grid is 8192 blocks flooding all 148 SMs), so the BMM launches onto a quiet GPU and its (2,1,1) clusters co-schedule normally instead of trickling onto SMs one pair at a time.
- That points at the defective path being a **cluster-scheduling-perturbation / tail-CTA race** in the cubin's TMEM alloc/dealloc accounting, rather than something the PDL pairing itself causes — consistent with #3971's observation that forcing `device_support_pdl=False` does **not** remove the hang: the sync helps because it removes co-resident kernels, not because it breaks PDL.
- It also guarantees visibility of any asynchronously-written input/scale/metadata buffers before the BMM reads them.

This is a mitigation with a real performance cost (it kills PDL overlap and cross-layer pipelining), not a fix — but it strongly constrains where the race window lives.

## Asks

1. Confirm whether the TMEM dealloc defect in the trtllm-gen NVFP4 grouped-BMM cubins is fixed on the current ≥0.6.15 artifact line — the hang issues #4032 and #3971 are still open.
2. Consider pre-release regression coverage for the generated BMM artifacts (dynamic per-expert token counts including zero-token groups, cluster (2,1,1), on both SM100 and SM103), since this defect has shipped once, been fixed (0.6.13), and been re-introduced by an artifact regeneration (0.6.14) already.

Happy to provide the cuda-gdb session logs (kernel/warp listings, SASS excerpts) if useful.

### Bug description

## Summary

`MoEEpMegaLayer` with `Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig` hangs indefinitely when the
routing concentrates a disproportionate share of tokens on the experts owned by
a single EP rank. The GPUs sit at 100% utilization with no forward progress, so
it presents as a livelock rather than a crash — every rank is parked in
`torch.cuda.synchronize()` waiting on a kernel that never retires.

The same layer, same shapes, same weights and the same number of launches
completes normally under uniform routing.

Concentration on individual *experts* is not the trigger — a "hot expert"
distribution with roughly 3x the per-expert load of the failing case runs fine.
What matters is that the hot experts belong to the same rank.

### Minimal reproduction


## Reproducer

```bash
# hangs
NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none NVSHMEM_SYMMETRIC_SIZE=8589934592 \
  torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 repro.py
```

```bash
# completes, prints "ALL OK"
SKEW=0 NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none NVSHMEM_SYMMETRIC_SIZE=8589934592 \
  torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 repro.py
```

```python
"""Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig hangs under rank-aligned routing skew."""
import os
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import flashinfer.moe_ep as mep

H, I, E, TOPK, T = 7168, 2048, 256, 8, 4096
SKEW = os.environ.get("SKEW", "1") == "1"

dist.init_process_group("nccl")
rank, world = dist.get_rank(), dist.get_world_size()
lr = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
torch.cuda.set_device(lr)
dev = torch.device("cuda", lr)
n_local = E // world

# Expert probabilities: uniform, or 30% of the routed mass onto the experts
# owned by rank 0.  Every expert stays individually balanced; only the *rank*
# is hot.
if SKEW:
    per = E // world
    p = torch.full((E,), 0.7 / (E - per), device=dev)
    p[:per] = 0.3 / per
else:
    p = torch.full((E,), 1.0 / E, device=dev)

g = torch.Generator(device=dev)
g.manual_seed(1234 + rank)
topk_ids = torch.multinomial(
    p.unsqueeze(0).expand(T, E).contiguous(), TOPK, replacement=False, generator=g
).int()
raw = torch.rand((T, TOPK), generator=g, device=dev)
topk_weights = (raw / raw.sum(-1, keepdim=True)).float()
x = torch.randn(T, H, generator=g, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
w13 = (torch.randn(n_local, 2 * I, H, generator=g, device=dev) * H**-0.5).bfloat16()
w2 = (torch.randn(n_local, H, I, generator=g, device=dev) * I**-0.5).bfloat16()

layer = mep.MoEEpMegaLayer(
    mep.BootstrapConfig(world_size=world, rank=rank, device=lr,
                        process_group=dist.group.WORLD),
    mep.FleetParams(num_experts=E, max_tokens_per_rank=T, token_hidden_size=H),
    mep.MoEWeightPack(w13=w13, w2=w2),
    mep.MegaConfig(megakernel=mep.Nvfp4CutedslMegaMoeConfig(
        intermediate_size=I, top_k=TOPK)),
)

t = mep.MoEEpTensors(hidden_states=x, topk_ids=topk_ids, topk_weights=topk_weights)
layer.warmup(t)
if rank == 0:
    print(f"warmup done (skew={SKEW})", flush=True)

for i in range(20):
    layer.forward(t)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    if rank == 0:
        print(f"iter {i} ok", flush=True)
if rank == 0:
    print("ALL OK", flush=True)
```

## Observed

`SKEW=0` prints `warmup done`, `iter 0 ok` .. `iter 19 ok`, `ALL OK`.

`SKEW=1` prints nothing at all and never terminates — the hang is already in
`layer.warmup(t)`, which performs the first forward. `nvidia-smi` shows 100%
utilization on all 8 GPUs indefinitely. Every rank's Python stack is:

## Expected

Either the layer completes, or it raises — a routing distribution should not be
able to livelock the kernel.

records.title: [Feature]:  Add NVFP4 W4A4 MLA decode for SM100/SM103
records.body:
### Before submitting

- [x] I have searched existing issues and this request has not been filed yet.

### Problem

MHA/GQA accepts an NVFP4 KV cache through the public `kv_cache_sf` argument (#2702). MLA does not: every trtllm-gen MLA invocation in `flashinfer/mla/_core.py` passes `None` for `key_block_scales` and `value_block_scales` (`_core.py:3291-3292`, `4167-4168` on `main`).

vLLM's guard is per-model, not per-layer — `nvfp4 KV cache is not supported with MLA (Multi-head Latent Attention) backends` — so a hybrid model keeps its whole cache at FP8. Kimi-K3-NVFP4 has 24 MLA layers out of 93.

The MLA latent is `kv_lora_rank=512` + `qk_rope_head_dim=64`. Per token per layer: 1152 B in BF16, 576 B in FP8, 324 B in NVFP4 (288 B data + 36 B block scales).

#4568 scopes MLA prefill/decode to BF16 I/O with an FP8 KV cache, so this is not tracked there.


### Requested outcome

MLA decode on SM100/SM103 with an NVFP4 paged KV cache and NVFP4 compute, matching the BF16 and FP8 MLA decode kernels in semantics.

- `kv_cache_sf` accepted on `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` and `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper`, replacing the hard-coded `None` block scales.
- NVFP4 query, with FP4 global scales folded into `bmm1_scale` / `bmm2_scale`.
- Both variants of the trailing `qk_rope_head_dim` channels: `mla_use_nope=true` (Kimi-K3) and RoPE applied (DeepSeek-style).
- An NVFP4 cache write path, rather than materializing BF16/FP8 and requantizing.

Dense MLA only; sparse MLA and DSA top-k paths are out of scope.

### Target hardware

SM100 (B200, GB200), SM103 (B300, GB300)

### Inference engine

vLLM

### Affected model or model family

nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4 — https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4

### Workload and configuration

- Data type and quantization: NVFP4 KV (packed `uint8` + FP8 E4M3 block scales, `sf_vec_size=16`,
  FP32 global scale) with NVFP4 query and compute. Baselines: existing BF16 and FP8 KV MLA decode.
- Sequence lengths: 32K, 128K, the 196,608 TP8 baseline in #4568, and the 1,048,576 architectural
  maximum. Speculative query lengths 1-8.
- Parallelism: TP-local query head counts 96, 48, 24, 12, 6; decode context parallelism.
- Relevant shapes: `kv_lora_rank=512`, `qk_nope_head_dim=128`, `qk_rope_head_dim=64`,
  `v_head_dim=128`, 96 global query heads over one latent KV head, `mla_use_nope=true`. Also
  DeepSeek-V3/R1-class MLA: same latent dims, 128 query heads, RoPE applied.


### Current workaround

FP8 KV cache. There is no per-layer opt-in — the vLLM guard rejects the whole model once an MLA
backend is selected.

### Impact

Memory capacity or bandwidth, Throughput

### Acceptance criteria

- Matches the BF16 MLA reference within the tolerance used by the FP8 MLA tests, across ragged
  and non-aligned lengths, permuted and prefix-shared block tables, query lengths 1-8, TP-local
  head counts 96/48/24/12/6, NoPE and RoPE, and CUDA-graph replay.
- End-task accuracy on `nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4` reported against the FP8 KV baseline. The same
  latent feeds BMM1 as K and BMM2 as V, so one FP4 buffer bounds both logits and output.
- Complete-call benchmark against the FP8 MLA path, including query quantization and metadata
  preparation, reporting decode throughput and KV pool token capacity.
- CUDA-graph safe as page tables, lengths, and scale tensors change in place, with no KV gather, per-step allocation, host synchronization, or device-to-host metadata copy in steady state.

### Related work, dependencies, or suggested scope

- #4568 — Kimi-K3-NVFP4 tracker; its MLA item reads "BF16 I/O, FP8 KV cache". This is the NVFP4
  upgrade of that item.
- #4178 — packed low-head and variable-Q MLA decode. State which of packed low-head tiles,
  compact variable-Q, and decode context parallelism the NVFP4 path supports or rejects.
- #2702, #2363 — NVFP4 KV cache for SM100. Reuse the layout: packed `uint8` latent
  `[num_pages, page_size, (kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim) / 2]` plus a swizzled FP8 E4M3
  block-scale tensor.
- Fail fast on a packed `uint8` MLA cache with no scales; keep the 3D and 4D `kv_cache` shapes
  accepted today working.

### Timing or release need

_No response_

### Bug description


  `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` returns different results when only the host-side
  `max_seq_len` argument changes. Every tensor input — including the device `seq_lens`
  buffer — is byte-identical; only the host int differs.

  `max_seq_len` is documented as *"max sequence length for kv_cache"*, i.e. an upper
  bound, and no validation ties it to `max(seq_lens)`. This matters because it is a
  **host** int: under full CUDA-graph capture it is frozen at capture time, so a serving
  stack (e.g. vLLM with `cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`) has no choice but to bake in
  `max_model_len` and can never reproduce its own eager/piecewise output bit-for-bit.

  **This is not an accuracy regression.** Against an fp32 reference both paths are
  equidistant and both stay under 1 bf16 ULP. The problems are (a) non-reproducibility
  across an argument documented as a bound, and (b) wasted work — a 253-token sequence
  gets a 19-way KV split plus a gmem reduction.

  Root cause appears to be that `mMaxSeqLenKv` drives two host-side heuristics:

  - `include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaKernels.cuh:617` computes `maxNumCtasPerSeqKv`
    from `mMaxSeqLenKv`, and `:649` derives the KV-split factor `numCtasPerSeqKv`.
    `:657` disables multi-CTA mode (and re-selects a kernel with the persistent
    scheduler) when the split is 1; `:679` upgrades to `CgaSmemReduction` when it is ≤ 16.
  - `:1051-1060` uses `mMaxSeqLenKv` in the kernel-selection cost model that picks
    `tileSizeQ`.

  A different split / reduction mode / kernel changes the accumulation order, hence the
  bf16 rounding. The cliff is visible at `seq_len` 4864 → 4865, which is exactly where
  `ceil(seq_len / 256)` crosses the SM-derived cap on a 152-SM GB200.

  The effect disappears at large batch (batch=32 shows bit-equality), because the split
  heuristic never engages there.

  ### Expected

  For a fixed set of tensor inputs, any `max_seq_len >= max(seq_lens)` should give the
  same result — or the docstring should state that `max_seq_len` perturbs numerics and
  that eager/CUDA-graph bit-exactness is not available.


  ### Output

  ```
  NVIDIA GB200  batch=1, q_len=1, 64q/8kv heads, head_dim=64, page=16, bf16

  seq_lens=[253]
     max_seq_len  bit-equal  max|d vs exact-hint|  max|d vs fp32|
             253       True             0.000e+00       9.863e-04
            8192      False             1.953e-03       1.815e-03
           32768      False             1.953e-03       1.815e-03
           65535      False             1.953e-03       1.815e-03

  seq_lens=[1024]
     max_seq_len  bit-equal  max|d vs exact-hint|  max|d vs fp32|
            1024       True             0.000e+00       9.955e-04
            8192      False             9.766e-04       8.219e-04
           32768      False             9.766e-04       8.219e-04
           65535      False             9.766e-04       8.219e-04

  seq_lens=[4096]
     max_seq_len  bit-equal  max|d vs exact-hint|  max|d vs fp32|
            4096       True             0.000e+00       3.865e-04
            8192      False             4.883e-04       3.251e-04
           32768      False             4.883e-04       3.251e-04
           65535      False             4.883e-04       3.251e-04

  seq_lens=[4864]
     max_seq_len  bit-equal  max|d vs exact-hint|  max|d vs fp32|
            4864       True             0.000e+00       3.752e-04
            8192       True             0.000e+00       3.752e-04
           32768      False             4.883e-04       3.565e-04
           65535      False             4.883e-04       3.565e-04

  seq_lens=[4865]
     max_seq_len  bit-equal  max|d vs exact-hint|  max|d vs fp32|
            4865       True             0.000e+00       3.077e-04
            8192       True             0.000e+00       3.077e-04
           32768       True             0.000e+00       3.077e-04
           65535       True             0.000e+00       3.077e-04
  ```


### Minimal reproduction

```python
"""trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache: the output changes when only the host-side
  `max_seq_len` argument changes."""

  import torch
  from flashinfer.decode import trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache

  H_Q, H_KV, D, P = 64, 8, 64, 16
  DEV = "cuda"


  def fp32_reference(q, kv_cache, block_table, seq_len):
      pages = block_table[: (seq_len + P - 1) // P]
      k = kv_cache[pages, 0].permute(1, 0, 2, 3).reshape(H_KV, -1, D)[:, :seq_len].float()
      v = kv_cache[pages, 1].permute(1, 0, 2, 3).reshape(H_KV, -1, D)[:, :seq_len].float()
      rep = H_Q // H_KV
      k, v = k.repeat_interleave(rep, 0), v.repeat_interleave(rep, 0)
      s = (q.float().squeeze(0).unsqueeze(1) @ k.transpose(1, 2)) * D**-0.5
      return (s.softmax(-1) @ v).squeeze(1).unsqueeze(0)


  def main():
      torch.manual_seed(0)
      n_pages = 65536 // P
      # canonical HND kv cache: [num_pages, 2, num_kv_heads, page_size, head_dim]
      kv_cache = torch.randn(n_pages, 2, H_KV, P, D, device=DEV, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
      block_table = torch.arange(n_pages, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEV)
      workspace = torch.zeros(128 * 1024 * 1024, dtype=torch.uint8, device=DEV)
      q = torch.randn(1, H_Q, D, device=DEV, dtype=torch.bfloat16)

      def decode(seq_lens, max_seq_len):
          return trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache(
              query=q,
              kv_cache=kv_cache,
              workspace_buffer=workspace,
              block_tables=block_table.unsqueeze(0),
              seq_lens=seq_lens,
              max_seq_len=max_seq_len,
              bmm1_scale=D**-0.5,
              bmm2_scale=1.0,
              backend="trtllm-gen",
          ).clone()

      print(f"{torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}  batch=1, q_len=1, {H_Q}q/{H_KV}kv heads, "
            f"head_dim={D}, page={P}, bf16\n")

      for seq_len in (253, 1024, 4096, 4864, 4865):
          seq_lens = torch.tensor([seq_len], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEV)
          ref = fp32_reference(q, kv_cache, block_table, seq_len)
          exact = decode(seq_lens, seq_len)
          print(f"seq_lens=[{seq_len}]")
          print(f"  {'max_seq_len':>12} {'bit-equal':>10} {'max|d vs exact-hint|':>21}"
                f" {'max|d vs fp32|':>15}")
          for hint in (seq_len, 8192, 32768, 65535):
              if hint < seq_len:
                  continue
              out = decode(seq_lens, hint)
              print(f"  {hint:>12} {str(torch.equal(out, exact)):>10}"
                    f" {(out.float() - exact.float()).abs().max().item():>21.3e}"
                    f" {(out.float() - ref).abs().max().item():>15.3e}")
          print()


  if __name__ == "__main__":
      main()
```

records.title: [Bug] flashinfer-jit-cache wheel build fails without nvidia-cutlass-dsl after #4526
records.body:
### Description

  Recent nightly release builds of flashinfer-jit-cache fail with:
  https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/actions/runs/32321975995 

  Failed to compile AOT modules: No module named 'cutlass'
  ```
    File "/workspace/flashinfer-jit-cache/build_backend.py", line 121, in _compile_jit_cache
      from flashinfer import aot
    File "/workspace/flashinfer/__init__.py", line 112, in <module>
      from .gemm import SegmentGEMMWrapper
    File "/workspace/flashinfer/gemm/gemm_base.py", line 66, in <module>
      from .kernels.utils import (
    File "/workspace/flashinfer/gemm/kernels/__init__.py", line 32, in <module>
      from flashinfer.cute_dsl.utils import (
    File "/workspace/flashinfer/cute_dsl/utils.py", line 25, in <module>
      import cutlass
  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cutlass'
```
### Suspected regression

  This appears to have been introduced by #4526 (f09227492c2654ede5315356fab58891adf70afa).

  That PR added the following package-level import to flashinfer/gemm/kernels/__init__.py:

  from flashinfer.cute_dsl.utils import (
      is_cute_dsl_available,
      is_rubin_cute_dsl_available,
  )

  However, flashinfer/cute_dsl/utils.py imports cutlass at module scope before is_cute_dsl_available() can be called:
```
  import cutlass
```
  Consequently, importing .kernels.utils first executes flashinfer.gemm.kernels.__init__, making cutlass an unconditional dependency of import flashinfer.

### Why this affects the JIT-cache build

  flashinfer-jit-cache/build_backend.py imports the main package while compiling AOT modules:
```
  from flashinfer import aot
```
  The isolated build dependencies in flashinfer-jit-cache/pyproject.toml do not include nvidia-cutlass-dsl, because CuTe DSL is intended to remain optional.

  Before #4526, importing flashinfer.gemm.kernels did not import flashinfer.cute_dsl.utils, so the JIT-cache wheel could be built without CuTe DSL.

### Expected behavior

  - import flashinfer should succeed without nvidia-cutlass-dsl.
  - The JIT-cache wheel should build in its declared isolated build environment.
  - CuTe DSL modules should only be imported when a CuTe DSL backend is requested.

  ### Suggested fix (By Codex)

  Keep flashinfer/gemm/kernels/__init__.py lightweight by removing the CuTe DSL package-level imports and re-exports added by #4526.

  The actual GEMM implementation already imports modules such as .kernels.bmm_fp8_wrapper lazily when the CuTe DSL backend is selected, so package-level re-exports do not appear necessary.

  Adding nvidia-cutlass-dsl to the JIT-cache build dependencies could mask the failure, but it would turn an optional dependency into a mandatory build dependency and would not address the broader import flashinfer regression.

  ### Regression test

  Add a test verifying that the following succeeds in an environment without nvidia-cutlass-dsl:

  python -c "import flashinfer"

  The existing isolated JIT-cache wheel build should also cover this case:

  python -m build --wheel flashinfer-jit-cache

records.title: [Bug] CUTLASS NVFP4 MoE rejects Relu2 intermediate_size=1856 due to scale-factor alignment mismatch
records.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I searched existing issues and did not find an existing report for this NVFP4 alignment mismatch.

## Environment

- FlashInfer version: `0.6.18`
- FlashInfer commit: `4927c0e`
- GPU: NVIDIA B300 (`NVIDIA_B300_SXM6_AC`)
- CUDA: 13.0
- Python: 3.12
- Container: `flashinfer/flashinfer-ci-cu130:20260811-e673f7f`
- Routine/backend: `cutlass_fused_moe` / CUTLASS NVFP4

## Bug description

`cutlass_fused_moe` rejects the valid non-gated Nemotron-3-Nano shape `hidden_size=2688, intermediate_size=1856` when using NVFP4 weights and `Relu2` activation.

The benchmark prepares the FC1 scale-factor N dimension with 128-element padding, so 1856 is padded to 1920. The CUTLASS binding validates that N dimension using `MinKDimAlignmentNVFP4` (64) instead of `MinNDimAlignmentNVFP4` (128), and therefore expects 1856. The resulting 1920-vs-1856 mismatch triggers the shape assertion.

Expected behavior: the non-gated NVFP4 case should run successfully with the real model dimensions. Dimensions should not need to be changed to 1920 merely to bypass validation.

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
python3 benchmarks/flashinfer_benchmark.py \
  --routine cutlass_fused_moe \
  --num_tokens 1 \
  --hidden_size 2688 \
  --intermediate_size 1856 \
  --num_experts 128 \
  --top_k 6 \
  --cutlass_variant nvfp4 \
  --input_dtype bfloat16 \
  --activation-type Relu2 \
  --verbose \
  --generate_repro_command \
  --case_tag Nemotron-3-Nano-decode
```

## Error messages / logs

```text
[ERROR] Error running test: --routine cutlass_fused_moe --num_tokens 1 --hidden_size 2688 --intermediate_size 1856 --num_experts 128 --top_k 6 --cutlass_variant nvfp4 --input_dtype bfloat16 --activation-type Relu2 --verbose --generate_repro_command --case_tag "Nemotron-3-Nano-decode"
[ERROR] Error: Check failed: (fc1_weight_block.size(0) == num_experts_on_rank && fc1_weight_block.size(1) == TmaWarpSpecializedGroupedGemmInput::alignToSfDim(inter_size, TmaWarpSpecializedGroupedGemmInput::MinKDimAlignmentNVFP4) && fc1_weight_block.size(2) * FP8_PER_INT32 * TmaWarpSpecializedGroupedGemmInput::NVFP4BlockScaleVectorSize == TmaWarpSpecializedGroupedGemmInput::alignToSfDim(hidden_size, TmaWarpSpecializedGroupedGemmInput::MinKDimAlignmentNVFP4)) is false: fc1 weight block size must be (num_experts_on_rank, inter_size, hidden_size // 4 // block_scale_vector_size)
```

## Additional context

The likely faulty check is in `csrc/fused_moe/cutlass_backend/flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe_binding.cu`, in the NVFP4 branch of `getQuantParams()`. FC1's outer/N dimension is checked with `MinKDimAlignmentNVFP4`; it appears that `MinNDimAlignmentNVFP4` should be used instead.

This is related to, but distinct from, #2731: that issue covered hardcoded gated-activation multipliers in MXFP8 paths, while this report concerns NVFP4 N/K scale-factor alignment.

records.title: [DSv4 TRT-LLM Attention] Accuracy/Perf fixes and API improvement
records.body:
Asks:
1. Tolerate padded inputs and mismatched sizing between input and metadata tables (ignore q rows beyond metadata; don't read per-token tables past num_tokens to the 64-row tile edge; invalid/-1 index = skip, never dereference). **Severity:** Highest. Functional WARs exists in framework, but sensitive to feature changes that can lead to accuracy degradation / IMA errors, and larger perf impact. See problems 1-3 for detailed insight.
2. Accept separate SWA + compressed tables and fuse the combine in-call. **Severity:** estimated low, functional WAR in framework available and perf drop should be negligible. See problem 3 for more details.
3. Accept a caller-owned persistent buffer on the DSv4 entry point, document the real sizing formula, and never allocate internally during capture. **Severity:** low, Functional WAR in framework is available and perf drop is negligible. See problem 4 for more details. 
4. Accept raw lengths tensor + a scalar offset to produce `sparse_topk_lens`. **Severity:** low, functional WAR in framework available and perf drop is negligible. See problem 5 for more details.

**Problem 1 (Stability/Accuracy):** Sensitivity to mismatch between Q and metadata table sizes. If Q is larger than the metadata tables, it will read into unallocated addresses, and the garbage data there could point anywhere rather than valid KV addresses, leading to IMA.
- **Occurs with:** DP + MTP. SGLang plans metadata before DP padding under this combination.
- **Kernel level (FI) Ask:** tolerate padded inputs and mismatching sizes better. For example, flashmla ignores the extra query rows.
- **Framework level fix:** (matches how TRT-LLM does it) pre-allocate a large metadata table, so that the indexing of dummy q rows reads dummy metadata that points to either sentinel values or real addresses. Since they are dummy rows it will get discarded downstream anyway, but this will avoid the IMA since we know the metadata contents will resolve to real addresses.
- **Current approach in SGLang:** checks for the real rows and only runs on that input, then fills the result into a pre-allocated zeroed result of the expected shape.

**Problem 2 (Stability/Accuracy):** Intermittent IMA with overlap scheduler + MTP. The signature is the same as problem 1 but the exact root cause is less clear. It also seems to cause silent accuracy degradation even when there is no crash. I need to test the above framework level fix to see if it is sufficient to resolve, but the kernel change may also be necessary.

**Problem 3 (Perf):** Combined vs Separate indexing metadata table
- API requires a combined table, which doesn't match the format SGLang uses natively for DSv4 metadata.
- Given problems 1 & 2 share this solution, I plan to investigate the framework level fix of pre-allocating a combined table. However, if vLLM has a similar issue, it may be valuable to support an API that accepts separate SWA + c4/c128 index tables, and fuses the operation to combine them in the call. TRT-LLM has a kernel to do this at the framework level.

following two summaries written by AI

**Problem 4 (API):** progress-counter buffer is under-sized and allocated per call
The kernel coordinates its split-KV thread blocks through an array of atomic counters, logically one per `(request, head-group, query-tile)`. Flashinfer allocates it internally every call, sized batch × heads — correct only for 1-token decode. Any multi-token launch (MTP, prefill) indexes counters past the end, leading to out-of-bounds atomic writes. Allocating inside graph capture also creates buffer-lifetime bugs. SGLang and currently monkeypatches a persistent over-sized buffer at runtime, mirroring TRT-LLM's `reserveSemaphoreArray.`
**Kernel (FI) Ask:** accept a caller-owned persistent buffer on the DSv4 entry point (the generic MLA API already has `multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer`), document the real sizing formula, and never allocate internally during capture.

**Problem 5 (API):** the lengths tensor bakes in a +128 convention
`sparse_topk_lens` must be the row's total valid length, including the fixed 128 SWA slots, but the indexer produces only the compressed-tier counts — so every layer we copy the indexer output and add 128 (two extra launches per layer, and forgetting the +128 silently truncates attention to SWA-only). 
**Kernel (FI) Ask:** accept the raw lengths plus a scalar offset (e.g. length_offset=128) so the indexer output passes straight through.

### Bug description

### What happens

`tests/gdn/test_prefill_delta_rule.py -k state_dtype` returns a different result
every time it runs. Four consecutive invocations, nothing changed in between:

```console
$ python -m pytest tests/gdn/test_prefill_delta_rule.py -k state_dtype -q -p no:cacheprovider
96 passed, 3516 deselected in 58.01s

$ python -m pytest tests/gdn/test_prefill_delta_rule.py -k state_dtype -q -p no:cacheprovider
96 failed, 3516 deselected in 59.54s

$ python -m pytest tests/gdn/test_prefill_delta_rule.py -k state_dtype -q -p no:cacheprovider
96 failed, 3516 deselected in 59.20s

$ python -m pytest tests/gdn/test_prefill_delta_rule.py -k state_dtype -q -p no:cacheprovider
72 failed, 24 passed, 3516 deselected in 58.28s
```

The failures are NaN in the kernel output. Smallest failing case — `(1, 1, 1)`
heads, `seq_lens=[64]`, bf16 state:

```
test_prefill_kernel_state_dtype[False-state_dtype0-bfloat16-seq_lens0-1-1-1-128-auto]

    torch.testing.assert_close(our_o, ref_o, atol=atol_o, rtol=rtol_o)
E   Mismatched elements: 8192 / 8192 (100.0%)
E   Greatest absolute difference: nan at index (0, 0, 0) (up to 0.1 allowed)
E   Greatest relative difference: nan at index (0, 0, 0) (up to 0.05 allowed)
```

**Within a single process the result is stable** — repeating the same call ten
times gives an identical output each time. The variation is between processes. A
loop inside one process therefore does not surface it, and a single green CI run
does not establish anything.

**Input data is not the trigger.** Holding your harness and reference fixed and
varying only the generator and the head layout — your `gen_qkv` versus inputs
with both q and k l2-normalised, `(16,16,32)` versus `(4,4,8)` — all eight
combinations flip together from run to run:

```
run 1:  ok      ok      ok      ok      ok      ok      ok      ok
run 2:  FAILED  FAILED  FAILED  FAILED  FAILED  FAILED  FAILED  FAILED
run 3:  FAILED  FAILED  FAILED  FAILED  FAILED  ok      FAILED  ok
```

**`initial_state` is not the trigger either** — `initial_state=None` produces
NaN as readily as a non-null state.

### Second, independent issue: the tolerance is larger than the signal

In runs where NaN does not strike, the output still differs from this repo's own
`blockwise_delta_rule` reference by a **relative L2 of ~0.25**. It passes
regardless, because `_test_prefill_kernel_state_dtype` asserts with `atol=1e-1`
while the outputs are ~0.03 in magnitude:

```
gen_qkv, (4,4,8) heads, seq_lens=[256,192,128], bf16 state
  relative L2 = 0.2502
  max|Δ|      = 0.0384      allowed: atol 1e-1 + rtol 5e-2 × 0.0731
  max|ref|    = 0.0731
```

The absolute tolerance exceeds the signal, so a green run of this test does not
show the kernel is numerically correct. Consider keying the tolerance to the
output norm, or asserting a relative-L2 bound instead of an absolute 1e-1.

### Why the neighbouring tests stay green

- `test_prefill_kernel_basic` always passes `initial_state=None`.
- `test_prefill_state_indices` compares the pooled path against the packed path
  — kernel against kernel — so it is satisfied whenever both are equally wrong.

`test_prefill_kernel_state_dtype` is the only test comparing a non-null
`initial_state` against a reference, and it is the one that flaps.


_No response_

records.title: [Bug] SM12x CuTe-DSL W4A16 MoE: host-side OverflowError in build_memref_desc for expert tensors >2 GiB (DGX Spark / GB10)
records.body:
## Summary

Launching the SM12x CuTe-DSL W4A16 fused-MoE kernel
(`flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell_sm12x/moe_w4a16_kernel.py`) with an
expert weight tensor of ~2.5 GiB fails **deterministically on the host side**
during argument marshalling: `nvidia_cutlass_dsl`'s `build_memref_desc` packs a
tensor size/stride into a 32-bit slot and raises

```
OverflowError: Value overflow: 2684354560 exceeds range of l
```

2,684,354,560 = 2.5 GiB — the flattened per-bank expert tensor of
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 (256 experts). Consumer SM120 cards with ≤32 GB VRAM
typically shard below the 2^31 boundary, which is likely why this path hasn't
been hit; on GB10's 128 GB unified memory the full bank crosses it.

Distinct from #2776 (device-side illegal memory access, trtllm fp4 path,
flashinfer 0.6.4) and #3383 (EP>1 illegal address after state_E patch): this
one never reaches the GPU — it's pure Python/ctypes marshalling in the DSL.

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | NVIDIA GB10 (DGX Spark), SM 12.1 |
| Driver / CUDA | 580.173.02 / 13.0 |
| flashinfer-python | 0.6.17 (+ flashinfer-cubin 0.6.17, flashinfer-jit-cache 0.6.17+cu130) |
| PyTorch | 2.11.0+cu130, Python 3.12, aarch64 |
| Caller | FreeToken MoE serving engine, NVFP4 "b12x" expert backend |
| Model | nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 |

## Traceback (tail)

```
File ".../flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell_sm12x/moe_w4a16_kernel.py", line 6150, in _w4a16_fused_moe_launch_op
  _w4a16_fused_moe_launch_flat(
File ".../flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell_sm12x/moe_w4a16_kernel.py", line 5979, in _w4a16_fused_moe_launch_flat
  fused.compiled(
File ".../nvidia_cutlass_dsl/dsl_packages/cutlass/base_dsl/jit_executor.py", line 1395, in __call__
File ".../nvidia_cutlass_dsl/dsl_packages/cutlass/base_dsl/jit_executor.py", line 661, in generate_execution_args
File ".../nvidia_cutlass_dsl/dsl_packages/cutlass/base_dsl/typing.py", line 239, in get_c_pointers
File ".../nvidia_cutlass_dsl/dsl_packages/cutlass/cute/runtime.py", line 924, in __c_pointers__
File ".../nvidia_cutlass_dsl/dsl_packages/cutlass/cute/runtime.py", line 434, in __c_pointers__
  self._memref_desc = self._dltensor_wrapper.build_memref_desc(
OverflowError: Value overflow: 2684354560 exceeds range of l
```

## Reproduction

Any `_w4a16_fused_moe_launch_op` call where one flattened expert-bank tensor
exceeds 2^31 elements/bytes. Observed on the first decode step (during CUDA
graph capture warmup) after loading Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 in the b12x layout
on GB10. Happy to provide a minimal standalone repro or test a patch on DGX
Spark hardware.

## Expected

64-bit sizes/strides in the memref descriptor (DLTensor fields are int64) —
or, failing that, a capability check that rejects >2 GiB banks with an
actionable error instead of an OverflowError five frames deep in the DSL.
